नक्षत्राणि ह त्वेवैषोऽग्निश्चितः । तानि वा एतानि सप्तविग्०शतिनक्षत्राणि । छंदाग्ंसि ह त्वेवैषोऽग्निश्चितः । तानि वा एतानि सप्तछंदाग्ंसि.... । सर्वाणि ह त्वेन भूतानि । सर्वॆ देवा एषोऽग्निश्चित आपो वै सर्वॆ देवाः सर्वाणि भूतानि ता हैता आस एवैषोऽग्निश्चितस्तस्य नाव्या एव परिश्रितस्ताः षष्टिश्च त्रीणि च शतानि भवंति षष्टिश्च ह वै त्रीणि च शतान्यादित्यं नाव्याः समंतं परियंति .... आत्मायमेव स योऽयं हिरण्मयः पुरुषः ॥ (*nakṣatrāṇi ha tvevaiṣo 'gniścitaḥ | tāni vā etāni saptavig0śatinakṣatrāṇi | chaṃdāgṃsi ha tvevaiṣo 'gniścitaḥ | tāni vā etāni saptachaṃdāgṃsi.... | sarvāṇi ha tvena bhūtāni | sarvè devā eṣo 'gniścita āpo vai sarvè devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tā haitā āsa evaiṣo 'gniścitastasya nāvyā eva pariśritastāḥ ṣaṣṭiśca trīṇi ca śatāni bhavaṃti ṣaṣṭiśca ha vai trīṇi ca śatānyādityaṃ nāvyāḥ samaṃtaṃ pariyaṃti .... ātmāyameva sa yo 'yaṃ hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 10-5-4-6 to 14)
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 230

This sacrificial altar is all the stars and the seven metres. It is the year. It is all beings. Just as the three hundred and sixty boats in the form of rays surround the sun, so the gods, humans and others, in the form of the Yajuṣmatī bricks, surround this altar. The body of this altar is the golden Person within the sun. How attractive and how great is the nature of this golden Person?

तस्यैते प्रतिष्ठे । रुक्ष्मश्च पुष्करपर्णं चापश्चादित्यमंडलं च स्रुचौ बाहू ताविंद्राग्नी द्वे स्वयमातृण्णे इयं चांतरिक्षं च तिस्रो विश्वज्योतिष एता देवता अग्निर्वायुरादित्य एता ह्येव देवता विश्वं ज्योतिर्द्वादशर्तव्याः संवत्सरः स आत्मा पंच नाकसदः पंच पंच चूडाः स यज्ञस्ते देवा अथ यद्विकर्णि च स्वयमातृण्णा चाश्मा........आत्मा स एष सर्वासामपां मध्यॆ स एष सर्वैः कामैः संपन्न आपो वै सर्वॆ कामाः स एषोऽकामः सर्वकामो न ह्येतं कस्य चन कामः ॥ (*tasyaite pratiṣṭhe | rukṣmaśca puṣkaraparṇaṃ cāpaścādityamaṃḍalaṃ ca srucau bāhū tāviṃdrāgnī dve svayamātṛṇṇe iyaṃ cāṃtarikṣaṃ ca tisro viśvajyotiṣa etā devatā agnirvāyurāditya etā hyeva devatā viśvaṃ jyotirdvādaśartavyāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ sa ātmā paṃca nākasadaḥ paṃca paṃca cūḍāḥ sa yajñaste devā atha yadvikarṇi ca svayamātṛṇṇā cāśmā........ātmā sa eṣa sarvāsāmapāṃ madhyè sa eṣa sarvaiḥ kāmaiḥ saṃpanna āpo vai sarvè kāmāḥ sa eṣo 'kāmaḥ sarvakāmo na hyetaṃ kasya cana kāmaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-5-4-15)

The golden vessel and the lotus leaf are the two feet of this golden Person within the sun. The two Sruc ladles on the sacrificial altar are his arms, and they are Indra and Agni. The two naturally perforated bricks are earth and atmosphere. The bricks in the form of the Viśvajyotis are all the deities; their number is three. These three reflect Agni, Vāyu and Āditya. The body of this altar is the end of all. This golden Person within the sun, in the form of the altar, has obtained all desires and therefore is free of desire and fully satisfied. In this way the greatness and extent of the altar are praised in many ways. Its glory is praised not only from the standpoint of the deities but also from the standpoint of the self. The same point is described in the present Ṛk in the words इयं वेदिः पृथिव्या अंतः (*iyaṃ vediḥ pṛthivyā aṃtaḥ*): the purport is that the altar is the highest place of the earth. To convey this same sense Sāyaṇa cites the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence एतावती वै पृथिवी यावती वेदिः । (*etāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vediḥ |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-4-1), and explains with न हि वेद्यतिरिक्ता भूमिरस्ति । (*na hi vedyatiriktā bhūmirasti |*) that there is no earth beyond or other than this sacrificial altar.

(2) Next, to the second question, पृच्छामि यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः (*pṛcchāmi yatra bhuvanasya nābhiḥ*), the answer अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः । (*ayaṃ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiḥ |*) is stated right there. The word nābhi is explained as संनाहः (*saṃnāhaḥ*): the question asks what is the binding thread that shows a connection among all the classes of beings. As the answer to this question the commentary says आयं यज्ञः भूतजातस्य संनहनं । तत्रैव वृष्ट्या दिसर्वफलोत्पत्तेः सर्वप्राणिनां बंधकत्वात् । (*āyaṃ yajñaḥ bhūtajātasya saṃnahanaṃ | tatraiva vṛṣṭyā disarvaphalotpatteḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ baṃdhakatvāt |*). From this sacrifice rain arises, and through that rain it binds all living beings; hence it is described as being in the form of the nābhi.

### Printed p. 231

It was stated earlier that the word nābhi has various meanings: dwelling place, pervasive connection, saṃnāhaka (that is, protector, binder), place of origin, and so on. If in the present Ṛk the sacrifice is called the nābhi, the use of the word can be shown in all these senses. To the question asked in पृच्छामि यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः (*pṛcchāmi yatra bhuvanasya nābhiḥ*) the words अयं यज्ञः (*ayaṃ yajñaḥ*) are themselves the answer. The sacrifice is the cause of the origin and continuance of all worlds, and is the binding means that builds mutual connection among all beings, gods, humans and others; therefore it (the sacrifice) is in the form of the nābhi — this is the intention.

देवान् भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयंतु वः । परस्परं भावयंतः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ (*devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayaṃtu vaḥ | parasparaṃ bhāvayaṃtaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha ‖*) (Bh. Gī. 3-11)**NOTE**

देवान् इंद्रादीन् भावयत वर्धयत अनेन यज्ञेन। ते देवा भावयंतु वृष्ट्वा दिना आप्याययंतु वः युष्मान् । एवं परस्परं अन्नोन्यं भावयंतः श्रेयः परं ब्रह्मविज्ञानप्राप्तिं क्रमेण अवाप्स्यथ । स्वर्गं वा परं श्रेयः अपाप्यथ ॥ (*devān iṃdrādīn bhāvayata vardhayata anena yajñena| te devā bhāvayaṃtu vṛṣṭvā dinā āpyāyayaṃtu vaḥ yuṣmān | evaṃ parasparaṃ annonyaṃ bhāvayaṃtaḥ śreyaḥ paraṃ brahmavijñānaprāptiṃ krameṇa avāpsyatha | svargaṃ vā paraṃ śreyaḥ apāpyatha ‖*)

The Bhagavadgītā teaches that the sacrifice is food for the gods; that humans must offer this food in the form of sacrifice; and that the gods, satisfied by it, must become the cause of human sustenance and growth through rain and the like. From this the sacrifice becomes the means of all welfare. Śaṅkara and others explain that if one understands the principle that this sacrifice is the means of welfare for the whole world and performs it in a spirit of service, it becomes a means to knowledge of Brahman as well.

This principle of sacrifice teaches the unity of the universe, and that the ground of this unity is the principle of the Supreme Brahman. What the Upaniṣads and other texts call the Supreme Brahman as the fundamental principle, the Saṃhitā and the Brāhmaṇas call Prajāpati, and they declare the identity of the sacrifice and Prajāpati. The creation of the universe is the fruit of Prajāpati's sacrifice and austerity. Prajāpati, the cause of the world, who before the creation of the world was without a second, had to offer himself as the oblation in order to carry out the sacrifice that is the means of creation.

य आत्मदा बलदा यस्य विश्व उपासते प्रशिषं यस्य देवाः । यस्य छायामृतं यस्य मृत्युः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥ (*ya ātmadā baladā yasya viśva upāsate praśiṣaṃ yasya devāḥ | yasya chāyāmṛtaṃ yasya mṛtyuḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-2)

As described in such mantras, Prajāpati carried out the work of creation by offering himself in his own universal sacrifice. The gods and the rest all obey his command. Death and immortality are his shadows. To such Prajāpati, the cause of the universe, let us also offer oblations and the like and worship him with sacrificial rites

### Printed p. 232

— thus the pre-eminence of the sacrifice is praised. The sacrifice is the root of creation, the cause of its continuance, and the means of welfare. This very matter is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in this way:

आथ देवाः ॥ अन्नोन्यमस्मिन्नेव जुह्वतश्चेरुस्तेभ्यः प्रजापतिरात्मानं प्रददौ यज्ञो हैषामास यज्ञो हि देवानामन्नं ॥ (*ātha devāḥ ‖ annonyamasminneva juhvataścerustebhyaḥ prajāpatirātmānaṃ pradadau yajño haiṣāmāsa yajño hi devānāmannaṃ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-1-8-2)

The gods performed the sacrifice and offered oblations favourable to one another. Then Prajāpati offered himself to them. Then the sacrifice became the property of the gods. For this very reason the sacrifice is called the food of the gods (the means of food). Moreover:

स एतेन यज्ञेन देवेभ्य आत्मानं निरक्रीणीत यद्व्रतमुपैति यथैव तत्प्रजापतिर्देवेभ्य आत्मानं प्रायच्छदेवमेवैष एतद्देवेभ्य आत्मानं प्रयच्छति तस्मादु संयत एवैताग्ं रात्रिं चिचरिषेद्यथा हविषा चरेदेवग्ं हनिर्ह्येष देवानां भवति ॥ (*sa etena yajñena devebhya ātmānaṃ nirakrīṇīta yadvratamupaiti yathaiva tatprajāpatirdevebhya ātmānaṃ prāyacchadevamevaiṣa etaddevebhya ātmānaṃ prayacchati tasmādu saṃyata evaitāgṃ rātriṃ cicariṣedyathā haviṣā caredevagṃ hanirhyeṣa devānāṃ bhavati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-1-8-3)

Prajāpati, satisfied by the sacrifice of the gods, offered himself to them, and afterwards created again a counterpart of himself representing the sacrifice. Because he thus created a counterpart of himself for the sake of the sacrifice and reflected the sacrifice, the knowers call Prajāpati himself by the synonymous name "sacrifice".

अथ यद्यज्ञं तनुते । यज्ञेनैवैतद्देवेभ्य आत्मानं निष्क्रीणीते यथैव तत्प्रजापतिर्निरक्रीणीतैवं अथ यद्धविनिर्नपति हविषैनैतद्यज्ञं निष्क्रीणाति हविरनुवाक्यानुवाक्यामवदानेनावदानं याज्यया याज्यां वषट्कारेण वषट्कारं ॥ (*atha yadyajñaṃ tanute | yajñenaivaitaddevebhya ātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīte yathaiva tatprajāpatirnirakrīṇītaivaṃ atha yaddhavinirnapati haviṣainaitadyajñaṃ niṣkrīṇāti haviranuvākyānuvākyāmavadānenāvadānaṃ yājyayā yājyāṃ vaṣaṭkāreṇa vaṣaṭkāraṃ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-1-8-4)

The Śatapatha says that whoever follows the path of Prajāpati, performs the sacrificial rite, repays his debt and is freed from the debt to the gods, helps Prajāpati in his work of creation. The same point is made in the Bhagavadgītā too:

इष्टान्भोगान् हि वो देवा दास्यंते यज्ञभाविताः । तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुंक्ते स्तेन एव सः । यज्ञशिष्टातिनः संतो मुच्यंते सर्वकिल्पिषैः । ते त्वघं भुंजते पापा ये पचंत्यात्मकारणात् ॥ (*iṣṭānbhogān hi vo devā dāsyaṃte yajñabhāvitāḥ | tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṃkte stena eva saḥ | yajñaśiṣṭātinaḥ saṃto mucyaṃte sarvakilpiṣaiḥ | te tvaghaṃ bhuṃjate pāpā ye pacaṃtyātmakāraṇāt ‖*) (Bh. Gī. 3-12, 13)

### Printed p. 233

The gods, satisfied by the sacrifice, give humans in return the things each desires. If one receives food and other wealth from the gods and then does not in return offer the gods a satisfying sacrificial oblation, he becomes a thief. Good people who perform the sacrificial rite become free of sin. Those who do not are sinners and experience the fruit of sin; for this sacrifice is the thread that shows a single connection for the whole universe. This is also called the wheel of the universe. For example:

अन्नाद्भवंति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्न संभवः । यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवं । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितं ॥ एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः । अघायुरिंद्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥ (*annādbhavaṃti bhūtāni parjanyādanna saṃbhavaḥ | yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ ‖ karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavaṃ | tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitaṃ ‖ evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ | aghāyuriṃdriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati ‖*) (Bh. Gī. 3-13 to 16)

From the sacrifice, which is action, comes Parjanya (rain); from Parjanya, food; from food, beings (living creatures). This action in the form of sacrifice arose from Brahman. Therefore the Supreme Brahman, who is the source of the creation of the universe, of all kinds of activities, and of the universe-wheel of recurrence, is eternally established in the sacrifice. Whoever, not knowing this principle of the universe in the form of sacrifice, does not follow the course of this fixed wheel of the universe, and acts at will, is the most sinful.

Thus, in the Gītā and other texts, the principle of sacrifice taught by the Vedic texts is explained. This principle of sacrifice, stated in the present Ṛk as भुवनस्य नाभिः (*bhuvanasya nābhiḥ*), is praised in the same way in other parts of the Ṛksaṃhitā also:

यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् । ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचंत यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः संति देवाः ॥ (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāstāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan | te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacaṃta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ saṃti devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-50; 10-90-16)

The gods worshipped Prajāpati, who is of the nature of sacrifice, by their sacrifice, which consisted of their resolve and was meditative. This kind of sacrifice became the source of all the worldly dharmas. These dharmas, established in the atmosphere, keep the gods who dwell in the heavenly world in their respective places. Through the sacrifice alone, all beings created by Prajāpati obtain the food and strength that are the cause of their continuance. Therefore the necessity of the sacrifice is taught in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in this way:

### Printed p. 234

प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ताः सृष्टाः क्षुधं न्यायन्त्स एतं नवरात्रमपश्यत्तमाहरत्तेनायजत ततो वै प्रजाभ्योऽकल्पत यर्हि प्रजाः क्षुधं निगच्छेयुस्तर्हि नवरात्रेण यजेतेमे हि वा एतासां लोका अक्षृप्ता॥ (*prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ kṣudhaṃ nyāyantsa etaṃ navarātramapaśyattamāharattenāyajata tato vai prajābhyo 'kalpata yarhi prajāḥ kṣudhaṃ nigaccheyustarhi navarātreṇa yajeteme hi vā etāsāṃ lokā akṣṛptā‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 7-2-4-1)

After Prajāpati created the creatures, they began to suffer from hunger. To remove their hunger he saw the sacrifice consisting of nine nights and performed the sacrifice with it. By that, the hunger of those creatures was appeased. Therefore it is natural that the sacrifice should be performed to appease hunger. This sacrifice keeps the three worlds in a single state and under regulation. How?

कल्पंतेऽस्मा इमे लोका ऊर्जं प्रजासु दधाति त्रिरात्रेणैवेमं लोकं कल्पयति त्रिरात्रेणांतरिक्षं त्रिरात्रेणामुं लोकं यथा गुणे गुणमन्वस्यत्येवमेव तल्लोके लोकमन्वस्यति धृत्या अशिथिलं भावाय ॥ (*kalpaṃte 'smā ime lokā ūrjaṃ prajāsu dadhāti trirātreṇaivemaṃ lokaṃ kalpayati trirātreṇāṃtarikṣaṃ trirātreṇāmuṃ lokaṃ yathā guṇe guṇamanvasyatyevameva talloke lokamanvasyati dhṛtyā aśithilaṃ bhāvāya ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 7-2-4-2)

By this sacrifice of the nine nights the three worlds obtained vitality. By one three-night period for the earth, by another three-night period for the atmosphere, and by the remaining three-night period for the heavenly world, Prajāpati arranged the power of continuance by the power of this sacrifice. Just as a cloth is made by joining thread with thread in warp and woof, he arranged by this sacrifice a connection of the nature of warp and woof for the three worlds, so as to bring about their non-slackening, and to produce a single power connected with the whole universe, so that the three worlds remain in their fixed state. This sacrifice is the pulse of the life of the universe. That is explained in the Śatapatha thus:

सर्वेषां वा एष भूतानाग्ं सर्वेषां देवानामात्मा यद्यज्ञस्तस्य समृद्धिमनु यजमानः प्रजया पशुभिर्युध्यते ॥ (*sarveṣāṃ vā eṣa bhūtānāgṃ sarveṣāṃ devānāmātmā yadyajñastasya samṛddhimanu yajamānaḥ prajayā paśubhiryudhyate ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 14-3-2-1)

This sacrifice is the very self of all humans and all gods. The man who performs this sacrifice obtains good offspring and wealth of cattle. And:

स यदग्नौ जुहोति । तद्देवेषु जुहोति तस्माद्देवाः संत्यथ यत्सदपि भक्षयंति तन्ननुष्येषु जुहोति तस्मान्मनुष्याः संत्यथ यद्धविर्धानयोर्नाराशग्‌ंसाः सीदंति तत्पितृषु जुहोति तस्मात्पितरः संति ॥ (*sa yadagnau juhoti | taddeveṣu juhoti tasmāddevāḥ saṃtyatha yatsadapi bhakṣayaṃti tannanuṣyeṣu juhoti tasmānmanuṣyāḥ saṃtyatha yaddhavirdhānayornārāśagṃsāḥ sīdaṃti tatpitṛṣu juhoti tasmātpitaraḥ saṃti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 2-6-2-25)

### Printed p. 235

What is offered in the fire is offered to the gods. Therefore the gods maintain their state. By the (Soma) juice distributed in the Sadas, the state of humans is maintained. The oblation offered from the Nārāśaṃsa vessel satisfies the ancestors. Therefore a man must repay both his debt to the gods and his debt to the ancestors by the sacrificial rite alone; without this there is no release for him. In the sentence quoted earlier from the Taittirīya Saṃhitā,

तल्लोके लोकमन्वस्यति धृत्या अशिथिलंभानाय । (*talloke lokamanvasyati dhṛtyā aśithilaṃbhānāya |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 7-2-4-2)**NOTE**

it is stated that the sacrificial rite is necessary so that the existence of the universe may be firm and not slack, and so that the connection of the three worlds may be interwoven like warp and woof. When the three debts are spoken of, too, this mutual bond is described.

ऋणग्ं ह वै जायते योऽस्ति स जायमान ऎव देवेभ्य ऋषिभ्यः पितृभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यः ॥ (*ṛṇagṃ ha vai jāyate yo 'sti sa jāyamāna èva devebhya ṛṣibhyaḥ pitṛbhyo manuṣyebhyaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-7-2-1)

During the whole life of every person, the debt to the gods, the debt to the seers and the debt to the ancestors, which came with his very birth, remain a burden upon him.

स यदेव यजेत । तेन देवेभ्य ऋणं जायते तद्धेभ्य एतत्करोति यदेभ्यो जुहोति ॥ (*sa yadeva yajeta | tena devebhya ṛṇaṃ jāyate taddhebhya etatkaroti yadebhyo juhoti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-7-2-2)

To be freed from this debt and to preserve his existence so that he too takes part in the continuance of the universe, every person must perform the sacrifice, repay the debt to the gods and be released from that debt. This matter is stated still more fully in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.

जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस्त्रिभिर्यणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्य एष वा अनृणो यः पुत्री यज्वा ब्रह्मचारिवासी ॥ (*jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhiryaṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇarṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhya eṣa vā anṛṇo yaḥ putrī yajvā brahmacārivāsī ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-11-5)

A Brahmin is born carrying three kinds of debts from birth: the debt to the seers, the debt to the gods and the debt to the ancestors. Here the debt to the seers means the duty that a Brahmin must perform toward the seers. The debts to the gods and to the ancestors are to be understood in the same way. By the vow of brahmacarya, dwelling in the teacher's house, and regularly studying the Veda with instruction from the teacher, the debt to the seers

### Printed p. 236

The debt to the ṛṣis is repaid. By worshipping the gods through sacrifices and other rites, the debt to the gods is repaid. By begetting lawful offspring on a wedded wife, the debt to the ancestors is repaid. Therefore it is said that a brāhmaṇa, as a householder, must carry out these three kinds of duty.

In this way, if every individual in the universal order is to preserve his own existence, which is full of influence, the sacrifice is the thread that links him to these generalities and particulars. This sacrifice, which has the form of a thread, grows at one time and contracts at another together with the expansion and contraction of the universe. It adjusts its own course to the course of the universe. Explaining this point, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa gives the etymology of the word yajña:

अथ यस्माद्यज्ञो नाम । घ्नंति वा एनमेतद्यदभिषुण्वंति तद्यदेनं तन्नते तदेनं जनयंति स तायमानो जायते स यन् जायते तस्माद्यज्ञो यञ्चो ह वै नामैतद्यज्ञ इति ॥ (*atha yasmādyajño nāma | ghnaṃti vā enametadyadabhiṣuṇvaṃti tadyadenaṃ tannate tadenaṃ janayaṃti sa tāyamāno jāyate sa yan jāyate tasmādyajño yañco ha vai nāmaitadyajña iti ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 3-9-4-23)

At the time of pressing they strike it (they crush the soma plants with a stone; this is the striking). They make it come into being again. Since it comes into being together with a course of expansion, the name yajña became established. This shows that there are contraction and expansion according to need, and that, because it accords with the states and courses of the universe, it is of benefit to the universe. How? —
(Śa. Brā. 9-4-1-11)

भुज्युः सुपर्ण इति । यज्ञो वै भुज्युः यज्ञो हि सर्वाणि भुनक्ति यज्ञो गंधर्वः ॥ (*bhujyuḥ suparṇa iti | yajño vai bhujyuḥ yajño hi sarvāṇi bhunakti yajño gaṃdharvaḥ ‖*)

The sacrifice requires all beings for its oblation, and again it extends itself for the benefit of all beings. Having thus shown the relation of identity between the universal principle and the sacrifice, the text says that the sacrifice is the cause of all the practical dealings of the world, that it alone is the protector, and that it alone is the relation in the form of a thread; this, described in many Vedic sentences, is described in the present Ṛk by the sentence यज्ञो विश्वस्य नाभिः (*yajño viśvasya nābhiḥ*). Therefore it is said that, to carry out this sacrifice which is the navel of the universe, a common faith is absolutely necessary for all, gods, men and the rest.

यो वै श्रद्धामनारभ्य यज्ञेन यजते नास्यॆष्टाय श्रद्दधतेऽपः प्रणयति श्रद्धा वा आपः श्रद्धामेवारभ्य यज्ञेन यजत उभयेऽस्य देवमनुष्या इष्टाय श्रद्दधते ॥ (*yo vai śraddhāmanārabhya yajñena yajate nāsyèṣṭāya śraddadhate 'paḥ praṇayati śraddhā vā āpaḥ śraddhāmevārabhya yajñena yajata ubhaye 'sya devamanuṣyā iṣṭāya śraddadhate ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 1-6-8-1)

### Printed p. 237

The sacrifice of one who sacrifices without faith does not succeed, that is, it does not bear fruit. The sacrifice must be performed with the water in the form of faith placed in front. All, gods, men and the rest, take part in the sacrifice only through faith; thus the necessity of faith is shown. Moreover:

श्रद्धयाग्निः समिध्यते श्रद्धया हूयते हविः (*śraddhayāgniḥ samidhyate śraddhayā hūyate haviḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-151-1)

The Ṛgveda too says that in sacrificial rites the fire must be churned out and kindled with faith, and that the offering of oblations in that fire, directed to the gods, must likewise be performed with faith.

This faith that must be placed in the principle of the sacrifice is not mere blind faith. It must have the power of grasping the spiritual principle. It must show the relation between the sacrifice, the navel of the world, and the Brahman principle. The sacrificer who has this faith, resting on spiritual knowledge, conceives an identity between himself and the sacrifice. Then he comes to know the identity of the sacrifice and Prajāpati. He knows that all the dealings of the earth, which has the form of Prajāpati, are contained in this principle of sacrifice, and he too takes his share in that wheel of the universe.

Now, to the third question, the sentence पृच्छामि त्वा वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः (*pṛcchāmi tvā vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ*), the answer given is आयं वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः (*āyaṃ vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ*). The question is: what is the seed (retas) of the Āditya (Brahman), who pours down rain and the like and pervades the world, that is, what is the power and capacity that is the cause of the world's origin? The answer given is that Soma is that seed. Here one must first understand which quality of the Āditya the synonym aśva shows, and then examine what is meant by saying that Soma is his seed. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa gives the etymology of the word aśva as follows:

प्रजापतेरक्ष्यश्वयत् तत्परापतत्ततोऽश्वः समभवद्यदश्वयत्तदश्वस्याश्वत्वं ॥ ( (*prajāpaterakṣyaśvayat tatparāpatattato 'śvaḥ samabhavadyadaśvayattadaśvasyāśvatvaṃ ‖ (*)
(Śa. Brā. 13-3-1-1)

The eye of Prajāpati swelled and fell down. From it the horse (aśva) came into being. Because it swelled (aśvayat), the name aśva became established for it. Having said this, the text goes on to explain how this horse is identical with the Āditya.

प्रजापतिर्वा इदमग्र आसीत्। . . . निरमिमीत मनसः पुरुषं चक्षुषोऽश्वं। (*prajāpatirvā idamagra āsīt| . . . niramimīta manasaḥ puruṣaṃ cakṣuṣo 'śvaṃ|*)
(Śa. Brā. 7-5-26)

### Printed p. 238

Having said that this horse was created from the eye of Prajāpati, the text then in many places shows the close relation between Varuṇa and this horse.

वारुणो ना अश्वः । तं देवतया व्यर्धयति । यत्प्राजापत्यं करोति । नमो राज्ञे नमोवरुणायेत्याह । वारुणो ना अत्वः ॥ (*vāruṇo nā aśvaḥ | taṃ devatayā vyardhayati | yatprājāpatyaṃ karoti | namo rājñe namovaruṇāyetyāha | vāruṇo nā atvaḥ ‖*)
(Tai. Brā. 3-9-16-1)

In showing the relation of Varuṇa to the horse, Sāyaṇa explains: अश्वस्याब्योनित्वाद्वरुणस्य चापां पतित्वादयमश्वो वारुणः (*aśvasyābyonitvādvaruṇasya cāpāṃ patitvādayamaśvo vāruṇaḥ*). Because the horse is born of the all-pervading water, and because Varuṇa is lord of the waters, the sacrificial horse belongs to the deity Varuṇa. Discussing what the hidden meaning of this Varuṇa-horse is, the scholar Eggeling says as follows in his translation of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa: the horse of Varuṇa, who is lord of heaven and earth and all, is none other than the sun, going through its daily revolution. The relation of Varuṇa to this horse is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows:

प्रजापतिर्वरुणायाश्वमनयत्स स्वां देवतामार्च्यत्स पर्यदीर्यत स एतं वारुणं चतुष्कपालमपश्यत्तं निरवपत्ततो वै स वरुणपाशादमुच्यत वरुणो वा एतं गृह्णाति योऽश्वं प्रतिगृह्णाति ॥ (*prajāpatirvaruṇāyāśvamanayatsa svāṃ devatāmārcyatsa paryadīryata sa etaṃ vāruṇaṃ catuṣkapālamapaśyattaṃ niravapattato vai sa varuṇapāśādamucyata varuṇo vā etaṃ gṛhṇāti yo 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇāti ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 2-3-12-1)

Prajāpati led the horse to Varuṇa. But the horse went to its own deity, Prajāpati. Then, since Varuṇa was aggrieved, Prajāpati offered a four-potsherd cake directed to Varuṇa. Then Prajāpati was freed from Varuṇa's noose. This is the explanation given.

Some more mantras help to understand this point clearly. They indicate that the word aśva is a synonym of the sun: Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-1; Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-12-1; Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1; Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-12-1, and so on. Soma is the seed of this all-pervading (aśva) Āditya; that is, it can be said that Soma is the seed of the Supreme Brahman who is in the form of the Āditya. How? That Soma is the generating seed for the creation of all beings is stated in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad as follows:

अथ यत्किंचेदमाद्र्रं तद्रेतसोऽसृजत तदु सोम एतावद्वा इदं सर्वमन्नं चैवान्नादश्च सोम एवान्नमग्निरन्नादः ॥ (*atha yatkiṃcedamādrraṃ tadretaso 'sṛjata tadu soma etāvadvā idaṃ sarvamannaṃ caivānnādaśca soma evānnamagnirannādaḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 1-4-6)

### Printed p. 239

The one without a second, the Supreme Brahman, created from his seed all the moist things in the universe. That seed is Soma. This Soma, offered in the fire, becomes with it mutually food and eater. This is described in the Maitrī Upaniṣad:

रविमध्ये स्थितः सोमः सोममध्यॆ हुताशनः (*ravimadhye sthitaḥ somaḥ somamadhyè hutāśanaḥ*)
(Mai. U. 6-38)**NOTE**

That is, Soma is said to stand in the middle of the solar orb, and Agni in the middle of Soma. The relation between the Āditya and Soma is commonly described in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā.

महत्तत्सोमो महिषश्चकारापां यद्गर्भोऽवृणीत देवान् । आदधादिंद्रे पवमान ओजोऽजनयत्सूर्ये ज्योतिरिंदुः ॥ (*mahattatsomo mahiṣaścakārāpāṃ yadgarbho 'vṛṇīta devān | ādadhādiṃdre pavamāna ojo 'janayatsūrye jyotiriṃduḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-41)

Soma, the embryo of the waters that abide in the Āditya, gratified even the gods. Existing in the form of semen, it created the universal light in the Āditya. This is what is said. And:

तं समुद्रो असि विश्ववित्कवे तनेमाः पंच प्रदिशो विधर्मणि । त्वं द्यां च पृथिवीं चाति जभ्रिषे तव ज्योतींषि पवमान सूर्यः ॥ (*taṃ samudro asi viśvavitkave tanemāḥ paṃca pradiśo vidharmaṇi | tvaṃ dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāti jabhriṣe tava jyotīṃṣi pavamāna sūryaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-29)

Here it is stated that Soma is the ocean in the atmosphere, the support of all light, and that the Āditya shines by the power of Soma. Explaining in the present Ṛk what principle Soma reflects here, Sāyaṇa says अग्नौ हुतः सोमरसः आदित्यं प्राप्य वृष्टादिफलं जनयति । (*agnau hutaḥ somarasaḥ ādityaṃ prāpya vṛṣṭādiphalaṃ janayati |*): the Soma offered in the fire reaches the Āditya and brings about the fruit of rain and the like. For this reason he says that it is described here as the seed of the Āditya.

Here the meaning must be taken not only on the adhidaivata side but also on the adhyātma side. On the adhyātma side, the Upaniṣadic sentences quoted above state the world-producing power of Soma in the form of seed, and the relation between Soma and the Āditya.

(4) The fourth question is पृच्छामि वाचः परमं व्योम (*pṛcchāmi vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma*): what is the highest place of speech, which is the cause of all dealings? The answer is ब्रह्मयं वाचः परमं व्योम (*brahmayaṃ vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma*). Sāyaṇa says मंत्रादिरूपायाः वाचः प्रजापतिरेव उत्कृष्टं रक्षकं स्थानं । तत्रैव उत्पत्तेस्तत्रैव पर्यवसानाच्च ॥ (*maṃtrādirūpāyāḥ vācaḥ prajāpatireva utkṛṣṭaṃ rakṣakaṃ sthānaṃ | tatraiva utpattestatraiva paryavasānācca ‖*). Since Prajāpati (Brahman) is both the place of origin and the end (final conclusion) of speech in the form of mantras and the like, he is the vyoman (place). Here

### Printed p. 240

the word vyoman is explained as उत्कृष्टं रक्षकं स्थानं (*utkṛṣṭaṃ rakṣakaṃ sthānaṃ*), an excellent, protecting support (place of refuge).

The word vyoman is read among the names of the atmosphere in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-10). It is formed from the root वैञ् (*vaiñ*), meaning to pervade or to cover; it means the all-pervading atmosphere. Further, the word vyoman may be formed from the root अव (*ava*) in the sense of protection, joined with the prefix वि (*vi*); it then means a place furnished with manifold protections. In this sense:

ऋतेन ऋतं धरुणं धारयंत यज्ञस्य शाके परमे व्योमन् । दिवो धर्मन्धरुणे सेदुषो नृञ्जा तैरजाता अभि ये ननक्षुः ॥ (*ṛtena ṛtaṃ dharuṇaṃ dhārayaṃta yajñasya śāke parame vyoman | divo dharmandharuṇe seduṣo nṛñjā tairajātā abhi ye nanakṣuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-15-2)

Here too the word is used as an attribute of the uttaravedi.

व्योमसदित्येष वै व्योमसद्व्योम ना एतत्सद्मानां यस्मिन्नेष आसन्नस्तपति ॥ (*vyomasadityeṣa vai vyomasadvyoma nā etatsadmānāṃ yasminneṣa āsannastapati ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 4-20)

In this sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also the word is used in the sense of a place of protection or a place of support.

How Prajāpati (Brahman) is the support or place of protection of speech is this: he is the cause of its origin and of its conclusion (end or destruction); so Sāyaṇa gives the meaning on the adhyātma side. Stating the identity of the Supreme Brahman and speech, the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad shows that all the dealings of the world go on on the basis of speech, that the Supreme Brahman is the support of this speech, and that speech makes manifest outwardly his very principle:

जनको ह वैदेह आसांचक्रेऽथ ह याज्ञवल्क्य आवव्राज तं होवाच याज्ञवल्क्य किमर्थमचारीः पशूनिच्छन्नण्वंतानीति । उभयमेव सम्राडिति होवाच ॥ (*janako ha vaideha āsāṃcakre 'tha ha yājñavalkya āvavrāja taṃ hovāca yājñavalkya kimarthamacārīḥ paśūnicchannaṇvaṃtānīti | ubhayameva samrāḍiti hovāca ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 4-1)

While Janaka of Videha was sitting in his court, the ṛṣi Yājñavalkya came to him. Then Janaka asked him: What is the purpose of your coming? Have you come to obtain cattle (wealth in the form of cattle, that is, property), or to carry on a discussion of the principle? Yājñavalkya replied: O lord, I have come intending both.

### Printed p. 241

यत्ते कच्चिदब्रवीत्तच्छृणवामेत्यब्रवीन्मे जिह्वा शैलिनिर्वाग्वै ब्रह्मति यभा मात्वमान् पितृमानाचार्यमान् ब्रूयात्तथा तच्छैलनिरब्रवीद्वाग्वै ब्रह्मेत्यवदतो हि किं स्यादित्यब्रवीत्तु ते तस्म्यायतनं प्रतिष्ठां न मेऽब्रवीदित्येकपाद्वा एतत्सम्राडिति स वै नो ब्रूहि याज्ञवल्क्य ॥ (*yatte kaccidabravīttacchṛṇavāmetyabravīnme jihvā śailinirvāgvai brahmati yabhā mātvamān pitṛmānācāryamān brūyāttathā tacchailanirabravīdvāgvai brahmetyavadato hi kiṃ syādityabravīttu te tasmyāyatanaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ na me 'bravīdityekapādvā etatsamrāḍiti sa vai no brūhi yājñavalkya ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 4-1)

Yājñavalkya asked Janaka: Explain what you know of this principle, or what you have learned from others. In answer Janaka said: Śailini said that speech is Brahman. Yājñavalkya accepted this; it was as though only one part of the truth had been stated in it. But, he asked, did he tell you the abode (āyatana) and the foundation (pratiṣṭhā, place of support) of that Brahman in the form of speech? Janaka replied that he had not told it. Then Yājñavalkya said that this Brahman has only one foot. When Janaka asked him to explain how, Yājñavalkya explained as follows:

नागेवायतनमाकाशः प्रतिष्ठा प्रज्ञेत्येतदुपासीत (*nāgevāyatanamākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhā prajñetyetadupāsīta*)

For this Brahman in the form of speech the tongue is the abode, space is the place of foundation. One should worship this, knowing it as prajñā. When this was said,

का प्रज्ञता याज्ञवल्क्य । नागेव सम्राडिति होवाच । वाचा वै सम्राड्बंधुः प्रज्ञायत ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्वांगिरस इतिहासः पुराणं विद्या उपनिषदः श्लोकाः सूत्राण्यनुव्याख्यानानि व्याख्यानानीष्टं हुतमाशितं पायितमयं च लोकः परश्च लोकः सर्वाणि च भूतानि वाचैव सम्राट् प्रज्ञायंते वाग्वै सम्राट् परमं ब्रह्म नैनं वाग्वहाति सर्वाण्येनं भूतान्यभि रक्षंति देवो भूत्वा देवानप्येति य एवं विद्वानेतदुपास्ते ॥ (*kā prajñatā yājñavalkya | nāgeva samrāḍiti hovāca | vācā vai samrāḍbaṃdhuḥ prajñāyata ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṃgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇyanuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānānīṣṭaṃ hutamāśitaṃ pāyitamayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraśca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni vācaiva samrāṭ prajñāyaṃte vāgvai samrāṭ paramaṃ brahma nainaṃ vāgvahāti sarvāṇyenaṃ bhūtānyabhi rakṣaṃti devo bhūtvā devānapyeti ya evaṃ vidvānetadupāste ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 4-1)

Janaka asked what the nature of that prajñā is. Yājñavalkya gave this answer: Speech itself is this knowledge, this is the kinsman, this is the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, Atharvaveda, the Itihāsa, Purāṇa and the rest, their commentaries and sub-commentaries, the sacrificial oblations, the principle of this world, the principle of the other world, and so on; everything is known only with the help of this speech. By speech alone Brahman too is known. Speech is the Supreme Brahman. Speech does not abandon those who, with this knowledge of the principle, worship Brahman in the form of speech. He too attains godhood. In this way Sāyaṇa has explained the point stated in the sentence ब्रह्मयं वाचः परमं व्योम (*brahmayaṃ vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma*); that is, he has stated the identity of speech and the Supreme Brahman. This same thing is stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also,

### Printed p. 242
The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too makes this known through sentences such as वाचस्पतिर्वाचं नः स्वदतु स्वाहेति प्रजापतिर्वै वाचस्पतिः । (*vācaspatirvācaṃ naḥ svadatu svāheti prajāpatirvai vācaspatiḥ |*) (Śa. Brā. 5-1-1-16). And in the account of the order of creation, the statement that the Supreme Brahman manifested itself in the form of speech likewise shows the relation of support and supported between speech and Brahman.

प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत । ताः सृष्टाः समश्लिष्यन् । ता रूपेणानुप्राविशत् । तस्मादाहुः । रूपं वै प्रजापतिरिति । ता नाम्नानुप्राविशत् । तस्मादाहुः । नाम वै प्रजापतिरिति ॥ (*prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata | tāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ samaśliṣyan | tā rūpeṇānuprāviśat | tasmādāhuḥ | rūpaṃ vai prajāpatiriti | tā nāmnānuprāviśat | tasmādāhuḥ | nāma vai prajāpatiriti ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 2-2-7-1)

After Prajāpati created the creatures, they all merged together without showing mutual individuality. Then, to show their distinguishing characteristics, he created both name (nāma) and form (rūpa). It is explained that form served the mental division, and name the division consisting of speech. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also:

मर्त्या ह वा देवा असुः । स यदैव ते ब्रह्मणापुरथामृता आसुः स यं मनस आघारयति मनो वै रूपं मनसा हि वेदेदग्ं रूपमिति तेन रूपमाप्नोत्यथ यं वाच आघारयति वाग्वै नाम वाचा हि नाम गृह्णाति तेन नामाप्नोत्येतावद्वा इदग्ं सर्वं यावद्रूपं चैव नाम च तत्सर्वमाप्नोति ॥ (*martyā ha vā devā asuḥ | sa yadaiva te brahmaṇāpurathāmṛtā āsuḥ sa yaṃ manasa āghārayati mano vai rūpaṃ manasā hi vededagṃ rūpamiti tena rūpamāpnotyatha yaṃ vāca āghārayati vāgvai nāma vācā hi nāma gṛhṇāti tena nāmāpnotyetāvadvā idagṃ sarvaṃ yāvadrūpaṃ caiva nāma ca tatsarvamāpnoti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-2-3-6)

So it says. In the beginning the gods were mortal, that is, they too were subject to death. They realised Brahman directly and obtained immortality (freedom from death). That Brahman has two forms, name and form. Form is the principle perceptible only to the mind. Therefore through the mental "pouring" (āghāra) one comes to know the Brahman that consists of speech. By knowing this Brahman principle, which is both of the nature of mind and of the nature of speech, a human being too attains Brahman-hood, that is, immortality. Thus the relation between speech and Brahman is made known.

In this way, the inquiry at the time of a sacrifice into any principle concerning the Supreme Brahman is called brahmodya. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa also there are questions and answers to be discussed for the brahmodya.

Question—किग्ग्स्विदासीत्पूर्वचित्तिरित्याह (*kiggsvidāsītpūrvacittirityāha*)
Answer—द्यान्वै वृष्टिः पूर्वचित्तिः (*dyānvai vṛṣṭiḥ pūrvacittiḥ*)

### Printed p. 243
Question—किग्स् स्विदासीद्बृहद्वय इत्याह (*kigs svidāsīdbṛhadvaya ityāha*)
Answer—अश्वो वै बृहद्वयः (*aśvo vai bṛhadvayaḥ*)
Question—किग्स् स्विदासीत्पिशिंगिलेत्याह (*kigs svidāsītpiśiṃgiletyāha*)
Answer—रात्रिर्वै पिशिंगिला (*rātrirvai piśiṃgilā*)
Q.—किग्स् स्विदासीत्पिलिप्पिलेत्याह (*kigs svidāsītpilippiletyāha*)
A.—श्रीर्वै पिलिप्पिला (*śrīrvai pilippilā*)
Q.—कः स्विदेकाकी चरतीत्याह (*kaḥ svidekākī caratītyāha*)
A.—असौ वा आदित्य एकाकी चरति (*asau vā āditya ekākī carati*)
Q.—क उ स्विज्जायके पुनरित्याह (*ka u svijjāyake punarityāha*)
A.—चंद्रमा वै जायते पुनः (*caṃdramā vai jāyate punaḥ*)
Q.—क्विग्स् विद्धिमस्य भेषजमित्याह (*kvigs viddhimasya bheṣajamityāha*)
A.—अग्निर्वै हिमस्य भेषजं (*agnirvai himasya bheṣajaṃ*)
Q.—किग्स् विदावपनं महदित्याह (*kigs vidāvapanaṃ mahadityāha*)
A.—अयं वै लोक आवपनं महत् (*ayaṃ vai loka āvapanaṃ mahat*)
Q.—पृच्छामि त्वा परमंतं पृथिव्या इत्याह (*pṛcchāmi tvā paramaṃtaṃ pṛthivyā ityāha*)
A.—वेदिर्वै परोऽन्तः पृथिव्याः (*vedirvai paro 'ntaḥ pṛthivyāḥ*)
Q.—पृच्छामि त्वा भुवनस्य नाभिमित्याह (*pṛcchāmi tvā bhuvanasya nābhimityāha*)
A.—यज्ञो वै भुवनस्य नाभिः (*yajño vai bhuvanasya nābhiḥ*)
Q.—पृच्छामि त्वा वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेत इत्याह (*pṛcchāmi tvā vṛṣṇo aśvasya reta ityāha*)
A.—सोमो वै वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः (*somo vai vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ*)
Q.—पृच्छामि वाचः परमं व्योमेत्याह (*pṛcchāmi vācaḥ paramaṃ vyometyāha*)
A.—ब्रह्मैव वाचः परमं व्योम (*brahmaiva vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma*)
(Tai. Brā. 3-9-5-2 to 6)

In a brahmodya any discussion concerning Brahman may take place. Twelve questions and their answers are stated above. The last four questions and their answers we have so far explained at length. In the same way the answers to the other questions can also be examined, and many such matters are worthy of examination. It is not possible to examine all of them here, and it is not relevant. And in the same place:

तेजसा वा एष ब्रह्मवर्चसेन व्युर्धते । योऽश्वमेधेन यजते । होता च ब्रह्मा च ब्रहोद्यं वदतः ॥ (*tejasā vā eṣa brahmavarcasena vyurdhate | yo 'śvamedhena yajate | hotā ca brahmā ca brahodyaṃ vadataḥ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-9-5-1)

### Printed p. 244
It is said, that is, in this discussion on the brahmodya the ṛtvij called Hotṛ and the ṛtvij called Brahmā take part. For, among the ṛtvijs only these two are the more learned, and to show that ordinary people cannot conduct such a discussion of the highest class, and to make known that they are held in greater honour and esteem than the other ṛtvijs, only the names Hotṛ and Brahmā are mentioned here as होता च ब्रह्मा च (*hotā ca brahmā ca*). If the other ṛtvijs, the sacrificer and others, are capable of discussing such matters, there is no restriction against their taking part in it too.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये ते॑ विप्र ब्रह्म॒स्पतः॑ सु॒ते सचा॒ वसू॑नां च॒ वसु॑नश्च दा॒वने॑।  
> प्र ते सु॒म्मस्य॒ मन॑सा प॒था भु॑व॒न्मदे॑ सु॒तस्य॑ सो॒म्यस्यान्द॑सः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । ते । विप्र । ब्रह्मकृतः । सुते । सचा । वसूनां । च । वसुनः । च । दावने ॥  
> प्र। ते । सुम्नस्य । मनसा । पथा । भुवन् । मदे । सुतस्य । सोम्यस्य । अंधसः ॥७॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विप्र मेधाविन्निंद्र ते तुभ्यं ये ब्रह्मकृतः स्तोत्रकृतो हविष्कर्तारो ना स्तोतारः सचा संघीभूताः सुते सोमेऽभिषुते वसूनां बहूनां
> धनानां वसुनश्चैकस्य निवासयोग्यस्य धनस्य च दावने दानाय परिचरंतीति शेषः ।
> अत्र वसूनामिति बहुवचनेनैहिकभोगसाधनानि धनान्यभिप्रेतानि । एकवचनांतेन च
> निवासयोग्यं स्वर्गाख्यं धनमभिप्रेतमित्यवगंतव्यं । तेऽनुष्ठातारः सुम्मस्य
> सुखस्य लाभाय मनसा पथा मनोमार्गेण । स्तोत्रवर्त्मनेत्यर्थः । प्र भुवन् ।
> प्रभवंतु । उक्तवसुदानाय योग्या भवंतित्यर्थः । कदेति उच्यते । सुतस्याभिषुतस्य सोम्यस्य सोमसंबंधिनोऽंधसोऽन्नस्य मदे सति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wise (vipra) Indra, those who make brahma for you, that is, the hymn-makers or offerers of oblations, the praisers, assembled together when the Soma is pressed, attend upon you for the giving (dāvane) of many riches (वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)) and of one riches (वसुनः (*vasunaḥ*)) fit for dwelling; the verb "attend" is to be supplied. Here the plural वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*) means the riches that are means of enjoyment in this world, and the singular means the wealth fit for dwelling called heaven. Those performers, for the gaining of felicity (सुम्मस्य (*summasya*) = happiness), by the pathway of the mind (मनसा पथा (*manasā pathā*)), that is, the path of praise, प्र भुवन् (*pra bhuvan*): may they prevail, that is, become fit for the said gift of riches. When? When there is exhilaration (मदे (*made*)) from the effused (सुतस्य (*sutasya*)) Soma food (अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)) belonging to Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्र (*vipra*)—O wise Indra
- ते (*te*)—for you
- ये ब्रह्मकृतः (*ye brahmakṛtaḥ*)—whatever persons, ṛtvijs, sacrificers and others, are praising or offering oblations
- सचा (*sacā*)—

### Printed p. 245
- all of them together
- सुते (*sute*)—after the Soma juice is pressed
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—of the plentiful worldly things, and
- वसुनश्च (*vasunaśca*)—of the wealth called heaven, needed by only one person
- दावने (*dāvane*)—for the gaining, they attend upon you
- ते (*te*)—those performers of the sacrifice
- सुम्मस्य (*summasya*)—for obtaining happiness
- मनसा पथा (*manasā pathā*)—by the path of praise, meditated in the mind itself
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—pressed
- सोम्यस्य (*somyasya*)—relating to the Soma juice
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—by the food
- मदे (*made*)—when Indra is delighted
- प्र भुवन् (*pra bhuvan*)—they become able to obtain the riches and the rest mentioned above

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Indra, the persons, ṛtvijs, sacrificers and others, who praise you or perform the sacrifice, all assembled together, after the Soma juice is pressed, attend upon you for the gaining of worldly riches and of the happiness called heaven. When Indra is delighted by the pressed Soma juice, those praisers, praising in the mind itself, become able to obtain from Indra the riches and the happiness they desire.

##### English translation
Sage Indra, the reciters of pious hymns to you who assembled together when (the Soma) is effused, (worship you) for the donation of riches and treasures : may they be competent (to acquire) your felicity by the path- way of the mind ; when you are exhilarated with the effused Soma food.

## Sūkta 51 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
For this sūkta and the next two sūktas (the 51st, 52nd and 53rd), the seer is the Agni called Saucīka. In sūkta 51 there is a conversation: for a certain reason Agni left his work of carrying the oblation to the gods, fled and hid in the water; the gods saw him and prayed that he should come back out of the water and take up again the task of carrying the oblation to them. Although we have explained matters concerning Agni at length in various places, here we shall write a general account suited to the occasion and afterwards explain the matter of Agni Saucīka.

Among the deities described in the Ṛksaṃhitā, Agni is the foremost. Apart from the praises of Indra, the sūktas that praise and describe Agni are the most numerous in the whole Ṛksaṃhitā. Except for the 8th and 9th maṇḍalas, all the other maṇḍalas begin with a sūkta addressed to Agni.

### Printed p. 246
Therefore some things that must necessarily be known about the deity Agni are explained here.

**The works of Agni**
Because he is directly connected with the sacrificial works, the most excellent of all human activities, Agni holds a most principal and venerable place. The chief quality of Agni is his immortality (1-44-6; 1-58-1; 2-10-1, 2; 3-2-1; 3-3-1; 3-11-2; 3-27-5; 3-27-2; 6-9-4; 7-4-4; 8-60-11; 10-79-1). Though by nature free from death, Agni, for the benefit of all humans and for the favour of mortal humans, abides on earth with them as their guest (1-44-4; 1-58-6; 2-4-1; 3-2-2; 4-1-20; 5-1-8; 5-8-2; 5-18-1; 6-2-7; 6-15-1; 6-15-4; 8-8-4; 8-73-1; 10-1-5; 10-91-2; 10-92-1).

Agni, immortal and gracious to humans, becomes the everlasting ṛtvij in the sacrificer's house. He is described by epithets such as purohita, ṛtvij, hotṛ, brahmā. In some passages he is praised as awakening together with the goddess Uṣas, in others as appearing even before Uṣas. 1-1-1; 1-12-1; 1-13-1, 4; 1-26-7; 1-36-3, 5; 1-44-7; 1-44-12; 1-45-3-7; 1-58-1, 6; 1-60-4; 1-68-4, 7; 1-76-2, 4; 1-127-1; 1-141-12; 1-149-4, 5; 2-5-1; 2-6-6; 2-9-1; 3-7-9; 3-10-2, 7; 3-11-1; 3-14-1; 3-19-1; 4-1-8; 5-11-2; 5-26-7; 6-15-1, 4, 16; 6-16-1; 7-7-5; 7-10-5; 7-11-1; 7-16-5, 12; 8-44-6; 8-49-1; 9-66-20; 10-1-6; 10-92-2.

Prayed to and regulated by gods and humans alike, he absorbs all sacrificial works into himself. Being himself the true performer, he is able alone to carry out all the sacrificial works that are assigned to the different ṛtvijs, the sacrificers, adhvaryu, hotṛ, potṛ and others. (1-94-6; 2-1-2; 2-5-2; 4-9-3, 4; 10-2-1) Because he has this power of accomplishment, he is prayed to thus by the sacrificers: "O Agni, you are the best of hotṛs. You are ever young. Joining the other ṛtvijs, who are of divine nature, and performing the works suited to the seasons, worship and satisfy the gods who desire sacrifice." Some more sentences describing the great qualities of Agni are explained and cited below.

"Agni is a wise poet, the divine one among all poets. (असुरो विपश्चितां (*asuro vipaścitāṃ*))" (the reference is printed as इ-इ-४ (*i-i-4*))**NOTE**

### Printed p. 247
"Such a Agni, the wise one, knows all kinds of acts of worship. He is the best leader, who brings success easily, the protector of all works. He helps devotees in works that are not easy for them and brings the work to completion with all its parts."

"O Agni, the sacrifice that you encompass and cause to be accomplished certainly goes and reaches the gods."

"O Agni, you are the first (the chief) of the Aṅgirasa seers, a friend who does good to all the gods." (1-31-1)

"O Agni, you alone are the principal means of carrying out all sacrificial work." (reference printed as इ-इ-इ (*i-i-i*))**NOTE**

"O most excellent seer, you are kindled. Protect the sacrifice." (3-21-3)

"Agni, the means of the sacrifice, of the nature of a seer, increasing the sacrifice, is in front as its eye." (3-27-2, 7)

"Among those who are not wise, he alone is the wise poet, possessed of the highest knowledge." (7-4-4)

"O gods, whatever faults of omission we may commit in the ordained performance of rites, Agni, who knows the rules of the seasons and understands how the gods are to be satisfied, corrects and sets right all our faults." (10-2-4)

"Many matters useful for carrying out the sacrifice never come within the understanding of us dull-witted people. Yet Agni, being omniscient and a venerable ṛtvij, knows all these secrets, worships the gods at the proper time, offers to each the oblations and the like that are suitable to him, and satisfies all." (10-2-5)

"As the eyes of the human sacrificers turn towards the sun, so they turn towards Agni." (10-91-3 **NOTE**)

### Printed p. 248
…"The Lord (Agni) is the father of all sacrificers, and he is their master. He is the banner of the sacrifice, manifest to the outward eye, and the overseer of all Vedic rites." (केतुं याज्ञानां (*ketuṃ yājñānāṃ*), पिता याज्ञानां (*pitā yājñānāṃ*), सम्राजं (*samrājaṃ*)): 3-3-3, 4; 3-10-4; 3-11-2; 4-3-1; 6-2-3; 8-43-24; 10-1-5; 10-6-3.

"The swift-moving Agni (रघुपत्वः (*raghupatvaḥ*)), entreated by the gods, travels from the earth to the atmosphere and from the atmosphere to the earth. He is the messenger of the gods and also the messenger of the human sacrificer, and so he builds up the lasting bond between gods and men. He delivers to the gods the divine praises and the oblations offered by men. At every desired time he brings the gods from heaven to the sacrificial ground on earth." (10-100-11; 10-150-4)

Agni's being the messenger of the gods and of men is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows—

"Agni was the messenger of the gods, Uśanas Kāvya of the asuras" अग्निर्देवानां दूत असीदुशना काव्योऽसुराणां (*agnirdevānāṃ dūta asīduśanā kāvyo 'surāṇāṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-5-8-5)

Agni was the messenger of the gods, and Kāvya Uśanas was the messenger of the asuras. How this messengership allowed the bond between gods and men to grow is praised as Agni's work in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (Tai. Brā. 2-4-1-6):

आ तंतुमग्निर्दैव्यं ततान । श्वं नस्तंतुरुत सेतुरग्ने । त्वं पंथा भवसि देवमानैः । त्वया अग्ने पृष्ठतु वयमारुहेम । अथ देवैः सधमादं मदेम ॥ (*ā taṃtumagnirdaivyaṃ tatāna | śvaṃ nastaṃturuta seturagne | tvaṃ paṃthā bhavasi devamānaiḥ | tvayā agne pṛṣṭhatu vayamāruhema | atha devaiḥ sadhamādaṃ madema ‖*)

O Agni, you stretch out the thread, the bond that exists between gods and men. You yourself are the thread for us. You are the chief bridge for going to heaven, the chief road to the world of the gods. By your grace may we, your worshippers, also reach heaven and enjoy together with the gods there the very happiness that they enjoy.

In the same way, there are very many passages in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in which his being the messenger of the gods, and through this messengership his helping to increase the bond between gods and men, are praised. Sentences such as "We choose Agni as messenger" (अग्निं दूतं वृणी महे (*agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇī mahe*)) praise Agni's help. (1-12-1; 2-4-8; 1-36-3, 4, 5; 1-44, 2, 3, 5, 9, 12; 2-10-6; 3-11-2; 4-2-3; 5-21-3; 7-17-6; 8-39-1, 9; 10-91-11; 1-27-4; 1-188-1; 3-5-2; 3-17-4; 4-7-8; 6-15-8 to 10; 8-19-21; 8-44-3; 10-122-7 **NOTE**; 1-58-1; 2-6-6, 7; 3-6-5; 3-21-1, 5; 4-8-2, 4;

### Printed p. 249
7-11-4; 8-23-18, 19; 10-4-2; 1-34-4, 7; 2-9-2; 3-9-8; 4-1-8; 5-8-6; 7-16-4; 10-46-10, etc.)

This same Agni, knowing fully the inner nature of the heavenly world, is fit to bring all the gods to receive the sacrificial share each deserves. (4-8-2)

In whatever chariots the gods come, Agni also comes seated in the same chariot. (3-4-11; 7-11-1)

Or, knowing the time, he comes even before them. (10-20-2)

Whatever worship and whatever sacrificial share belong to all the other gods, all of it is due to Agni as well and is offered to him. (1-36-4; 2-12-1)

He brings Varuṇa to the sacrifice. He brings Indra from the heavenly world and the Maruts from the atmosphere. (10-20-11)

He makes the oblations offered in the sacrifice fragrant (हव्यानी सुरभीणि कृत्वी (*havyānī surabhīṇi kṛtvī*)). (10-15-12; Vā. Saṃ. 19-66)

Without Agni's help in the sacrifice the gods have no satisfaction of any kind. (7-11-1)

Therefore it is Agni himself who directly offers the oblations to all those gods. (7-11-3; 8-91-16; 10-7-6)

Because the gods receive oblations and the like through Agni, he is often praised, as taking the chief part in the sacrifice performed by gods and men, as the mouth of the gods, and as the very tongue with which they drink Soma and the rest (आस्यं त्वां जिह्वां (*āsyaṃ tvāṃ jihvāṃ*)). (2-1-13; 2-1-14) In some other places he is entreated to eat all the oblations himself, and he is directly invited to drink the Soma offered in the sacrifice. (3-21-1; 3-28-1 to 6; 1-14-10; 7-19-9)

### Printed p. 250
**Agni's hiding in the waters**

First of all, in this section Agni's office as carrier of the oblation is praised. The performance of the sacrifice, which is the foundation of all the affairs of the world, is indispensable for the maintenance of the world. For this sacrifice to be fully accomplished, Agni must be the one who accomplishes this task. Therefore he must be the chief Hotṛ and the carrier of the oblation. "I think of you, Jātavedas, as the one who will carry the oblations continuously" (मन्ये त्वा जातवेदसं स हव्यावक्ष्यानुषक् (*manye tvā jātavedasaṃ sa havyāvakṣyānuṣak*)): the seer first expresses his faith, his firm conviction that Agni, in the form of Jātavedas, is the unfailing carrier of the oblation (5-9-1).

The gods, who rely on the oblation as their food, become agitated if Agni, who distributes the sacrificial oblation, is out of sight even briefly. In such circumstances they entreat Agni humbly to perform the work of carrying the oblation. Some such circumstances are described in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā itself. For example, the exposition of Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 10-51 may be examined here. In this sūkta, which is being cited, the gods entreat Agni for the work of carrying the oblation. Agni names one condition dear to him, and gives the assurance that if the gods observe that condition he will perform the work of carrying the oblation.

An earlier story, explaining why Agni hid in the waters, is told both in the present sūkta of the Ṛgveda and in the Yajurveda.

अग्नेः पूर्वे भ्रातरो अर्थमेतं रथीनाध्वानमन्वावरीवुः । तस्माद्भिया वरुण दूरमायं गौरो न क्षेप्नोरविजे ज्यायाः । कुर्मस्त आयुरजरं यदग्ने यथा युक्तो जातवेदो न रिष्याः । अथा वहानि सुमनस्यमानो भागं देवेभ्यो हविषः सुजाश ॥ प्रयाजान्मे अनुयाजांश्च केवलानूर्जस्वंतं हविषो दत्त भागं । घृतं चापां पुरुषं चौषधीनामग्नेश्च दीर्घमायुरस्तु देवाः ॥ तव प्रयाजा अनुयाजाश्च केवल उर्जस्वंतो हविषः संतु भागाः । तवाग्ने यज्ञो ३ यमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमंतां प्रदिशश्च तस्रः ॥ (*agneḥ pūrve bhrātaro arthametaṃ rathīnādhvānamanvāvarīvuḥ | tasmādbhiyā varuṇa dūramāyaṃ gauro na kṣepnoravije jyāyāḥ | kurmasta āyurajaraṃ yadagne yathā yukto jātavedo na riṣyāḥ | athā vahāni sumanasyamāno bhāgaṃ devebhyo haviṣaḥ sujāśa ‖ prayājānme anuyājāṃśca kevalānūrjasvaṃtaṃ haviṣo datta bhāgaṃ | ghṛtaṃ cāpāṃ puruṣaṃ cauṣadhīnāmagneśca dīrghamāyurastu devāḥ ‖ tava prayājā anuyājāśca kevala urjasvaṃto haviṣaḥ saṃtu bhāgāḥ | tavāgne yajño 3 yamastu sarvastubhyaṃ namaṃtāṃ pradiśaśca tasraḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. 90. 10-51-6 to 9) **NOTE**

In this sūkta the conversation between the gods and Agni is given. The main point is this: Agni had three elder brothers named Bhūpati, Bhuvanapati and Bhūtānāṃ Pati. Like Agni, they used to carry to the gods the oblation offered by the sacrificers in the sacrifice. While this was so, in the course of the offerings made in the sacrifice, these three brothers died through the offerings made with the vaṣaṭ-call, which is like a thunderbolt. Seeing this, Agni, the youngest, feared that the same fate might befall him, and

### Printed p. 251
went in fear and hid in the waters. When the gods, not finding Agni anywhere, were searching for him, the fish in the water told the gods that Agni was in the water. Then the gods came to Agni and conversed with him in this way. This very conversation is set out in this sūkta. When the gods begged Agni to rise from the water and carry the oblation to them as before, Agni said that since his brothers had died the same fate would come to him, and therefore he would not come. When the gods said that he need not fear death and that they would see to it that he had no fear of death, Agni spoke again: "Good; besides freeing me from the fear of death, you must give me in the sacrifices certain special offerings: the prayājas, anuyājas, urjasvat, sviṣṭakṛt, ājyabhāga and the like." The gods agreed to this, gave him the shares of oblation he asked for, granted him the boon that he should take the chief part in the sacrifice, be saluted by all, and live long, and appointed him as before to the work of carrying the oblation. This is the main purport of this sūkta. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda the matter stands thus:

अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायाग्‌ंसो भ्रातर आसन्ते देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहंतः प्रामियंत सोऽग्निरबिभेदित्थं वाव स्य आर्तिमारिष्यतीति स निलायत सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छन्तं मत्स्यः प्राब्रवीत्तमपशपद्धियाधिया त्वा वध्यासुर्यो मा प्रावोच इति तस्मान्मत्स्यं धियाधिया घ्नंति शप्पो हि तमन्वनिंदन्तमब्रुवन्नुप न आ वर्तस्व हव्यं नो वहेति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै यदेव गृहीतस्याहुतस्य बहिः परिधिस्कंदात्तन्ने भातृणां भागधेयमसदिति तस्माद्यद्गृहीतस्याहुतस्य बहिः परिधि स्कंदति तेषां तद्भागधेयं तानेव तेन प्रीणाति परिधीन्परि दधाति रक्षसामपहत्यै॥ (*agnestrayo jyāyāgṃso bhrātara āsante devebhyo havyaṃ vahaṃtaḥ prāmiyaṃta so 'gnirabibheditthaṃ vāva sya ārtimāriṣyatīti sa nilāyata so 'paḥ prāviśattaṃ devatāḥ praiṣamaicchantaṃ matsyaḥ prābravīttamapaśapaddhiyādhiyā tvā vadhyāsuryo mā prāvoca iti tasmānmatsyaṃ dhiyādhiyā ghnaṃti śappo hi tamanvaniṃdantamabruvannupa na ā vartasva havyaṃ no vaheti so 'bravīdvaraṃ vṛṇai yadeva gṛhītasyāhutasya bahiḥ paridhiskaṃdāttanne bhātṛṇāṃ bhāgadheyamasaditi tasmādyadgṛhītasyāhutasya bahiḥ paridhi skaṃdati teṣāṃ tadbhāgadheyaṃ tāneva tena prīṇāti paridhīnpari dadhāti rakṣasāmapahatyai‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1, 2)

Formerly Agni had three elder brothers. They used to carry to the gods the oblation that the sacrificer offers in sacrifices and the like. When they died, Agni feared that the same fate might overtake him, ran away, entered the water and hid so that no one could see him. When the gods were searching where Agni had gone, a fish in the water told the gods that Agni was hidden in the water. Hearing this tale-bearing of the fish, Agni was angry and cursed that henceforth people should catch and kill the fish in the water with nets and other means. Accordingly, even now people catch fish with nets and other means, kill them and eat them. Then the gods said to Agni, "O Agni, come back and be ready for the work of carrying the oblation for us." To this Agni said that, in the offering made in the sacrifice, the paridhi (

### Printed p. 252
the name for the special darbha-grass laid on the four sides of the fire-pit so that rākṣasas may not come and obstruct the sacrifice) — that the portion of the offerings such as the ājya that falls outside, that is, on this side, should be the share of his brothers; if this boon were granted, he would rise from the water and carry the oblation as before. The gods agreed and gave him the boon in that way. Such is the story.

When Agni was entreated to take the chief place in the sacrifice and help the gods, a conversation took place between Agni and the other gods, which shows Agni's pre-eminence and his exceeding power. That conversation, which is the substance of the present sūkta, runs as follows. (10-51)

The gods: O Agni, the covering with which you have hidden yourself and gone into the water is very thick and entirely concealing. But, O Jātavedas, one god only (Prajāpati) knows fully your many different forms.

Agni: Who among you knows my forms? Which god knows fully all the variety of my shapes? O Mitra and Varuṇa, if there is one among you who knows my radiant forms, the means of carrying the oblation to the gods, will you tell me where they all lie hidden?

The gods: O Agni, in order to find you, who had taken many forms and gone into the water and the plants, we searched for you. Then Yama alone discovered your great flames hidden in the ten places beginning with the earth.

Agni: O Varuṇa, from fear that the gods might again impose on me the work of carrying the oblation, I came here and hid. For that very reason I have hidden myself within the water in different forms. This much only I can say: I do not wish to bear again the burden of that office.

The gods: O Agni, the devout Manu waits to worship you and perform the sacrifice. You have adorned yourself and gone into the water. Make safe the paths on which the gods travel, and carry the offered oblations to the gods.

Agni: O Varuṇa, my elder brothers agreed to perform this very duty of carrying the oblation. But in the course of performing that duty they died. For that reason I

### Printed p. 253
was frightened and ran here. As the gaur, as soon as it sees the hunter's bow and arrows, takes fright and runs, so I too ran here trembling. (This occasion was told earlier.)

The gods: O Agni, you need not harbour that fear. We give you a life free from decay. With its help you can escape death. O Agni, of excellent birth, be well disposed toward us, and again take up the burden of carrying the oblation of the gods and distributing it to them.

Agni: O gods, set aside for me alone, specially assigned, the vigorous oblations in the form of prayājas and anuyājas. Offer me the essence of the waters (ghee) and the essence of the plants. May my life, that of Agni, be long.

The gods: O Agni, we set the oblations of prayāja and anuyāja aside specially for you alone. May all the vigorous portions of the oblations be yours. O Agni, may this sacrifice too be offered to you alone. May the four quarters bow before you in humility and salute you. Such is the account of the conversation in sūkta 10-51. It is after this that in the next sūkta Agni proclaims himself the lord of the whole sacrifice. Moreover he gives the due assurance of offering his cooperation to the gods, and asks them to tell him in what way he can help them.

Concerning sūktas 51, 52 and 53, which deal with Saucīka Agni, the great sage Śaunaka, in the seventh chapter of his work called Bṛhaddevatā, says as follows—

वैश्वानरे गृहपतौ यविष्टेऽग्नौ च पावके । वषट्कारेण वृक्षेषु भातृष्टग्नौ सहिसुते ॥ ६१ ॥ अपचक्राम देवेभ्यः सौचीकोऽग्निरिति श्रुतिः । (*vaiśvānare gṛhapatau yaviṣṭe 'gnau ca pāvake | vaṣaṭkāreṇa vṛkṣeṣu bhātṛṣṭagnau sahisute ‖ 61 ‖ apacakrāma devebhyaḥ saucīko 'gniriti śrutiḥ |*)

Agni, famed under names such as Vaiśvānara, Gṛhapati and Pāvaka, had three brothers. Their names were Bhūpati, Bhuvanapati and Bhūtānāṃ Pati. Among these brothers Agni was the youngest. Formerly Agni's three elder brothers used to carry to the gods, and make reach them, the offerings that sacrificers make with the vaṣaṭ-call in sacrifices and the like. According to the śruti sentence वज्रो वै वषट्कारः । वज्र मेव भातृवेभ्यः प्रहरति । (*vajro vai vaṣaṭkāraḥ | vajra meva bhātṛvebhyaḥ praharati |*), if there is even a little excess or deficiency in the vaṣaṭ offerings, it strikes like a thunderbolt both those who utter the mantra and those who carry the oblation. Therefore Agni's elder brothers, who carried the vaṣaṭ offerings to the gods, met death through the blow of the vaṣaṭ-call. Seeing this, the youngest, Saucīka Agni, thinking that the same fate would befall him,

### Printed p. 254

…and afraid, he ran far away from the gods. This matter is stated in the Śruti passages themselves.

स प्राविशदपक्रम्य ऋतूनपो वनस्पतीन् (*sa prāviśadapakramya ṛtūnapo vanaspatīn*) (62)
ततोऽसुराः प्रादुरासन्नष्टेऽग्नौ हव्यवाहने (*tato 'surāḥ prādurāsannaṣṭe 'gnau havyavāhane*)
तेऽग्निमेवान्ववैक्षंत देवा हत्वासुरान्युधि (*te 'gnimevānvavaikṣaṃta devā hatvāsurānyudhi*) (63)
तं तु दूराद्यमश्चैव वरुणश्चान्वपश्यतां (*taṃ tu dūrādyamaścaiva varuṇaścānvapaśyatāṃ*)
उभावेनं समादाय देवानेवाभिजग्मतुः (*ubhāvenaṃ samādāya devānevābhijagmatuḥ*) (64)

Agni left the gods and ran away. He entered the seasons, the trees and the waters and hid himself so that no one could see him. After Agni had gone, war broke out between the gods and the asuras, and the gods killed the asuras in battle and became victorious. Afterwards, not seeing Agni, who used to carry the oblations to them, they searched for him in all places. Then Yama and Varuṇa, who were among the gods, saw the place where Agni was, took him along with them, and went to the gods.

दृष्ट्वा देवास्तेनमूचुरग्ने हव्यानि नो वह (*dṛṣṭvā devāstenamūcuragne havyāni no vaha*)
वरान् गृहाण चास्मत्तश्चित्रभानो भजस्व नः (*varān gṛhāṇa cāsmattaścitrabhāno bhajasva naḥ*)
देवयानान् सुगान् पथः कुरुष्प सुमनाः स्वयं (*devayānān sugān pathaḥ kuruṣpa sumanāḥ svayaṃ*) (65)
प्रत्युवाच तानग्निर्विश्वे देवा यदूच मां (*pratyuvāca tānagnirviśve devā yadūca māṃ*)
तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंच जना मम (*tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃca janā mama*) (66)

The gods saw that Agni had come to them and said: "O Agni, you shine with a wondrous, manifold radiance. From now on you must bring and carry to us the oblations that the sacrificers offer in the sacrifice. Ask for whatever boons you wish; we shall give them." Agni replied: "O gods, I shall do just as you say. But the five peoples (pañcajanāḥ) must accept my office of Hotṛ, that is, my priesthood, and become my helpers."

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः (*śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ*)
उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते संच जनाः स्मृताः (*uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete saṃca janāḥ smṛtāḥ*) (67)

An explanation is necessary on the question who the five peoples are here, so it is given. There are differences of opinion on this matter, and some of them are set out here. By difference of position Agni is known to be of five kinds: (1) the fire established near the door of the sacrificial hall; (2) the fire that is brought, according to rule and with mantras, from the place of fire-churning to the northern altar and installed on the sacrificial altar; (3) the fire called Gṛhapati (the guardian of the house), established in the house of the sacrificer or in the sacrificial house

### Printed p. 255

; (4) the Āhavanīya fire on the northern altar; (5) the fire called Dakṣiṇāgni. Some say that these five kinds of fire are the five peoples.

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरसराक्षसाः (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvorasarākṣasāḥ*)
गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः (*gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ*) (68)
यास्येमन्यवावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् (*yāsyemanyavāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān*)

Men, fathers, gods, gandharvas, serpents, rākṣasas — or gandharvas, fathers, gods, asuras, yakṣas and rākṣasas: these five groups are the five peoples, according to the teachers Yāska and Aupamanyava.

निषादपंचमान् वर्णान्यंते शाकटायनः (*niṣādapaṃcamān varṇānyaṃte śākaṭāyanaḥ*) (69)
ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते (*ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate*)
होताध्वर्युस्तथोद्गाता ब्रह्मा चेति वदंति तान् (*hotādhvaryustathodgātā brahmā ceti vadaṃti tān*) (70)

The five classes of people — Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, Śūdra and Niṣāda (hunters) — are called the five peoples, according to the teacher Śākaṭāyana. The four priests together with the sacrificer — Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Udgātṛ, Brahmā and the sacrificer — are the five peoples, according to Śākapūṇi.

चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः (*cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ*)
गंधर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा (*gaṃdharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā*) (70)**NOTE**
सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयंते हैतरेयके (*sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyaṃte haitareyake*)
ये चान्ये पृथिवीजाता देवाश्चान्येऽथ यज्जियाः (*ye cānye pṛthivījātā devāścānye 'tha yajjiyāḥ*) (72)

The eye, the ear, the mind, speech and the breath — these five are the five peoples, say the ātmavādins, that is, the Vedāntins. Gandharvas and apsarases, gods, men, fathers, and serpents — these five classes are renowned as the five peoples, as stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. Besides, any five groups of people born on the earth and worthy of sacrifice, or other gods not in the list stated above, may also be reckoned as the five peoples.

आयुरस्तु च मे दीर्घं हवींषि विविधानि च (*āyurastu ca me dīrghaṃ havīṃṣi vividhāni ca*)
अरिष्टिः पूर्वजानां च भ्रातृणामध्वरेऽध्वरे (*ariṣṭiḥ pūrvajānāṃ ca bhrātṛṇāmadhvare 'dhvare*) (73)
प्रयाजाश्चानुयाजाश्च घृतं सोमे च यः पशुः (*prayājāścānuyājāśca ghṛtaṃ some ca yaḥ paśuḥ*)
मद्वैवत्यानि वै संतु यज्ञो मद्देवतोऽस्तु च (*madvaivatyāni vai saṃtu yajño maddevato 'stu ca*) (74)

### Printed p. 256

Asking for the boons he wanted, Agni went on to say: "Let me live long, that is, let long life be granted to me; and let various kinds of oblations be offered to me. Let my elder brothers be protected from harm in every sacrifice. The prayājā offerings that are made to me first when the oblations are offered, the anūyājā offerings made at the end, the ghee (ājya), and the animal offered in the Soma sacrifice — let all of these belong to me, and let me be the deity of all of them. In the sacrifice too let me be the deity and my influence be the greater." Thus he asked for the boons he wanted.

तवाग्ने यज्ञ इत्येतत्प्रत्यार्थि स्विष्टकृच्च सः (*tavāgne yajña ityetatpratyārthi sviṣṭakṛcca saḥ*)
यस्य त्रीणि सहस्राणि नव त्रीणि शतानि च (*yasya trīṇi sahasrāṇi nava trīṇi śatāni ca*) (75)
त्रिंशश्चैव तु देवानां सर्वानेव वरान्ददुः (*triṃśaścaiva tu devānāṃ sarvāneva varāndaduḥ*)

The gods agreed: "So be it." "O Agni, let this sacrifice be yours" — that is, take the principal part in it and carry it through completely; so saying, all the gods, three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine in number, together granted Agni the boon.

ततोग्निः सुमनाः प्रीतो विश्वैर्देवैः पुरस्कृतः (*tatogniḥ sumanāḥ prīto viśvairdevaiḥ puraskṛtaḥ*) (76)
विधूयांगानि यज्ञेषु चक्रे होत्रमतंद्रितः (*vidhūyāṃgāni yajñeṣu cakre hotramataṃdritaḥ*)
भ्रातृभिः सहितः प्रीतो दिव्यात्मा हव्यवाहनः (*bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ prīto divyātmā havyavāhanaḥ*) (77)

Thereafter, honoured by all the gods, Agni became calm in mind and content. Free of every anxiety, glad at heart and the bearer of the oblation, he rejoiced together with his brothers and performed the office of Hotṛ, that is, the conduct of the sacrifice, in all the ritual parts of the sacrifices.

तस्यास्थि देवदार्वासीन्मेदो मांसं च गुग्गुलुः (*tasyāsthi devadārvāsīnmedo māṃsaṃ ca gugguluḥ*)
सुगंधितेजनं स्नायु शुक्रं रजतकांचने (*sugaṃdhitejanaṃ snāyu śukraṃ rajatakāṃcane*) (78)
रोमाणि काशाः केशास्तु कुशाः कूर्मा नखानि च (*romāṇi kāśāḥ keśāstu kuśāḥ kūrmā nakhāni ca*)
अंत्राणि चैवाप्यवका मज्जा सिकतशर्कराः (*aṃtrāṇi caivāpyavakā majjā sikataśarkarāḥ*) (79)
अस्यक् पित्तं च विविधा धातवो गैरिकादयः (*asyak pittaṃ ca vividhā dhātavo gairikādayaḥ*)
एवनग्निश्च देवाश्च सूक्तैर्महदिति त्रिभिः (*evanagniśca devāśca sūktairmahaditi tribhiḥ*) (80)

The bone of Agni, the conductor of the sacrificial work, became the deodar tree. His fat (medas) and flesh were transformed into guggulu (a fragrant substance). His sinews

### Printed p. 257

(nerves) became the fragrant reeds called tejana. His semen became silver and gold; his hairs (romāṇi) became the grass called kāśa. The hairs of his head became the darbha grass called kuśa; his nails became tortoises; his entrails became the creepers called avaka. His fat, sand and gravel became earth; his blood and bile became various minerals such as red ochre, and metals. In this way the conversation conducted by the gods and Agni together is set out in the three sūktas beginning with महत्तत् (*mahattat*) (sūktas 51–53).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महत्तदिति नवर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । वज्रभूतेन वषट्कारेण देवानां हविर्वहनेन च हतेषु भ्रातृषु कनिष्ठः सौचीको नामाग्निर्वषट्कारहनिर्वहनाभ्यां
> भीतो देवेभ्यो निर्गत्यापः प्राविशत् । स च मत्स्यैः प्रदर्शितः सन्नन्वेषुमागतैर्देवैः सहेदमादिसूक्तत्रयेण संवादं कृतवान् । अस्य सूक्तस्य द्वितीयादियुजश्चतस्रो विश्वे देवाः शास्त्रनेति षडृचमुत्तरसूक्तं चेति दशर्चोऽग्नि वाक्यं ।
> अयुजः प्रथमाद्याः पंचर्चो यमैच्छाम मनसेत्येकादशर्चमुत्तरसूक्तं च
> देवानां वाक्यं । तत्र तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीयेति दृचस्त्वगेर्वाक्यं ।
> अतोऽग्नि वाक्येषु देवा देवताग्निर्ऋषिः । देवोक्तिष्टग्निर्देवता देवा ऋषयः ।
> अनादेशपरिभाषयेदमुत्तरं च द्वे त्रैष्टुभे विशेषानभिधानात् । शथा जानुक्रांतं। वषट्कारेण वृक्षेषु भ्रातृषु सौचीकोऽग्नि रपः प्रविश्य देवैः समवददुत्तरै.
> स्प्रिभिर्महत्तन्नव तत्र युजोऽग्नि वाक्यं विश्व इत्युत्तरं षट्कमयुजो देवानां
> यमैच्छामेत्युत्तरं चैकादशकं तदद्येति तु दृचोऽग्निरिति ॥ गतो
> विनियोगः ॥ सूक्तत्रयोक्तार्थे तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणं । अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांसो
> भ्रातर आसन् ते देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहंतः प्रामीयंत सोऽग्निरबिभेदित्थं
> नाव स्य अर्तिमारिष्यतीति स निलायत सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवाःप्रैषमैच्छन्नित्यादि ।
> तै. सं. २.६.६ । तत्राद्यया देवा अग्निमाहुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ninth sūkta, of nine Ṛks, beginning महत्तत् (*mahattat*). When his brothers had been killed by the vajra-like वषट्कार (*vaṣaṭkāra*) and by the carrying of the oblation for the gods, the youngest, the fire named Saucīka, was afraid of the वषट्कार (*vaṣaṭkāra*)-killing and of the carrying; he left the gods and entered the waters. Shown to the gods by fish, when they came searching, he held a conversation with them in this sūkta and the two that follow. Of this sūkta the even Ṛks (the second onward), four in number, together with the six Ṛks beginning विश्वे देवाः शास्त्रन (*viśve devāḥ śāstrana*) and the following sūkta, make ten Ṛks that are Agni's speech. The odd Ṛks, the first five, together with the eleven Ṛks of the following sūkta beginning यमैच्छाम (*yamaicchāma*), are the speech of the gods; and in that group, the Ṛks beginning तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya*) are Agni's speech. Hence in the Ṛks that are Agni's speech the gods are the deity and Agni the seer; in the Ṛks spoken by the gods, Agni is the deity and the gods the seers. The two Ṛks that are Agni's speech are in this follow-on; by the rule of non-specification both this and the following sūkta are in Triṣṭubh, since no special metre is stated. The Anukramaṇī is cited accordingly: वषट्कारेण वृक्षेषु भ्रातृषु सौचीकोऽग्निरपः प्रविश्य देवैः समवददुत्तरैस्त्रिभिर्महत्तन्नव तत्र युजोऽग्नि वाक्यं विश्व इत्युत्तरं षट्कमयुजो देवानां यमैच्छामेत्युत्तरं जैकादशकं तदद्येति तु द्वृचोऽग्नेः । (*vaṣaṭkāreṇa vṛkṣeṣu bhrātṛṣu saucīko 'gnirapaḥ praviśya devaiḥ samavadaduttaraistribhirmahattannava tatra yujo 'gni vākyaṃ viśva ityuttaraṃ ṣaṭkamayujo devānāṃ yamaicchāmetyuttaraṃ jaikādaśakaṃ tadadyeti tu dvṛco 'gneḥ |*). The use (viniyoga) is already stated. For the matter told in the three sūktas the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa is cited: अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांसो भ्रातर आसन् ते देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहंतः प्रामीयंत सोऽग्निरबिभेदित्थं नाव स्य अर्तिमारिष्यतीति स निलायत सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवाःप्रैषमैच्छन्नित्यादि । (*agnestrayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsan te devebhyo havyaṃ vahaṃtaḥ prāmīyaṃta so 'gnirabibheditthaṃ nāva sya artimāriṣyatīti sa nilāyata so 'paḥ prāviśattaṃ devāḥpraiṣamaicchannityādi |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2.6.6); in it, with the first Ṛk the gods address Agni.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning महत्तत् (*mahattat*) is the ninth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. An episode is told in this sūkta: when the three elder brothers of Agni, who carried the oblations to the gods by means of the vajra-like वषट्कार (*vaṣaṭkāra*) offerings, had died, the youngest, the fire Saucīka, saw this and became afraid. Thinking that carrying the वषट्कार (*vaṣaṭkāra*) oblation to the gods was a very dangerous work, he ran away from the gods without telling or asking anyone, entered the water and lay hidden. While the gods were searching where Agni had gone, a fish in the water told the gods that Agni was hiding in the water. Then the gods came to the water, saw Agni, and the conversation they held is set out in this sūkta and the next two sūktas. In this sūkta the even-numbered Ṛks 2, 4, 6, 8, and the six Ṛks of the next sūkta beginning विश्वेदेवाः शास्त्रन (*viśvedevāḥ śāstrana*), ten Ṛks in all, are Agni's speech. The five odd-numbered Ṛks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and the nine Ṛks of the 53rd sūkta beginning यमैच्छाम (*yamaicchāma*) other than its Ṛks 4–5, fourteen Ṛks in all, are the speech of the gods. Ṛks 4–5 of the 53rd sūkta are Agni's speech.

### Printed p. 258

Therefore, for the Ṛks containing Agni's speech, Agni is the seer and the gods are the deity; for the Ṛks containing the speech of the gods, the gods are the seers and Agni is the deity. The Ṛks of this sūkta and the next are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: वषट्कारेण वृक्षेषु भ्रातृषु सौचीकोऽग्निरपः प्रविश्य देवैः समवददुत्तरैस्त्रिभिर्महत्तन्नव तत्र युजोऽग्नि वाक्यं विश्व इत्युत्तरं षट्कमयुजो देवानां यमैच्छामेत्युत्तरं जैकादशकं तदद्येति तु द्वृचोऽग्नेः । (*vaṣaṭkāreṇa vṛkṣeṣu bhrātṛṣu saucīko 'gnirapaḥ praviśya devaiḥ samavadaduttaraistribhirmahattannava tatra yujo 'gni vākyaṃ viśva ityuttaraṃ ṣaṭkamayujo devānāṃ yamaicchāmetyuttaraṃ jaikādaśakaṃ tadadyeti tu dvṛco 'gneḥ |*). The use has been stated earlier. The matter stated in these three sūktas is told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, in the passages beginning अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायाग्ंसो भ्रातर आसन्ते देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहन्तः प्रामियंत सोऽग्निरबिभेदित्थं नाव स्य आर्तिमारिष्यतीति स निलायत सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छन् । (*agnestrayo jyāyāgṃso bhrātara āsante devebhyo havyaṃ vahantaḥ prāmiyaṃta so 'gnirabibheditthaṃ nāva sya ārtimāriṣyatīti sa nilāyata so 'paḥ prāviśattaṃ devatāḥ praiṣamaicchan |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6). In the first Ṛk of the present sūkta, महत्तत् (*mahattat*), the gods speak, addressing Agni.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 51
- Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 51
- Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 1; Varga 10, 11
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9
- Seer: Ṛks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 — the gods; Ṛks 2, 4, 6, 8 — Agni Saucīka
- Deity: Ṛks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 — Agni Saucīka; Ṛks 2, 4, 6, 8 — the gods
- Metre: Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हत्तदुल्पं॒ स्थवि॑रं॒ तदा॑सी॒द्येनावि॑ष्टितः प्रवि॒वेशि॑था॒पः ।  
> विश्वा॑ अपश्यद्बहु॒धा ते॑ अग्ने॒ जात॑वेदस्त॒न्वो॑ दे॒व एकः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महत् । तत् । उल्बं । स्थविरं । तत् । आसीत् । येन । आविष्टितः । प्रविवेशिथः ।  
> अपः ॥

### Printed p. 259

> विश्वाः । अपश्यत् । बहुधा । ते । अग्ने । जातवेदः । तन्नः । देवः । एकः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तुदुल्बं वक्ष्यमाणं प्रावरणं महत् स्थविरमत्यंतं स्कूलं च तदासीत्
> येनोल्पेनाविष्टित आवेष्टितः सन् हे अग्ने प्रविवेशिथापः उदकानि प्रविष्टवानसि ।
> हे अग्ने जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञान विश्वाः सर्वास्तन्वस्तनूः सर्वाण्यंगानि बहुधा
> बहुप्रकारमेको देवोऽपश्यत् । दृष्टवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The covering (उल्बं (*ulbaṃ*)) that will be spoken of was great and very thick (स्थविरं (*sthaviraṃ*)), and with that small (?) wrapping of which, O Agni, you entered the waters, you were enveloped. O Agni Jātavedas, endowed with knowledge, one deity saw all your bodies, that is, all your limbs, in many ways.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- येन (*yena*)—by which covering
- आविष्टितः (*āviṣṭitaḥ*)—you, being enveloped
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- प्रविवेशिथ (*praviveśitha*)—you entered
- तत् उल्बं (*tat ulbaṃ*)—that covering
- महत् (*mahat*)—of great extent
- स्थविरं आसीत् (*sthaviraṃ āsīt*)—is also thick (stout)
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who are of the nature of Jātavedas
- ते (*te*)—your
- विश्वाः तन्नः (*viśvāḥ tannaḥ*)—all forms
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many ways
- एकः देवः (*ekaḥ devaḥ*)—one deity alone
- अपश्यत् (*apaśyat*)—has seen

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods: O Agni, the covering, of the nature of उल्ब (*ulba*), enveloped by which you entered the waters, is great in extent and thick. O Agni, who are of the nature of Jātavedas, one deity alone has seen all your forms in many ways.

##### English translation
(The gods speak :) Great and very dense is the covering enveloped by which, Agni, you have entered into the waters. Agni Jatavedas, one deity has beheld all your mainfold forms,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उल्बं (*ulbaṃ*)—Yāska has given the etymology of this word: उल्बमूर्णोतेर्वणोतेर्वा । महत्तदुल्बं स्थविरं तदासीदित्यपि निगमो भवति (*ulbamūrṇotervaṇotervā | mahattadulbaṃ sthaviraṃ tadāsīdityapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 6-35); the passage quoted is *mahattadulbaṃ sthaviraṃ tadāsīd*. The word उल्ब (*ulba*) is derived either from the root ūrṇu, meaning to cover, to wrap, or from the root vṛ. It means covering, wrapping. As stated in the Śruti passage उल्बं गर्भो जरायु (*ulbaṃ garbho jarāyu*), the words ulba, garbha and jarāyu are synonyms. The layer of skin that covers (wraps) the infant is called garbha. The other words have the same meaning.

> को मा ददर्श कतमः स देवो यो मे तन्नो बहुधा  
> पर्यपश्यत् ।
