> देवस्य । पश्य । काव्यं । महित्वा । अद्य । ममार । सः । ह्यः । सं । आन ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये विधुं दद्राणमित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । आ याह्यर्वाजुप
> वंधुरेष्ठा विधुं दद्राणमिति ॥
> अनया कालात्मक इंद्रः स्तूयते । विधुं विधातारं सर्वस्य युद्धादेः
> कर्तारं । विपूर्वो दधातिः करोत्यर्थः । तथा समने अननमनः प्राणनं । सम्यगननोपेते संग्रामे बहूनां शत्रूणां दद्राणं द्रावकं ईदृक्षामर्थ्योपेतं
> युवानं संतं पुरुषं पलितो जरा जगार । निगिरतींद्राज्ञया । एवमुक्तलक्षणं
> वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणं च देवस्य कालात्मकस्येंद्रस्य महित्वा महत्वेनोपेतं काव्यं
> सामर्थ्यं पश्य । पश्यत हे जनाः । तथा जरसा प्राप्तोऽयं ममार । म्रियते । स
> ह्यः परेद्युः समान । सम्यक्क्षेष्टते । पुनर्जन्मांतरे प्रादुर्भवतीत्यर्थः । तदेवं
> चत्वारि नामानि शरीराण्युक्तानि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya, this verse विधुं दद्राणं (*vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ*) is used. It is also put in sūtra form: आ याह्यर्वाजुप वंधुरेष्ठा विधुं दद्राणमिति (*ā yāhyarvājupa vaṃdhureṣṭhā vidhuṃ dadrāṇamiti*). By this verse Indra in the form of Time is praised. विधुं (*vidhuṃ*) is the arranger, the doer of everything, of war and the rest; the root दधाति (*dadhāti*) with वि (*vi*) has the meaning "does". समने (*samane*): *ananaṃ* is breathing; in a battle where there is fully breathing, the man who scatters many enemies, endowed with such ability, who is young, grey old age swallows, at Indra's command. Thus, O people, behold the power of the deity Indra, whose form is Time, endowed with greatness, such as has been described and will be described. Then this same man, overcome by old age, dies; and on the next day समान (*samāna*), he breathes again; that is, he appears again in another birth. Thus four names, that is bodies, have been stated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विधुं (*vidhuṃ*)—one who has the ability to carry through many wars
- समने (*samane*)—in battle
- बहूनां (*bahūnāṃ*)—many enemies
- दद्राणं (*dadrāṇaṃ*)—the man who drives them off
- युवानं संतं (*yuvānaṃ saṃtaṃ*)—though young
- पलितः (*palitaḥ*)—old age
- जगार (*jagāra*)—covers him
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—(O men) of Indra, whose form is Time
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—endowed with majesty
- काव्यं (*kāvyaṃ*)—power
- पश्य (*paśya*)—behold
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same man
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- ममार (*mamāra*)—meets death
- ह्यः (*hyaḥ*)—the next day
- समान (*samāna*)—breathes again (obtains rebirth)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

A man who has the ability to carry through many wars and who destroys many enemies in battle, though he is young, old age covers him. O people, behold the majestic power of Indra, whose form is Time. That same man dies today. Again, after a time, he obtains rebirth.

##### English translation
The grey-haired has swallowed the warlike (man), the scatterer of many foes, in battle being young; behold the power of the deity (endowed) with might ; he dies to-day ; he is alive to-morrow.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this verse विधुं दद्राणं (*vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ*) is to be recited among the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras in the Mahāvrata sacrifice is explained by the sentence of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, आ याह्वर्वाजुप वंधुरेष्ठा विधुं दद्राणं (*ā yāhvarvājupa vaṃdhureṣṭhā vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-1).

> शाक्कना । शक्त्येव शाक्क । शक्कना बलेन शाकः शक्तः ॥ शक्त्यशक्तौ । स्वशक्तैव
> सर्वं कर्तुं शक्त इत्यर्थः। न हींद्रस्य सहायांतरापेक्षास्तींद्रत्वादेव ।
> अरुणोऽरुणवर्णः सुपर्णः कश्चिच्छोभनपर्णः पक्ष्या गच्छतीत्यध्याहारः । उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । यो महो महाञ्चरो विक्रांतः सनात्
> पुराणोऽनीळोऽनीडो नीडस्याकर्ता । न हींद्रोऽग्निवत् कुत्रचिदपि यज्ञे
> निकेतनं करोति । एवं सुपर्णरूपेणेंद्रमाह । स पक्षींद्रो यच्चिकेत कर्तव्यत्वेन जानाति तत्सत्यमित् सत्यमेव न तु मोघं व्यर्थं भवति । स स्पार्हं स्पृहणीयं वसूत जेता जयति शत्रुभ्यः सकाशात् उतापि दाता प्रयच्छति च स्तोतृभ्यः॥
> न लोकाव्ययेत्यादिना षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

शाक्कना (*śākkanā*) means by power, by strength; शाकः (*śākaḥ*) is capable. That is, he is able to do everything by his own power alone; for Indra, by his very Indra-hood, needs no other help. अरुणः (*aruṇaḥ*) is red-coloured; सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*) is one with beautiful wings; "goes by flight" is to be supplied, and "comes" is supplied from the preverb आ (*ā*) heard in the verse. He who is महः (*mahaḥ*), great, शूरः (*śūraḥ*), valiant, सनात् (*sanāt*), ancient, अनीळः (*anīḷaḥ*), makes no nest; for Indra, unlike Agni, does not make a dwelling anywhere in the sacrifice. Thus he speaks of Indra in the form of a bird. What that bird Indra knows as to be done, that is truly true, not vain. He is the winner of desirable wealth from enemies, and also the giver of it to the praisers. The rest of the passage cites the rule न लोकाव्ययेत्यादिना (*na lokāvyayetyādinā*) for the prohibition of the genitive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शाक्मना (*śākmanā*)—endowed with inner power
- शाकः (*śākaḥ*)—joined with strength
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great-souled
- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—valiant
- सनात् (*sanāt*)—ancient
- अनीळः (*anīḷaḥ*)—nestless
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—in the form of a bird
- अरुणः (*aruṇaḥ*)—the golden-hued Indra
- आ (*ā*)—comes
- यत् (*yat*)—what (that same Indra)
- चिकेत (*ciketa*)—knows
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- सत्यं इत् (*satyaṃ it*)—is truly of the nature of truth
- न मोघं (*na moghaṃ*)—not false
- स्पार्हं (*spārhaṃ*)—desired by all
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- जेता (*jetā*)—the conqueror
- उत (*uta*)—and
- दाता (*dātā*)—the giver

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who, endowed with inner power, is great-souled, valiant, ancient, and a nestless bird in form, such golden-hued Indra comes. That which the same Indra knows is truly of the nature of truth. It does not become false. Indra is the winner of attractive wealth and the giver of it.

##### English translation
Vigorous with (innate) vigour, (comes a) purple-coloured bird, mighty, heroic, ancient, having no nest : that which he knows is truth, and is not vain :(he is) the conqueror and distributor of desirable wealth.

> ये । कर्मणः । क्रियमाणस्य । मह्ना । ऋतेऽकर्मं । उत् अजायंत । देवाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्र विभिर्मरुद्भिः सह वृष्ण्यानि वर्षकाणि पौंस्यानि बलान्याददे । आदत्ते ।
> येभिर्मरुद्भिः सहितो वृत्रहत्याय । प्राण्युपकारकवृष्ट्यावरकत्वाद्वृत्रः पापं ।
> तस्य हत्याय । मनुष्याणामुपद्रवशमनायेत्यर्थः । तदर्थं वज्री वज्रवानिंद्र
> औक्षत् । वर्षति । ये च मरुतो देवा मह्ना महतेंद्रेण क्रियामाणस्य
> कर्मणो वृष्टिप्रदानलक्षणस्य! साहायार्थमृतेकर्म मृतकर्मवृष्टिप्रदानकर्म
> प्रत्युदजायंत उन्मुखा जायंते स्वयमेव तैरेभिर्दद इति समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra takes up the rain-making, mighty powers together with the Maruts, in whose company he, the wielder of the thunderbolt, rained for the slaying of Vṛtra. Vṛtra is sin, because he obstructs the rain that benefits living beings; his slaying means the removal of troubles for men. For that purpose Indra rained. Those Maruts, who are gods, arose of their own accord, facing the work of giving rain that the great Indra was performing, in order to help in it. So the construction is: with them he takes up these powers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्री (*vajrī*)—Indra

- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by the great Indra
- क्रियमाणस्य (*kriyamāṇasya*)—which is to be carried out
- कर्मणः (*karmaṇaḥ*)—for the work
- ऋतेकर्मं (*ṛtekarmaṃ*)—protecting the acts of giving rain and the like
- उदजायंत (*udajāyaṃta*)—were born
- विभीः (*vibhīḥ*)—with the Maruts
- वृष्ण्या (*vṛṣṇyā*)—rain-causing
- पौंस्यानि (*pauṃsyāni*)—powers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, together with the Maruts in whose company he poured down rain for the destruction of sin, and who as divine beings were born, intent on the acts of giving rain and the like, for the work to be accomplished by the great Indra, takes up with such Maruts the rain-causing powers.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra, with the help of the Maruts, brings forth works such as the pouring of rain. He is of pervading strength, a destroyer of Rākṣasas (रक्षोहा (*rakṣohā*)), all-minded, that is, exceedingly intelligent, and a swift overcomer of enemies. Such a mighty Indra comes from the heaven-world, drinks the Soma, and growing in strength, being a hero, he blows away the foes with his weapon or his stroke. The meaning is that he drives away the Asuras by battle.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who together with the Maruts produces works such as the sending of rain, who has strength spread everywhere, destroys the wicked, has a mind extended everywhere, swiftly conquers enemies, who has come from the heaven-world after drinking the Soma, grown in strength, and is valiant, destroys the enemies with weapons.

**English Translation**
Accomplishing his duty with their assistance, the all-powerful Indra, the destroyer of the wicked, the all-wise, the quick subduer of foes, descending from heaven, and quaffing the Soma, invigorated and a hero he demolishes the Dasyus with his thunderbolt.

## Sūkta 56 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
The seer of this sūkta, Bṛhaduktha, when his son Vāji died, was seized with grief and in this sūkta prays that the various parts of the dead son may merge into the five great elements. Accordingly: that the fire present in the body as heat may join the external fire; that the vital breath may join the external wind in the sky; and that the self may join the sun, who shines in heaven in the form of the supreme Brahman, and become one with him. These matters are set out in the Ṛks of this sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदं त इति सप्तर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं । वामदेवपुत्रो बृहदुक्ष ऋषिः ।
> चतुर्थीपंचमीषष्ट्यो जगत्यः । आदितस्तिस्रः सप्तमी च त्रिष्टुभः । विश्वे देवा
> देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इदं ते सप्त वैश्वदेवं तु चतुर्थ्याद्यास्तिस्रो जगश्य
> इति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ आहवनीये वाद्यादिकारणेनायतनान्निष्कम्य शम्यापरासादर्वाचीने देशे दीप्यमाने सति तमग्निमनया पुनरायतने संवपेत् ।
> सूत्रितं च । आहवनीयमवदीप्यमानमर्वाक् शम्यापरासादिदं त एकं पर ऊ त
> एकमिति संवपेत् । आ. ३-१० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning इदं ते (*idaṃ te*) has seven Ṛks and is the fourteenth sūkta. The seer is Bṛhaduktha, son of Vāmadeva. The fourth, fifth and sixth Ṛks are Jagatī; the first three and the seventh are Triṣṭubh. The deity is the Viśve Devāḥ. The Anukramaṇī says: इदं ते सप्त वैश्वदेवं तु चतुर्थ्याद्यास्तिस्रो जगत्यः (*idaṃ te sapta vaiśvadevaṃ tu caturthyādyāstisro jagatyaḥ*). The use of the sūkta has been given. Use: when the Āhavanīya fire, having left its hearth for some reason such as a sound, blazes up in a place on this side of the Śamyā-throw, one should restore that fire to its hearth with this sūkta. It is laid down in the sūtra: आहवनीयमवदीप्यमानमर्वाक् शम्यापरासादिदं त एकं पर ऊ त एकमिति संवपेत् । (*āhavanīyamavadīpyamānamarvāk śamyāparāsādidaṃ ta ekaṃ para ū ta ekamiti saṃvapet |*) (Ā. 3-10).

The Kannada Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning इदं त एकं (*idaṃ ta ekaṃ*) is the fourteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Bṛhaduktha, son of Vāmadeva; its fourth, fifth and sixth Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. The first three Ṛks of the sūkta and the seventh are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The deity is the Viśve Devāḥ; in the Anukramaṇī—

### Printed p. 341
it is said: इदं ते सप्त वैश्वदेवं तु चतुर्थ्याद्यास्तिस्रो जगत्यः (*idaṃ te sapta vaiśvadevaṃ tu caturthyādyāstisro jagatyaḥ*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

Seer: Bṛhaduktha Vāmadevya.
Deity: Viśve Devāḥ.
Metre: 1-3, 7 Triṣṭubh; 4-6 Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दं त॒ एकं॑ प॒र ऊ॑ त॒ एकं॑ तृ॒तीये॑न॒ ज्योति॑षा॒ सं वि॑शस्व ।  
> सं॒वेश॑ने त॒न्नग१॒॑श्चारु॑रेधि प्रि॒यो दे॒वानां॑ पर॒मे ज॒नित्रे॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । ते । एकं । परः । ऊं इति । ते। एकं । तृतीयेन । ज्योतिषा। सं । विशस्व ।  
> संवेशने । तन्नः । चारुः । एधि । प्रियः । देवानां । परमे । जनित्रे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एतदादिभिर्बृहदुक्को वाजिनं नाम स्वपुत्रं मृतं वदति । हे मृत पुत्र ते
> तवेदं । उपरि ज्योतिषेति वक्ष्यमाणत्वादत्रेदंशब्देन ज्योतिरभिधीयते । इदं
> ज्योतिरग्न्याख्यमेकमेकोऽ०शः । आतस्तमग्निं तव देहगताग्न्यंशेन बाह्यमग्निं
> सं विशस्व । संगच्छस्व । तथा पर उ अन्नोऽपि ते तवैकं वाय्वाख्योऽ०शः । ते तव
> प्राणवाय्वाख्येनांशेन संविशस्व । शरीराग्नि प्राणवाय्वर्बाह्याग्निवाय्वोश्च कत्वादंशत्वमिति भावः । तथा तृतीयेन ज्योतिषादित्याख्येन तेजसा तवात्मना संविशस्व ।
> सूर्यगतात्मचैतन्यदेहगतात्मचैतन्ययोरभेदादंशत्वं । तद्योऽहं सोऽसौ
> योऽसौ सोऽहं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थु षश्चेति श्रुतेरात्मनः सूर्यप्रवेशो
> युक्तः । तन्नस्तन्वाः संवेशने तस्मिन्सूर्यॆ संविश्य चारुरेधि । कल्याणो भव ।
> कीदृशस्वं । प्रियस्तेन सह प्रीयमाणः । कीदृशे तस्मिन् । देवानां परम
> उत्तमे जनित्रॆ जनके । देवानां हैतत्परमं जनित्रं यत्सूर्य इति हि श्रुतिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk and those that follow, Bṛhaduktha addresses his dead son, named Vāji. "O dead son, this of yours": since "with light" is said further on, the word इदं (*idaṃ*) here denotes light. This light, called fire, is one portion. So join the external fire with the fire-portion present in your body. Likewise that other, wind, is one portion of yours; join with it by the portion that is the vital breath. The bodily fire and breath are portions because they are one with the external fire and wind. Likewise with the third light, the radiance called Āditya, join with your self. The self-consciousness in the sun and that in the body are not different, hence the sense of portion. The Śruti तद्योऽहं सोऽसौ योऽसौ सोऽहं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थु षश्च (*tadyo 'haṃ so 'sau yo 'sau so 'haṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthu ṣaśca*) makes the self's entry into the sun fitting. "In the entering of your body": having entered that sun, become lovely, that is, auspicious, and be dear, delighted together with him. He is the supreme, the best, begetter of the gods; the Śruti says: देवानां हैतत्परमं जनित्रं यत्सूर्य (*devānāṃ haitatparamaṃ janitraṃ yatsūrya*).

- सं विशस्व (*saṃ viśasva*)—enter the external fire and become one with it (likewise)

- परः उ (*paraḥ u*)—of the vital breath within the body
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—with another portion
- सं विशस्व (*saṃ viśasva*)—enter the external wind and be merged in it (and)
- तृतीयेन ज्योतिषा (*tṛtīyena jyotiṣā*)—with the radiance of Āditya, called the third radiance
- सं विशस्व (*saṃ viśasva*)—enter with your self and become one in it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O dead son, enter the external fire with the fire-form portion of your body and become one with it. Enter the wind in the outer sky with the wind-form radiance and become one with it. And with the third, the self-form portion, enter Āditya and become one with him. When entering Āditya, the supreme place of origin even for the gods, become dear to Āditya and obtain joy.

**English Translation**
This (light) is one (portion) of you, and this other is one (portion); with your third light enter into (outer radiance); on the entrance of the body into (the sun), the supreme birthplace of the gods, become lovely and beloved.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the bodies of all living beings the Vaiśvānara fire pervades as heat, and in the belly as the digestive fire. This was explained when Vaiśvānara fire was described. The fire on earth, or the fire in the form of Āditya, is the origin of every kind of heat. Therefore when the body perishes, it is natural to wish that the heat in it merge into the external fire that is its source. Likewise it is quite fitting to say that the vital breath should merge in the external wind in the sky, and the self in the sun, the cause of all consciousness. Moreover, that the sun or Āditya is the supreme Brahman is stated plainly in Śruti passages such as आसावादित्यो बह्मेति (*āsāvādityo bahmeti*) and सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*).

> महो महतो देवांस्तव कारणभूतान् दिवीव ज्योतिर्द्युलोके वर्तमानं
> सूर्यं च । इवशब्दश्चार्थे निपातानामनेकार्थत्वात् । तं च स्वं तव स्वभूतमा
> मिमीयाः । आविश ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Vāji", son of that name, this earth, the body (तनू (*tanū*)) that carries your body to its own body: since both are earthly, it is fitting that when your body reaches the earth she should lead it. May such an earth grant us desirable wealth and grant happiness to you. Being unfallen, enter the great gods who are your cause, and the light that exists in heaven, the sun. The word इव (*iva*) is in the sense of "and", since particles have many meanings. Enter also your own self.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वार्जि (*vārji*)—O son named Vāji **NOTE**
- ते (*te*)—your
- तन्नं (*tannaṃ*)—body
- नयंती (*nayaṃtī*)—carrying
- तनूः (*tanūḥ*)—this earth
- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—attractive wealth
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- धातु (*dhātu*)—may she give
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- शर्म (*śarma*)—may she give happiness
- अह्रुतः (*ahrutaḥ*)—without stumbling anywhere
- धरुणाय (*dharuṇāya*)—for your firm support
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- दिवीव (*divīva*)—in the heaven-world
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—Āditya
- स्वं (*svaṃ*)—your own form
- आ मिमीयाः (*ā mimīyāḥ*)—enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O son named Vāji, may this earth, which carries your body, give us attractive wealth. May she give you happiness. Without stumbling anywhere, enter, for your firm support, the great gods, Āditya who dwells in the heaven-world, and your own form.

### Printed p. 344

##### English translation
May this body (the earth) conveying your body; Vajin, give precious wealth to us and hapiness to you; and do you, without stumbling, enter among the great gods for their support; and the light that is in heaven (the sun) and your own (light).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वा॒ज्य॑सि॒ वाजि॑नेना सुवे॒नीः सु॑वि॒तः स्तोमं॑ सुवि॒तो दिवं॑ गाः ।  
> सु॒वि॒तो धर्म॑ प्रथ॒मानु॑ स॒त्या सु॑वि॒तो दे॒वान्तु॑सवि॒तोऽनु॒  ॑
> पत्न्य ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वाजी । असि । वाजिनेन । सुवेनीः । सुवितः । स्तोमं । सुवितः । दिवं । गाः ।  
> सुवितः । धर्म । प्रथमा । अनु । सत्या । सुवितः । देवान् । सुवितः । अनु । पत्न्य ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुत्र त्वं पाजिनेनान्नरसेन बलेन वा वाज्यसि । तद्वान्भवसि । कीदृशस्त्वं ।
> सुवेनीः । सुष्टु कांतः ॥ वि गत्यादिषु ॥ तादृशस्त्वं सुवितः सुष्टु प्रेरितस्त्वं
> स्तोमं पूर्वं त्वया कृतं स्तोत्रं तदभिमानिदेवमनु गाः । अन्वगाः । अनुगच्छ ।
> तथा सुवितो दिवं गाः । तथा सुवितो धर्मत्वया संपादितानि धर्माण्यनुगच्छ ।
> कीदृशानि । प्रथमा मुख्यानि सत्या सत्यफलानि । तथा सुवितो देवानिंद्रादीन् । तथा
> सुवितः पत्म पतज्योतिरादित्याख्यमनु गाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O son, you are वाजी (*vājī*), possessed of वाजिनेन (*vājinena*), that is, food-essence or strength." सुवेनीः (*suvenīḥ*) means "well-beloved, handsome". Being such, and सुवितः (*suvitaḥ*), well urged, follow the स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*), the praise composed earlier by you, that is, the deity who is its object. Likewise, urged, go to heaven. Likewise, urged, follow the धर्म (*dharma*), the rites accomplished by you, which are प्रथमा (*prathamā*) (chief) and सत्या (*satyā*) (true in their fruit). Likewise, urged, follow the gods, Indra and the others. Likewise, urged, follow the पत्म (*patma*), the light called Āditya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजिनेन (*vājinena*)—by food-essence (O son)
- वाजी असि (*vājī asi*)—you are endowed with strength
- सुवेनीः (*suvenīḥ*)—you possess an attractive form
- सुवितः (*suvitaḥ*)—urged by that
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—towards the goal of your act of praise
- अनु गाः (*anu gāḥ*)—follow and go
- सुवितः (*suvitaḥ*)—stimulated from there
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—to heaven
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—go
- सुवितः (*suvitaḥ*)—urged there
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—excellent
- सत्या (*satyā*)—true in nature
- धर्म (*dharma*)—proceed according to the dharma performed by you
- सुवितः (*suvitaḥ*)—urged by that dharma
- देवान् (*devān*)—join the gods, Indra and others
- सुवितः (*suvitaḥ*)—urged from there too
- पत्त्म (*pattma*)—the light in the form of Āditya
- अनु (*anu*)—follow and go

### Printed p. 345

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O son, you are strong through food-essence and possess an attractive form. Urged by that, follow the goal of the praise you made before. Stimulated from there, go to heaven. Urged there, proceed according to the dharma, excellent and true in nature, practised by you. Urged by that dharma, join the gods, Indra and the others. Urged there too, join the light in the form of Āditya.

##### English translation
You are, Vajin, (strong) through food; you (are) well-beloved: urged
thereto follow (the object of your) praise : urged thereto proceed to heaven:
urged thereto pursue the duties that are the most important and sure of
reward : urged thereto follow the gods : urged thereto follow (the light),
descending (from heaven).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हि॒म्म ए॑षां पि॒तर॑श्च॒नेशि॑रे दे॒वा दे॒वेष्ट॑दधु॒रपि॒ क्रतुं॑ ।  
> सम॑विव्यचुरु॒त यान्यत्वि॑षु॒रैषां॑ त॒नूषु॒ नि वि॑विशुः॒ पुनः॑ ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महिम्नः । एषां । पितरः । चन । ईशिरे । देवाः । देवेषु । अदधुः । अपि । क्रतुं ।  
> सं । अविव्यचुः । उत । यानि । अत्विषुः । आ एषां । तनूषु । नि । विविशुः । पुनरिति ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पितरश्चनास्मत्पितरोऽप्यंगिरस एषां देवानां महिन्नो महत्त्वस्येशिरे ।
> ईश्वरा अभवन् । ते देवा अपि देवत्वं प्राप्ता अंगिरसो देवेष्ट्विंद्रादिषु क्रतुं
> संकल्पमदधुः । धृतवंतः । उतापि च यानि तेजांस्यतिषुर्दिप्यंते तानि समविव्यचुः । संगता आसन् । एषां देवानां तनूषु शरीरेषु नि विविशुः । निविशंति
> पितरोऽप्यंगिरसः । अतस्त्वमपि तथा कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पितरश्चन (*pitaraścana*): our fathers, the Angirasas, became lords of the greatness of these gods. Having attained godhood, the Angirasas placed their क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*), their resolve, in the gods, Indra and the others, that is, they held it there. And the radiances that shine, these they joined; they became united with them. They have entered the bodies of these gods; our fathers the Angirasas enter. Therefore you too should do likewise: this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पितरश्चन (*pitaraścana*)—our fathers, the Angirasas
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these gods
- महिम्नः (*mahimnaḥ*)—to the greatness

### Printed p. 346
- ईशिरे (*īśire*)—became lords
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—they, having attained godhood
- देवेषु अपि (*deveṣu api*)—among the gods too, Indra and the others
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—their resolve
- अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—bore (made their own resolve be fulfilled)
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यानि (*yāni*)—which radiances
- अत्विषुः (*atviṣuḥ*)—shine, those
- समविव्यचुः (*samavivyacuḥ*)—joined and became one with them
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these gods
- तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)—in the bodies
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- नि विविशुः (*ni viviśuḥ*)—have entered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Our fathers, the Angirasas, obtained a greatness exceeding even that of the gods and became lords over them all. Having attained godhood, they made their own resolve be fulfilled even among Indra and the other gods, and entered all the radiances. They entered again into the bodies of the gods.

##### English translation
Our progenitors (the Angirasas) were lords over the might of those
(divinities), they having become gods imposed their will upon the gods ;
they attained also (the radiances) which shone forth and they again entered
the bodies of those (gods).

> रजांस्युच्यंत इति निरुक्तं । पूर्वा पूर्वाणि धामानि स्थानान्यमितानैरमितानि
> मिमानाः परिच्छिंदंतः परिचक्रमुः । पर्यक्रामन् । किंच तथा कुर्वंतो विश्वा
> सर्वाणि भुवना भूतजातानि नियेमीरे । नियमितवंतः । किंच पुरुध पुरुधा बहु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

My fathers, by their own सहोभिः (*sahobhiḥ*) (powers), traversed the whole रजः (*rajaḥ*), the world; "worlds are called rajas" (Nirukta). Measuring, that is, delimiting, the ancient places that had not been measured, they traversed them. Doing so, they also restrained all beings. And they spread out, in many ways, the प्रजा (*prajā*) …

### Printed p. 347

> प्रकारं प्रजा अनु ज्योतींष्युदकानि वा प्रासारयंत । प्रसारितवंतः । अस्मत्पितरः
> पूर्वेंगिरसः स्वसामर्थ्येन सर्वं लोकं व्याप्य पुरातनानि ग्रहनक्षत्रादीनि परिच्छिद्य सर्वभूतानि नियम्य प्रजा अनूदकानि तेजांसि वा प्रसारितवंत इत्यर्थः ।
> आतस्त्वमस्येवं कुर्विति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

… that is, lights or waters, following the creatures. The meaning: our fathers, the ancient Angirasas, pervading the whole world by their own power, delimiting the ancient planets, stars and the rest, restraining all beings, spread out lights or waters in accordance with the creatures. The intent is: "therefore you too do likewise."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—my fathers, the Angirasas
- अमिता (*amitā*)—not measured by anyone before
- पूर्वा (*pūrvā*)—ancient
- धामानि (*dhāmāni*)—places
- सहोभिः (*sahobhiḥ*)—by their powers
- मिमानाः (*mimānāḥ*)—measuring
- विश्वं रजः (*viśvaṃ rajaḥ*)—all the worlds
- परि चक्रमुः (*pari cakramuḥ*)—traverse
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—beings
- तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)—according to their respective forms
- नि येमिरे (*ni yemire*)—restrain
- पुरुध (*purudha*)—in many ways
- प्रजाः (*prajāḥ*)—creatures
- अनु प्रासारयंत (*anu prāsārayaṃta*)—have divided and spread in the world

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Our fathers, the Angirasas, traverse all the worlds, measuring by their powers the ancient places not measured by anyone before. They restrain all beings according to their respective forms. They have divided the creatures in many ways and spread them in the world.

##### English translation
By their powers they traversed the whole world, measuring the ancient divisions (till then) unmeasured :  they restricted all existent beings to their proper forms ;  they distributed in many directions (light) among the people.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वां प्र॒जां पि॒तरः॒ पित्र्यं॒ सह॒ आव॑रेष्टदधु॒स्तंतु॒मात॑तं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूनव आदित्यस्य पुत्रा देवा अंगिरसः । देवानां ह्येतत्परमं जनित्रं
> यत्सूर्य इति प्रदर्शितत्वादादित्यस्य सूनव इति गम्यते । असुरं बलवंतं स्वर्विदं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*) are the sons of Āditya, the gods, the Angirasas. That this is so is understood from what is shown: देवानां ह्येतत्परमं जनित्रं यत्सूर्य इति (*devānāṃ hyetatparamaṃ janitraṃ yatsūrya iti*), that Āditya is their origin. असुरं (*asuraṃ*) is the powerful one; स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)

### Printed p. 348

> सर्वज्ञं स्वर्गस्य लंभकं वादित्यं तृतीयेन कर्मणा प्रजोत्पत्ताख्येन । ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्यः । तै. सं. ६-३-१०-५ । इति
> श्रुतेः प्रजोत्पादनस्य तृतीयकर्मत्वं । तेनादित्यं द्विधास्थापयंत । द्विप्रकारमास्थापयंति । उदितं चास्त्रमितं च कुर्वंति । उद्गाभं च निग्राभं च
> ब्रह्म देवा अनीवृधन् । तै. सं. १-१-१३-१ । इति मंत्रस्य ब्राह्मणेऽसौ
> वा आदित्य उद्यन्नुद्गाभ एष निम्मोचन्निग्राभः । तै. सं. ५-४-६-६ । इति
> श्रुतत्वाद्देवानामादित्यस्य द्विःस्थापनमुदयास्तमयकरणमिति गम्यते । किंच
> पितरो मदीया अंगिरसः स्वां प्रजां । उत्पाद्येति शेषः। पित्रं सहः पितुरादित्यस्य
> संबंधिनमपराभिभवक्षमं बलमवरेष्वादधुः । निकृष्टेपु स्वप्रजाभूतेषु मनुष्येषु स्थापितवंतः । यथा पित्रं धनं सम्यक् परिरक्ष्य स्वपुत्रेभ्यः प्रयच्छंति
> तद्वत्पितुरादित्यस्य प्रकाशादिबलं मनुष्येषु न्यदधुरित्यर्थः। किंच तंशुं प्रजामाततं
> विततं कृतवंत इति शेषः । पुत्रपौत्रादिरूपेणानवच्छिन्नां प्रजामित्यर्थः । अयं
> ह्यातततंतुर्यत्प्रजेति ब्राह्मणं । प्रजातंतुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः । तै. आ. ७-११-१ ।
> इति च । तंतुं तन्नन् । ऋ. १०.५३-६ । इत्यस्य ब्राह्मणं प्रजा वै तंतुः । ऐ. ब्रा.
> ३-३८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

… is the all-knowing one, or the obtainer of heaven: Āditya. By the तृतीयेन कर्मणा (*tṛtīyena karmaṇā*), the third act, called the begetting of offspring: ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्यः (*brahmacaryeṇarṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhyaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-5); by this śruti the begetting of offspring is the third act. By it they established Āditya in two ways; they make him risen and set. The mantra उद्गाभं च निग्राभं च ब्रह्म देवा अनीवृधन् (*udgābhaṃ ca nigrābhaṃ ca brahma devā anīvṛdhan*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-1-13-1) has the Brāhmaṇa असौ वा आदित्य उद्यन्नुद्ग्राभ एष निम्मोचन्निग्राभः (*asau vā āditya udyannudgrābha eṣa nimmocannigrābhaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-4-6-6). From this it is understood that the gods' double establishment of Āditya is the causing of rising and setting. Moreover, my fathers the Angirasas, having begotten their own offspring (this is the supplied remainder), placed the पित्रं सहः (*pitraṃ sahaḥ*), the strength of their father Āditya, able to overcome rivals, in the अवरेषु (*avareṣu*), the lowly, men who are their own offspring. As fathers carefully guard paternal wealth and give it to their own sons, so they placed the father Āditya's strength of light and the rest in men. Further, they made the तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*), the line of offspring, extended (this is the supplied remainder), that is, offspring uninterrupted as sons, grandsons and so on. The Brāhmaṇa says: अयं ह्यातततंतुर्यत्प्रजेति (*ayaṃ hyātatataṃturyatprajeti*); and प्रजातंतुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः (*prajātaṃtuṃ mā vyavacchetsīḥ*) (Tai. Ā. 7-11-1). For तंतुं तन्नन् (*taṃtuṃ tannan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.53-6) the Brāhmaṇa is प्रजा वै तंतुः (*prajā vai taṃtuḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 3-38).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*)—the Angirasas, sons of Āditya
- तृतीयेन कर्मणा (*tṛtīyena karmaṇā*)—by the third act, the begetting of offspring
- असुरं (*asuraṃ*)—the powerful one
- स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)—the support of heaven, Āditya
- द्विधा (*dvidhā*)—in two ways, rising and setting
- आ स्थापयंत (*ā sthāpayaṃta*)—have established
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—our fathers, the Angirasas
- स्वां प्रजां (*svāṃ prajāṃ*)—having begotten their own offspring
- अवरेषु (*avareṣu*)—among those lowly men too
- पित्र्यं सहः (*pitryaṃ sahaḥ*)—the strength of Āditya
- आ दधुः (*ā dadhuḥ*)—have placed
- तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*)—the line of offspring
- आ ततं (*ā tataṃ*)—have caused to grow extensively

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Angirasas, sons of Āditya, by their third act, the begetting of offspring, have established Āditya, the powerful one and the support of heaven, in two ways, rising and setting. Our fathers the Angirasas, having begotten their offspring, have placed Āditya's strength even in those lowly men. They have caused the line of offspring to grow extensively.

##### English translation
The sons (of Aditya, the Angirasas), established by the third act of duty, the mighty, all-wise (sun) in his two-fold (condition of rising and setting) : our progenitors (having begotten) their own progeny, deposited

### Printed p. 349
in the best (of them) the paternal strength, (making) an extended line (of
progeny).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On how the gods and the Angirasas became sons of Āditya, the commentator cites the Brāhmaṇa sentence देवानां हैतत्परमं जनित्रं यत्सूर्यः (*devānāṃ haitatparamaṃ janitraṃ yatsūryaḥ*). Since there is a śruti statement असौ ना आदित्यो बह्म (*asau nā ādityo bahma*), it is natural to say that the gods are sons of Āditya, who is of the nature of Brahman.

तृतीयेन कर्मणा (*tṛtīyena karmaṇā*)—It is customary to say that the begetting of offspring is the third act. How? जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस्त्रिभिर्यणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्यः (*jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhiryaṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇarṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhyaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-5). As the Taittirīya Saṃhitā says, a Brāhmaṇa is born already bearing three kinds of debts (loans, or duties). To discharge them, he must perform sacrifice and discharge the duty (debt) owed to the gods; he must study the Veda and discharge the debt to the ṛṣis; he must beget lawful offspring and discharge the debt to the fathers. Therefore, among the three duty-acts, sacrifice, Vedic study and begetting offspring, the begetting of offspring is said here to be the third act.

आ अस्थापयंत (*ā asthāpayaṃta*)—द्विधा द्रिप्रकारमास्थापयंति । उदितं चास्त्रमितं च कुर्वंति (*dvidhā driprakāramāsthāpayaṃti | uditaṃ cāstramitaṃ ca kurvaṃti*). That the gods established in two ways means that they fixed for the sun the two kinds of act, rising and setting. On this the commentator cites two śruti sentences: उद्ग्राभं च निग्राभं च ब्रह्म देवा अवीवृधन् (*udgrābhaṃ ca nigrābhaṃ ca brahma devā avīvṛdhan*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-1-13-1); असौ वा आदित्य उद्यन्नुद्ग्राभ एष निम्मोचन्निग्राभः (*asau vā āditya udyannudgrābha eṣa nimmocannigrābhaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5.4-6-6).

तंतुं आततं (*taṃtuṃ ātataṃ*)—Here तंतु (*taṃtu*) means the line of offspring. As a thread is unbroken and continuous, so the succession of sons, grandsons and so on is; hence the line of offspring is called a thread. The meaning is that they made this unbroken line of offspring extend, that is, grow.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ना॒वा न क्षोदः॑ प्र॒दिशः॑ पृथि॒व्याः स्व॒स्तिभि॒रति॑ दु॒र्गाणि॒ विश्वा॑ ।  
> स्वां प्र॒जां बृ॒हदु॑क्थो महि॒त्वाव॑रेष्टदधा॒दा परे॑षु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नावा । न । क्षोदः । प्रदिशः । पृथिव्याः । स्वस्तिभिः । अति । दुःगानि । विश्वा ।  
> स्वां । प्रजां । बृहत् उक्तः । महित्वा । आ । अवरेषु । अदधात् । आ । परेषु ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नावा नोदकोत्तरणसाधनेनेव क्षोद उदकं यथा मनुष्या नावोदकम.
> तितरंति यथा वा स्वस्तिभिः क्षेमैर्विश्वा सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि दुःखेन गंतव्यान्यतितरंति
> तद्वद्बृहदुक्थः स्वां प्रजां वाजिनं मृतं पुत्रं महित्वा स्वमहत्वेनावरेष्वाग्न्यादिष्टादधात् । कृतवान् । तदा परेषु दिव्येषु सूर्यादिष्ठादधात् । एवमृषिर्भूते
> स्वयमेव ना स्वात्मानं परोक्षेणाह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As men cross the water (क्षोद (*kṣoda*), that is, water) with a boat, the instrument for crossing water, or as they cross all difficult places, those to be traversed with pain, by means of blessings (स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*), that is, by well-being), so Bṛhaduktha, by his own greatness, placed his own offspring, the dead son, among the beings on this side, Agni and the rest. Then he placed him among the heavenly ones, Sūrya and the rest. In this way the seer speaks of himself indirectly. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- प्रदिशः (*pradiśaḥ*)—to go and reach the various quarters
- क्षोदः (*kṣodaḥ*)—the water met on the way
- नावा न (*nāvā na*)—as one crosses with a boat
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—by blessings
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- दुर्गाणि अति (*durgāṇi ati*)—as one crosses over sorrows
- बृहदुक्थः (*bṛhadukthaḥ*)—the seer named Bṛhaduktha
- स्वां प्रजां (*svāṃ prajāṃ*)—his own dead son
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by his greatness
- अवरेषु (*avareṣu*)—in the fires and other lights that are on earth
- आ दधात् (*ā dadhāt*)—has established
- परेषु आ (*pareṣu ā*)—has established also in the lights of the heavenly world, Āditya and the rest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As one crosses with a boat the water met on the way in going to the various quarters of the earth, and as one crosses all sorrows by means of blessings, so the seer Bṛhaduktha, by his greatness, has established his dead son in the lights of Agni and the rest that are on earth. He has established him also in the lights of Āditya and the rest that are in the heavenly world.

##### English translation
As men pass over the water to the several quarters of the earth in a ship ; (as they pass over) all difficulties by the blessings (of fortune), Brihaduktha by his might has committed his own offspring to those on this side, and to those on the other side.

**Introduction**
The seers of the four sūktas from the 57th to the 60th of this Maṇḍala are the brothers beginning with Bandhu, the sons of Gopāyana. They were the family priests of a king of the Ikṣvāku line named Asamāti.

### Printed p. 351

That king, misled by the bad counsel of some, dismissed the four brothers who were his priests, Bandhu, Subandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu, and appointed two men skilled in magical arts, Kilāta and Ākuli. Hence enmity arose between the former priests, Bandhu and the others, and the new priests, Kilāta and Ākuli, and it ended in the death of Subandhu, one of the four. The bhāṣyakāra has described this matter briefly in the introduction to this sūkta; we shall set it out further on. Now what Śaunaka has said on this matter in his Bṛhaddevatā is set out.

Verses 84–86 of the Bṛhaddevatā (Bṛ. De. 5-84, 85, 86), given in Sanskrit in the Kannada, begin: "Hear from me, who wish to tell the sūkta together with its story." The Kannada explains them as follows. There is an account (upākhyāna) concerning these sūktas (sūktas 57–60). Listen, I shall tell it. Among the kings of the Ikṣvāku line there was a king named Asamāti, son of Rathaproṣṭha. He removed from the priesthood four brothers beginning with Bandhu, his family priests, of the family of Atri, seers of the Ṛks in the dvipadā virāṭ metre (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-24). He judged two twice-born men, Kirāta and Ākuli, to be the best and the most skilled in priestly work, and appointed them his priests.

Verses 87–90 follow in Sanskrit. The Kannada explains them thus. These new priests, by their magical power and yogic power, took the form of pigeons and went to the sons of Gopāyana, Bandhu and the others. They caused the man named Subandhu to fall in a swoon.

### Printed p. 352

Then they took his life away and went to their own king, Asamāti. Seeing Subandhu fallen motionless on the ground, having given up his life, his brothers Bandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu recited, for the welfare of their dead brother Subandhu, the sūkta beginning मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10, sūkta 57), and, to bring his life back into the body, the sūkta beginning यत्ते यमं (*yatte yamaṃ*) (sūkta 58).

Verses 91–94 follow in Sanskrit. The Kannada explains them thus. Then, as a remedy for the dead man, the three Ṛks beginning प्रतार्यायुः (*pratāryāyuḥ*) (the first three Ṛks of sūkta 59) are to be recited in order to drive away Nirṛti, the deity of sin. In the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta, मो षु णः सोम (*mo ṣu ṇaḥ soma*), the first three pādas praise the deity Soma. The fourth pāda concerns Nirṛti. So this whole Ṛk praises Soma and Nirṛti. In the next two, that is, Ṛks 5 and 6, Asunīti is praised. But Yāska is of the opinion that in the last pāda of the 6th Ṛk the deity named Anumati is praised. In the 7th Ṛk the deities Bhūḥ, Dyauḥ, Soma, Pūṣan, Antarikṣa, Pathyā and Svasti are praised for the pacification of Subandhu. In Ṛks 8–10 Heaven and Earth are praised for pacification. In the first half of the last Ṛk, the tenth, beginning समिंद्रेरय (*samiṃdreraya*), Indra is praised.

Verses 95–97 follow in Sanskrit. The Kannada continues as follows.

### Printed p. 353

They praised Heaven and Earth for the destruction of the body's ill-health. Ill-health (रपः (*rapaḥ*)), or disease, is the mark of sin committed in the past. With the first four Ṛks of the next sūkta (the 60th) they praised the king (Asamāti), the ornament of the Ikṣvāku line. Then, for his well-being and increase, they prayed to Indra with the Ṛk beginning इंद्र क्षत्र (*iṃdra kṣatra*). Seeing himself praised in this way and Indra being prayed to for his welfare, King Asamāti was ashamed of the wrong he had done; he went to Bandhu and the others, the sons of Gopāyana, and stood silent with his head bowed in shame.

Verses 98–101 follow in Sanskrit (Bṛ. De. Adhyāya 7). The Kannada explains them thus. As Agni was praised before in the Atri Maṇḍala (Maṇḍala 5, sūkta 24), so now too they praised Agni with Ṛks in the dvipadā virāṭ metre. Agni, satisfied by this, spoke thus: "O Bandhu and the others, behold, the life of your brother Subandhu and that of the king of the Ikṣvāku line (Asamāti) is right within the circle of the sacrificial fire. Until now I myself have been guarding the lives of these two." Saying this, and saying "O Subandhu, live again," he gave his life back to him. Then Agni, greatly praised by the Gaupāyanas, that is, by Bandhu and the others, the sons of Gopāyana, went off to heaven, glad. Afterwards Bandhu and the others, with satisfied minds, called back the life (the self) of Subandhu with the 7th Ṛk of this sūkta, आयं माता (*āyaṃ mātā*). They showed Subandhu's body lying there motionless, prayed that it should enter it again, and for that purpose, that is, so that life might arise in the dead body, they recited the Ṛks of this sūkta to the end. Reciting the last (12th) Ṛk, आयं मे हस्ते भगवान् (*āyaṃ me haste bhagavān*), each of the three brothers separately touched Subandhu, now alive again, with his hands.

## Sūkta 57 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मा प्र गामेति पडृचं पंचदशं सूक्तं गायत्रं वैश्वदेवं । ऐक्ष्वाकोऽसमातिर्नाम राजा । तस्य बंधुः सुबंधुः श्रुतबंधुर्विप्रबंधुश्चति चत्वारः पुरोहिता आसन् । ते च गौपायनाः । स च राजा तांस्कृत्यान् मायाविनावृषी
> पुरोहितत्वेनावृणीत। ततो बंध्वादयः क्रुद्धाः संत इमं राजानमभिचरितवंतः।
> एतज्ञात्वा मायाविनौ पुरोहितावेषामन्यतमं सुबंधुं प्राणैर्वियो जितवंत् ।
> मृतस्यास्य भ्रातरो बंधुः श्रुतबंधुर्विप्रबंधुरित्येऽविनाशप्राप्ति हेतुभूतमिदं
> दृष्ट्वा जपंति स्म । अतस्तेऽस्य सूक्तस्यर्षयः । प्रतिपाद्यत्वादावर्तमानं मनो
> देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अथ हैक्ष्वाको राजासमातिर्गौपायनान्बंध्वादीन्पुरोहितांस्कृत्यान् मायाविनौ श्रेष्ठतमौ मत्वा पुरोदधे तमितरे क्रुद्धा
> अभिचेरुः अथ तौ मायाविनौ सुबंधोः पाणानाचिक्षिपतुरथ हास्य भ्रातरस्त्रयो
> मा प्र गामेति षट्कं गायत्रं स्वस्त्ययनं जप्तोति ॥ अग्नि समीपाद्देशांतरगमनसमय इदं सूक्तं जप्यं । सूत्रितं च । प्रव्रजेदनपेक्षमाणो मा प्र गामेति
> सूक्तं जपन् । अ. २-५ । इति ! महापितृयज्ञेऽप्येतदृत्विर्जप्यं । सूत्रितं च । मा
> प्र गामाग्नेत्वं न इति जपंतः । आ. २-१९ । इति ॥ निविदः स्थानातिपत्ताविदं सूक्तं शस्त्रा
> सूक्तांतरे निवित्प्रक्षेप्तव्या । सूत्रितं च । स्थानं चेन्निविदोऽतिहरेन्मा प्र गामेति
> पुरस्तात्तूक्तं शस्त्रा । अ. ६-६ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*) has six Ṛks, is in the Gāyatra metre, and is addressed to the Viśvedevas. There was a king of the Ikṣvāku line named Asamāti. He had four priests, Bandhu, Subandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu, Gopāyanas. The king set them aside and chose as priests two skilled in magic. Then Bandhu and the others, angered, performed abhicāra (hostile rites) against the king. Learning this, the two magician priests deprived Subandhu, one of them, of his life. His brothers Bandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu, seeing him dead, recited this sūkta. **NOTE** Therefore they are the seers of this sūkta, and the deity is the "returning mind" (*āvartamānaṃ manaḥ*), because it is what is spoken of. So says the Anukramaṇī, whose passage he quotes, ending with the three brothers reciting the six-Ṛk Gāyatra auspicious hymn मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*).

Ritual use: this sūkta is to be recited when one goes from the vicinity of the fire to another place; he cites the sūtra प्रव्रजेदनपेक्षमाणो (*pravrajedanapekṣamāṇo*) and following words, Ā. Sū. 2-5. **NOTE** At the Mahāpitṛyajña too the officiating priests recite it; he cites the sūtra ending जपंतः (*japaṃtaḥ*), 2-19. When the place of the nivid is overstepped, this sūkta is to be inserted in another sūkta of the śastra, as the sūtra स्थानं चेन्निविदोऽतिहरेन्मा (*sthānaṃ cennivido 'tiharenmā*) and following states, 6-6.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*), is the fifteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its deity is the Viśvedevas; its metre is Gāyatrī. Formerly, among the kings of the Ikṣvāku line there was a king named Asamāti. Four seers, sons of the seer named Gopāyana, Bandhu, Subandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu, were his priests. But the king set aside the four, Bandhu and the others, his family priests, and appointed two others, magicians (deceivers), as priests. Seeing this, the brothers Bandhu and the others were angered and did harm to the king by abhicāra (magic or sorcery). Learning this, those two seers, the royal priests, took the life of Subandhu, the second of the four brothers. Seeing that their brother Subandhu had died, the remaining three brothers recited this sūkta for the welfare of their dead brother. Therefore the three brothers Bandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu are the seers of this sūkta; and the Anukramaṇī says, in the passage beginning अथ हैक्ष्वाको (*atha haikṣvāko*) and running on

### Printed p. 355

to "having recited the Gāyatra auspicious hymn of six Ṛks, मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*)." The use is as follows. That a householder is to recite this sūkta when he leaves his Agnihotra and the like and goes to another place is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, the sūtra प्रव्रजेदनपेक्षमाणो (*pravrajedanapekṣamāṇo*) and following words (Ā. 2-5). That the officiating priests are to recite this sūkta also in the iṣṭi called Mahāpitṛyajña is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, the sūtra ending इति जपंतः (*iti japaṃtaḥ*) (Ā. 2-19). And when, in reciting the nivid sūkta, another sūkta has to be recited, this sūkta is to be recited in its place, that is, in exchange for it, and the nivid sūkta is to be inserted in the middle of the other sūkta, as the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra explains in the sūtra स्थानं चेन्निविदोऽतिहरेन्मा (*sthānaṃ cennivido 'tiharenmā*) and following words (Ā. 6-6).

Sūkta 57
Maṇḍala 10. Anuvāka 4. Sūkta 57.
Aṣṭaka 8. Adhyāya 1. Varga 19.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6.
Seers: Bandhu, Śrutabandhu and Viprabandhu, the Gaupāyanas.
Deity: Viśvedevas.
Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा प्र गा॑म प॒थो व॒यं मा य॒ज्ञा दिं॑द्र सो॒मिनः॑ ।  
> मांतःस्थु॑र्नो॒ अरा॑तयः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । प्र । गाम । पथः । वयं । मा । यज्ञात् । इंद्र । सोमिनः ॥  
> मा । अंतरिति । स्थुः । नः । अरातयः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रोक्ताख्याने शाट्यायनकं । असमातिं राथप्रौष्ठं गौपायना अभ्यगमंस्ते खांडवे सत्प्रमासताथ हाससातौ राथप्रौष्ठे किलाताकुली ऊषतुरसुरमाय् तं ह स्मानग्नौ निधायौदनं पचतोऽग्नौ मांसमथासुरान्नं दग्ध्वेक्ष्वाकवः पराबभूवुः । तमसमातिं राथप्रौष्ठं गौपायनानामाहुतयोऽभ्यतपन्
> सोऽब्रवीदिमौ किलाताकुली इमा वै मा गौपायनानामाहुतयोऽभितसंतीति
> तावब्रूतां तस्य वा आवामेव भिषजौ स्व आवां प्रायश्चित्तिरानां तथा करिष्यावो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the story told here, the Śāṭyāyanaka (Brāhmaṇa) says: the Gaupāyanas approached Asamāti, son of Rathaproṣṭha. They were in the Khāṇḍava, and two, Kilāta and Ākuli, lived with Rathaproṣṭha's son, using asura magic. Placing the cooked rice and the flesh in the fire, they burned the asura food, and the Ikṣvākus were overthrown. The oblations of the Gopāyanas tormented that Asamāti, son of Rathaproṣṭha. He said: "Kilāta and Ākuli, these oblations of the Gopāyanas are tormenting me." The two answered that they were his physicians, and that they would see to the expiation for it, and that they would do so. (The passage is cut off here.)

### Printed p. 356

> यथा नैता नाभितपंतीति । तौ परेत्य सुबंधोर्गौपायनस्य स्वपतः प्रमत्तस्यासुमाहुत्यांतःपरिधि न्यधत्तामित्यादि । तं सुबंधोरसुमादातुं खांडवादसमातिं
> प्रतिगच्छंतो गौपायना वदंति । हे इंद्र वयं गौपायनाः पथः समीचीनान्मार्गान्ना प्र गाम । मा परागच्छाम । असमातिगृहमेव गच्छाम । मा च सोमिनोऽसमातेर्यज्ञात्प्र गाम । मा स्थुर्मा तिष्ठंतु नोऽस्माकमंतर्मार्गमध्येऽरातयः
> शत्रवः । यद्वा । सोमिनः सोमवतो यागान्मा प्र गाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa quotes the end of the story: यथा नैता नाभितपंतीति । तौ परेत्य सुबंधोर्गौपायनस्य स्वपतः प्रमत्तस्यासुमाहुत्यांतःपरिधि न्यधत्तामित्यादि । (*yathā naitā nābhitapaṃtīti | tau paretya subaṃdhorgaupāyanasya svapataḥ pramattasyāsumāhutyāṃtaḥparidhi nyadhattāmityādi |*). The two priests went and placed the life-breath of Subandhu Gaupāyana, who was sleeping unguarded, inside the inner fire-boundary with an oblation. The Gopāyanas, going to Asamāti to take Subandhu's life back from him, say: "O Indra, we Gopāyanas shall not depart from the right paths. Let us not turn aside; let us go to Asamāti's house itself. Let us not depart from the sacrifice of Asamāti, the Soma-offerer. Let not our enemies stand in our way, in the middle of the road." Alternatively: "Let us not depart from the sacrifices of the Soma-possessor."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—from the good path
- मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*)—let us not go far away
- सोमिनः (*sominaḥ*)—of Asamāti, who offers Soma
- यज्ञात् मा (*yajñāt mā*)—let us not go away from the sacrifice
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle of the road
- अरातयः (*arātayaḥ*)—enemies
- मा स्थुः (*mā sthuḥ*)—let them not stand across (our way)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let us not go far away from the good path. Let us not go away from the sacrifice of King Asamāti, the offerer of Soma. Let no enemies stand across our way in the middle of the road.

##### English translation
Let us not depart, Indra, from the path; let us not (depart) from the sacrifice of the offerer of the libation; let not our adversaries remain (in our place).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the commentary on this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa has cited an anecdote from the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa.
असमातिं राथप्रौष्ठं गौपायना अभ्यगमंस्ते खांडवे सत्रमासताथ हासमात् राथप्रौष्ठे किलाताकुली ऊषतुरसुरमायौ तं ह स्मानग्नौ निधायोदनं पचतोऽग्नौ मांसमथासुरान्नं दग्धीक्ष्वाकवः पराबभूवुः । तमसमातिं राथप्रौष्ठं गौपायनानामाहुतयोऽभ्यतपन् सोऽब्रवीदिमौ किलाताकुली इमा वै मा गौपायनानामाहुतयोऽभितपंतीति तावब्रूतां तस्य ना आवामेव भिषजौ स्व आवां प्रायश्चित्तिरानां तथा करिष्यावो यथा नैता नाभितपंतीति । तौ परेत्य सुबंधोर्गौपायनस्य स्वपतः प्रमत्तस्यासुमाहुत्यांतःपरिधि न्यधत्तां । (*asamātiṃ rāthaprauṣṭhaṃ gaupāyanā abhyagamaṃste khāṃḍave satramāsatātha hāsamāt rāthaprauṣṭhe kilātākulī ūṣaturasuramāyau taṃ ha smānagnau nidhāyodanaṃ pacato 'gnau māṃsamathāsurānnaṃ dagdhīkṣvākavaḥ parābabhūvuḥ | tamasamātiṃ rāthaprauṣṭhaṃ gaupāyanānāmāhutayo 'bhyatapan so 'bravīdimau kilātākulī imā vai mā gaupāyanānāmāhutayo 'bhitapaṃtīti tāvabrūtāṃ tasya nā āvāmeva bhiṣajau sva āvāṃ prāyaścittirānāṃ tathā kariṣyāvo yathā naitā nābhitapaṃtīti | tau paretya subaṃdhorgaupāyanasya svapataḥ pramattasyāsumāhutyāṃtaḥparidhi nyadhattāṃ |*) and so on.
Once the sons of Gopāyana, Bandhu and the others, were performing a sattra sacrifice in the forest region called Khāṇḍava. Then they came to the king named Asamāti, son of Rathaproṣṭha. At that time

### Printed p. 357
the king had two priests, Kilāta and Ākulī. They were skilled in the abhicāra (hostile rites) and māyā (magic) practised by asuras. They had the king offer flesh and the food of the asuras in the fire. Because of this, the Ikṣvāku kings were defeated in battle. Displeased at this, the Gopāyana sons, Bandhu and the others, made offerings in the fire, and by that offering King Asamāti, son of Rathaproṣṭha, felt a heat in his body as if he were burning greatly. Distressed by it, Asamāti said to his new priests Kilāta and Ākulī: "These oblations offered in the fire by the Gopāyana sons are burning me." They answered: "Do not fear; we shall be your physicians. We shall perform a rite of expiation for this and remove the burning of your body." Having consoled him thus, they set out from there and came to the Gopāyana sons, Bandhu and the others. Then, by their power of magic they took away the life-breath of one named Subandhu, who was sleeping among them without being on guard, and brought it and placed it in the middle of the inner fire-boundary of the fire. Thus, beginning so, runs the anecdote. When going to King Asamāti's house to bring back the life-breath of the dead Subandhu, Bandhu and the others praised Indra with the Ṛks of this sūkta beginning मा प्र गाम (*mā pra gāma*).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो य॒ज्ञस्य॑ प्र॒साध॑न॒स्तंतु॑र्दे॒वेष्टात॑तः ।  
> तमाहु॑तं नशीमहि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । यज्ञस्य । प्रसाधनः । तंतुः । देवेषु । आततः ॥  
> तं। आहुतं । नशीमहि ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽयमग्नाख्यस्तंतुराहवनीयादिरूपेण विस्त्रतो यज्ञस्य प्रसाधनः
> प्रकर्षेण साधयिता दैन्वैः स्तोतृभिर्ऋत्विग्निर्विस्तारितो वर्तते वेद्यां तमाहुतं
> सर्वतो हूयमानं नशीमहि । प्राफ्नुयाम । नशतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni is the thread of the sacrifice, spread out in the form of the Āhavanīya and the other fires; he is the one who accomplishes the sacrifice. He is extended on the vedi by the priests, the praisers, among the gods. We would obtain him, who is offered oblations on all sides. The root नश (*naśa*) has the sense of pervading.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- तंतुः (*taṃtuḥ*)—who is like the thread of the sacrifice
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice
- प्रसाधनः (*prasādhanaḥ*)—who is like its ornament
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—by the priests
- आततः (*ātataḥ*)—who is brought to the sacrifice
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*)—Agni, who is worthy of invocation (to whom oblations are offered everywhere)
- नशीमहि (*naśīmahi*)—let us approach

### Printed p. 358

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us approach Agni, who is like the thread of the sacrifice, like its ornament, who is brought by the priests, and to whom oblations are offered everywhere.

##### English translation
May we obtain (the favour of) him to whom burnt offerings are presented, (Agni), who is the thread, the perfecter of sacrifice, drawn out (by the priests) to the gods.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मनो॒ न्वा हु॑वामहे नाराशं॒सेन॒ सोमे॑न ।  
> पि॒त्था॒णां च॒ मन्म॑भिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मनः । नु । आ । हुवामहे । नाराशंसेन । सोमेन ॥  
> पित्थाणां । च । मन्मभिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पिंडपितृयज्ञे मनो न्वा हुवामह इति तृचेन पिंडाभिमानिनः पितर उपस्थेयाः । सूत्रितं च । मनो न्वा हुवामह इति चतसृभिरथैनान्प्रवाहयेत् ।
> आ.२-७ । इति ॥
> वयं बंधुश्रुतबंध्वादयो मनः सुबंधोः संबंधि मायाविभिरपहृतं
> नु क्षिप्रमा हुवामहे । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । नाराशंसेन नराशंसचमसगतेन सोमेन । नरैः शस्यंत इति नराशंसाः पितरः । तेषां चमसानां कंपनमेव
> होमः । तथाविधेन सोमेन पितृणामंगिरसां मन्मभिर्मगनीयैः स्तोत्रैश्च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Piṇḍapitṛyajña, the Pitṛs who preside over the piṇḍas are to be approached with the triplet beginning मनो न्वा हुवामहे (*mano nvā huvāmahe*). It is laid down in the sūtra: मनो न्वा हुवामह इति चतसृभिरथैनान्प्रवाहयेत् (*mano nvā huvāmaha iti catasṛbhirathainānpravāhayet*) (Ā. 2-7). **NOTE**
We, Bandhu, Śrutabandhu and the others, quickly call back the mind of Subandhu, which has been carried off by the magicians. By what means is then told: with the Soma placed in the Narāśaṃsa cup. The Pitṛs are the Narāśaṃsas, "those praised by men"; the shaking of their cups is itself the oblation. We call with such Soma, and with the मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*) (praise-hymns worthy of thought) of the Pitṛs, the Aṅgirases. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नाराशंसेन (*nārāśaṃsena*)—offered from the cup dedicated to the Pitṛs
- सोमेन (*somena*)—with the Soma
- पितृणां (*pitṛṇāṃ*)—of the Aṅgirases
- मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*)—with the praises
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind of Subandhu
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- आ हुवामहे (*ā huvāmahe*)—we call

### Printed p. 359

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

With the Soma offered from the cup dedicated to the Pitṛs and with the praises of the Aṅgirases, we quickly call back Subandhu's mind.

##### English translation
We call upon the spirit (of Subandhu) with the Soma appropriated to the progenitors, with the praises of the pitris.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the iṣṭi called Piṇḍapitṛyajña, when the Pitṛ deities who preside over the piṇḍas are approached (prayed to), the three Ṛks (3-6) beginning मनो न्वा हुवामहे (*mano nvā huvāmahe*) are to be recited. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra मनो न्वा हुवामह इति च तिसृभिरथैनान्प्रवाहयेत् (*mano nvā huvāmaha iti ca tisṛbhirathainānpravāhayet*) (Ā. 2-7).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ त॑ एतु॒ मनः॒ पुनः॒ क्रत्वे॒ दक्षा॑य जी॒वसे॑ ।  
> ज्योक्च॒ सूर्यं॑दृ॒शे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । एतु । मनः । पुनरिति । क्रत्वे । दक्षाय । जीवसे ॥  
> ज्योक् । च । सूर्यं । दृशे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे संबंधो ते मनः पुनरैतु । अभिचरतः सकाशात्पुनरागच्छतु । किमर्थ.
> मिति उच्यते । क्रत्वे कर्मणे लौकिकवैदिकविषयाय दक्षाय बलाय च । यद्वा ।
> क्रत्वेऽपानाय दक्षाय प्राणाय । प्राणो वै दक्षोपानः क्रतुरिति हि श्रुतिः ।
> जीवसे जीवनाय च । ज्योश्च चिरकालं सूर्यं दृशे । सूर्यं द्रष्टुं । अत्यंतं
> चिरजीवनायेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Subandhu, let your mind come back again, return from the one who is working the hostile rite. For what? For क्रत्वे (*kratve*): for action, worldly and Vedic; and for दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*): for strength." Or else: क्रत्वे (*kratve*) for the apāna and दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*) for the prāṇa, for the Śruti says प्राणो वै दक्षोपानः क्रतुरिति (*prāṇo vai dakṣopānaḥ kraturiti*). जीवसे (*jīvase*): for living. ज्योक् (*jyok*): for a long time; सूर्यं दृशे (*sūryaṃ dṛśe*): to see the sun. The meaning is: for a very long life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Subandhu) क्रत्वे (*kratve*)—for performing good action
- दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*)—for the establishing of strength
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for living
- ज्योक् (*jyok*)—for a long time
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun

### Printed p. 360
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—for seeing
- ते (*te*)—your
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- आ एतु (*ā etu*)—let it come back from the hostile rite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Subandhu, for performing good action, for the establishing of strength, for living, and for seeing the sun for a long time, let your mind (life-breath) come back again from the magician.

##### English translation
May (your) spirit (of Subandhu) come back again to perform pious acts ; to exercise strength ; to live ; and long to see the sun.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुन॑र्नः पितरो॒ मनो॒ ददा॑तु॒ दैवो॒ जनः॑ ।  
> जी॒वं व्रातं॑ सचेमहि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनः । नः । पितरः । मनः । ददातु । दैव्यः । जनः ॥  
> जीवं । व्रातं । सचेमहि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं पितरः पितृभूता अंगिरसो जनः । तेषां संघ इत्यर्थः ।
> स्वच जीवं व्रातं प्राणादींद्रियसंघातं पुनर्ददातु । तथा दैव्यू जनः । जनशब्दः
> संघवचनः । देवानां संघोऽपि जीवं व्रातं च ददातु । वयं च तदुभयं
> सचेमहि । प्राप्नुयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

नः (*naḥ*) is "our"; पितरः (*pitaraḥ*) are the Aṅgirases who have become our fathers. जनः (*janaḥ*) means their host. Let them give back the living व्रातं (*vrātaṃ*), the aggregate of the senses beginning with the prāṇa. So also दैव्यः जनः (*daivyaḥ janaḥ*): the word जन (*jana*) denotes a host, so let the host of the gods too give the living व्रातं (*vrātaṃ*). And let us obtain both (सचेमहि (*sacemahi*): let us attain).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पितरः जनः (*pitaraḥ janaḥ*)—the Aṅgirases, our fathers
- न (*na*)—to us
- जीवं व्रातं मनः (*jīvaṃ vrātaṃ manaḥ*)—the aggregate of the vital breaths together with the senses and the rest
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—let them bestow
- दैव्यः (*daivyaḥ*)—let the host of the gods also grant it to us
- सचेमहि (*sacemahi*)—let us fully obtain and experience it

### Printed p. 361

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Aṅgirases, our fathers, bestow again on us the aggregate of the vital breaths together with the senses and the rest; may the host of the gods also grant it to us. May we fully experience it.

##### English translation
May our progenitors, may the host of the gods, restore (your) spirit; may we obtain (for you) the aggregate of the functions of life.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यं सो॑म व्र॒ते तव॒ मन॑स्त॒नूषु॒ बिभ्र॑तः ।  
> प्र॒जावं॑तः सचेमहि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वयं । सोम । व्रते । तव । मनः । तनूषु । बिभ्रतः ॥  
> प्रजावंतः । सचेमहि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम देव वयं बंध्वादयस्तव व्रते त्वदीये कर्मणि । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम । तव तनूषु तदीयेष्वंगेषु च मनो विभ्रतस्तात्पर्ययुक्तां बुद्धिं
> धारयंतः प्रजावंतः प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिर्युक्ताः सचेमहि । संगच्छेमहि ।
> जीवं व्रातं चेति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O god Soma, we, Bandhu and the others, in your व्रते (*vrate*), in your rite (व्रातं (*vrātaṃ*) is a name for action), and in your तनूषु (*tanūṣu*), your limbs, bearing a mind devoted to that, प्रजावंतः (*prajāvaṃtaḥ*), endowed with offspring (sons, grandsons and so on), let us be united." The remainder to be supplied is: जीवं व्रातं च (*jīvaṃ vrātaṃ ca*), "the living host".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O god Soma
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- तव व्रते (*tava vrate*)—in the rite of worshipping you
- तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)—in regard to you
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- बिभ्रतः (*bibhrataḥ*)—having placed
- प्रजावंतः (*prajāvaṃtaḥ*)—endowed with sons and others
- सचेमहि (*sacemahi*)—may we attain happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Soma, in the rite of worshipping you and in regard to you, meditating on you alone, may we attain the happiness of obtaining sons and others.

### Printed p. 362
English Translation of the previous sūkta's last Ṛk:

##### English translation
Soma, fixing our minds on your worship and its details, may we, blessed with progeny, obtain (the aggregate of the functions of life).

## Sūkta 58 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्ते यममिति द्वादशर्चं षोडशं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं । बंध्वादय
> ऋषयः सुबंधुदेहान्निर्गतस्येंद्रियवर्गसहितस्य मनसः पुनस्तस्मिन्प्रवेशनार्थमिदं सूक्तं दृष्ट्वाजपन् । अतस्तेऽस्यर्षयः । प्रतिपाद्यत्वादावर्तमानं मन एव
> देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । यत्त इति द्वादशर्चमानुष्टुभं मनआवर्तनं जेपुरिति ।
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning यत्ते यमं (*yatte yamaṃ*) has twelve Ṛks and is the sixteenth sūkta, in the Anuṣṭubh metre. Bandhu and the others are the seers: they saw and muttered this sūkta so that the mind, together with the group of sense-organs, which had departed from the body of Subandhu, might enter it again. Hence they are its seers. Because it is what the sūkta expounds, the mind that is being turned back (मन एव (*mana eva*)) is the deity. The Anukramaṇī says: यत्त इति द्वादशर्चमानुष्टुभं मनआवर्तनं जेपुरिति (*yatta iti dvādaśarcamānuṣṭubhaṃ manaāvartanaṃ jepuriti*). The viniyoga has already been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, यत्ते यमं (*yatte yamaṃ*), is the sixteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. Its seers are Bandhu and the others, sons of Gopāyana; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. In this sūkta Bandhu and the others pray that the mind (the self), together with the senses, which had gone out of the dead body of Subandhu, may come back and settle again in that dead body. Therefore Bandhu and the others are the seers of this sūkta. The mind (the vital breath) that is expounded in the sūkta is the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: यत्त इति द्वादशर्चमानुष्टुभं मन आवर्तनं जेपुः (*yatta iti dvādaśarcamānuṣṭubhaṃ mana āvartanaṃ jepuḥ*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Sūkta 58. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 58. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 1; Vargas 20, 21. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12.
Seer: Bandhu, Śrutabandhu, Viprabandhu, the Gaupāyanas.
Deity: Manaāvartanaṃ (the turning back of the mind).
Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्ते॑ य॒मं वै॑वस्व॒तं मनो॑ ज॒गाम॑ दूर॒कं ।  
> तत्त॒ आ व॑र्तयामसी॒ह क्षया॑य जी॒वसे॑ ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 363

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ते । यमं । वैवस्वतं । मनः । जगाम । दूरकं ।  
> तत् । ते । आ । वर्तयामसि । इह । क्षयाय । जीवसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुरुषस्य म्रियमाणस्य मनो नाम महद्भूतं बहुधा विशीर्णं भवति। तस्य
> पुनःसंभरणमत्तोच्यते । हे म्रियमाण पुरुष यत्ते तव मनो वैवस्वतं विवस्वतः पुत्रं यमं दूरकमत्यंतं दूरं यथा भवति तथा जगाम ते तव तन्नन आ
> वर्तयामसि । आवर्तयामः । किमर्थं । इह क्षयायेह लोके निवासाय
> जीवसे । चिरकालजीवनायेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In a dying man the great element called mind becomes scattered in many ways; its re-gathering is spoken of here. O dying man, that mind of yours which has gone to Yama, son of Vivasvat, to a very great distance—that of yours we turn back (आवर्तयामः (*āvartayāmaḥ*)). For what purpose? इह क्षयाय (*iha kṣayāya*): to dwell in this world; जीवसे (*jīvase*): for living long.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Subandhu, now on the point of death) यत् (*yat*)—if
- ते मनः (*te manaḥ*)—your consciousness
- वैवस्वतं (*vaivasvataṃ*)—of Vivasvat's son
- यमं (*yamaṃ*)—to Yama
- दूरकं (*dūrakaṃ*)—as if very far from us
- जगाम (*jagāma*)—has gone
- ते (*te*)—your
- तत् (*tat*)—that same mind
- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—to dwell
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—to live long
- आ वर्तयामसि (*ā vartayāmasi*)—we cause to come back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Subandhu, who are on the point of death: even if your mind (vital breath) has gone, as if very far from us, to Yama, son of Vivasvat, we cause that same mind of yours to return, to dwell in this world and to live a long time.

##### English translation
Although your spirit have gone far away to Yama, son of Vivaswat, we bring back that (spirit) of yours to dwell here, to live (long).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word मनः (*manaḥ*) in this Ṛk and in the following Ṛks means consciousness, vital breath or self. The words of Bandhu and the others, saying that they will try to bring back again the breath or self that was in the body of the dead Subandhu and has gone to Yama in the Yama-world, in a very distant region, are set forth in the Ṛks of this sūkta. For further explanation see the introduction to sūkta 57 and the commentator's explanation.

> यत्ते॒ दिवं॒ यत्पृ॑थि॒वीं मनो॑ ज॒गाम॑ दूर॒कं ।  
> तत्त॒ आ व॑र्तयामसी॒ह क्षया॑य जी॒वसे॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । ते । आ । वर्तयामसि । इह । क्षयाय । जीवसे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुबंधो यन्मनो दिवं जगाम यच्च पृथिवीं दूरकं । दूरकमिति
> क्रियाविशेषणं । तदिह निवासाय जीवनाय चावतर्यामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Subandhu, the mind that has gone to heaven and that has gone to earth, दूरकं (*dūrakaṃ*) (an adverb, qualifying the action)—that we turn back for dwelling here and for life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Subandhu) यत् (*yat*)—if
- ते मनः (*te manaḥ*)—your consciousness
- दूरकं (*dūrakaṃ*)—as if far from us
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—to the heavenly world
- जगाम (*jagāma*)—has gone
- यत् (*yat*)—if
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—to the earth (has gone)
- तत् ते (*tat te*)—that same consciousness of yours
- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—to dwell
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—to live long
- आ वर्तयामसि (*ā vartayāmasi*)—we cause to come back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Subandhu, whether your consciousness, as if far from us, has gone to the heavenly world or to the earth, we cause that same consciousness of yours to return here, to dwell in this world and to live a long time.

##### English translation
Although your spirit have gone far away to heaven, or to earth, we bring back that (spirit) of yours to dwell here, to live (long).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्ते॒ मरी॑चीः प्र॒वतो॒ मनो॑ ज॒गाम॑ दूर॒कं ।  
> तत्त॒ आ व॑र्तयामसी॒ह क्षया॑य जी॒वसे॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ते । मरीचीः । प्रवतः । मनः । जगाम । दूरकं ।  
> तत् । ते । आ । वर्तयामसि । इह । क्षयाय । जीवसे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुबंधो यत्ते मनः प्रवतः प्रगच्छंतीर्मरीचीर्दिप्तीर्जगाम तदिति
> गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Subandhu, the mind of yours that has gone to the मरीचीः (*marīcīḥ*), the shining rays, प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*), going forth—that we turn back; तदिति गतं (*taditi gataṃ*) (the rest as already explained).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते मनः (*te manaḥ*)—your consciousness
- दूरकं (*dūrakaṃ*)—as if far from us
- प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*)—ever moving
- मरीचीः (*marīcīḥ*)—to the world of rays (the sun)
- जगाम (*jagāma*)—has gone
- तत् ते (*tat te*)—that same consciousness of yours
- इह (*iha*)—here
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—to dwell
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—to live long
- आ वर्तयामासि (*ā vartayāmāsi*)—we cause to come back

## Sūkta 59 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र तारीति दशर्चं सप्तदशं सूक्तं बंध्वादीनां त्रयाणां गौपायनानामार्षं ।
> आदितः सप्त त्रिष्टुभः । अष्टमी पंचाष्टका पंक्तिः । नवमी षडष्टका महापंक्तिः ।
> दशमी पंक्त्युत्तरा । आद्य दशकावष्टकास्त्रयः । आनु. ९-११. । इत्युक्तलक्षणसद्भावात् ।
> एकाक्षराधिक्याद्भूरिग्विशेषेणेयं वेदितव्या सूक्तस्यादितश्चतस्रो देहात्मानिर्गम
> यित्र्या निर्ऋतेर्निवृत्यर्थं बंध्वादयोऽजपन् । मो षु णः सोमेति चतुर्थ्या
> मेव मृत्युनिवृत्यर्थं सोममस्तुवन् । अतश्चतसृणां निर्ऋतिर्देवता चतुर्थ्याः
> सोमश्च । असुनीते मन इति द्वाभ्यामसुनीतिनामीं देवीमस्तुवन् । आतस्तयोः
> सा देवता । पुनर्नो असुमित्यस्याः पृथिव्याद्या लिंगोक्ता देवताः । ततस्तिसृभिः
> शिष्टाभिः पंक्तिमहापंक्तिपंक्त्युत्तराभिर्द्यानापृथिव्याविति द्यावापृथिव्यौ देवते ।
> समिंद्रेत्यर्धर्चस्येंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्र तारीति दशर्चे चतस्रो
> निर्ऋत्यपनोदनार्थं जेपुश्चतुर्थ्यां सोमं चास्तुवन्मृत्यूरपगमायोत्तराभ्यां दैवीमसुनीतिं सप्तम्यां लिंगोक्तदेवताः शिष्टाभिः पंक्तिमहापंक्तिपंक्त्युत्तराभिर्द्यावापृथिव्यौ समिंद्रेतींद्रं चार्धर्चेनेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्र तारी (*pra tārī*) has ten Ṛks and is the seventeenth sūkta; its seer is the three Gaupāyanas, Bandhu and the others. The first seven Ṛks are Triṣṭubh; the eighth is a Paṅkti of five pādas of eight syllables; the ninth is a Mahāpaṅkti of six pādas of eight; the tenth is a Paṅkty-uttarā. He cites the definition आद्य दशकावष्टकास्त्रयः । आनु. ९-११. (*ādya daśakāvaṣṭakāstrayaḥ | ānu. 9-11.*) This Ṛk is to be known as a Bhurij variety through one syllable in excess. The first four Ṛks of the sūkta were muttered by Bandhu and the others to turn away Nirṛti, who drives the soul out of the body. With the fourth, मो षु णः सोम (*mo ṣu ṇaḥ soma*), they praised Soma to turn away death. So the deity of the four is Nirṛti, and of the fourth also Soma. With the two Ṛks असुनीते मन (*asunīte mana*) they praised the goddess named Asunīti; she is their deity. The deities of *punarno asuṃ* are Pṛthivī and others, as stated by the gender-indications. Of the remaining three, Paṅkti, Mahāpaṅkti and Paṅkty-uttarā, the deities are Heaven and Earth (द्यावापृथिव्यौ (*dyāvāpṛthivyau*)). The half-Ṛk समिंद्र (*samiṃdra*) has Indra as deity. He quotes the Anukramaṇī to the same effect: प्र तारीति दशर्चं सप्तदशं सूक्तं बंध्वादीनां त्रयाणां गौपायनानामार्षं । आदितः सप्त त्रिष्टुभः । अष्टमी पंचाष्टका पंक्तिः । नवमी षडष्टका महापंक्तिः । दशमी पंक्त्युत्तरा । आद्य दशकावष्टकास्त्रयः । आनु. ९-११. । इत्युक्तलक्षणसद्भावात् । एकाक्षराधिक्याद्भूरिग्विशेषेणेयं वेदितव्या सूक्तस्यादितश्चतस्रो देहात्मानिर्गम यित्र्या निर्ऋतेर्निवृत्यर्थं बंध्वादयोऽजपन् । मो षु णः सोमेति चतुर्थ्या मेव मृत्युनिवृत्यर्थं सोममस्तुवन् । अतश्चतसृणां निर्ऋतिर्देवता चतुर्थ्याः सोमश्च । असुनीते मन इति द्वाभ्यामसुनीतिनामीं देवीमस्तुवन् । आतस्तयोः सा देवता । पुनर्नो असुमित्यस्याः पृथिव्याद्या लिंगोक्ता देवताः । ततस्तिसृभिः शिष्टाभिः पंक्तिमहापंक्तिपंक्त्युत्तराभिर्द्यानापृथिव्याविति द्यावापृथिव्यौ देवते । समिंद्रेत्यर्धर्चस्येंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्र तारीति दशर्चे चतस्रो निर्ऋत्यपनोदनार्थं जेपुश्चतुर्थ्यां सोमं चास्तुवन्मृत्यूरपगमायोत्तराभ्यां दैवीमसुनीतिं सप्तम्यां लिंगोक्तदेवताः शिष्टाभिः पंक्तिमहापंक्तिपंक्त्युत्तराभिर्द्यावापृथिव्यौ समिंद्रेतींद्रं चार्धर्चेनेति ॥ (*pra tārīti daśarcaṃ saptadaśaṃ sūktaṃ baṃdhvādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ gaupāyanānāmārṣaṃ | āditaḥ sapta triṣṭubhaḥ | aṣṭamī paṃcāṣṭakā paṃktiḥ | navamī ṣaḍaṣṭakā mahāpaṃktiḥ |
