##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fifth anuvāka there are eight sūktas. Of these the first, इदमित्था (*idamitthā*), has twenty-seven ṛks; its seer is Nābhānediṣṭha, son of Manu, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. The six sūktas beginning with this are addressed to the Viśvedevas, as the Anukramaṇī says: इदमित्था सप्ताधिका नाभानेदिष्टो मानवो वैश्वदेवं तदिति (*idamitthā saptādhikā nābhānediṣṭo mānavo vaiśvadevaṃ taditi*). Use: on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭhya rite, in the Vaiśvadeva śastra, this sūkta is recited in place of उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), which would come by extension from the Abhiplava; it is also prescribed by the sūtra: उद्धृत्य चोत्तमं सूक्तं त्रीणेदमित्था रौद्रमिति (*uddhṛtya cottamaṃ sūktaṃ trīṇedamitthā raudramiti*) (Ā. Sū. 8-1). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (5-14) begins: नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं भ्रातरो निरभजंत्सोऽब्रवीदेत्य किं मह्यमभाक्तेत्येतमेव निष्कामवनवदितारमित्यब्रुवन्न (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ vai mānavaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vasaṃtaṃ bhrātaro nirabhajaṃtso 'bravīdetya kiṃ mahyamabhāktetyetameva niṣkāmavanavaditāramityabruvanna*) and so on. According to it, Nābhānediṣṭha, rejected by his brothers in the partition, came to his father and asked why no share had been fixed for him. The father said: what need of that share? The Aṅgirases, seated at a sattra for heaven, grow bewildered when they reach the sixth day; have them recite these two sūktas beginning इदमित्था (*idamitthā*); going to heaven they will give a thousand cows. Sent by his father, he went to the Aṅgirases, had them prepare a thousand cows, and made them recite the two sūktas on the sixth day. By the power of that recitation they carried the sacrifice to its end and, wishing to go to heaven, gave him the thousand cows. As he took them, a man in dark garments rose from the north and said: "Brahmin, do not take my share of the sacrificial remainder." He answered that the Aṅgirases had given it to him. The man said: ask your father to whom the share falls. Having gone to his father, he was told that it rightly belongs to Rudra, and so reported to the man that his father said it was his. Pleased at the truthful speech, the man gave the share to Nābhānediṣṭha himself. In the Adhvaryu Brāhmaṇa also, मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजत् स नाभानेदिष्टं (*manuḥ putrebhyo dāyaṃ vyabhajat sa nābhānediṣṭaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4), this matter is stated. All that is to be borne in mind here.

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

In the fifth anuvāka of the tenth Maṇḍala there are eight sūktas; of them this sūkta इदमित्था (*idamitthā*) is the first, with twenty-seven ṛks. Its seer is Nābhānediṣṭha, son of Manu; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The six sūktas from this one onward are addressed to the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇī says: *idamitthā saptādhikā nābhānediṣṭo

### Printed p. 407
mānavo vaiśvadevaṃ tat*. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (8-1), उद्धृत्य चोत्तमं सूक्तं त्रीणेदमित्था रौद्रमिति (*uddhṛtya cottamaṃ sūktaṃ trīṇedamitthā raudramiti*), explains that on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭha rite, in the Vaiśvadeva śastra mantra, this sūkta is to be recited in place of the Abhiplava-related sūkta उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*). Regarding this sūkta the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says: नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवं ब्रह्मचर्यं वसंतं भ्रातरो निरभजन्सोऽब्रवीदेत्य किं मह्यमभाक्तेत्यतमेव निष्ठावनववदितारमित्यब्रुवन् (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ vai mānavaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vasaṃtaṃ bhrātaro nirabhajanso 'bravīdetya kiṃ mahyamabhāktetyatameva niṣṭhāvanavavaditāramityabruvan*) (Ai. Brā. 5-14), and so on. The commentator has stated that same matter briefly here. Manu had a son named Nābhānediṣṭha, who was studying the Veda in his teacher's house as a celibate student. Meanwhile his elder brothers divided the property of their father Manu and shared it among themselves. When Nābhānediṣṭha returned after finishing his Vedic study and saw that his brothers had shared out even his portion, he asked them where his share was; they said, "Ask your father." He asked his father, who said: "O son, if your brothers have taken all the property, let them take it; do not worry. The Aṅgiras sages are now performing a sattra. They have performed it up to the sixth day and, not knowing what to do on that day, are in doubt. Go there and recite this sūkta इदमित्था (*idamitthā*). Their sacrifice will proceed, and they will give you a thousand cows and go to heaven." As his father said, Nābhānediṣṭha went to the Aṅgirases and recited this sūkta at their sacrifice. Their sacrifice was thereby completed and they gave him a thousand cows. As he was returning with those cows, a man in soiled garments met him on the way and said: "O Nābhānediṣṭha, these thousand cows you are now taking, the remainder of the sacrifice, are mine." Nābhānediṣṭha said, "How so? The Aṅgirases themselves gave me these cows in the sacrifice." The man said, "Then ask your father about this." So Nābhānediṣṭha came to his father, told what had happened, and asked to whom the cows should belong. His father Manu said: "O son, as that man said, it is right that these cows belong to that man, who is Rudra." Hearing this, Nābhānediṣṭha went to the man and said: "As you said, these cows must belong to you; my father has said so. You may take them." Pleased at hearing Nābhānediṣṭha speak the truth, the man gave those thousand cows back to Nābhānediṣṭha. This is the main purport of the account. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā too, by sentences such as मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजत्सनाभानेदिष्टं (*manuḥ putrebhyo dāyaṃ vyabhajatsanābhānediṣṭaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4), this matter is set out; one may see it there.

> क्राणा । यत् । अस्य । पितरा । मंहनेऽस्थाः । पर्षत् । पक्षे । अहन् । आ । सप्त ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Nābhānediṣṭha, of uplifted speech, गूर्तवचा (*gūrtavacā*), makes this hymn, ब्रह्म (*brahma*) = stotra, Rudra's, रौद्रं (*raudraṃ*) = composed by Rudra, in the manner now being done, इत्था (*itthā*); "makes" is to be supplied. Having fashioned it by his insight, क्रत्वा (*kratvā*) = प्रज्ञानेन (*prajñānena*), he makes it in the rite, शच्यामंतः (*śacyāmaṃtaḥ*), in the midst of the sattra, आजौ (*ājau*), in the assembly of the Aṅgirases. The hymn which his parents, क्राणा (*krāṇā*) = making the share, and the brothers, मंहनेष्ठा (*maṃhaneṣṭhā*) = engaged in giving the share, made the means of obtaining cows (the verb "made" is to be supplied). By it Nābhānediṣṭha, on the day to be matured, पक्षे अहन् (*pakṣe ahan*), that is the sixth day, since the Brāhmaṇa says (Ai. Brā. 5-14): "They are bewildered when they reach the sixth day; have them recite these two sūktas on the sixth day." सप्त होतृन् (*sapta hotṛn*): the seven priests, Hotṛ, Praśāstṛ, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the rest, he पर्षत् (*parṣat*) filled on every side; that is, by the two sūktas इदं (*idaṃ*) and इत्था (*itthā*) he brought the sacrifice to its end.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- क्राणा (*krāṇā*)—those engaged in making the partition
- अस्य पितरा (*asya pitarā*)—Nābhānediṣṭha's parents
- मंहनेष्ठाः (*maṃhaneṣṭhāḥ*)—his brothers, engaged in giving the shares
- यत् (*yat*)—which hymn they made the means of obtaining cows;

### Printed p. 409
- रौद्रं (*raudraṃ*)—praising Rudra
- इदं ब्रह्म (*idaṃ brahma*)—this hymn
- गूर्तवचाः (*gūrtavacāḥ*)—Nābhānediṣṭha of uplifted voice
- इत्था (*itthā*)—as will be told below
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by the power of his insight
- शच्यां अंतः (*śacyāṃ aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle of the rite
- आजौ (*ājau*)—among the Aṅgirases he fashioned it
- पक्ष्ये अहन् (*pakṣye ahan*)—(with the help of this mantra) on the sixth day, when the rite reaches completion
- सप्त होत्यन् (*sapta hotyan*)—the seven priests, Hotṛ and the rest
- आ पर्षत् (*ā parṣat*)—he made ready so that the sacrifice became complete

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Nābhānediṣṭha's parents, engaged in making the partition, and his brothers, engaged in giving the shares, made a certain hymn the means of obtaining cows. This hymn in praise of Rudra, Nābhānediṣṭha of uplifted voice, as will be told below, fashioned by the power of his insight in the midst of the rite among the Aṅgirases. With the help of this mantra, on the sixth day, when the rite reaches completion, he prepared the sacrifice to be made complete by the seven priests, Hotṛ and the rest.

##### English translation
The fierce-voiced (Nabhanedishtha repeated) through his intelligence this praise of Rudra, in the midst of the ceremony at the assembly (of the Angirasas), which (praise)his parents, making (the partition)and his brothers engaged in giving (the shares accomplished); he perfected the seven priests (therewith) on the day on which the rite was to be matured.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

स इत् (*sa it*): that man in dark garments, called Rudra, दानाय (*dānāya*) for giving wealth to those who praise him, and दभ्याय (*dabhyāya*) for the slaying of enemies, वन्सन् (*vansan*) favouring the praisers, सूदैः (*sūdaiḥ*) with the cooks, the destroyers (the sentence is cut off here).

> शस्त्रैश्चानो रक्षांसि च्यावयन् वेदिममिमित । परिमितवान् । यज्ञवास्त्वधिष्ठितवानित्यर्थः । तं कृष्णशवास्युत्तरत उपोत्थायाब्रवीन्मम वा इदं मम वै वास्तुहमितीति ब्राह्मणं । ऐ. ब्रा. ५-१४ । तदेवाह । तूर्वयाणस्तूर्णगमनो गूर्तवचस्तमोऽत्यंतमुद्यतवचा रुद्रः क्षोदो नोदकमिव । उदकं यथा घनः सिंचति
> तद्वद्रेतः स्वसामर्थ्यमितऊतीतोगमनवद्यथा भवति तथा सिंचत् । प्रेरितवानित्यर्थः।
> यद्वा । अनेनोत्तरार्धेनोत्तराभ्यां च प्रासंगिक्यश्विनोः स्तुतिः क्रियते । तूर्वयाणस्तूर्णगमनोऽतिशयेनोद्यतवचनो रुद्रः क्षोदो नोदकमिव रेतः
> उत्पादनसामर्थ्योपेतं रेत इतलूति सिंचत् । जनयामासाश्विन् । अन्यत्रेतऊतीत्यश्विनोरभिधानादन्यत्र तयो रुद्रपुत्रत्वसिद्धेश्छायमर्थो लभ्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses the second half of the verse. The one who dwells in the dark night, Rudra, drives away the Rākṣasas with weapons and has "measured out" (अमिमीत (*amimīta*)) the altar, that is, he has taken possession of the sacrificial site. A Brāhmaṇa is cited: the Kṛṣṇaśavāsī, standing up on the north side, said "This is mine, indeed this site is mine" (Ai. Brā. 5-14). Swift in going (तूर्वयाणः (*tūrvayāṇaḥ*)) and with most vehement speech (गूर्तवचस्तमः (*gūrtavacastamaḥ*)), Rudra sprinkled (सिंचत् (*siṃcat*)) his seed, his own power, in the way a cloud pours water. Here इतऊति (*itaūti*) means "as in going from here", that is, sent forth.
Alternatively, with this second half of the verse and the next verses an incidental praise of the Aśvins is made. Rudra, swift and most vehement in speech, sprinkled seed endowed with generative power like water, and begot the Aśvins. Because the Aśvins are named elsewhere in connection with इतऊति (*itaūti*), their being Rudra's sons is established, and so this meaning is obtained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स इत् (*sa it*)—that same Rudra
- *dhana dānāya*—for giving wealth to the worshippers
- दभ्याय (*dabhyāya*)—for the destruction of enemies
- वन्वन् (*vanvan*)—satisfying the worshippers
- सूदैः (*sūdaiḥ*)—with destructive weapons
- च्यवानः (*cyavānaḥ*)—striking down and driving off enemies
- वेदिं (*vediṃ*)—the sacrificial altar
- अमिमीत (*amimīta*)—has constructed
- तूर्वयाणः (*tūrvayāṇaḥ*)—swift in going
- गूर्तवचस्तमः (*gūrtavacastamaḥ*)—Rudra, who has the loudest voice
- क्षोदो न (*kṣodo na*)—as a cloud pours water
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—his creative power
- इतऊति (*itaūti*)—as if spreading it all around
- सिंचत् (*siṃcat*)—has sent forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same Rudra, with the purpose of bestowing wealth on his worshippers and making them content, has constructed the sacrificial altar, driving off the enemies with his enemy-destroying weapons. Swift in going and with the loudest voice, Rudra has sent forth his creative power so that it spreads all around, as a cloud pours water.

##### English translation
He (Rudra) bestowing on his worshippers the gift (of wealth) and the defeat (of their foes), casting down (the Rakshasas) with his weapons, has constructed the altar ; rapid in movement, most fierce in speech, and shedding the procreative fluid like water around.

> आ । यः । शर्याभिः । तुविनृम्मः । अस्य । अश्रीणीत । आदिशं । गभस्तौ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विन् युवां मनो न मन इव यथा मनस्तिग्मं तीक्ष्णमाशु
> धावति आगच्छति एवं येषु हवनेष्वाह्वानेषु विपः स्तोतुः शच्या प्रज्ञानेन गंतव्यमिति बुद्ध्या द्रवंता द्रवंतौ गच्छंतौ वनुथः संभजथः । योऽध्वर्युरा अभिमुख्येन तुविनृम्मः प्रभूतहनिर्लक्षणधनः सन्नस्य कर्मणि प्रवृत्तस्य मम संबंधी
> शर्याभिरंगुलीभिरश्रीणीत श्रीणाति । किं कृत्वा । गभस्तौ हस्ते धृत्वादिशं । इदमश्विभ्यामिति निर्दिश्येत्यर्थः । तादृशं मदीयमध्वर्युं येषु हवनेषु वनुथः
> संभजथः तौ युवां हुव इत्युत्तरत्र संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Aśvins, in whatever invocations, you go swiftly, like the mind, which runs and comes quickly, to the worshipper (विपः (*vipaḥ*)), running with the thought 'we must go' through his understanding (शच्या (*śacyā*)), and you favour him." The Adhvaryu, facing you, rich in abundant oblation, who belongs to me and is engaged in this rite, mixes (अश्रीणीत (*aśrīṇīta*)) the oblation with his fingers (शर्याभिः (*śaryābhiḥ*)). Having done what? Having taken it in the hand (गभस्तौ (*gabhastau*)) and indicated (आदिशं (*ādiśaṃ*)) "this is for the Aśvins". Such an Adhvaryu of mine you favour in those invocations; "I call you two" is connected with the following verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvins) यः (*yaḥ*)—the Adhvaryu who
- (येषु (*yeṣu*)—at whichever sacrificial times)
- गभस्तौ (*gabhastau*)—in his hand
- तुविनृम्मः (*tuvinṛmmaḥ*)—having abundant oblation
- आदिशं (*ādiśaṃ*)—intending you alone
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this rite, engaged
- शर्याभिः (*śaryābhiḥ*)—with the fingers
- अश्रीणीत (*aśrīṇīta*)—prepares the oblation
- (and) येषु हवनेषु (*yeṣu havaneṣu*)—at whichever times of invocation
- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—you
- मनो न (*mano na*)—like the speed of the mind
- तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)—quickly
- विपः (*vipaḥ*)—to the worshipper (praiser)
- शच्या (*śacyā*)—with your favouring intention
- द्रवंता (*dravaṃtā*)—running to him
- वनुथः (*vanuthaḥ*)—you satisfy the sacrificer (we call such you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, at whichever sacrificial times the Adhvaryu, holding the oblation fully in his hand, prepares it with fingers engaged in the rite, intending you alone, and at whichever sacrifices you come swiftly and with your favouring intention satisfy the sacrificer, to those sacrifices we call you.

##### English translation
(I call you to these) oblations, to which hastening, (Ashwins), swift as thought at the invitation of the worshipper, you rejoice my (worshipper),

who, affluent in the wealth of sacrifice, mixes (the oblation) with his fingers in your presence, (holding) in his hand the sacrifice intended (for you)

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वी॒तं मे॑ य॒ज्ञमा ग॑तं मे॒ अन्नं॑ नव॒न्वांसा॒ नेष॒मस्मै॑तध्रू ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो नपाता दीप्यमानस्य स्वर्गस्य प्रकाशात्मकस्य यागस्य वा न पातयितारौ हे
> अश्विनौ वां हुवे । आह्वये । नीतं कामयेथां मेऽन्नं हविर्लक्षणं । तदर्थं मे
> यज्ञमा गतं । आगच्छतं । इषमन्नं ववन्वांसा न संभजमानावश्वानिव । तद्वदा
> गतं । कीदृशौ युवां । अस्मृतध्रू । अस्मृतद्रोहौ मयि द्रोहमस्मरंतौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the dark night settles among the red cows, that is, Uṣas mounts her chariot to shine (the red cows being those of the dawns, Nirukta), at dawn-time, "O you two, sons of heaven", not causing the fall of the shining heaven or of the radiant sacrifice, "O Aśvins, I call you." You desire my food, the oblation; for that come to my sacrifice. Come like horses sharing food together. What are you like? अस्मृतध्रू (*asmṛtadhrū*): not remembering any offence, remembering no wrong done to me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवो नपाता (*divo napātā*)—you who are sons of the heavenly world
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvins
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- कृष्णा (*kṛṣṇā*)—the dark-coloured night
- अरुणेषु (*aruṇeṣu*)—among the golden-coloured
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—cows
- सीदत् (*sīdat*)—unites (when the night is over and the dawn appears)
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- हुवे (*huve*)—I call to the sacrifice
- अस्मृतध्रू (*asmṛtadhrū*)—you who do not wish us harm
- मे (*me*)—my
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—oblation
- वीतं (*vītaṃ*)—desire
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- ववन्वांसा न (*vavanvāṃsā na*)—you, united like two horses eating together
- मे यज्ञं (*me yajñaṃ*)—to my sacrifice
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities, sons of the heavenly world, when the dark night joins the dawn, that is, at the time of Uṣas's appearance, I call you to our sacrifice. You, who wish us no harm, desire our oblation. United like two horses eating a mouthful together, come to my sacrifice.

### Printed p. 413

##### English translation
When the dark night retires before the purple oxen (of the chariot of the dawn), I inyoke you, Ashwins, children of heaven : be desirous of my sacrifice : come to my food and to my viands like (two horses) eating together, oblivious of offence.

> नेतृभ्यो देवेभ्यो हितो रुद्रोऽपौहत् । अपोहति । तदेवाह । पुनन्तद्रेत
> आ वृहति । सर्वत उत्पिदति ! उद्गमयति पुरुषाकारेण स्वयमुत्पन्नः सन् । कीदृशं
> रेतः । यद्रेतः कनायाः कांताया दुहितुः स्वपुत्राः । तस्यामित्यर्थः । तत्र
> प्रजापतिनानुभृतमाः आसीत् ॥ अस्तेः सिपि— — ॥ कीदृशो रुद्रः । अनर्वान्यस्मिन्नप्रत्यृतः । प्रजापतिवै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यधायद्दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ये ।
> ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३३ । इति ब्राह्मणं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To show how the venerable Rudra, from a portion of himself, or Prajāpati, created Rudra the lord of the site, he speaks with this and the following two verses. Of the Prajāpati whose eager virile act (वीरकर्म (*vīrakarma*)), a change of gender, meaning seed, by which heroes come to be, such seed was spread out. That seed, deposited by Prajāpati for offspring, Rudra, benefactor of men (नर्यः (*naryaḥ*)), or of the leading gods, drew back (अपौहत् (*apauhat*)). Again he gathers that seed (आ वृहति (*ā vṛhati*)), draws it up from all sides, himself arising in the form of a man. What kind of seed? The seed which was placed in the beloved maiden, his own daughter, by Prajāpati. What kind of Rudra? Unopposed (अनर्वा (*anarvā*)), unassailed by any. The Brāhmaṇa is cited: "Prajāpati desired his own daughter, some say heaven, others say Uṣas" (Ai. Brā. 3-33).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Prajāpati
- *iṣṇat*—productive of offspring
- वीरकर्मं (*vīrakarmaṃ*)—the seed
- प्रथिष्ट (*prathiṣṭa*)—was in the course of growing and spreading; that
- अनुष्ठितं (*anuṣṭhitaṃ*)—seed applied for the sake of progeny

### Printed p. 414
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—Rudra, beneficial to men
- अपौहत् (*apauhat*)—held back
- यत् (*yat*)—which seed
- कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)—in the maiden-formed
- दुहितुः (*duhituḥ*)—daughter (of Prajāpati)
- अनर्वा (*anarvā*)—the unopposed Rudra
- अनुभृतं अः (*anubhṛtaṃ aḥ*)—deposited
- तत् रेतः (*tat retaḥ*)—that same seed
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- आ वृहति (*ā vṛhati*)—he makes it productive of creation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Rudra, beneficial to men, held back that seed of Prajāpati, productive of offspring, which was in the course of growing and spreading, applied for the sake of progeny. The seed which the unopposed Rudra deposited in the maiden daughter of Prajāpati, that same seed he again makes productive of creation.

##### English translation
(Rudra), the benefactor of man, whose eager virile energy was developed, drew it back when disseminated (for the generation of offspring); again the irresistiblec (Rudra) concentrates (the energy) which was communicated to his maiden daughter.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this verse and the next two verses it is said that Prajāpati desired union with his daughter Uṣas and that Rudra prevented it; the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa has an account of this. We give it here, as set out in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 13-33, 34), just as it stands there.
प्रजाप्रतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद्धिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ये तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं भूतामभ्यैत्तं देवा अपश्यन्नकृतं वै प्रजापतिः करोतीति ते तम्मैच्छन्य एनमारिष्यत्येतमन्योन्यस्मिन्नाविंदंस्तेषां या एव घोरतमास्तन्व आसंस्ता एकधा समभरंस्ताः संभृता एष देवोऽभवत्तदस्यैतद्भूतवन्नाम भवति वै स योऽसैतदेवं नाम वेद ॥ (*prajāpratirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyaddhivamityanya āhuruṣasamityanye tāmṛśyo bhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāmabhyaittaṃ devā apaśyannakṛtaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ karotīti te tammaicchanya enamāriṣyatyetamanyonyasminnāviṃdaṃsteṣāṃ yā eva ghoratamāstanva āsaṃstā ekadhā samabharaṃstāḥ saṃbhṛtā eṣa devo 'bhavattadasyaitadbhūtavannāma bhavati vai sa yo 'saitadevaṃ nāma veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-23)
Once, in the past, Prajāpati, seeing his own daughter, became infatuated as one is infatuated with a wife, and kept thinking of her form. As to who that daughter of Prajāpati was, there is a difference of opinion even among the great seers: some say she was the deity of the heavenly world, others that she was the deity Uṣas. However that may be, Prajāpati then took the form of a kind of deer (animal) called Ṛśya. His daughter took the form of a red deer called Rohita. (Here the commentators explain the words रोहितं प्राप्ता (*rohitaṃ prāptā*) as "she became fertile".)

### Printed p. 415
Prajāpati approached his daughter in the Rohita form and became intent on copulation. Seeing Prajāpati thus enamoured of his own daughter and bent on union, the gods said to one another: "This Prajāpati is engaged in a forbidden act that no one has ever done. Who is the man able to prevent this act?" They searched everywhere. However much they searched, no man able to restrain Prajāpati was found. The gods asked one another in turn, "If you have the power, slay Prajāpati", but none of them appeared to have that capacity. Then all the gods together gathered their fierce forms (it is well known that gods can take any form they wish; therefore it is said here that, leaving their gentle forms, they gathered fierce ones) and created one man of most terrible form. This man received the name Rudra. Therefore the names Bhūtavān and Bhūtapati are well known in the world for Rudra. Hence the man who has acquired this state of being Bhūtavat, of Rudra, becomes Bhūtimān (prosperous).
तं देवा अब्रुवन्नयं वै प्रजापतिरकृतमकरिमं विध्येति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्स वै वो वरं वृणा इति वृणीष्टेति स एनमेव वरमवृणीत पशूनामाधिपत्यं तदस्यैतत्पशुमन्नाम पशुमान्भवति योऽस्यैतदेवं नाम वेद ॥ (*taṃ devā abruvannayaṃ vai prajāpatirakṛtamakarimaṃ vidhyeti sa tathetyabravītsa vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣṭeti sa enameva varamavṛṇīta paśūnāmādhipatyaṃ tadasyaitatpaśumannāma paśumānbhavati yo 'syaitadevaṃ nāma veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-22)
Then the gods addressed that man (Rudra): "O Rudra, Prajāpati has committed a forbidden act; so, to punish him, strike him with this arrow." Rudra agreed, "So be it", but asked as a boon that he be lord over all animals. The gods gave him the boon accordingly. Therefore Rudra became famous by the name Paśupati. The man who knows this obtains wealth in cattle.
तमभ्यायत्याविध्यत्स विद्ध ऊर्ध्व उदप्रपतत्तमेतं मृग इत्याचक्षते य उ एव मृगव्याधः स उ एव स या रोहित्सा रोहिणी यो एवेषुस्त्रिकांडा सो एवेषुस्त्रिकांडा ॥ (*tamabhyāyatyāvidhyatsa viddha ūrdhva udaprapatattametaṃ mṛga ityācakṣate ya u eva mṛgavyādhaḥ sa u eva sa yā rohitsā rohiṇī yo eveṣustrikāṃḍā so eveṣustrikāṃḍā ‖*)
Then Rudra came forward, strung his bow, fitted the arrow, drew it back, aimed at Prajāpati and shot. The arrow struck Prajāpati, who was in the form of Ṛśya, and he leapt upward into the sky. People all see Prajāpati leaping upward in the sky and call it the constellation called Mṛga (Stars in the Orion).

### Printed p. 416

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That is, they say it is the Mṛgaśīrṣa asterism that lies between the asterisms Rohiṇī and Ārdrā. The idea is that Prajāpati exists in the form of an asterism. Rudra, who struck Prajāpati (who was in the form of a deer) with an arrow, appears in the sky under the name Mṛgavyādha. The daughter of Prajāpati, who was in the form of a red deer called Rohita (a doe), appears in the sky as the asterism Rohiṇī. The arrow shot by Rudra came to have three parts: kāṇḍa (the long shaft of the arrow), śalya (the barb) and tip (the sharp point). Therefore the arrow even now has three parts.

तद्वा इदं प्रजापते रेतः सिक्तमधावत्तत्सरोऽभवत्ते देवा अब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो दुषदिति यदब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो दुषदिति तन्मादुषमभवत्तन्मादुषस्य मादुषत्वं माडुषं ह वै नामैतद्यन्मानुषं सन्मानुषमित्याचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः ॥ (*tadvā idaṃ prajāpate retaḥ siktamadhāvattatsaro 'bhavatte devā abruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto duṣaditi yadabruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto duṣaditi tanmāduṣamabhavattanmāduṣasya māduṣatvaṃ māḍuṣaṃ ha vai nāmaitadyanmānuṣaṃ sanmānuṣamityācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-22)

Now, since the semen (virility) of Prajāpati, who was in the form of a deer, was abundant, a part of it was shed in his daughter, the doe, and the remainder fell on the earth, began to flow like a river in the form of a stream, collected in a low-lying place and became a great lake. Seeing it, the gods wished that people should not think Prajāpati's virility untouchable (not to be touched), nor मादुषत् (*māduṣat*) bad. Because the gods called it मादुषत् (*māduṣat*), the lake, which was the semen of the faultless Prajāpati, came to be named मादुषत् (*māduṣat*). People read the word मादुष (*māduṣa*) with the letter na in place of its da, and so call Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and other people मानुष (*mānuṣa*). Rightly considered, the meaning of the word मानुष (*mānuṣa*) (मादुष (*māduṣa*)) is "being free from fault". That being so, instead of referring to their bodies by the word मानुष (*mānuṣa*) of ordinary meaning, people refer to them by the word of indirect meaning (that is, of the excellent meaning मादुष (*māduṣa*)). Therefore men who are worthy and worshipful like the gods are, in worldly usage, fond of the indirect (satisfied with words of hidden meaning, not of a directly apparent meaning). For example, instead of the ordinary names Devadatta and so on given them by their parents, they are satisfied with names of apt meaning that make their fame shine, such as Upādhyāya, Ācārya, Svāmī. The gods too do not appear directly but accept praise and the like while remaining unseen; therefore they say the gods are fond of the indirect. Hence, to show indirectness, they put na in place of da in the word मादुष (*māduṣa*) and use मानुष (*mānuṣa*).

तदग्निना पर्यादधुस्तन्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्न प्राच्यावयत्तदग्निना वैश्वानरेण पर्यादधुस्तन्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्वैश्वानरः प्राच्यावयत्तस्य यद्रेतसः प्रथममुददीप्यत तदसावादित्योऽभवद्यद्ध्वितीयमासीत्तद्भृ (*tadagninā paryādadhustanmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirna prācyāvayattadagninā vaiśvānareṇa paryādadhustanmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirvaiśvānaraḥ prācyāvayattasya yadretasaḥ prathamamudadīpyata tadasāvādityo 'bhavadyaddhvitīyamāsīttadbhṛ*)

### Printed p. 417
गुरभवत्तं वरुणो न्यगृह्णीत तस्मात्स भृगुर्वारुणिरथ यत्तृतीयमदीदेविव त आदित्या अभवन्येऽज्जारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गरसोऽभवन्यदंगाराः पुनरवशांता उददीप्यंत तद्बृहस्पतिरभवत् ॥ (*gurabhavattaṃ varuṇo nyagṛhṇīta tasmātsa bhṛgurvāruṇiratha yattṛtīyamadīdeviva ta ādityā abhavanye 'jjārā āsaṃste 'ṅgaraso 'bhavanyadaṃgārāḥ punaravaśāṃtā udadīpyaṃta tadbṛhaspatirabhavat ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-24)

Then, after the gods had made Prajāpati's semen faultless, they thought that this semen, which was in liquid form in the shape of the lake, should be made free of liquid; so they lit fire all round that lake and began to heat it. While the fire blazed all round the lake, the wind churned the semen into turmoil in order to dry up the liquid mixed in it. Even so, because the liquid portion in the semen was very great, the fire with its heat was unable to remove it and turn it into a lump (a solid substance, a hard material). Therefore the gods tried to accomplish this task, which the fire could not accomplish, through the particular form of fire named Vaiśvānara. This Vaiśvānara fire enters the bellies of all creatures in the form of the digestive fire and is engaged in digesting food and drink.

अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधं ॥ (*ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ | prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidhaṃ ‖*)

The Lord himself has said: "I, dwelling in the bodies of creatures in the form of the Vaiśvānara fire, joined with the vital airs prāṇa and apāna, digest the four kinds of food that creatures eat." Therefore the gods, knowing that the power of the Vaiśvānara fire is exceptional, set the Vaiśvānara fire all round the lake to dry up (desiccate) Prajāpati's semen. The wind too, as before, entered the lake, churned it into turmoil and began to dry it. Thus, with the help of the wind, the Vaiśvānara fire separated Prajāpati's semen from its liquid state and turned it into a solid substance in lumps. In this way the semen was transformed into many lumps (globes) and began to shine, blazing. Of these, the first lump, the mass of brilliance, became the Āditya seen in heaven (in the sky). The second lump became the sage Bhṛgu. Varuṇa accepted this Bhṛgu as his son; therefore the sage Bhṛgu came to be called भृगुर्वारुणिः (*bhṛgurvāruṇiḥ*), the sage Bhṛgu the son of Varuṇa. Because he is the son of Varuṇa he is also called Vāruṇi. With this in mind the students of the Taittirīya branch recite: भृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार ॥ (*bhṛgurvai vāruṇiḥ | varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra ‖*) (Tai. U. 3-1). Then the third lump, shining exceedingly, became famous under the name Ādityas, as sons of Aditi. Āditya means the sun within the disc. Here it should be understood that the word आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*) indicates the other gods, sons of Aditi. Then some further lumps burned well (were consumed) and became embers.

### Printed p. 418
From those embers the sages called Aṅgiras were produced; and from the embers that were still burning and had not gone out, that is, that again and again began to blaze brightly, Bṛhaspati was produced.

यानि परीक्षाणान्यासंस्ते कृष्णाः पशवोऽभवन्या लोहिनी मृत्तिका ते रोहिता अथ यद्भस्मासीत्तत्परुष्यं व्यसर्पद्गौरो गवय ऋश्य उष्टो गर्दभ इति ये चैतेरुणाः पशवस्ते च । (*yāni parīkṣāṇānyāsaṃste kṛṣṇāḥ paśavo 'bhavanyā lohinī mṛttikā te rohitā atha yadbhasmāsīttatparuṣyaṃ vyasarpadgauro gavaya ṛśya uṣṭo gardabha iti ye caiteruṇāḥ paśavaste ca |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-34)

Then, when the embers had gone out and become aṅgāra (charcoal), they became black animals. After the fire had burned, the red clay (earth) that lay at the bottom became red animals. From the ashes (bhasma) arose the paruṣya animals, that is, the forest beasts gaur, gavaya and ṛśya, and also the camel and the donkey; and so on. From this legend the origin of the sages Aṅgiras, their relation to Agni, and the reason why Agni got the name Aṅgiras are all explained.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒ध्या यत्कर्त्व॒मभ॑वद॒भीके॒ कामं॑ कृण्वा॒ने पि॒तरि॑ युव॒त्यां ।  
> म॒ना॒नग्रेतो॑ जहतुर्वि॒यंता॒ सान्॒ निषि॑क्तं सुकृ॒तस्य॒  ॑
> योन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मध्या । यत् । कर्त्वं । अभवत् । अभीके । कामं । कृण्वाने । पितरि । युवत्यां ।  
> मनानक् । रेतः । जहतुः । वियंता । सानौ । निसिक्तं । सुकृतस्य । योन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कामं यथेच्छं कृष्णाने कुर्वाणे पितरि प्रजापतौ युवत्यां दुहितर्युषसि दिवि वा । दिवमित्यन्य इति हि ब्राह्मणं प्रदर्शितं । मध्या तयोर्मध्येऽंतरिक्षमध्ये नाभीके समीपे यत्कर्त्वं कर्माभवत् मिथुनीभावाख्यं तदानीं मनानगनल्पं रेतो जहतुः । त्यक्तवंतौ । किं कुर्वाणाविति तत्राह । वियंतौ परस्परमभिगच्छंतौ । प्रजापतिना सानौ समुच्च्रिते स्थाने सुकृतस्य यज्ञस्य योन्नि निषिक्तमासीदित्यर्थः । ततो रुद्र उत्पन्न इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

कामं (*kāmaṃ*) means "at will": while the father, Prajāpati, acts at will with his young daughter, Uṣas or Heaven. He notes that the Brāhmaṇa has shown "the other (reading) is Heaven". मध्या (*madhyā*): in the middle of those two, in mid-air, in the neighbourhood, the act that took place, namely the union, then the two let go मनानक् (*manānak*), which he glosses "not little" (*analpaṃ*), semen. What were they doing? He says: वियंतौ (*viyaṃtau*), going toward each other. The semen was poured by Prajāpati on a सानौ (*sānau*), a raised place, in the womb (योन्नि (*yonni*)) of the sacrifice (सुकृतस्य (*sukṛtasya*)). Thence Rudra arose. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—independently
- कृष्णाने (*kṛṣṇāne*)—who was acting
- पितरि (*pitari*)—the father, Prajāpati
- युवत्यां (*yuvatyāṃ*)—the daughter, Uṣas
- मध्या (*madhyā*)—in the middle of the sky
- अभीकॆ (*abhīkè*)—nearby

### Printed p. 419
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- कर्त्वं (*kartvaṃ*)—the act of uniting together
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—when they performed it, then
- वियंता (*viyaṃtā*)—those two who had come together
- मनानक् (*manānak*)—to a small extent
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—semen
- जहतुः (*jahatuḥ*)—loosened and let go
- सानौ (*sānau*)—in the elevated place
- सुकृतस्य (*sukṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- योन्सौ (*yonsau*)—in the middle
- निषिक्तं (*niṣiktaṃ*)—was poured (the semen)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the father, Prajāpati, who acted independently, and the daughter, Uṣas, came together in the middle of the sky, they let go a little of the semen. That semen was poured in the middle of the sacrifice that stands in an elevated place.

##### English translation
When the deed was done in mid-heaven in the proximity of the father working his will, and the daughter coming together, they let the seed fall slightly ; it was poured upon the high place of sacrifice.

> षिंचत् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पिता प्रजापतिर्यद्यदा स्वां दुहितरं दिवमुषसं वाधिष्कन् अध्यस्कंदत्
> तदासीमेव क्षया पृथिव्या सह संजग्मानः संगच्छमानः प्रजापतिरस्मिल्लोके
> रोहितो भूत्वा रेतो नि षिंचत् । निषेकमकरोत् । तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं
> भूतामभ्यैदिति ब्राह्मणं । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३३ । तदानीं स्वाध्यः सुध्यानाः सुकर्माणो
> ना देवा ब्रह्माजनयन् । उदपादयन् । किं तद्ब्रह्मेति तदाह । वास्तोष्पतिं

### Printed p. 420

> यज्ञवास्तुस्वामिनं व्रतपां व्रतस्य कर्मणो रक्षःप्रभृतिभ्यः पालकं निरतक्षन् ।
> समुदपादयन् । यज्ञवास्तु स्वामित्वं दत्त्वा कर्मरक्षकत्वेन निर्मितवंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the father Prajāpati sprang upon (*adhiṣkan*, he glosses अध्यस्कंदत् (*adhyaskaṃdat*)) his own daughter, Heaven or Uṣas, then, uniting with क्षया (*kṣayā*), the earth, Prajāpati, having become Rohita (the red stag) in this world, poured out the semen, that is, made the pouring. The Brāhmaṇa says: becoming a doe (ऋश्य (*ṛśya*)) she approached him who had become Rohita (Ai. Brā. 3-33). At that time the स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*), the gods of good thought and good works, brought forth ब्रह्म (*brahma*). What is that ब्रह्म (*brahma*)? He answers: वास्तोष्पतिं (*vāstoṣpatiṃ*), the lord of the sacrificial site, व्रतपां (*vratapāṃ*), the protector of the rite (व्रत (*vrata*)) against rākṣasas and the like. निरतक्षन् (*niratakṣan*) means they produced (him): having given him lordship of the sacrificial site, they fashioned him as the guardian of the rite.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पिता (*pitā*)—the father, Prajāpati
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- स्वां दुहितरं (*svāṃ duhitaraṃ*)—with his own daughter, Uṣas
- अधिष्ठन् (*adhiṣṭhan*)—when he united and had intercourse, then
- क्ष्मया (*kṣmayā*)—with the earth
- संजग्मानः (*saṃjagmānaḥ*)—having united with (in this world)
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—semen
- नि षिंचत् (*ni ṣiṃcat*)—poured out
- (then) स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*)—the doers of excellent works
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—Brahmā
- अजनयन् (*ajanayan*)—produced
- वास्तोष्पतिं (*vāstoṣpatiṃ*)—lord of the sacrifice
- व्रतपां (*vratapāṃ*)—protector of the rite, that is Brahmā
- (Vāstoṣpati) निरतक्षन् (*niratakṣan*)—they produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the father Prajāpati united with his daughter Uṣas and had intercourse, he, joined with the earth, poured out the semen in this world. Then the gods, the doers of excellent works, produced Brahmā. They produced Brahmā (Vāstoṣpati), the lord of the sacrifice and protector of the rite.

##### English translation
When the father united with the daughter, then associating with the earth, he sprinkled it with the effusion : then the thoughtful gods begot Brahma : they fabricated the lord of the hearth (of sacrifice); the defender of sacred rites.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स ईं॒ वृषा॒ न फेन॑मस्यदा॒जौ स्मदा परै॒दप॑ द॒भ्रचे॑ताः ।  
> सर॑त्प॒दा न दक्षि॑णा परा॒वृज्ञ ता नु मे॑ पृश॒न्यो॑ जगृभ्रे ॥८॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । ईं । वृषा । न । फेनं । अस्यत् । आजौ । स्मत् । आ । परा । ऐत् । अप ।  
> दभ्रचेताः ।  
> सरत् । पदा । न । दक्षिणा । परावृक् । न । ताः । नु । मे । पृशन्यः । जगृभ्रे ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 421

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंगिरसां सत्क्रांते नाभानेदिष्टो गा निरोधयंतं वास्तोष्णतिं पुरतः
> पश्यन्वदति । स ईं । सोऽयं वृषा न वर्षक इंद्र इव स यथा नमुचेर्वधार्थमाजौ संग्रामे फेनमस्यत् क्षिप्तवान् तद्वत्क्षेपमना वास्तोष्णतिरिदानीं तवैव
> वास्तुभागो युक्त इति यथार्थकथनानंतरं स्मदस्मत्त आप परैत् । अपपरागच्छति ।
> दभ्रचेता अल्पमनस्को यः कश्चिद्दक्षिणा दक्षिणार्थानां गवां परावृक् परावर्जयिता सन् पदा पदानि न सरत् । न सरति। अस्मदभिमुखमागच्छति । मे मम संबंधिन्यस्ता गा अंगिरोभिर्दत्ताः पृशन्यः पथिकानामभिस्पर्शनकुशलो रुद्रो न जगृभ्रे ।
> न गृह्णातीत्येवमाशास्त्रे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the sattra of the Aṅgirases, Nābhānediṣṭha, seeing in front of him वास्तोष्णतिं (*vāstoṣṇatiṃ*) who was holding back the cows, speaks. स ईं (*sa īṃ*): this one, वृषा न (*vṛṣā na*), like the showerer, Indra: as he, for the slaying of Namuci, cast foam (फेनं (*phenaṃ*)) in battle (आजौ (*ājau*)), so Vāstoṣpati, with the intention of casting it, after saying truthfully, "Now the share of the site is rightly yours alone", goes away from us (स्मत् (*smat*) = स्मत् (*smat*); आप परैत् (*āpa parait*)). दभ्रचेताः (*dabhracetāḥ*): anyone of small mind, being one who turns away (परावृक् (*parāvṛk*)) the cows meant for the dakṣiṇā, does not step (पदानि न सरत् (*padāni na sarat*)), does not come toward us. Those cows of mine, given by the Aṅgirases, पृशन्यः (*pṛśanyaḥ*), Rudra, skilled in touching travellers, does not seize (न जगृभ्रे (*na jagṛbhre*)); so he says in the *āśāstre*. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स ईं (*sa īṃ*)—that same Vāstoṣpati
- वृषा न (*vṛṣā na*)—like Indra, the maker of rain
- आजौ (*ājau*)—in battle
- फेनं (*phenaṃ*)—foam
- अस्यत् (*asyat*)—poured out and spread all around
- स्मत् (*smat*)—from us
- आ अप परैत् (*ā apa parait*)—moved away and came
- दभ्रचेताः (*dabhracetāḥ*)—one of small mind
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—the cows meant for the dakṣiṇā
- परावृक् (*parāvṛk*)—abandoning
- पदा (*padā*)—even a step
- न सरत् (*na sarat*)—does not put forward
- (but) पृशन्यः (*pṛśanyaḥ*)—Rudra, skilled in plundering
- मे (*me*)—belonging to me
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those same cows
- न जगृभ्रे (*na jagṛbhre*)—did not snatch away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vāstoṣpati, like Indra the maker of rain, poured out and spread foam all around in battle. He moved away from us. Any other person of small mind would leave the cows meant for the dakṣiṇā and not put forward even a step. But Rudra, skilled in plundering, did not snatch away those same cows that belong to me.

##### English translation
He, like the showerer (Indra), cast foam around in the combat, and came away from us with a niggard mind ; he advances not a step, relin- quishing the donations ; though skilled in rapine, he seizes not these my (cows)

#### Ṛk 9
**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒क्ष्मा न वह्निः॑ प्र॒जाया॑ उप॒ब्बिर॒ग्निं न न॒ग्न उप॑ सीद॒दूधः॑ ।  
> सनि॑ते॒ध्मं सनि॑तो॒त वाजं॒ स ध॒र्ता ज॑ज्ञे॒ सह॑सा यवी॒युत् ॥

### Printed p. 422

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मक्षु । न । वह्निः । प्रजायाः । उपब्धिः । अग्निं । न । नग्नः । उप । सीदत् । ऊधः॥  
> सनिता । इध्मं । सनिता । उत । वाजं । सः । धर्ता । जज्ञे । सहसा । यवियुत् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वास्तोष्पतिना रुद्रेण गोप्यमानेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे वह्निर्वह्नि वद्दाहको राक्षसादिर्मक्षु न शीघ्रं नोप सीदत् । नागच्छति । यो वह्निः प्रजाया उपब्बिरुपपीडको भवति यज्ञविघातार्थमागच्छति । ऋत्विगादिरूपायाः प्रजाया न पीडां
> करोत्यहनि । तथोधः । रात्रिनामैतत् । रात्रावप्यग्निं ज्वलंतं नग्नो विवसनो
> राक्षसादिर्नोप सीदत् । एवं रुद्रे रक्षितरि सति सोऽग्निरिध्मं सनिता जज्ञे । उत्पन्नः ।
> उतापि च वाजमन्नं हविः सनिता जज्ञे । स धर्तार्यज्ञस्य फलस्य ना धारक उत्पन्नः
> सोऽग्निः सहसा बलेन यवीयुद्यज्ञमिश्रयित्कृणां रक्षःप्रभृतीनां योद्धा जज्ञे॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

While the guardian of the dwelling, Rudra, protects this sacrifice, the "fire-bearer" (वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)), meaning a fire-like burner such as a Rākṣasa, does not approach quickly. He does not come, though he is the oppressor of the people (प्रजायाः (*prajāyāḥ*)), meaning the priests and others, and comes to wreck the sacrifice. He does not harm them by day. Likewise ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*) is a name for night: even at night the naked one (नग्नः (*nagnaḥ*)), the unclothed Rākṣasa and the like, does not approach the blazing fire. Rudra being the protector, that Agni has been born as the giver of fuel (इध्मं (*idhmaṃ*)). Moreover he has been born as the giver of food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), the oblation. He has arisen as the upholder (धर्ता (*dhartā*)) of the sacrifice and its fruit. By his might (सहसा (*sahasā*)) he has become the fighter (यवीयुत् (*yavīyut*)) of the Rākṣasas and others who mix up and spoil the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (at the time when Rudra protects our sacrifice) वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—the Rākṣasa who can burn like fire
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- न उप सीदत् (*na upa sīdat*)—cannot approach
- प्रजायाः (*prajāyāḥ*)—to the sacrificer and the others
- उपबिद्धिः (*upabiddhiḥ*)—the one who harms, and
- नग्नः (*nagnaḥ*)—the Rākṣasa who stands naked
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—the sacrificial fire
- ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*)—even at night
- न (*na*)—cannot approach
- इद्मं (*idmaṃ*)—the kindling-sticks and the like, the means of kindling
- सनिता (*sanitā*)—the god who gives
- जज्जॆ (*jajjè*)—has been born
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वातं (*vātaṃ*)—food
- सनिता (*sanitā*)—one who can supply
- यवीयुत् (*yavīyut*)—one who strikes and drives off Rākṣasas and the like
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—the upholder of the sacrifice
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—together with his strength (has been born)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time when Rudra protects our sacrifice, the Rākṣasa who can burn like fire cannot easily approach us. The Rākṣasa who harms the sacrificer and the others, and who stands naked, cannot approach the sacrificial fire even at night. Agni, who gives the kindling-sticks and the like that serve for blazing, who gives food, who drives off the Rākṣasas and the like, and who upholds the sacrifice, has been born together with his strength.

##### English translation
The fire, harming the people, does not approach qnically (by day):
the naked (Rakshasas approach) not Agni by night;  the giver of fuel, and
### Printed p. 423
the giver of food, he the upholder (of the rite), is born, overcoming
enemies by his might.
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒क्पू क॒नायाः॑ स॒ख्यं नव॑ग्वा ऋ॒तं वदं॑त ऋ॒तयु॑क्तिमग्मन् ।  
> द्वि॒बर्ह॑सो॒ य उप॑ गो॒पमागु॑रदक्षि॒णासो॒ अच्यु॑ता  
> दुदुक्सन् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मक्षु । कनायाः । सख्यं । नवग्वाः । ऋतं । वदंतः । ऋतयुक्तिं । अग्मन् ।  
> द्विबर्हसः । ये । उप । गोपं । आ । आगुः । अदक्षिणासः । अच्युता । दुधुक्षन् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नवग्वा अंगिरसः । गवामयनाख्यं सत्रमनुतिष्ठतामंगिरसां मध्ये ये
> नवसु मासेषु लब्धगावः संत उत्थितास्ते नवग्वाः । त ऋतं वदंतो मक्षु शीघ्रं
> कनायाः कमनीयायाः स्तुतेर्नाभानेदिष्टप्रेरितायाः सकाशादृतयुक्तिमग्मन् ।
> उक्तयोगपरिसमाप्तिमग्मन् । प्राप्ताः । यद्वा । ऋतयुक्तिं यज्ञयोगोपेतमृतं शब्दं स्तुतिं वदंतोऽंगिरसः कनायाः पृश्न्याः सख्यमग्न्निति योजना ।
> द्विबर्हसो द्वयोः स्थानयोर्द्यावापृथिव्योः परिवृढा येऽंगिरसो गोपं
> गोपायितारं नाभानेदिष्टमिंद्रं वोपागुः उपगताः तेदक्षिणासो दक्षिणारहिताः ।
> अदक्षिणानि सत्राणीत्याहुरिति हि वचनं ये यजमानास्त ऋत्विज इति । ते चाच्युतोदकान्यक्षीणानि फलानि वा दुधुक्सन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Navagvas are Aṅgirases. Among the Aṅgirases performing the sacrificial session called Gavāmayana, those who rose up after obtaining cows in the nine months are the Navagvas. Speaking the truth (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)), they quickly (मक्षु (*makṣu*)) attained the completion of the sacrificial connection (ऋतयुक्तिं (*ṛtayuktiṃ*)) from the lovely (कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)) praise sent forth by Nābhānediṣṭha. Or else: the Aṅgirases, uttering the praise (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)) joined to the sacrifice, attained the friendship (सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)) of Pṛśni (कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)); so the construction runs. Those Aṅgirases who, pervading both places, heaven and earth (द्विबर्हसः (*dvibarhasaḥ*)), came to the protector (गोपं (*gopaṃ*)), that is Nābhānediṣṭha or Indra, were without sacrificial fees (अदक्षिणासः (*adakṣiṇāsaḥ*)). The saying is that sessions are said to be without fees, and that the sacrificers are themselves the priests. They milked out (दुधुक्सन् (*dudhuksan*)) the unfailing waters or the unfailing fruits.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतुयुक्तिं (*ṛtuyuktiṃ*)—useful for the sacrifice
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the praise
- वदंतः (*vadaṃtaḥ*)—those who recite
- नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*)—the Aṅgirases called Navagvas
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)—of Pṛśni
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—friendship
- अग्मन् (*agman*)—attained
- द्विबर्हसः (*dvibarhasaḥ*)—who had a place in both heaven and earth
- ये (*ye*)—which Aṅgirases
- गोपं (*gopaṃ*)—the protector Indra
- उप आगुः (*upa āguḥ*)—approached, they
- अदक्षिणासः (*adakṣiṇāsaḥ*)—without receiving a fee
- अच्युता (*acyutā*)—the imperishable waters
- दुधुक्सन् (*dudhuksan*)—milked

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, called Navagvas, who recite the praise useful for the sacrifice, quickly attained the friendship of the cow named Pṛśni. Those Aṅgirases who had a place in both heaven and earth approached Indra the protector. Receiving no fee, they milked out the imperishable waters.
### Printed p. 424

##### English translation
The Angirasas, who were engaged in the nine months' ceremonial, reciting the praise suited to the rite, quickly attained the friendship of the maiden : those who seated in the two seats (heaven and earth) came to their protector, as they had no donation, milked forth the inexhaustible (waters).
#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒क्स्य क॒नायाः॑ स॒ख्यं नवी॑यो॒ राधो॒ न रेत॑ ऋ॒तमित्तु॑  
> रण्यन् ।  
> शुचि॒ यत्ते॒ रेक्ष्ण॒ आय॑जंत सब॒र्दुघा॑याः॒ पय॑  
> उ॒स्रिया॑याः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मक्षु । कनायाः । सख्यं । नवीयः । राधः । नः । रेतः । ऋतं । इत् । तुरण्यन् ।  
> शुचि । यत् । ते । रेक्ष्णः । आऽ अयजंत । सबःदुघायाः । पयः । उस्रियायाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मक्षु शीघ्रं कनायाः कमनीयाया घर्मदोग्धा ्य नवीयो नवतरं
> सख्यं । प्राप्येति शेषः । अथवा नवीय इति राधोविशेषणं । नवतरं राधो
> धनमिव रेतः सिच्यमानमृतमुदकं तुरण्यन् । दिवः सकाशात्प्रेरितवंतः । हे इंद्र
> ते तुभ्यं यद्यदा रेक्ष्णः पाथोलक्षणं धनमाभिमुखमयजंत अपूजयन् ।
> कीदृशं रेक्ष्णः । सबर्दुघायाः । सबरित्यमृतनाम । अमृतदोग्धा ्य उस्रियाया
> गोः पयः पानयोग्यं रसं । तदोदकं तुरण्यन्निति । अत्राध्वर्युब्राह्मणं ।
> अंगिरसो वै सत्रमासत तेषां पृश्निर्घर्मधुगासीत् सर्जिषेणाजीवत् तेऽब्रुवन्
> कॆस्मै नु सत्रमास्महे येऽस्या ओषधीर्न जनयाम इति ते दिवो वृष्टिमसृजंत ।
> तै. ब्रा. २-१-१-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Quickly (मक्षु (*makṣu*)), having obtained a newer (नवीयः (*navīyaḥ*)) friendship with the lovely (कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)) cow that yields the hot milk-offering ("having obtained" is to be supplied). Or else नवीयः (*navīyaḥ*) qualifies राधः (*rādhaḥ*): like newer wealth they sent down, from the sky, the water (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)) that falls like seed (रेतः (*retaḥ*)). "O Indra, when they offered to you (ते (*te*)) the wealth in the form of milk (रेक्ष्णः (*rekṣṇaḥ*))": what kind? सबर्दुघायाः (*sabardughāyāḥ*): सबः (*sabaḥ*) is a name for ambrosia, so the cow (उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*)) yields ambrosia, and its milk (पयः (*payaḥ*)) is a drinkable essence; then they sent down water. Here is the Adhvaryu Brāhmaṇa: अंगिरसो वै सत्रमासत तेषां पृश्निर्घर्मधुगासीत् सर्जिषेणाजीवत् तेऽब्रुवन् कॆस्मै नु सत्रमास्महे येऽस्या ओषधीर्न जनयाम इति ते दिवो वृष्टिमसृजंत । (*aṃgiraso vai satramāsata teṣāṃ pṛśnirgharmadhugāsīt sarjiṣeṇājīvat te 'bruvan kèsmai nu satramāsmahe ye 'syā oṣadhīrna janayāma iti te divo vṛṣṭimasṛjaṃta |*) Tai. Brā. 2-1-1-1.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) शुचि (*śuci*)—pure
- सबर्दुघायाः (*sabardughāyāḥ*)—of the one that yields ambrosia
- उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*)—of the cow
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—in the form of milk
- रेक्णः (*rekṇaḥ*)—the wealth
- यत् (*yat*)—when
### Printed p. 425
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ते (*te*)—towards you
- अयजंत (*ayajaṃta*)—they offered, then
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)—of the milch cow called Pṛśni
- नवीयः (*navīyaḥ*)—new
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—having obtained friendship
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—flowing
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—water
- राधः न (*rādhaḥ na*)—as if pouring wealth
- तुरज्यन् (*turajyan*)—they sent down from the sky

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when they offered to you the wealth in the form of milk, fit for drinking, of the cow that yields pure ambrosia, then, quickly obtaining the new friendship of the milch cow called Pṛśni, they sent down from the sky the flowing water as if pouring wealth.

##### English translation
Quickly (obtaining) the friendship of the maiden, they poured forth water like new wealth, when they offered to you (Indra) the pure riches, the milk of the cow, that yields ambrosia.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वसो॑र्वसु॒त्वा का॒रवो॑ऽने॒हा विश्वं॑ विवेष्टि॒ द्रवि॑ण॒मुप॒ क्षु ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पश्वा । यत् । पश्चा । वियुता । बुधंत । इति । ब्रवीति । वक्तरि । रराणः ।  
> वसोः । वसुत्वा । कारवः । अनेहा । विश्वं । विवेष्टि । द्रविणं । उप । क्षु ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदा स्तोतारः पश्वा पशुना । गोसमूहेनेत्यर्थः । तेन वियुता
> वियुक्तानि स्वकीयानि गोस्थानानि पश्चा पश्चाद्बुधंत अजानन् तदानीं कारवः ।
> कारुरित्यर्थः । इति ब्रवीति । इत्थं ब्रूते । किमिति । वक्तरि स्तोतरि रराणो रममाणो
> वसोर्वासकाद्वसुत्वातिशयेन वासयिता । यद्वा । वसुत्वेति समूहार्थे त्वा
> नामकरणः । गोरूपधनवतोऽतिशयेन गोसमूहवानित्यर्थः । अनेहा अपाप
> इंद्रो विश्वं सर्वं द्रविणं गोरूपं पणिभिरपहृतं धनं क्षु । मक्ष्वित्यर्थः ।
> शीघ्रमुप विवेष्टि । उपव्याप्नोति पुनरादातुं । आयमर्थः । यदेंद्रस्य स्तोतारोऽसुरैरपहृतमात्मीयं गोधनं जानंति ततः प्रागेवागत्येंद्रस्तं न्यरुधदिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the worshippers afterwards (पश्चा (*paścā*)) found their own cow-stalls bereft (वियुता (*viyutā*)) of the herd of cattle (पश्वा (*paśvā*)), at that time the poet (कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)), that is the praiser, speaks (ब्रवीति (*bravīti*)) thus. What does he say? Indra, delighting (रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)) in the speaker, the praiser, is the one who gives dwelling more abundantly than the dweller-giver (वसोः (*vasoḥ*)) (वसुत्वा (*vasutvā*)). Or else वसुत्वा (*vasutvā*) has the affix त्वा (*tvā*) in the sense of a collection: he who has the greatest herd of cows, wealth in the form of cattle. Indra, the sinless (अनेहा (*anehā*)), quickly (क्षु (*kṣu*), that is मक्षु (*makṣu*)) approaches (उप विवेष्टि (*upa viveṣṭi*)), pervades, all (विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)) the wealth (द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)) in the form of cows carried off by the Paṇis, in order to take it back. The meaning is that when Indra's praisers learn that their cattle have been carried off by the Asuras, Indra arrives beforehand and holds the Asuras back.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the sacrificers see that the cattle have been carried off from their stalls, the praiser proclaims: "Indra, who delights in the praisers, who has more wealth than the wealthy, who is sinless, quickly makes all the wealth in the form of cows come back."

the affluent lord of affluence, the compassionate the sinless, quickly recovers
all the wealth (that has been carried off )."

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Right there, quickly, the attendants (परिषद्वानः (*pariṣadvānaḥ*)) of this Indra, namely the rays abiding around him, came forth (अग्मन् (*agman*)) to shine. The Asuras, sitting (सदंतः (*sadaṃtaḥ*)) in many artificial forms (पुरु (*puru*)), wished to split (बिभित्सन् (*bibhitsan*)) the son of Nṛṣad (नार्षदं (*nārṣadaṃ*)). Moreover, this Indra
### Printed p. 427

> कस्यासुरस्य पुरुप्रजातस्य बहुप्रादुर्भावस्य संग्रथितं मर्म विदत् । वेत्ति ।
> अयमिंद्रो यदसुरस्य दुज्ञेयं मर्म गुहा गुहायां गोपितं तद्विदत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

...finds (विदत् (*vidat*)) the joined-together (संग्रथितं (*saṃgrathitaṃ*)) vital spot of the Asura named Śuṣṇa, who has many manifestations (पुरुप्रजातस्य (*puruprajātasya*)). Indra learns that vital spot of the Asura, hard to know, which was hidden in a cave (गुहा (*guhā*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तदित् (*tadit*)—right then
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Indra
- परिषद्वानः (*pariṣadvānaḥ*)—the rays that are like attendants
- अग्मन् (*agman*)—came out and shone
- पुरु (*puru*)—exceedingly
- सदंतः (*sadaṃtaḥ*)—the Asuras dwelling in many places
- नार्षदं (*nārṣadaṃ*)—the son of Nṛṣada
- बिभित्सन् (*bibhitsan*)—wished to destroy
- (but) पुरु प्रजातस्य (*puru prajātasya*)—of the one who takes many kinds of forms
- शुष्णस्य (*śuṣṇasya*)—of the Asura named Śuṣṇa
- यत् गुहा (*yat guhā*)—of whatever hidden place there is
- संग्रथितं (*saṃgrathitaṃ*)—the vital spot built up compactly
- अनर्वा (*anarvā*)—Indra the unopposed
- विदत् (*vidat*)—knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Right then, quickly, the rays that are like attendants of Indra came out and shone. The Asuras, dwelling exceedingly in many places, wished to destroy the son of Nṛṣada. But Indra the unopposed knows the compactly built vital spot, in the hidden place of the Asura named Śuṣṇa, who takes many kinds of forms.

##### English translation
Then the attendant (rays of light) quickly gathered round him, and
(the Asuras) dwelling in many regions sought to destroy the son of Nrishad,
but the irresistible (Indra) found the wel-knit mail of Shushna, whose
offspring was numerous, which was hidden in the cave.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Bharga is the well-known name of that radiance of Agni on whose triple-seated sacred grass the gods who are present sit down, just as they sit in heaven. That radiance is also called Agni, and also Jātavedas ("knower of what is born"). Bharga, Agni and Jātavedas are thus three names of it. Then he turns to the direct address: O Hotṛ, accomplisher of the oblation, bearing the names stated, invoker of the gods who belong to the sacrifice, free from malice, hear our invocation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये देवाः (*ye devāḥ*)—those gods who are
- स्वर्ण (*svarṇa*)—as if seated in heaven
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Agni, endowed with radiance
- त्रिषधस्ते (*triṣadhaste*)—on the seat of sacred grass
- निषेदुः (*niṣeduḥ*)—they sit down
- (तत्) ह (*(tat) ha*)—to that radiance
- भर्गो ह नाम (*bhargo ha nāma*)—the name may be Bharga
- उत (*uta*)—or
- अग्नि र्ह नाम (*agni rha nāma*)—its name may be Agni
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—or its name may be Jātavedas (all-knowing)
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—O Agni, in the form of the Hotṛ
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—for the sacrifice
- होता (*hotā*)—you who call the gods
- अध्रुक् (*adhruk*)—without doing harm to us
- नः (*naḥ*)—our invocation
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiance on whose sacred grass the gods sit as if in heaven may be named Bharga, or Agni, or Jātavedas. O Agni in the form of the Hotṛ, you who call the gods to the sacrifice, hear our invocation without doing us harm.

##### English translation
Whether Bharga is the name of that radiance, on the triple seat of which those who are gods are seated, as if in heaven, or whether it be Agni, or Jatavedas ; invoker (of the gods), who are the ministrant priest of the sacrifice, here our guileless invocation.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And, O Indra, those two famous ones are sons of Rudra; the sonship of Rudra has been stated in क्षोदो न रेत इतऊति सिंचत् (*kṣodo na reta itaūti siṃcat*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-2). The two luminous Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, are to be present for my praise and for the sacrifice (this is supplied). Further: as at the sacrifice of my father Manu, so for me, who have strewn the sacred grass, may they be delighting, exhilarating, with wealth set forth, **NOTE** and worthy to be sacrificed to (this is supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्या (*tyā*)—famous
- रौद्रा (*raudrā*)—sons of Rudra
- अर्चिमंता (*arcimaṃtā*)—and radiant
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—the Aśvin deities
- मे (*me*)—my
- गूर्तये (*gūrtaye*)—let them be present facing my praise
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—and facing the sacrifice
- मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*)—as they sat at the sacrifice of Manu and gave him delight
- वृक्तबर्हिषे (*vṛktabarhiṣe*)—to me who have prepared the sacred grass
- रराणा (*rarāṇā*)—giving delight
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—among us
- मंदू (*maṃdū*)—and joyful
- हितप्रयसा (*hitaprayasā*)—possessing wealth which they give to us
- यज्यू (*yajyū*)—and worthy of the sacrifice, let them be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may the famous, radiant Aśvin deities, sons of Rudra, be present facing my praise and my sacrifice. As they sat at Manu's sacrifice and gave him delight, so may they give delight to me who have prepared the sacred grass, and be joyful among us the priests, possessing wealth which they give to us, and worthy of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
And, Indra, let those two brilliant sons of Rudra, the Nasatyas, (be present) at my praise and sacrifice ; being propitious to (me seated) on the strewn grass, as (at the sacrificee of ) Manu, cheerful, liberal of wealth to the people, deserving of adoration

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं वेधाः सर्वस्य विधाता राजा सोमः स्तुतः सर्वैर्विंदि । स्तूयतेऽस्माभिः । किंच विप्रो विशेषेण पूरको विप्रवच्चुद्धो ना स्वसेतुर्यस्य स्वभूता
> रश्मयो जगद्बंधकाः संति स सोमोऽपश्चांतरिक्षं च तरति । लंघयति प्रतिदिनं ।
> स सोमः कक्षीवंतमृषिं पर्वतमध्यॆ सोमार्थं गतं रेजयत् सः स एवाग्निं
> हनिर्वोढुमशक्तं संतं पलाय्याप्सु प्रविष्टं रेजयत् । अकंपयत् । कंपने
> दृष्टांतः । नेमिं नमनशीलं रघुद्रु लघुगमनं चक्रमर्वतोर्वंतोऽश्वा इव
> ते यथा तथा रेजयत् ॥ नुमभावश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This creator of all, the king Soma, is praised by all; he is praised by us. Further, the sage, as it were a purifier in a special sense, is svasetu: his own rays are binders of the world. That Soma crosses the waters and the atmosphere, passing over them every day. That Soma made the ṛṣi Kakṣīvat, who had gone to the middle of the mountain for the sake of Soma, tremble. He likewise made Agni, who was unable to carry the oblation and had fled and entered the waters, tremble. The illustration of the trembling: as horses make a bending, swift-moving wheel (of a chariot) shake, so he made him tremble. The loss of the nasal augment is Vedic.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजा (*rājā*)—lord

- वंदि (*vaṃdi*)—is saluted by us
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise one
- स्वसेतुः (*svasetuḥ*)—Soma, who has a causeway made by himself from his own rays
- अपश्च (*apaśca*)—the atmosphere
- तरति (*tarati*)—crosses
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Soma
- कक्षीवंतं (*kakṣīvaṃtaṃ*)—the ṛṣi named Kakṣīvat
- रेजयत् (*rejayat*)—

### Printed p. 431
made to tremble
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—excellent horses
- नेमिं (*nemiṃ*)—fit for travelling
- रघुद्रु (*raghudru*)—and swiftly moving
- चक्रं न (*cakraṃ na*)—as they make a wheel (revolving) shake
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Soma
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—made Agni tremble

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The creator, lord, praised by all, the god Soma, is saluted by us. Soma, the wise one, who has a causeway made by himself from his own rays, crosses the atmosphere. That same Soma made the ṛṣi Kakṣīvat tremble. As horses whirl and shake a wheel that is fit for travelling and moves swiftly, so that same Soma made Agni, who had hidden in the water without carrying the oblation, tremble.

##### English translation
This royal (Soma), this glorified creator, is praised (by all), and, like a sage, constituting his own causeway, he traverses the firmament : he made Kakshivat tremble, he (made) Agni (shake) as horses (agitate) the light-whirling, revolving-wheel (of a chariot).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोग्निर्द्विबंधुर्द्वयोर्लोकयोर्बंधुभूतो वैतरणः सर्वस्य विशेषेण
> तारयिता । यद्वा । वितरणार्हो हविष्णदानार्हः । यष्टा देवानां याजकोग्निः
> सबर्धुममृतोपमपयोदोग्धीं धेनुमस्वमप्रसूतां निवृत्तप्रसवां शयवे
> दुहध्यै दोहायाकरोत् । यद्यदा स शयुर्मित्रावरुणावर्यमणं च ज्येष्ठेभिर्ज्येष्ठैः प्रशस्त्यैर्वरूथैर्वर्णेय्रुक्थैः शस्त्रैः सं वृंजे सम्यक् स्तौति ।
> यदा स शयुर्मित्रावरुणार्यम्मां स्तुतिं करोति तदा तेषामाज्ञयाग्निर्निवृत्तप्रसवां पयोदोग्धिमकरोदिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Agni is dvibandhu, a kinsman of the two worlds, and vaitaraṇa, the special conveyer of all across; or else he is worthy of giving across, worthy of the gift of oblations. Agni, sacrificer for the gods, made the cow that yields ambrosia-like milk, though she had not given birth and her calving had ceased, yield milk for Śayu. When that Śayu praises Mitra and Varuṇa and Aryaman with the best, choice ukthas, that is, śastras, he praises well. When Śayu praises Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, then by their command Agni made the cow, whose calving had ceased, yield milk.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time when Śayu praised Mitra and Varuṇa and Aryaman fully with praiseworthy, chosen śastra-mantras, Agni, kinsman of both heaven and earth, conveyer of all across difficulty, worshipper of the gods, made the cow that yields ambrosia (milk) yield milk although she had not borne a calf.

##### English translation
The kinsman of the two (worlds, Agni) the conveyer (of all), the sacrificer, (made) the ambrosia-yielding cow, which had not given birth, to yield milk (for Shayu), when he praises Mitra, Varuna and Aryaman, with most excellent and choice hymns.

> वेनन् ।

> त्यदपत्यभूत इति यावत् । षष्ठीसामर्थ्यत्संबंधसामान्यं प्रतीयते । तच्चादित्यपुत्रो मनुर्मनोः पुत्रो नाभानेदिष्य इत्येवं सूर्यापत्यत्वं पर्यवस्यति ।
> सूर्यनाभानेदिष्टयोः संबंधश्चरमपाद उत्तरमंत्रे च वक्ष्यते । स च धियंधाः
> कर्मणां धारको नाभानेदिष्टो वेनन्नंगिरोदत्तं गोसहस्रं वेनन्कामयन्
> प्र रपति । प्रलपति । स्तौतीत्यर्थः । वापि चेत्यर्थः । सा द्यौर्नोऽस्माकं परमोत्कृष्टा
> नाभिर्बंधिका चास्यादित्यस्याधिष्ठानभूतास्ति । घेति पूरणः । अहं तत्तस्यादित्यस्य पश्चा
> पश्चादनंतरं कतिथः कतिपयानां पूरण आस । अभवं । अनेन ममादित्येन जन्यजनकभावः संबंधः संनिकृष्ण इत्युक्तं भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Tadbandhu: that very earth is the seat of origin of the kinsman, so that he has that as his basis; the meaning is that he has her as his mother. Sūri is the impeller of praise, and is yours, that is, your offspring, who are present in heaven (the words are supplied). From the force of the genitive a general relationship is understood, and this settles as descent from Sūrya: the son of Āditya is Manu, and the son of Manu is Nābhānediṣṭha. The relationship of Sūrya and Nābhānediṣṭha will be stated in the last pāda and in the next mantra. That same Nābhānediṣṭha, supporter of rites, desiring the thousand cows given by Aṅgiras, speaks forth, that is, praises; the sense is also "or". That heaven is our supreme bond, the binding tie, and is the seat of this Āditya; घेति (*gheti*) is a filler. I became, after that Āditya, some (generations) later, the ordinal of a few. By this, a relationship of begotten and begetter with Āditya, a close one, is declared.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तद्बंधुः (*tadbaṃdhuḥ*)—near kinsman of the earth
- सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)—the utterer of praise
- दिवि (*divi*)—abiding in heaven
- ते (*te*)—belonging to you
- धियंधाः (*dhiyaṃdhāḥ*)—supporter of rites
- नाभानेदिष्टः (*nābhānediṣṭaḥ*)—Nābhānediṣṭha
- वेनन् (*venan*)—desiring the recompense in the form of cows
- प्र रपति (*pra rapati*)—praises
- सा (*sā*)—that heaven
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- परमा (*paramā*)—excellent
- नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*)—a bond (it is)
- अस्य (*asya*)—and for Āditya (it is the dwelling-place)
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- तत् (*tat*)—than Āditya
- पश्चा (*paścā*)—afterwards
- कतिथः (*katithaḥ*)—after some generations
- आस (*āsa*)—have been born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Nābhānediṣṭha, the near kinsman of the earth, the utterer of praise, belonging to you who abide in heaven, the supporter of rites, praises you desiring the recompense in the form of cows. Heaven is for us an excellent bond and the dwelling-place of Āditya. I was born in the line of that same Āditya, some generations after him.

##### English translation
The kinsman of the earth, the utterer of praise(belonging)to you(who abide) in heaven, Nabhanedishtha, the supporter of the rite, desiring (the recompense), repeats (this praise) : the (heaven) our most excellent bond (is the site)of the (sun), and I was after many (degrees) descended from him.

> द्विजा अह प्रथमजा ऋतस्येदं धेनुरदुहज्जायमाना ॥१९॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । मे । नाभिः । इह । मे । सधस्थं । इमे । मे । देवाः । अयं । अस्मि ।  
> सर्वः ।  
> द्विजाः । अह । प्रथमजाः । ऋतस्य । इदं । धेनुः । अदुहत् । जायमाना ॥१९॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयं माध्यमिका वाग्मे नाभिः संनाहिनी । आदित्यस्य तस्याश्चाभेदादस्यर्षेर्माध्यमिका वाग्बंधिका भवति । तथा च ब्राह्मणं । सा या वागसौ स आदित्य इति
> ब्राह्मणं । इहास्मिन्मंडले मे मम सधस्थं स्थानं । इमे मे देवा द्योतमाना
> रश्मयो मे मम स्वभूताः । अयमहमस्मि सर्वः । सूर्यस्य स्वस्योक्तेन । प्रकारेणाभेदात्तद्द्वारा सर्वात्मकत्वं । अह किंचेत्यर्थः । द्विजा विप्रा ऋतस्य प्रथमजाः
> सत्यस्य प्रथमजाः सत्यभूतस्य ब्रह्मणः प्रथमोत्पन्नाः । धेनुः । पृश्नि देवता
> माध्यमिका वाग्जायामानेदं सर्वमदुहत् । दुदोह । उदपादयदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This middle-region speech is my नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*), my binding tie. Āditya and that speech are non-different, so for this seer the middle speech is the binder. Sāyaṇa cites the Brāhmaṇa: सा या वागसौ स आदित्य इति ब्राह्मणं (*sā yā vāgasau sa āditya iti brāhmaṇaṃ*). Here, in this orb, is my seat. These shining rays are my own. I am this all, because I am non-different from Sūrya in the manner stated, and so, through him, all-embracing. अह (*aha*) means "and also". The द्विजाः (*dvijāḥ*) are the learned (vipras), the first-born of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), that is, first arisen from Brahman, who is truth. The धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*) is the deity Pṛśni, the middle speech. As she was being born she milked forth this whole universe, that is, produced it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this middle-region goddess of speech
- मे (*me*)—to me
- नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*)—one closely related
- इह (*iha*)—in this solar orb
- मे (*me*)—my
- सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*)—abiding-place there is
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—luminous
- इमे (*ime*)—these rays
- मे (*me*)—belong to me
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—I myself
- सर्वः अस्मि (*sarvaḥ asmi*)—am everything
- प्रथमजाः (*prathamajāḥ*)—first produced from Brahman, who is of the nature of truth
- द्विजाः (*dvijāḥ*)—the groups of twice-born form, these too I am
- धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*)—the goddess of speech in the form of Pṛśni
- जायमाना (*jāyamānā*)—as soon as she was born
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this whole universe
- अदुहत् (*aduhat*)—she produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The goddess of the middle-region speech is closely related to me, and in this solar orb is my abode. These luminous rays belong to me. I myself am everything. I am also the groups of the twice-born, first produced from Brahman, who is of the nature of truth. As soon as the goddess of speech in the form of Pṛśni was born, she produced this whole universe.

##### English translation
This (aerial voice) is my bond of affinity : here, (in the solar orb) is my abiding-place : these are my resplendent (rays) : I am this all : I am

### Printed p. 435
the twice-born : the first-born of truth ; the cow, as soon as born, milked forth this (universe).

> अधाथासु चतसृषु दिक्षु मंद्रो मोदमानोऽरतिर्गंता विभावा दीप्तिमान् द्विवर्तनिर्द्वयोर्लोकयोर्गंता वनेषाड्वने काष्ठानामभिभविताग्निरव
> स्यति । अवसन्नो भवति यागार्थं । यच्च योऽग्निरूर्ध्वर्ोन्मुखा श्रेणिर्न शिशुः
> शंसनीयः सेनेव मक्षु शीघ्रं दन् शत्रुन्ममयति तमिमं स्थिरं निश्चलं शेवृधं
> सुखस्य वर्धकं मातारणिः सूत । यज्ञे जनयामास ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In these four directions Agni is मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*), delighted. He is अरतिः (*aratiḥ*), a goer, विभावा (*vibhāvā*), radiant, द्विवर्तनिः (*dvivartaniḥ*), a goer between the two worlds, and वनेषाट् (*vaneṣāṭ*), the overcomer of wood in the forest. He अवस्यति (*avasyati*), that is, is brought to his end for the sacrifice. The Agni who is upward-facing, like a श्रेणिः (*śreṇiḥ*), like a शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*) who is praiseworthy, like an army, quickly subdues his enemies **NOTE**. Him, steady and unmoving, the increaser of happiness, the mother, the मातारणिः (*mātāraṇiḥ*) (araṇi), brought forth at the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आसु (*āsu*)—in all the directions
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—one who attains delight
- अरतिः (*aratiḥ*)—ever moving
- विभावा (*vibhāvā*)—shining
- द्विवर्तनिः (*dvivartaniḥ*)—one who moves in both worlds
- वनेषाट् (*vaneṣāṭ*)—Agni, who burns the forest
- अव स्यति (*ava syati*)—comes to an end for the sake of the sacrifice
- यत् (*yat*)—which Agni
- श्रेणिः न (*śreṇiḥ na*)—like a long line
- ऊर्ध्वा (*ūrdhvā*)—with face turned upward
- शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—and praiseworthy
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- दन् (*dan*)—who destroys enemies, such
- स्थिरं (*sthiraṃ*)—motionless
- शेवृधं (*śevṛdhaṃ*)—Agni, who increases happiness
- माता (*mātā*)—the araṇi
- सूत (*sūta*)—bore

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni is delighted in all directions, ever moving, shining, moving in both worlds, and burning the forest. With his face turned upward like a long line, and praiseworthy, he quickly destroys his enemies. He comes to an end when needed for the sacrifice (at the conclusion of the rite). The araṇi bore Agni, who is motionless and the increaser of happiness.

### Printed p. 436

##### English translation
He, who, exulting in these (regions), unresting, bright-shining, traversing the (two worlds), consuming the forest, terminates (in the fire of sacrifice), who, upward rising, like a line, adorable, quickly subdues (his foes) : him, unchangeable, the augmenter of happiness, his mother has brought forth.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॒ गाव॒ उप॑मातिं क॒नाया॒ आनु॑ श्वां॒तस्य॒ कस्य॑ चि॒त्परे॑युः ।  
> श्रु॒धि त्वं सु॑द्रविणो न॒स्त्वं या॑ळाश्व॒घ्नस्य॑ वावृधे सू॒नृता॑भिः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अथ । गावः । उपमातिं । कनायाः । अनु । श्वांतस्य । कस्य । चित् । परा । ईयुः ।  
> श्रुधि । त्वं । सुद्रविणः । नः । त्वं । याट् । आश्वघ्नस्य । ववृधे । सूनृताभिः ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अध संप्रति कस्य चिच्छांतस्य प्रवृद्धस्य श्रांतस्य वा । आत्मनो निर्दॆशः । ईदृशस्य नाभानेदिष्टस्य कनायाः कमनीयायाः स्तुतेर्गावो वाचः । यद्वा । वाचः
> स्तुतयः कनायाः कमनीयायाः स्तुतेरुपमातिमुपमानभूतमिंद्रमनु परेयुः । अनु परागच्छंति । हे सुद्रविणः सुधनाग्ने त्वं श्रुधि । शृणु । नोऽस्माकमिममिंद्रं याट् । अयाट् । यज । त्वं चाश्वघ्नस्य । अश्वघ्नोऽश्वमेधयाजी
> मनुः । तस्य पुत्रस्य मम सूनृताभिः स्तुतिभिर्ववृधे । वर्धसे ॥ पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥
> अथवायं वर्धत इति परोक्षेण निर्देशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now, of a certain श्वांतस्य (*śvāṃtasya*), one tranquil (or advanced, or weary), there is a reference to the speaker himself. Of such a one, Nābhānediṣṭha, the गावः (*gāvaḥ*), that is, the words of lovely praise, follow the उपमातिं (*upamātiṃ*), the model. Or else: the words, the praises, follow Indra, who is the model of the lovely praise; they go after him. O Agni, सुद्रविणः (*sudraviṇaḥ*), rich in wealth, hear us. याट् (*yāṭ*) is अयाट् (*ayāṭ*), "sacrifice": offer sacrifice to this Indra of ours. You are magnified by the praises of Aśvaghna, Manu, the performer of the horse sacrifice, whose son I am. ववृधे (*vavṛdhe*) stands for "you are magnified", a change of person. Or else the statement is indirect: "he grows".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कस्य चित् श्वांतस्य (*kasya cit śvāṃtasya*)—of the tranquil-minded Nābhānediṣṭha
- कनायाः (*kanāyāḥ*)—of the delightful praise
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the words
- उपमातिं (*upamātiṃ*)—Indra, the ideal person
- अनु परेयुः (*anu pareyuḥ*)—go and join
- सुद्रविणः (*sudraviṇaḥ*)—O Agni, possessor of excellent wealth
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our praise
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear
- याट् (*yāṭ*)—worship the gods
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- आश्वघ्नस्य (*āśvaghnasya*)—of me, the son of Manu, the performer of the horse sacrifice
- सूनृताभिः (*sūnṛtābhiḥ*)—by excellent praises
- ववृधे (*vavṛdhe*)—you attain increase

### Printed p. 437

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The delightful words of praise of the tranquil-minded Nābhānediṣṭha go and join Indra, the ideal person. O Agni, possessor of excellent wealth, hear our earth **NOTE**. Worship the gods. You attain increase through the excellent praises of me, the son of Manu, the performer of the horse sacrifice.

##### English translation
The words of the desiraale (praise), of a certain tranquil person (Nabhanedishtha), attain the prototype (Indra), Do you, who are the giver of wealth (Agni), here us : offer sacrifice, you are magnified by the sincere eulogiums of Ashwaghna,

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ त्वमिं॑द्र वि॒ध्य१॒॑गस्मान्म॒हो रा॒ये नृ॑पते॒ वज्र॑बाहुः ।  
> रक्षा॑ च नो म॒घोनः॑ पा॒हि सू॒रीन॑ने॒हस॑स्ते हरिवो अ॒भिष्टौ॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । त्वं । इंद्र । विद्धि । अस्मान् । महः । राये । नृपते । वज्रबाहुः ।  
> रक्ष । च । नः । मघोनः । पाहि । सूरीन् । अनेकहसः । ते । हरिवः । अभिष्टौ ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अधाधुना वज्रबाहुस्त्वमस्मान्महो महते राये धनाय विद्धि ।
> जानीहि । हे इंद्र मघोनो हविष्मतः सूरीन् स्तुतिप्रेरकान्नोऽस्मान्द्रक्ष च ।
> हे हरिवो हरिभ्यां तद्वन्निंद्र ते तवाभिष्टावभिगमनेऽनेहसोऽपापाः स्यामेति
> शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, now you, bearing the thunderbolt in your arm, know us for great wealth. O Indra, protect us, the मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*), the possessors of oblations, the सूरीन् (*sūrīn*), who impel the praise. O हरिवः (*harivaḥ*), Indra with the two bay horses, at your approach (अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)) may we be अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*), free from sin. "May we be" is the word to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृपते (*nṛpate*)—lord of all men
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अध (*adha*)—now
- वज्रबाहुः (*vajrabāhuḥ*)—you who hold the thunderbolt in your hand
- आस्मान् (*āsmān*)—us
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of great
- राये (*rāye*)—wealth
- विद्धि (*viddhi*)—know as worthy
- मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)—possessing oblations
- सूरीन् (*sūrīn*)—who are praisers
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- (पाहि) रक्ष (*(pāhi) rakṣa*)—protect
- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, possessor of horses
- ते (*te*)—your
- अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)—at the time of your coming
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—may we be free from sin

### Printed p. 438

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of all men, you who hold the thunderbolt weapon in your hand, know us as worthy of great wealth. Protect us, who possess oblations and are praisers. O Indra, possessor of horses, at the time of your coming may we be free from sin.

##### English translation
Do you, Indra, king of men, who are the bearer of the thunderbolt, regard us now to (give us) great riches, and protect us who are affluent in (oblations), who utter (your) praise ; may we, lord of bay steeds, (be) free from blame on your approach.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ यद्रा॑जाना॒ गवि॑ष्टौ॒ सर॑त्सर॒ण्युः का॒रवे॑ जर॒ण्युः ।  
> विप्रः॒ प्रेष्ठः॒ स ह्ये॑षां ब॒भूव॒ परा॑ च॒ वक्ष॑दु॒त स॑र्षदेनान् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । यत् । राजाना । गोऽइष्टौ । सरत् । सरण्युः । कारवे । जरण्युः ।  
> विप्रः । प्रेष्ठः । सः । हि । एषां । बभूव । परा । च । वक्षत् । उत । पर्षत् । एनान् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजाना राजमानौ मित्रावरुणौ आधाधुना सत्रसमाप्तौ यद्यस्माद्दविष्टौ
> गवामेषणायां सत्यां सरुण्युः सरणशीलो यमः सरत् गच्छति कारवे कर्माणि
> कुर्वते०ऽगिरसां गणाय । किमिच्छन् । जरण्युस्तस्मा अंगिरसां गणाय स्तुतिमिच्छन् ।
> तस्यात्स विप्रो नाभानेदिष्ट एषामंगिरसां प्रेष्ठः प्रियतमो बभूव । भवतु । हीति
> पूरणः । तेषां कर्तव्यं परा च वक्षत् । परावहतु । उतापि चैनानंगिरसः पर्षत्
> पारयत्वित्यात्मन एवाशास्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O royal Mitra and Varuṇa, now, at the completion of the sacrificial session, because Yama, who is swift-moving by nature, goes in the search for cows (गविष्टौ (*gaviṣṭau*)) to the कारवे (*kārave*), the group of the Aṅgirases who perform rites, desiring praise for that group, therefore that विप्रः (*vipraḥ*), Nābhānediṣṭha, has become प्रेष्ठः (*preṣṭhaḥ*), the dearest, to these Aṅgirases; let him be so. The word हि (*hi*) is a filler. Let him carry out their duty (परा च वक्षत् (*parā ca vakṣat*), "let him carry away"), and let him bring these Aṅgirases across (पर्षत् (*parṣat*)). In this way he asks it for himself.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजाना (*rājānā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, who are lords
- अध (*adha*)—now
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- गविष्टौ (*gaviṣṭau*)—at the time of searching for cows
- सरण्युः (*saraṇyuḥ*)—Yama, who is of moving nature
- कारवे (*kārave*)—to help the Aṅgirases, the praisers

### Printed p. 439
- जरण्युः (*jaraṇyuḥ*)—desiring their praise
- सरत् (*sarat*)—comes; because of that
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Nābhānediṣṭha
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—to these Aṅgirases
- प्रेष्ठः (*preṣṭhaḥ*)—as the very dearest
- बभूव (*babhūva*)—let him be
- परा च वक्षत् (*parā ca vakṣat*)—let him carry out their duty
- उत (*uta*)—and
- एनान् (*enān*)—the Aṅgirases
- पर्षत् (*parṣat*)—let him make them accomplish their work

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, who are lords, since Yama, who is of moving nature, comes at the time of searching for cows to help the Aṅgirases, the praisers, desiring their praise, therefore let the wise Nābhānediṣṭha be the very dearest to these Aṅgirases. Let him bring their duty to completion without obstacle.

##### English translation
Since, royal (Mitra and Varuna), the impetuous (Yama) now approa-ches in expectation of (the gift of) cattle, and desiring praise for the sacrificing (band of the Angirasas); the sage (Nabhanedishtha) has been held most dear by them ; may he accomplish (what has to be effected), and make them successful.

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॒न्व॑स्य॒ जेन्य॑स्य पु॒ष्टौ वृथा॒ रेभं॑त ईमहे॒ तदू॒ नु ।  
> स॒र॒ण्युर॑स्य सू॒नुरश्वो॒ विप्र॑श्चासि॒ श्रव॑सश्च सा॒तौ ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । नु । अस्य । जेन्यस्य । पुष्टौ । वृथा । रेभंतः । ईमहे । तत् । ऊं इति । नु ।  
> सरण्युः । अस्य । सूनुः । अश्वः । विप्रः । च । असि । श्रवसः । च । सातौ ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया वरुणं पृथक् स्तौति । अधाथ नु क्षिप्रमस्य जेन्यस्य जयशीलस्य स्तुत्या
> जेतव्यस्य वा तत्स्वभूतं गवादिधनं पुष्पौ पोषे निमित्ते सति तस्य पुष्ट्यर्थं वा
> वृथानायासेन रेभंतः स्तुवंतो नु क्षिप्रमीमहे । याचामहे । सरण्युः शीघ्रसरणशीलोऽश्वोऽस्य वरुणस्य सूनुः पुत्रः। वरुणाद्यश्व उत्पन्नः । अथ प्रत्यक्षकृतः।
> हे वरुण त्वं विप्रश्चासि । विप्रवत्पूज्यः शुद्धो वा भवसि । श्रवसश्चान्नस्य सातौ लाभेऽस्माकमन्नलाभाय प्रवृत्तश्च भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this verse he praises Varuṇa separately. Now, quickly, in the nourishment (पुष्टौ (*puṣṭau*)) of this जेन्यस्य (*jenyasya*), who is victorious by nature (or who is to be won by praise), his own wealth of cattle and the like, or for its nourishment, we, रेभंतः (*rebhaṃtaḥ*), praising without effort, quickly ask for it. सरण्युः (*saraṇyuḥ*), the swift-moving horse, is the सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*), the son, of this Varuṇa: the horse was produced from Varuṇa, and has now been made manifest. O Varuṇa, you are a विप्रः (*vipraḥ*): you are worshipful like a vipra, or pure. In the gaining (सातौ (*sātau*)) of श्रवसः (*śravasaḥ*), food, you are engaged for our gaining of food.
