##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—thereafter
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- जेन्यस्य अस्य (*jenyasya asya*)—of this victorious Varuṇa
- तत् (*tat*)—his wealth of cattle and the like
- पुष्टौ (*puṣṭau*)—as a cause of nourishing (or, for the contentment of Varuṇa)
- वृथा (*vṛthā*)—of our own accord
- रेभंतः (*rebhaṃtaḥ*)—we who praise
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask
- सरण्युः (*saraṇyuḥ*)—swift-moving
- अश्वः (*aśvaḥ*)—the horse
- अस्य (*asya*)—to Varuṇa
- सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—is in the form of a son
- (O Varuṇa) विप्रः असि (*vipraḥ asi*)—you are wise
- श्रवसः सातौ (*śravasaḥ sātau*)—you are fit to give us the gift of food

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We who praise of our own accord ask for the contentment of the victorious Varuṇa. The swift-moving horse is in the form of a son to Varuṇa. O Varuṇa, you are wise, or worthy of reverence like a Vipra. You are also engaged in giving us food.

##### English translation
And for the contentment of this victorious (Varuna), praising (him) without an effort, we solicit this (of him), (that) his progeny, a swift horse, (may be ours), and you, (Varuna), are wise, and (are occupied) in procuring us food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Since it is said in Śruti passages such as वारुणो ना अश्वः (*vāruṇo nā aśvaḥ*) that the horse was born from Varuṇa, the horse is here described as being in the form of Varuṇa's son.

> विश्वत्र । यस्मिन् । आ । गिरः । संईचीः । पूर्वीऽइव । गातुः । दाशत् । सूनृताय्कॆ ॥

### Printed p. 441

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ युवोर्युवयोः शर्धाय बलवतेऽस्मे अस्माकं सख्याय ।
> यद्वा । युवयोः सख्यायास्मे अस्माकं शर्धाय बलाय च । यदि नमस्वान्नवानध्वर्युः स्तोत्रवान्होता वा सोमं जुजुषे सेवते । यस्मिन् सख्यॆ सिद्धे सति
> विश्वत्र विश्वस्मिञ्जनपदे गिरोऽंगिरसां संबंधिन्यः समीचीः समीच्य आ गच्छंतीति
> शेषः । उदाराणां गृह इदं गृहाणेदं गृहाणेत्येवंरूपाः श्रूयंत इत्यर्थः ।
> यद्वा । यागानुष्ठात्कृणां स्तुतिगिर आगच्छंतीति । पूर्विव गातुः प्राची दिगिव सा
> यथा गच्छतां सुखं प्रयच्छति तद्वत् । यद्वा । पूर्वि पुरा प्रसिद्धा पुरातनीव
> गातुः सरणिरिव सा यथा गच्छतां सुखं प्रयच्छति तद्वत् । सूनृताय्कॆ प्रियसत्यरूपाय्कॆ स्तुतिवाचे दाशत् । प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, "for your friendship, for our strength" (शर्धाय (*śardhāya*) is "strong"), or alternatively "for your friendship and for our strength and force". If the adhvaryu, possessed of homage (or the hotṛ, the reciter of praise), enjoys (जुजुषे (*jujuṣe*)) the Soma, then, once that friendship is established, the praises of the Aṅgirasas come from every region, converging; that is, they are heard in the form "take this, take this" in the houses of the generous. Or else the praise-songs of the sacrificers come. "Like an ancient path" (पूर्विव गातुः (*pūrviva gātuḥ*)): as the eastern quarter gives comfort to travellers; or as a long-known, ancient road gives comfort to travellers. Let him give (दाशत् (*dāśat*)) to the speech of praise, which is in the nature of dear truth (सूनृताय्कॆ (*sūnṛtāykè*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Mitra and Varuṇa) यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—on which friendship being established
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises of the Aṅgirasas
- विश्वत्र (*viśvatra*)—in all regions
- समीचीः (*samīcīḥ*)—with one aim
- आ (*ā*)—spread forth; of such (friendship)
- युवोः सख्याय (*yuvoḥ sakhyāya*)—for your friendship
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our
- शर्धाय (*śardhāya*)—for the gain of strength
- नमस्वान् (*namasvān*)—the adhvaryu or hotṛ, with oblation
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the hymn
- जुजुषे (*jujuṣe*)—recites
- पूर्वी गातुः इव (*pūrvī gātuḥ iva*)—as travel on an ancient road brings comfort
- सूनृताय्कॆ (*sūnṛtāykè*)—to the excellent praiser
- दाशत् (*dāśat*)—may Mitra and Varuṇa give comfort

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, on the establishment of which friendship of yours the praises of the Aṅgirasas spread in all regions with one aim, for that friendship of yours and for the gain of our strength, the adhvaryu with oblation, or the hotṛ who praises, recites the hymn. As travel on an ancient road brings comfort, may Mitra and Varuṇa give comfort to the excellent praiser.

##### English translation
If the priest offer homage to you two (Mitra and Varuna) for the sake of your friendship and our invigoration, on (the formation of) which (friendship) the praises (of the Angirasas go) everywhere in a common direction ; may he give (pleasure) to the utterer of praise, like an ancient road.

> सः । गृणानः । अत्भिः । देववान् । इति । सुबंधुः । नमसा । सुउक्तैः ।  
> वर्धत् । उक्षैः । वचसिभिः । आ । हि । नूनं । वि । अध्वा । एति । पयसः । उस्रियायाः ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवताभिर्देववान् सुबंधुः शोभनबंधनः स वरुण इतीत्थं कृतप्रकारेण
> नमसा नमस्कारेण सूक्तैश्च गृणानः स्तूयमानः सन्वर्धत् । वर्धतां । उक्तैर्वचोभिरुच्यमानैः प्रशस्त्यर्वा स्तुतिवचोभिनूर्नमिदानीमा गच्छत्विति शेषः । हीति
> पूरणः । तस्य यागार्थमुस्रियाया गोः पयसोऽध्वा मार्गो व्येति। स्तनाग्राणि
> क्षरंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa, accompanied by the gods and of good kinship, being thus praised with homage and with hymns, may he grow. Let him come now, drawn by the recited prayers or by words of praise. The word हि (*hi*) is a filler. For his sacrifice the path of the milk of the cow (उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*)) is opened; that is, the tips of the udder flow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स वरुणः (*sa varuṇaḥ*)—the well-known Varuṇa
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—together with all the waters
- देववान् (*devavān*)—together with all the gods
- सुबंधुः (*subaṃdhuḥ*)—is possessed of excellent kinship
- इति (*iti*)—in this manner
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with homage
- सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*)—with hymns
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—Varuṇa, being praised
- वर्धत् (*vardhat*)—grows
- उक्तैः (*uktaiḥ*)—with the recited mantras
- वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)—drawn by words of praise
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- आ (*ā*)—let him come
- उस्रियायाः (*usriyāyāḥ*)—of the cow
- पयसः (*payasaḥ*)—of the milk
- अध्वा (*adhvā*)—the path
- वि एति (*vi eti*)—is open for his worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praised and honoured with the words, "The well-known Varuṇa, together with all the waters and all the gods, has excellent kinship", Varuṇa grows. Drawn by the recited mantras and the praises, may Varuṇa come to us. The path of the cow's milk is opened (made ready) for Varuṇa's worship.

##### English translation
Being praised with reverence and hymns thus, "the god-accompanied (Varuna) of good lineage, together with the waters," may he be magnified : (attracted) by hymns and prayers (may he) now (approach); the path of the milk of the cow is open (for his worship)

> यूयं । उ इति पूरणः । महो महते नोऽस्माकमूतये रक्षणाय सजोषाः
> संगता भूत। भवत। ये च यूयमंगिरसो मह्यं वाजानन्नान्यनयत प्रापयत।

> सजोषा भूतेति समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Ṛk the seer, an Aṅgiras, makes a petition. O adorable gods, you, for our great protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)), be united (सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)); the word उ (*u*) is a filler. You Aṅgirasas who bring me food, going about constantly in various directions to recite praise; and you who are अमूराः (*amūrāḥ*), free of bewilderment in performance, are the finders of cattle (निचेतारः (*nicetāraḥ*)): be, such as you are, united. This is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—worshipful
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods
- ये (*ye*)—you who
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—food
- अनयत (*anayata*)—bring to us (and)
- वियंतः (*viyaṃtaḥ*)—moving about everywhere
- ये (*ye*)—you who
- अमूरः (*amūraḥ*)—free from bewilderment
- निचेतारः (*nicetāraḥ*)—finding the cattle
- स्थ (*stha*)—are such
- ते (*te*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—united
- भूत (*bhūta*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipful gods, you who are givers of food to us and who, moving about everywhere without the least bewilderment, find and bring us cattle, be united, such as you are, for our great protection.

## Sūkta 62 (Maṇḍala 10)
Second chapter in the eighth Aṣṭaka; the sixty-second sūkta of the tenth Maṇḍala.

**Introduction**
Like the 61st sūkta, Idamitthā, of the previous chapter, this sūkta too was seen by the seer Nābhānediṣṭha. The matters concerning these two sūktas have therefore been explained in the introduction to the previous sūkta, on pages 398–407, and may be learned there.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्र ये यज्ञेनेत्येकादशर्चमनुवाकापेक्षया द्वितीयं सूक्तं । मानवस्य नाभानेदिष्टस्यार्षं । आदितश्चतस्रो जगत्यः । पंचम्यनुष्टुप् । षष्ठी बृहती ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of these, taking the eleven-verse यज्ञेन (*yajñena*) sūkta into account in the anuvāka, this is the second sūkta. Its seer is Nābhānediṣṭha, son of Manu. The first four Ṛks are in Jagatī; the fifth is Anuṣṭubh; the sixth is Bṛhatī.

### Printed p. 446

> सप्तमी सतोबृहती । अष्टमीनवम्यावनुष्टुभौ । दशमी गायत्री । एकादशी
> त्रिष्टुप् । आदितः षण्णां विश्वे देवा अंगिरसो वा देवता । सप्तमी वैश्वदेवी । अष्ट
> म्याद्यासु चतसृषु सावर्णेर्महाराजस्य दानं स्तूयते। अतस्तास्तद्देवताकाः। तथा
> चानुक्रम्यते। ये यज्ञेनैकादशाद्याः षळंगिरसां स्तुतिर्वांत्या त्रिष्टुप्पंचम्यनुष्टुप्पगाथोऽनुष्टुभौ गायत्री चतस्रोऽन्त्याः सावर्णॆर्दानस्तुतिरिति॥ षष्ठेhहनि
> वैश्वदेवशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । इदमित्था रौद्रमिति प्रागुपोत्तमाया ये
> यज्ञेनेत्यावपते । आ. ८-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his introduction to the sūkta. The seventh verse is Sato-bṛhatī; the eighth and ninth are anuṣṭubh; the tenth is gāyatrī; the eleventh is triṣṭubh. For the first six verses the deities are the Viśve Devāḥ or the Aṅgirases. The seventh is addressed to the Viśve Devāḥ (Vaiśvadevī). In the four verses beginning with the eighth, the gift of the great king Sāvarṇi is praised, so these have that gift as their deity. He cites the Anukramaṇī to the same effect. The sūkta is used in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra on the sixth day, and it is prescribed in the sūtra of Āśvalāyana (Ā. 8-1).

##### Anuvāda

In the previous chapter the sixty-one sūktas of the tenth maṇḍala were completed. Now this chapter begins with the sixty-second sūkta, "ये यज्ञेन (*ye yajñena*)". This sūkta is the second sūkta in the fifth anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala. It has eleven ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nābhānediṣṭha, the son of Manu. The first four ṛks of this sūkta are in the Jagatī metre; the fifth is in Anuṣṭubh; the sixth is in Bṛhatī; the seventh is in Sato-bṛhatī; the eighth and ninth are in Anuṣṭubh; the tenth is in Gāyatrī; the eleventh is in Triṣṭubh. For the first six ṛks of this sūkta the deities are the Viśve Devāḥ or the Aṅgirases; the seventh ṛk is addressed to the Viśve Devāḥ; since the four ṛks from the eighth onward (ṛks 8–11) describe the praise of the gift of the great king named Sāvarṇi, that praise of the gift is the deity of those four ṛks. This is what the Anukramaṇī states. The use of this sūkta, when the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited on the sixth day of the sacrifice, is set out by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra beginning "Idam itthā raudram" (Ā. 8-1).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 62. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 62. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 2; Vargas 1, 2. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Ṛṣi: Nābhānediṣṭha Mānava. Deity: 1–6 Viśve Devāḥ or the Aṅgirases; 7 Viśve Devāḥ; 8–11 the praise of the gift of Sāvarṇi. Metre: 1–4 Jagatī; 5, 8, 9 Anuṣṭubh; 6 Bṛhatī; 7 Sato-bṛhatī; 10 Gāyatrī; 11 Triṣṭubh.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नाभानेदिष्टः स्वपित्रा मनुनाभ्यनुज्ञातः सत्प्रमासीनानंगिरसोऽभ्येत्य मां
> प्रतिगृह्णीत युष्मभ्यं यज्ञं प्रज्ञापयामिति यदुक्तवान् तदुच्यते । इतिहासस्त्विदमिथ्येति पूर्वसूक्ते नाभानेदिष्टं शंसति नाभानेदिष्टं वै मानवमिति ब्राह्मणानुसारेण मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यभजदिति तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणानुसारेण च
> सप्रपंचमभिहितः । तथा चास्या ऋचोऽयमर्थः । यज्ञेन यजनियेन हविषा
> दक्षिणयर्त्विग्भो देयया समक्ताः संगता येऽहीनैकाहसत्राणि कुर्वंतो
> यूयमिंद्रस्य सख्यं सखिकर्म अत एवामृतत्वममरणधर्म० देवत्वमानश
> आनशिद्धे प्राप्ताः स्थ ॥ अश्नोतेर्लिटि मध्यमे व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं। अश्नोतेश्वेति
> नुडागमः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥ हे अंगिरसः तेभ्यो वो युष्मभ्यं भद्रं
> कल्याणं कर्मास्तु । हे सुमेधसः सुप्रज्ञा हे अंगिरसः ते यूयमिदानीमागतं
> मानवं मनोः पुत्रं मां प्रति गृभ्नित । प्रतिगृह्णीत । मयि प्रतिगृहीते सति यज्ञं
> साधु करिष्यामीति तदर्थ० प्रतिगृह्णीत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Nābhānediṣṭha, having been given leave by his father Manu, approached the Aṅgirases seated at their sattra and said, "Accept me; I will make the sacrifice known to you." What he said is now told. The story was set out in full in the preceding sūkta, following the Brāhmaṇa (*nābhānediṣṭaṃ vai mānavaṃ*) and the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa. The meaning of this ṛk: you who are joined with the sacrificial offering and with the dakṣiṇā to be given to the priests, performing ahīna, ekāha and sattra sacrifices, have attained the friendship of Indra and therefore immortality, that is, divinity. May good, auspicious action be yours, Aṅgirases. O sages of fine understanding, accept me, the son of Manu, who have now come; when I am accepted I shall perform the sacrifice well, and for that purpose accept me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—with the offering fit for sacrifice
- दक्षिणाय (*dakṣiṇāya*)—with the wealth in the form of an honorarium that is to be given to the priests
- समक्ताः (*samaktāḥ*)—united
- ये (*ye*)—you Aṅgirases, who are performing the sattra sacrifice
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—the friendship
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—the divinity that is free from death
- आनश (*ānaśa*)—you have obtained
- तेभ्यः वः (*tebhyaḥ vaḥ*)—to such of you
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—welfare or well-being
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be
- सुमेधसः (*sumedhasaḥ*)—O men of intelligence
- (हे) अंगिरसः (*(he) aṃgirasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirasa sages, you
- मानवं (*mānavaṃ*)—me, the son of Manu
- प्रतिगृभीत (*pratigṛbhīta*)—accept

### Printed p. 448

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aṅgirasa sages, you who have prepared the offering fit for sacrifice and the wealth for the dakṣiṇā to be given to the priests, have gained the friendship of Indra and the divinity that is free from death. May welfare come to you, who are distinguished by such qualities. O Aṅgirases, men of understanding, accept me, the son of Manu, who have come to you; that is, listen respectfully to the words I speak.

##### English translation
You, who associated with sacrifice and pious donotions, have acquired
the friendship of Indra and immortality ; upon you, Angirasas, may good
fortune attend ; welcome, sages, the son of Manu,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As said in the introduction to the previous sūkta, the seer of this sūkta, the sage Nābhānediṣṭha, following his father's word, came to the place where the Aṅgirasa sages were performing a sacrifice, addressed them, and spoke in this way. What he said is stated in this ṛk and in the next three ṛks. For further detail see the introduction to sūkta 61.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॒दाज॑िन्पि॒तरो॑ गो॒मयं॒ वस्व॒तेनाभिं॑दन्परिवत्स॒रे व॒लं ।  
> दी॒र्घा॒यु॒त्वमं॑गिरसो वो अस्तु॒ प्रति॑ गृभ्णीत मान॒वं  ॑
> सुमेधसः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । उत्आजन् । पितरः । गोमयं । वसु । ऋतेन । अभिंदन् । परिवत्सरे  
> वलं ।  
> दीर्घायुत्वं । अंगिरसः । वः । अस्तु । प्रति । गृभ्णीत । मानवं । सुमेधसः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये अंगिरसः पितरोऽस्माकं पूर्वजत्वेन पितृभूता ये यूयं गोमयं गवात्मकं हणिभिरपहृतं वसु धनमुदाजन् तैरधिष्ठि तात्पर्वतादुदगमयन् ।
> किंचर्तॆन सत्यभूतेन यज्ञेन परिवत्सरे पर्यागते वत्सरे संपूर्णे । सत्रांत

### Printed p. 449

> इत्यर्थः । तत्र वलं वलनामानं गवामपहर्तारमसुरमभिंदन् व्यनाशयनन् तेभ्यो
> वो युष्मभ्यं दीर्घायुत्वं प्रभूतजीवनमस्तु । शेषं पूर्ववत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases, who by being earlier-born are as fathers to us, drove up the wealth consisting of cattle, which the Paṇis had carried off, from the mountain that they held. Further, by true sacrifice, when the year was completed, that is, at the end of the sattra, they destroyed Vala, the Asura who steals cattle. May long life, abundant living, be theirs. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirasa sages
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—worthy to be called fathers, because you are elders to us
- ये (*ye*)—you who
- गोमयं (*gomayaṃ*)—in the form of cattle carried off by the Paṇis
- वसु (*vasu*)—the wealth
- उदाजन् (*udājan*)—you drove out and brought from the mountain region, and
- यतेन (*yatena*)—by sacrifice, that is, by performing sacrifice **NOTE**
- परिवत्सरे (*parivatsare*)—a period of one year was passed by you (and you)
- वलं (*valaṃ*)—the Asura called Vala
- अभिंदन् (*abhiṃdan*)—destroyed
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to such of you
- दीर्घायुत्वं (*dīrghāyutvaṃ*)—long life
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be
- सुमेधसः (*sumedhasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirases, men of intelligence, you
- मानवं (*mānavaṃ*)—me, the son of Manu
- प्रति गृभीत (*prati gṛbhīta*)—accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aṅgirases, because you are our elders you are to be honoured like fathers. You brought out the cattle carried off by the Paṇis from the mountain region where they had hidden them. You completed the sattra sacrifice that you were performing for a year. You destroyed the Asura named Vala. May long life be yours, such as you are. Accept me, the son of Manu.

##### English translation
May length of life be yours, Angirasas, our progenitors, who drove
forth the wealth of cattle, and by means of your sacrifice when the year was
ended, demolished (the Asura) Bala : welcome, sages, the son of Manu.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

We have described the matter of the Asura named Vala in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 5, page 692, and on pages 14-634.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य ऋ॒तेन॒ सूर्य॒मारो॑हयन् दि॒व्यप्र॑थयन्पृथि॒वीं मा॒तरं॒ वि ।  
> सु॒प्र॒जा॒स्तमं॑गिरसो वो अस्तु॒ प्रति॑ गृभ्णीत मान॒वं सु॑मेधसः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 450

> ये । ऋतेन । सूर्यं । आ । अरोहयन् । दिवि । अप्रथयन् । पृथिवीं । मातरं ।  
> वि ।  
> सुप्रजाःत्वं । अंगिरसः । वः । अस्तु । प्रति । गृभ्णीत । मानवं । सुमेधसः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अंगिरसः ये भवंत ऋतेन सत्यभूतेन यज्ञेन दिवि द्युलोके सूर्यं
> सुष्टु सर्वस्य प्रेरकमादित्यमारोहयन् अस्थापयन् किंच मातरं सर्वॆषां
> निर्मात्रीं पृथिवीं व्यप्रथयन् प्रसिद्धामकुर्वन् सत्प्रादिकर्मकरणेन तेभ्यो
> युष्मभ्यं सुप्रजास्त्वं सुपुत्रत्वमस्तु॥ नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोरित्यसिच्छमासांतः।
> तस्माद्भावप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aṅgirases, you who by true sacrifice set the sun in heaven, well, as the impeller of all, the Āditya; and who by performing sattras and the like made famous the earth, the mother, the maker of all: to you may there be good offspring, fine sons.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirases
- ये (*ye*)—you who
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—by the power of performing sacrifice, which is of the nature of truth
- दिवि (*divi*)—in heaven (the atmosphere)
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the Āditya, the impeller of all
- आरोहयन् (*ārohayan*)—you have established (and)
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—who is of the nature of a mother to all
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- वि अप्रथयन् (*vi aprathayan*)—you have made famous by your sattra and other sacrifices
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to such of you
- सुप्रजास्त्वं (*suprajāstvaṃ*)—excellent offspring of sons
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be
- सुमेधसः (*sumedhasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirases, men of intelligence
- मानवं (*mānavaṃ*)—me, the son of Manu
- प्रति गृभ्नीत (*prati gṛbhnīta*)—receive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aṅgirases, through the greatness of your performance of sacrifice, which is of the nature of truth, you have established the Āditya, the impeller of all, in heaven (the atmosphere). You have made this earth, which is a mother to all, famous by good works such as the performance of sacrifice. O Aṅgirases, men of intelligence, may excellent offspring be yours. Accept me, the son of Manu.

##### English translation
May the possession of posterity be yours, Angirasas, who elevated by the (power) of sacrifice the Sun in heaven, and made the maternal earth renowned : welcome, sages, the son of Manu.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं नाभा॑ वदति व॒ल्गु वो॑ गृ॒हे देव॑पुत्रा ऋषय॒स्तच्छृ॑होतन ।

> सुब्रह्मण्यमंगिरसो पो अस्तु प्रति गृभ्णीत मानवं सुमेधसः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । नाभा । वदति । वल्गु । वः । गृहे । देवपुत्राः । ऋषयः । तत् । शृणोतन ।  
> सुब्रह्मण्यं । अंगिरसः । वः । अस्तु । प्रति । गृभ्नीत । मानवं । सुमेधसः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवपुत्रा देवानां पुत्रा अग्नेः पुत्रा ऋषयोऽतींद्रियार्थस्य
> द्रष्टारो हेऽंगिरसः आयं नाभा नाभानेदिष्टः पुरोवर्ति जनो वो युष्माकं
> गृहे गृहभूते यज्ञॆ वल्गु कल्याणं वचो वदति । तद्वाकृं यूयं शृणोतन ।
> महातादरेण शृणुत ॥ श्रु श्रवणे । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तनबादेशः ॥ तेभ्यो
> युष्मभ्यं सुब्रह्मण्यं शोभनं ब्रह्मवर्चसमस्तु । इदानीमागतं मानवं मां प्रति
> गृभ्नीत । प्रतिगृह्नीत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O sons of the gods, that is, sons of Agni, O seers of what is beyond the senses, Aṅgirases: this Nābhā, that is, Nābhānediṣṭha, standing before you, speaks fair, auspicious words in your house, that is, at the sacrifice that is your house. Hear those words with great respect. To you may there be fine brahmavarcasa. Accept me, the son of Manu, who have now come.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवपुत्राः (*devaputrāḥ*)—O you who are sons of the god Agni
- ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*)—and seers of matters beyond the senses
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirases
- अयं नाभा (*ayaṃ nābhā*)—this one called Nābhānediṣṭha (I)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- गृहे (*gṛhe*)—in the house of sacrifice
- वल्गु (*valgu*)—auspicious speech
- वदति (*vadati*)—speaks
- तत् (*tat*)—that statement, you
- शृणोतन (*śṛṇotana*)—hear respectfully
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—O Aṅgirases
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you
- सुब्रह्मण्यं (*subrahmaṇyaṃ*)—excellent brahmavarcasa
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be
- सुमेधसः (*sumedhasaḥ*)—O men of intelligence
- मानवं (*mānavaṃ*)—me, the son of Manu
- प्रति गृभ्नित (*prati gṛbhnita*)—accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aṅgirases, sons of the god Agni and knowers of things beyond the senses, Nābhānediṣṭha, who is now conversing with you (I), speaks one auspicious word in your sacrificial house. Listen to it with respect. May excellent brahmavarcasa be yours. O Aṅgirases, men of intelligence, accept me, the son of Manu; that is, give heed to the word I speak and listen to it respectfully.

##### English translation
Rishis, sons of the gods, this (Nabhanedishtha) addresses to you in
the house of (sacrifice) his bendiction ; here it : may divine splendour,
Angirasas, be yours : welcome, sages the, son of Manu.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विरू॑पास॒ इदृष॑य॒स्त इद्गं॑भी॒रवे॑पसः ।  
> ते अंगि॑रसः सू॒नव॒स्ते अ॒ग्नेः परि॑ जज्जिरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विरूपासः । इत् । ऋषयः । ते । इत् । गंभीरवेपसः ।  
> ते । अंगिरसः । सूनवः । ते । अग्नेः । परि । जज्जिरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परोक्षतयर्षिराह । ऋषयः कर्मणां द्रष्टार एत ऋषयो विरूपास
> इदन्योन्यं वर्णतो रूपतश्च नानारूपा भवंति । त इत्त एवामी अंगिरसो
> गंभीरवेपसः । वेप इति कर्मनाम । गंभीरकर्माणो भवंति । त इमेऽंगिरसः
> सूनवः पुत्राः खलु । तदेवाह । त इमेऽगिरसोऽग्नेः परि जज्जिरे। सर्वतो जाताः
> प्रादुर्भूताः । येऽंगारा आसंस्थेऽंगिरसोऽभवन्। ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३४ । इति ब्राह्मणं ।
> अत्र निरुक्तं च द्रष्टव्यं। नि. ३-१७ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains the Ṛk indirectly, speaking of the seers. The seers, who see the rites, are विरूपास इत् (*virūpāsa it*), that is, they differ from one another in colour and in form. त इत् (*ta it*) means "these very" Aṅgirases, who are गंभीरवेपसः (*gaṃbhīravepasaḥ*): वेप (*vepa*) is a name for work, so they are of profound works. These Aṅgirases are indeed sons. He states it: these Aṅgirases were born around Agni, that is, came forth on every side. He quotes the Brāhmaṇa: येऽंगारा आसंस्थेऽंगिरसोऽभवन् (*ye 'ṃgārā āsaṃsthe 'ṃgiraso 'bhavan*) (Ai. Brā. 3-34), and adds that the Nirukta (Ni. 3-17) is to be consulted here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*)—the seers
- विरूपास इत् (*virūpāsa it*)—they are of many forms, in colour, in form and in shape
- त इत् (*ta it*)—(therefore) these Aṅgirases
- गंभीरवेपसः (*gaṃbhīravepasaḥ*)—engaged in profound or deep sacrificial rites and observances
- ते अंगिरसः (*te aṃgirasaḥ*)—these Aṅgirasa seers
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—to Agni
- सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*)—as sons
- परि जज्जिरे (*pari jajjire*)—have been born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seers are of various kinds in colour, form and shape. These Aṅgirases are engaged in deep sacrificial rites. These Aṅgirases are sons of Agni, that is, they have been born as Agni's sons.

##### English translation
These Rirhis, however different in form, are verily of profound piety: they are the Angirasas who have been born as the sons of Agni.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the form-derivation of the word Aṅgiras, Yāska says अंगारेष्टंगिराः । अंगारा अंकनाः ॥ (*aṃgāreṣṭaṃgirāḥ | aṃgārā aṃkanāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 3-17). That is, they got the name Aṅgirāḥ because they were born in the aṅgāras (embers).
### Printed p. 453
What is an aṅgāra? Where it is placed, the place turns black, hence the name अंकनाः (*aṃkanāḥ*). Having said this, he explains the present Ṛk thus: बहुरूपा ऋषयस्ते गंभीरकर्माणो वा गंभीरप्रज्ञा वा ते अंगिरसः पुत्रास्ते अग्नेरधिजज्निर इत्यग्निजन्म ॥ (*bahurūpā ṛṣayaste gaṃbhīrakarmāṇo vā gaṃbhīraprajñā vā te aṃgirasaḥ putrāste agneradhijajnira ityagnijanma ‖*) (Ni. 11-17).
When Prajāpati desired the deity of heaven or the deity Uṣas, his semen fell on the earth and stood in the form of a great lake. When the gods kindled it with the help of Vaiśvānara Agni, from that blazing fire Āditya, Bhṛgu and the Aṅgirases were born; this is known from the narrative of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 13-34). Because they were born of fire or of embers, these seers got the name Aṅgirasas, and they are also called sons of Agni. That is what is said here: these seers are बहुरूपाः (*bahurūpāḥ*), of many kinds of form; गंभीरवेपसः (*gaṃbhīravepasaḥ*) means doers of profound works, or of immeasurable intelligence. This is the meaning of the explanation.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये अ॒ग्नेः परि॑ जज्जि॒रे विरू॑पासो दि॒वस्परि॑ ।  
> नव॑गो॒ नु दश॑गो॒ अंगि॑रस्तमः॒ सचा॑ दे॒वेषु॑ मंहते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । अग्नेः । परि । जज्जिरे । विरूपासः । दिवः । परि ।  
> नवग्वः । नु । दशग्वः । अंगिरःतमः । सचा । देवेषु । मंहते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विरूपासो विविधरूपा येऽज्जिरसो दिवस्परि द्युलोकादग्नेः परि जज्जिरे
> परितो जाताः । यद्वा । दिवस्परि । परिः पंचम्यर्थद्योतकः । स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानादग्नेर्जाताः। तेषां मध्यॆ नवगो दशग्वश्चांगिरस्तमोऽंगिरसां वरिष्ठः। सत्रमासीनानामंगिरसां मध्यॆ केचन नवसु मास्सु कर्म कृत्योदतिष्मन् केचन दशसु
> मास्त्वत्येवमंगिरसामयनमुक्तं । तेषामग्निर्नवग्वश्च दशग्वश्चोक्तः । तादृशो
> देवेषु सचा सहावस्थितः सोऽग्निर्मंहते । मह्यं धनं प्रयच्छति । मंहतिर्दानकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Aṅgirases of various forms who were born around Agni from the heaven-world. Or else, दिवस्परि (*divaspari*): परि (*pari*) indicates the ablative sense; they were born of Agni shining with his own radiance. Among them नवग्व (*navagva*) and दशग्व (*daśagva*) are the foremost of the Aṅgirases. Of the Aṅgirases sitting at a sattra, some rose after performing the rite for nine months, some after ten; thus the Aṅgirases' session is described. Of them Agni is called navagva and daśagva. Such an Agni, abiding with the gods, मंहते (*maṃhate*): gives me wealth; मंहति (*maṃhati*) is a verb of giving.
### Printed p. 454

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विरूपासः (*virūpāsaḥ*)—having many kinds of forms
- ये अंगिरसः (*ye aṃgirasaḥ*)—which Aṅgirasa seers
- दिवः परि (*divaḥ pari*)—in the upper part of the heaven-world
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—from Agni
- परि जज्जिरे (*pari jajjire*)—were born (among such Aṅgirasa seers)
- नवग्वः (*navagvaḥ*)—those who completed the sattra in nine months
- दशग्वः (*daśagvaḥ*)—those who completed the sattra in ten months
- अंगिरस्तमः (*aṃgirastamaḥ*)—the foremost among the Aṅgirases are there
- देवेषु सचा (*deveṣu sacā*)—Agni, who is with the gods
- मंहते (*maṃhate*)—gives me wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirasa seers of many forms were born of Agni in the heaven-world. Some of them completed the sattra (to be done in a year) in nine months, some in ten months, and gained fame as the foremost of the Aṅgirases. Agni, who is with the gods, graciously gives me wealth and the like.

##### English translation
Among those who have sprung from Agni is many forms, (and sprung) from heaven, the chief Angirasas, the celebrator of the nine-month rite, the celebrator of the ten-month rite, accompanied by the gods bestows (upon me wealth).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For an explanation of the words navagva and daśagva, see Ṛ. Saṃ. pages 18-534 and 19-501.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रे॑ण यु॒जा निः सृ॑जंत वा॒घतो॑ व्र॒जं गोमं॑तम॒श्विनं॑।  
> स॒हस्रं॑ मे॒ दद॑तो अष्टक॒र्ण्य१॒॑१ः श्रवो॑ दे॒वेष्व॑क्रत ॥ ७ ॥

> सहस्रं । मे । ददतः । अष्टकर्ण्यः । श्रवः । देवेषु । अक्रत ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाघतः कर्मणां वोढारो विश्वे देवा अंगिरसो वेंद्रेण युजा सहायेन निः सृजंत । निरगमयन् । किं । गोमंतं गोयुक्तमश्विनमश्ववंतं पणिभि-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The वाघतः (*vāghataḥ*), bearers of the rites, namely all the gods or the Aṅgirases, with Indra as युजा (*yujā*) (helper), निः सृजंत (*niḥ sṛjaṃta*): led out the
### Printed p. 455

> रवरुद्धं व्रजं । ते मे मां प्रति सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याकं धनं सत्प्रपरिवेषणमष्टकर्ण्यः ॥ अष्ट इति अशू व्याप्त निष्ठायां रूपं ॥ विस्त्रतकर्णाः । उपलक्षणमेतत् ।
> व्याप्तसर्वावयवा गाश्च ददतो मह्यं प्रयच्छंतो देवेष्विंद्रादिषु श्रवो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं कीर्तिं वाक्रत अकृषत ॥ करोतेर्लुजि मंत्रे घसेति चेर्लुक् ॥
> एवं नाभानेदिष्टेनांगिरसः स्तुतास्तस्मै धनं प्रादुः। तदुक्तं शौनकेन। ऋषयोऽ०-
> गिरसस्तुष्टा यद्ददुर्मानवाय तु । तत्पुण्याय च कर्मणि ये यज्ञेनेत्यकीर्तयत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

pen व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*), full of cows and horses, which the Paṇis had confined. Those, giving me a thousand (सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)) of wealth, with cattle अष्टकर्ण्यः (*aṣṭakarṇyaḥ*): अष्ट (*aṣṭa*) is a form from the root अशू (*aśū*) in the sense of pervading, with the ending निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*); that is, broad-eared; this is indicative, meaning with all limbs full-grown. They, giving me cows, अक्रत (*akrata*) made, among the gods, Indra and the others, श्रवः (*śravaḥ*): food in the form of oblation, or renown. Thus the Aṅgirases, praised by Nābhānediṣṭha, gave him wealth. This was said by Śaunaka: — ऋषयोंगिरसस्तुष्टा यद्ददुर्मानवाय तु । तत्पुण्याय च कर्माणि ये यज्ञेनेत्यकीर्तयत् ॥ (*— ṛṣayoṃgirasastuṣṭā yaddadurmānavāya tu | tatpuṇyāya ca karmāṇi ye yajñenetyakīrtayat ‖*)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाघतः (*vāghataḥ*)—the Viśvedevas or Aṅgirasa seers who carry out the (sacrificial) rite
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—by Indra
- युजा (*yujā*)—and with his help
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—provided with cows
- अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)—provided with horses
- व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*)—the herd of cattle
- निः सृजंत (*niḥ sṛjaṃta*)—they brought out (from the mountain region where they were hidden)
- मे (*me*)—to me
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—a thousand
- अष्टकर्ण्यः (*aṣṭakarṇyaḥ*)—cows with long ears
- ददतः (*dadataḥ*)—wishing to give
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods, that is, directed to the gods, for completing the sacrifice
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food in the form of oblation
- अक्रत (*akrata*)—offered in the fire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirasa seers (or the Viśvedevas), the carriers of the sacrifice, with Indra's help freed the herd of cows and horses, which the asuras called Paṇis had stolen and hidden in a secret mountain region, and brought them out of that region. To give me a thousand long-eared cows, those Aṅgirases made offerings directed to the gods and completed the sacrifice.

##### English translation
The accepters of oblations, with Indra for their associate, have emptied pastures crowded with cows, and horses, giving me a thousand full-grown (cattle), they have gained renown among the gods,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk refers to the Aṅgirases giving a thousand cows to Nābhānediṣṭha at the conclusion of the sattra they were performing. On this matter the sage Śaunaka says in his work Bṛhaddevatā:
ऋषयोंगिरसस्तुष्टा यद्ददुर्मानवाय तु । (*ṛṣayoṃgirasastuṣṭā yaddadurmānavāya tu |*)
तत्पुण्याय च कर्माणि ये यज्ञेनेत्यकीर्तयत् ॥ (*tatpuṇyāya ca karmāṇi ye yajñenetyakīrtayat ‖*)
### Printed p. 456
That is, the Aṅgirases, pleased with the mantra recited by Nābhānediṣṭha, gave him cows. Nābhānediṣṭha described this in the present sūkta beginning ये यज्ञेन (*ye yajñena*).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र नू॒नं जा॑यताम॒यं मनु॒स्तोक्मे॑व रोहतु ।  
> यः स॒हस्रं॑ श॒ताश्वं॑ स॒द्यो दा॒नाय॒ मुंह॑ते ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । नूनं । जायतां । अयं । मनुः । तोक्मइव । रोहतु ।  
> यः । सहस्रं । शत्रुअश्वं । सद्यः । दानाय । मंहते ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत्तराभिश्चतसृभिरस्मै मानवायर्षये सावर्णिना यद्दत्तं तत्पशस्यते । तदप्युक्तं शौनकेन । सावर्णिना च यद्दत्तं मानवाय महद्वसु । तदुक्तं सूक्तशेषेण
> प्र नूनं जायतामिति ॥
> अयं सावर्णिर्मनुर्नुनं क्षिप्रं प्र जायतां । प्रजातो भवतु धनादिभिः
> पुत्रादिभिश्च रोहतु । प्रादुर्भवतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । तोक्मेव । यथा जलक्लिन्नं
> बीजं प्रादुर्भवति एवं कर्मफलसंयुक्तः स मनुः पुत्रादिभी रोहतु । योऽयं
> मनुः शताश्वं बहश्वसंयुक्तं सहस्रं गवां सद्यस्तदानीमेव दानाय मंहते ।
> आस्मा ऋषये दातुं प्रेरयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the four following Ṛks, what Sāvarṇi gave to this seer, the son of Manu, is praised. Śaunaka also said so: सावर्णिना च यद्दत्तं मानवाय महद्वसु । तदुक्तं सूक्तशेषेण प्र नूनं जायतामिति ॥ (*sāvarṇinā ca yaddattaṃ mānavāya mahadvasu | taduktaṃ sūktaśeṣeṇa pra nūnaṃ jāyatāmiti ‖*) This Sāvarṇi Manu, quickly प्र जायतां (*pra jāyatāṃ*): let him be born forth, and with wealth and sons रोहतु (*rohatu*): let him arise. The illustration is तोक्मेव (*tokmeva*): as a seed soaked in water sprouts, so let that Manu, endowed with the fruit of his works, arise with sons and the rest. This Manu, who सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*) at that very moment impels the giving of a thousand cows with a hundred horses, मंहते (*maṃhate*): urges to give to this seer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this (Manu) called Sāvarṇi
- मनुः (*manuḥ*)—Manu
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—quickly
- प्र जायतां (*pra jāyatāṃ*)—let him be born forth
- तोक्मेव (*tokmeva*)—as a seed soaked in water quickly sprouts (so may this Sāvarṇi, with wealth and sons)
- रोहतु (*rohatu*)—let him arise
- यः (*yaḥ*)—(who) this Manu
- शताश्वं (*śatāśvaṃ*)—many horses
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—thousands of cows
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—right now
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—for giving to this seer
- मुंहते (*muṃhate*)—impels

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this Manu called Sāvarṇi, who impels the giving to this seer of many horses and thousands of cows, accompanied by his sons and wealth, be born forth right now, like a seed soaked in water quickly sprouting.
### Printed p. 457

##### English translation
May this Manu (Savarni) quickly be born, may he increase like (well-watered) seed, who sends me at once a thousand and a hundred horses for a present.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and in the next three Ṛks, there is praise of the gift made to the seer by the Manu called Sāvarṇi. Śaunaka too has said:
सावर्णिना च यद्दत्तं मानवाय महद्वसु । (*sāvarṇinā ca yaddattaṃ mānavāya mahadvasu |*)
तदुक्तं सूक्तशेषेण प्र नूनं जायतामिति ॥ (*taduktaṃ sūktaśeṣeṇa pra nūnaṃ jāyatāmiti ‖*)
That is, the wealth given by the Manu called Sāvarṇi to Nābhānediṣṭha, son of Manu, is praised in the Ṛks of the present sūkta from प्र नूनं जायतां (*pra nūnaṃ jāyatāṃ*) to the end of the sūkta.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न तम॑श्नोति॒ कश्च॒न दि॒व इ॑व॒ सान्वा॒रभं॑ ।  
> सा॒व॒र्णस्य॒ दक्षि॑णा॒ वि सिंधु॑रिन पप्रथे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । तं । अश्नोति । कः । चन । दिवःऽइव । सानु । आऽरभं ।  
> सावर्ण्यस्य । दक्षिणा । वि । सिंधुऽइव । पप्रथे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं सावर्णीं मनुं कश्चन कश्चिदप्यारभमारुब्धुं स्वकर्मणा नाश्नोति । न व्याप्नोति । यथा मनुः प्रयच्छति तथान्यो दातुं न शक्नोतीत्यर्थः । कथंस्थितं । दिव
> इव द्युलोकस्य सानु समुच्च्रितं तेजसा कैश्चिदप्यप्रधृष्यमादित्यमिन स्थितं ॥ आरभं ।
> शकि णमुल्कमुलौ । पा. ३-४-१२. । इति कमुल् ॥ तस्य सावर्ण्यस्य मनोरियं गवादिदक्षिणा सिंधुरिव स्यंदमाना नदीव पृथिव्यां पप्रथे । विपप्रथे । विस्तीर्णा भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

No one कश्चन (*kaścana*) can reach, आरभं (*ārabhaṃ*), that is, climb up to or equal, that Sāvarṇi Manu by his own work; as Manu gives, so another cannot give. How is he placed? Like the सानु (*sānu*), the summit of the heaven-world, lofty, unassailable by any in his radiance, like the Āditya. आरभं (*ārabhaṃ*): with the affix कमुल् (*kamul*) (Pā. 3-4-12). The gift of cows and the rest from that Sāvarṇi Manu has spread out widely over the earth, like a flowing river सिंधु (*siṃdhu*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिव इव (*diva iva*)—like the Āditya shining in heaven
- सानु (*sānu*)—seated in a lofty place by his own radiance
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Manu called Sāvarṇi
- आरभं (*ārabhaṃ*)—to equal in gifts and other works
- कश्चन (*kaścana*)—no person
- न अश्नोति (*na aśnoti*)—is able
- सावर्ण्यस्य (*sāvarṇyasya*)—of Sāvarṇi

### Printed p. 458
- *sāvarṇyasya*—of that Manu (Sāvarṇi)
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—the gifts and the like
- सिंधुरिव (*siṃdhuriva*)—like a flowing river
- वि पप्रथे (*vi paprathe*)—spreads out widely everywhere

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

No other man is able to give as the Manu called Sāvarṇi gives, who sits on a lofty place and shines like the sun shining in heaven. The gifts of cows and the like made by that Manu called Sāvarṇi spread out everywhere and become widely extended, like a flowing river.

##### English translation
No one succeeds in reaching him; (elevated) like the summit of heaven, the liberality of Savarni has broadened out like a river.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त दा॒सा प॑रि॒विषे॒ स्मद्दि॑ष्टी॒ गोप॑रीणसा ।  
> यदु॑स्तु॒र्वश्च॑ मामहे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । दासा । परिविषे । स्मद्दिष्टी इति स्मत् ऽदिष्टी । गोपरीणसा ।  
> यदुः । तुर्वः । च । ममहे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च स्मद्दिष्टी कल्याणादेशिनौ गोपरीणसा गोपरीणसौ गोभिः परिवृता
> बहुगवादियुक्ता दासा दासवत्पेष्यवत्स्थितौ तेनाधिष्ठितौ यदुश्च तुर्वश्चैतन्नामका
> राजर्षी परिविषेऽस्य सावर्णेर्मनोर्भोजनाय ममहे । पशून्प्रयच्छतः ॥
> प्रत्येकमन्वयादेकवचनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Also" (उत (*uta*)): the two who speak auspicious words (स्मद्दिष्टी (*smaddiṣṭī*)), who are surrounded by cows (गोपरीणसा (*goparīṇasā*)), that is, who have many cows and the like, stand as servants (दासा (*dāsā*)) like attendants, ruled over by him. Yadu and Turvaśa, royal sages of those names, give animals for the meal (परिविषे (*pariviṣe*)) of this Manu Sāvarṇi (ममहे (*mamahe*)). The singular verb is used because the construction applies to each of them separately.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- स्मद्दिष्टी (*smaddiṣṭī*)—those whose speech is auspicious
- गोपरीणसा (*goparīṇasā*)—those accompanied by many cows
- दासा (*dāsā*)—those who render service
- यदुः (*yaduḥ*)—Yadu
- तुर्वश्च (*turvaśca*)—and Turva
- परिविषे (*pariviṣe*)—for Sāvarṇi's enjoyment
- ममहे (*mamahe*)—provided animals

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Yadu and Turva, whose speech is auspicious, who are accompanied by many cows and who render service, provided animals for Sāvarṇi's enjoyment.

### Printed p. 459

##### English translation
Yadu and Indra speaking auspiciously, and possessed of numerous cattle, gave them like (appointed) servants, for the enjoyment (of Manu Savarni) **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒ह॒स्र॒दा ग्रा॑म॒णीर्मा रि॑ष॒न्मनुः॒ सूर्ये॑णास्य॒ यत॑मानैतु॒  ॑
> दक्षिणा ।  
> साव॑णेर्दे॒वाः प्र ति॑रं॒त्वायु॒र्यस्मि॒न्नश्रां॑ता॒ अस॑नाम॒  ॑
> वाजं ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्रदाः । ग्रामनीः । मा । रिषत् । मनुः । सूर्येण । अस्य । यतमाना । एतु ।  
> दक्षिणा ।  
> सावर्णेः । देवाः । प्र । तिरंतु । आयुः । यस्मिन् । अश्रांताः । असनाम । वाजं ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्रदा गवादीनां सहस्रस्य दाता ग्रामणीर्ग्रामाणां नेता कर्ता जनपदानामयं मनुर्मा रिषत् । न कैश्चिदपि रिष्टो हिंसितो भवतु । यद्वा । कर्मनेत्यनस्मान्मा हिनस्तु किंतु धनादिदानेन पूजयशु । अस्य यतमाना गच्छंती दक्षिणासूर्येण सहैतु । संगच्छतां । त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रसिद्धा भवत्वित्यर्थः । तस्यास्य
> सावर्णॆः सवर्णपुत्रस्य मनोर्देवा इंद्रादय आयुर्जीवनं प्र तिरंतु । प्रवर्धयंतु । अश्रांताः कर्मन्वनलसाः सर्वं कर्म कुर्वंतो वयं यस्मिन्मन् वाजं
> गोलक्षणमन्नमसनाम संभजेमहि । नाभानेदिष्टोऽहमलभ इत्याशास्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Giver of a thousand" (सहस्रदा (*sahasradā*)) is the giver of a thousand cows and the like; "leader of villages" (ग्रामणीः (*grāmaṇīḥ*)) is the leader or maker of the districts. May this Manu not be harmed (मा रिषत् (*mā riṣat*)) by anyone. Or else: the text here is damaged, but the sense seems to be that he should not harm us but honour us by giving wealth and the like **NOTE**. May his dakṣiṇā, going forth and striving, go together with the sun, that is, become famous in the three worlds. May the gods, Indra and the others, prolong (प्र तिरंतु (*pra tiraṃtu*)), that is, increase, the life of Sāvarṇi, the Manu who is the son of Savarṇa. We, unwearied in rites and doing all work, in whom (that is, through whose favour) we may enjoy (असनाम (*asanāma*)) food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)) of the nature of cows: so he expresses the hope, adding नाभानेदिष्टोऽहमलभ (*nābhānediṣṭo 'hamalabha*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहस्रदाः (*sahasradāḥ*)—one who makes many gifts
- ग्रामणीः (*grāmaṇīḥ*)—a guide to all the villagers
- मनुः (*manuḥ*)—the Manu
- मा रिषत् (*mā riṣat*)—may he not be harmed by anyone
- अस्य (*asya*)—by him
- यतमाना (*yatamānā*)—given generously
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—the dakṣiṇā
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—with the sun
- एतु (*etu*)—may it join (may it become famous in the three worlds)
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in whom (through whose generosity)
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—the food of the nature of cows
- आश्रांताः (*āśrāṃtāḥ*)—we who are not slack in rites

### Printed p. 460
- असनाम (*asanāma*)—we shall enjoy; such
- सावर्णेः (*sāvarṇeḥ*)—to the Manu who is the son of Savarṇa
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- प्रति तिरंतु (*prati tiraṃtu*)—may they increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Sāvarṇi Manu, who makes many gifts and is a guide to all the villagers, not be harmed by anyone. May the dakṣiṇā generously given by him go together with the sun and gain fame in all three worlds. May Indra and the other gods increase the life of that Manu, the son of Savarṇa, through whose generosity we, not slack in rites, enjoy food of the nature of cows.

##### English translation
May the donor of a thousand (cows), the head of the district, the Manu, never suffer wrong, may his liberality go spreading (in glory) with the sun ; may the gods prolong the life of Savarni (from whom) unwearied (in his service) we enjoy abundant food.

## Sūkta 63 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परावतो य इति सप्तदशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं प्लतेः पुत्रस्य गयस्यार्षं ।
> षोडशीसप्तदश्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ । पंचदशी त्रिष्टुब्बगती वा । शिष्टाश्चतुर्दश जगत्यः । स्वस्ति
> नः पथ्यास्त्विति द्वे पथ्यास्वस्ति देवताके । शिष्टा वैश्वदेव्यः। तथा चानुक्रांतं । परावतस्कृना गयः प्लातो द्वित्रिष्टुबंतं तु स्वस्ति नस्त्रिष्टुब्बा सह चोत्तरया पथ्यास्वस्तिदेवत्येति ॥ पृष्ठाभिप्लवयोस्तृतीयेऽहनि वैश्वदेव एतत्तूक्तं वैश्वदेवं निविद्धानं । सूत्रितं च । अनश्वो जातः परावतो य इति वैश्वदेवं । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning परावतो य (*parāvato ya*) has seventeen Ṛks and is the third sūkta. It is the vision of Gaya, son of Plati. The sixteenth and seventeenth verses are in Triṣṭubh; the fifteenth is Triṣṭubh or Jagatī; the remaining fourteen are Jagatī. The two verses beginning स्वस्ति नः पथ्यासु (*svasti naḥ pathyāsu*) have Pathyāsvasti as deity; the rest are addressed to the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇī says the same. At the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava rites, on the third day, in the Vaiśvadeva, this sūkta is the Vaiśvadeva nivid-dhāna. It is prescribed by the sūtra Ā. 7-7.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "परावतो ये (*parāvato ye*)" is the third sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has seventeen Ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Gaya, son of the ṛṣi called Plata. The sixteenth and seventeenth Ṛks of this sūkta have the Triṣṭubh metre; the fifteenth has Triṣṭubh or Jagatī; the remaining fourteen Ṛks are in Jagatī. The two Ṛks beginning "स्वस्ति नः पथ्यासु (*svasti naḥ pathyāsu*)" (Ṛks 15–16) have Pathyāsvasti as deity; the remaining Ṛks have the Viśvedevas as deity. This is what is said in the Anukramaṇikā.

### Printed p. 461
On the third day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, in the Vaiśvadeva śastra mantras, this sūkta is to be recited as the Vaiśvadeva nivid-dhāna sūkta; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 7-7).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 63. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 2; Vargas 3, 4, 5. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 17. Ṛṣi: Gaya Plāta. Deity: 1–14, 17, Viśvedevas; 15, 16, Pathyāsvasti. Metre: 1–14, Jagatī; 15, Jagatī or Triṣṭubh; 16–17, Triṣṭubh. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒रा॒वतो॒ ये दिधि॑षंत॒ आप्यं॒ मनु॑प्रीतासो॒ जनि॑मा वि॒वस्व॑तः।  
> य॒यात्रे॒र्यॆ न॑हु॒ष्य॑स्य ब॒र्हिषि॑ दे॒वा आस॑ते॒ ते अधि॑ ब्रुवंतु नः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परावतः । ये । दिधिषंते । आप्यं । मनुप्रीतासः । जनिम । विवस्वतः ।  
> ययातेः । ये । नहुष्यस्य । बर्हिषि । देवाः । आसते । ते । अधि । ब्रुवंतु । नः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये देवाः परावतो दूरदेशादागत्याप्यं ज्ञातेयं मनुष्यैः सह
> बंधुत्वं दिधिषंते धारयंति । यद्वा । हविषां प्रदातृभिर्मनुष्यैः सह सख्यं
> कुर्म इति परस्परं शब्दायंते ॥ धिष शब्दे । चौहोत्यादिकः । छांदसो झस्यांतादेशः । धिष धारण इति कैश्चिदप्युपगम्यते ॥ उक्तार्थमेव विशिनष्टि । दुनुप्रीतासो
> मनुष्यैः प्रीता देवा विवस्वतो विवस्वत्पुत्रस्य मनोर्जनिम जन्मानि मनुष्यान्धारयंति । किंच ये देवा नहुष्यस्य नहुषपुत्रस्य ययातेरेतन्नामकस्य राजर्षेर्बर्हिषि यज्ञ आसते उपविंशति ते देवा नोऽस्मानधि ब्रुवंतु । धनादिप्रदानेनास्मानधिकं वदंतु । पूजयंत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods who come from a distant place (परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)) hold (दिधिषंते (*didhiṣaṃte*)) kinship (आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)) with men. Or else: they call to one another, "We make friendship with the men who offer oblations." The gods, pleased by men (मनुप्रीतासः (*manuprītāsaḥ*)), support the births (जनिम (*janima*)), that is, the men, of Manu, the son of Vivasvat. Further, the gods who sit on the sacred grass, that is at the sacrifice, of the royal sage Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, may those gods speak above (अधि ब्रुवंतु (*adhi bruvaṃtu*)) us, that is, speak of us as superior by the gift of wealth and the like; may they honour us.

- मनुप्रीतासः (*manuprītāsaḥ*)—those who are the objects of men's love
- ये (*ye*)—which gods
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—of the Manu, son of Vivasvat
- जनिम (*janima*)—supporting the births (the offspring)
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—coming from a very distant place
- आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)—the kinship with men
- दिधिषंते (*didhiṣaṃte*)—make manifest
- ये देवाः (*ye devāḥ*)—the gods who
- नहुष्यस्य (*nahuṣyasya*)—of the son of Nahuṣa
- ययातेः (*yayāteḥ*)—of the royal sage called Yayāti
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—at the sacrifice
- आसते (*āsate*)—sit
- ते (*te*)—those gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अधि ब्रुवंतु (*adhi bruvaṃtu*)—may they praise (may they favour)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May those gods who are dear to men, who support the offspring of Manu, the son of Vivasvat, who come from a very distant place and make manifest their kinship with men, and who sit at the sacrifice of the royal sage Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, praise our rites and favour us.

##### English translation
May the gods who, (coming) from afar proclaim their affinity (with men), and beloved by men, (support) the generations of (Manu, the son of) Vivaswat ; may they who are seated on the sacred grass of Yayati, the son of Nahusha, speak favourably unto us.

> ये देवा इंद्रादयः । हिरवधारणे । वो युष्माकमेव नामानि नमनीयानि विश्वा सर्वाणि शरीराणि नमस्यानि नमस्करार्हाणि भवंति वंद्या वंद्यानि स्तोतव्यानि च भवंति । ये यूयमदितेरदीनाद्दुलोकादद्भ्यः । अंतरक्षनामैतत् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, Indra and the others: हि (*hi*) is for emphasis. Your names alone are to be bowed to; all your bodies (विश्वा (*viśvā*)) are worthy of salutation (नमस्यानि (*namasyāni*)), and are adorable and to be praised (वंद्या (*vaṃdyā*)). You who are born (जाताः (*jātāḥ*)) from Aditi, that is the undivided heaven, from the waters (अद्भ्यः (*adbhyaḥ*); this is a name of the atmosphere), and from the earth, having become manifest: come here to this sacrifice and hear (श्रुत (*śruta*)) my invocation. The word परि (*pari*) marks the ablative sense.

- ये (*ye*)—you all who
- अदितेः परि (*aditeḥ pari*)—from the undivided heaven
- अद्भ्यः (*adbhyaḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—from the earth

- ते (*te*)—you all
- इह (*iha*)—coming here to this our sacrifice
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—invocation
- श्रुत (*śruta*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and the other gods, all kinds of your forms are worthy of salutation, of praise and of sacrifice. All of you who are born from the undivided heaven, from the atmosphere and from the earth, come to this our sacrifice and hear my invocation.

##### English translation
All your appellations, gods, are to be revered and praised, and worshipped, and whether you are sprung from heaven, or from the firma-ment, or from earth, hear at this (solemnity) my invocation.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> येभ्यो॑ मा॒ता मधु॑म॒त्पिन्व॑ते॒ पयः॑ पी॒यूषं॒ द्यौरदि॑ति॒रद्रि॑बर्हाः ।  
> उ॒क्तशु॑ष्मान्वृषभ॒रान्तन्वप्न॑स॒स्ता आ॑दि॒त्या अनु॑ मदा स्व॒स्तये॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> येभ्यः । माता । मधुमत् । पिन्वते । पयः । पीयूषं । द्यौः । अदितिः ।  
> अद्रिबर्हाः ।

> उक्तशुष्मान् । वृषभरान् । सुअप्नसः । तान् । आदित्यान् । अनु मद । स्वस्तये ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निष्टोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे येभ्यो मातेत्येषाधाय्या । सूत्रितं च । अयं
> वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भा येभ्यो माता मधुमत् । अ-५-१८ । इति ॥
> माता सर्वस्य निर्मात्री पृथिवी येभ्यो देवेभ्यो देवार्थं मधुमद्माधुर्योपेतं पयः सारभूतं क्षीरं पिन्वते क्षरति । तथादितिरदीनाद्रिबर्हा मेघैः
> परिवृद्धा प्रवृद्धा परिवृद्धमेघा वा द्यौश्च पीयूषं पिन्वते । द्यावापृथिव्यौ हविरुत्पादयत इत्यर्थः । ऋषिरात्मानं संबोध्याह । उक्तशुष्मानतिबलान् वृषभरान्वृष्टेराहर्त्यन् ॥ हृग्रहोर्भ इति भः ॥ स्वप्नसः सुकर्मणस्तनादित्यानदितेः पुत्रान्देवान् स्वस्तयेऽविनाशयानु मद । अनुस्तुहि ॥ माद्यशेर्लोटि व्यत्ययेन शप् ।
> मंदतेर्वा स्तुत्यर्थसानित्यमागमशासनमिति नुमभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Agniṣṭoma, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, this Ṛk येभ्यो माता (*yebhyo mātā*) is the dhāyyā. It is prescribed in the sūtra अयं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भा येभ्यो माता मधुमत् (*ayaṃ venaścodayatpṛśnigarbhā yebhyo mātā madhumat*) (Ā. Sū. 5-18). The mother, the earth that fashions all, yields for those gods sweet, essential milk. Likewise Aditi, undiminished, grown great with clouds (or with grown clouds), and heaven yield ambrosia: heaven and earth produce the oblation. The seer addresses himself: praise the Ādityas, whose strength is praise, who are the bringers of rain, the doers of good deeds, the sons of Aditi, and delight them for welfare, that is, for freedom from destruction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येभ्यः (*yebhyaḥ*)—for which deities
- माता (*mātā*)—the earth, maker of the world
- मधुमत् (*madhumat*)—sweet
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- पिन्वते (*pinvate*)—supplies (and likewise)
- अद्रिबर्हाः (*adribarhāḥ*)—encompassed by clouds
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—undivided
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the heavenly world
- पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)—supplies ambrosia, such (deities)
- वृषभरान् (*vṛṣabharān*)—those who bear rain
- उक्तशुष्मान् (*uktaśuṣmān*)—whose strength is the fruit of praise
- स्वप्नसः (*svapnasaḥ*)—of good works
- तान् आदित्यान् (*tān ādityān*)—those Ādityas
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for welfare
- अनु मद (*anu mada*)—praise and gratify

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praise and gratify those Ādityas, bringers of rain, whose strength is the fruit of praise, doers of good works, for whom the earth, maker of the world, supplies sweet milk, and for whom heaven, encompassed by clouds and undivided, supplies ambrosia; thereby you will have welfare.

##### English translation
To (these deities) to whom the maternal (earth) yields the sweet-flavoured milk, and the cloud-invested, undepressed heaven (yields) ambrosia, to those Adityas whose strength is sacred praise, who are the bringers of rain, the doers of good actions, offer for your welfare laudation.

### Printed p. 465

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, when the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, this Ṛk येभ्यो माता (*yebhyo mātā*) is to be recited as the dhāyyā mantra; this is made clear by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अयं वेनश्चोदयत्प्रश्निगर्भा येभ्यो माता मधुमत् (*ayaṃ venaścodayatpraśnigarbhā yebhyo mātā madhumat*) (Ā. 5-18).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नृ॒चक्ष॑सो॒ अनि॑मिषंतो अ॒र्हणा॑ बृ॒हद्दे॒वासो॑ अमृत॒त्वमा॑नशुः ।  
> ज्यो॒तीर॑था॒ अहि॑माया॒ अना॑गसो दि॒वो व॒ष्माणं॑ वसते  ॒॑
> स्वस्तये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नृचक्षसः । अनिमिषंतः । अर्हणा । बृहत् । देवासः । अमृतत्वं । आनशुः ।  
> ज्योतिःरथाः । अहिमायाः । अनागसः । दिवः । वर्ष्णाणं । वसते । स्वस्तये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नृचक्षसः कर्मनेत्यणां मनुष्याणां द्रष्टारः अत एवानिमिषंतो निमेषमकुर्वाणाः सर्वदा जागरूका देवासो देवा अर्हणा लोकस्य परिचरणार्थं
> स्तोतव्यत्वाय बृहद्बृंहितममृतत्वममरणधर्ममानशुः । प्राप्ताः । देवाः खलु
> मनुष्यैः पूज्याः । तस्मात्तूजाहेतुं देवत्वमानशिरे । आत एव ज्योतीरथा दीप्यमानरथोपेता अहिमायाः कैश्चितप्यहंतव्यप्रज्ञा अनागसः पापरहिता आदित्या दिवो
> द्युलोकस्य वर्ष्णाणं नाभिस्थानं समुच्च्रितं देशं स्वस्तयेऽविनाशाय लोकस्य
> क्षेमकरणार्थं वसते । अधिवसंति । यद्वा । स्वतेजसाच्छादयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods are नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*), beholders of men, the leaders of rites; hence अनिमिषंतः (*animiṣaṃtaḥ*), not winking, ever watchful. For the world's service, to be worthy of praise, they have attained great immortality, the state of not dying. Gods are indeed worshipped by men, so they attained godhood as the cause of worship. Hence the Ādityas, with shining chariots, of wisdom that none can strike down, sinless, dwell in the navel-place of heaven, a lofty region, for the welfare, the safety, of the world. Or else: they cover it with their own radiance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनिमिषंतः (*animiṣaṃtaḥ*)—those who are watchful without closing the eyelids
- नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*)—who can see the conduct of men
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- अर्हणा (*arhaṇā*)—having obtained fitness for the oblation
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—very great
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—freedom from death
- आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*)—have acquired
- ज्योतीरथाः (*jyotīrathāḥ*)—having a chariot of radiance
- अहिमायाः (*ahimāyāḥ*)—of unassailable wisdom

### Printed p. 466
- अनागसः (*anāgasaḥ*)—sinless Ādityas
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- वर्ष्णाणं (*varṣṇāṇaṃ*)—in the very lofty region
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for the welfare of the world
- वसते (*vasate*)—dwell

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, watchful without closing their eyelids and able to see the conduct of men, having obtained fitness for the oblation, have attained great freedom from death. The Ādityas, with chariots of radiance, of unassailable wisdom, sinless, dwell in the loftiest region of heaven for the welfare of the world.

##### English translation
The gods, the never-slumbering beholders of mankind, and entitled (to their adoration), have abtained great immortality : conveyed in chariots of light, possessed of unsurpassaable wisdom, devoid of sin, they inhabit the exalted station of heaven for the well-being (of the world).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सम्राजः (*samrājaḥ*) are kings of all, shining well by their own radiance; सुवृधः (*suvṛdhaḥ*), well grown. The gods who come to the sacrifice to partake of the oblation of Soma and the rest, and who, अपरिह्वृताः (*aparihvṛtāḥ*), injured by none, make their dwelling in heaven. The seer addresses himself: महः (*mahaḥ*), great through excess of qualities, those well-known Ādityas, sons of Aditi,

> परिचरणकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

and Aditi, their mother, so named, for welfare, that is, freedom from destruction, serve with नमसा (*namasā*), the oblation in the form of food, and with सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*), fair praises. विवास (*vivāsa*) means: wait on them face to face; विवासतिः (*vivāsatiḥ*) is a verb of service.

- सम्राजः (*samrājaḥ*)—lords of the whole world

- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heavenly world
- क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)—a dwelling-place
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—have taken, they
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- आययुः (*āyayuḥ*)—have come
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of great qualities
- आदित्यान् (*ādityān*)—sons of Aditi

- नमसा (*namasā*)—with oblations
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with excellent praises
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for welfare
- आ विवास (*ā vivāsa*)—the seer worships

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods who are lords of the whole world, greatly grown, subject to no one's harm, and who have their dwelling in the heavenly world, have come to the sacrifice. Those gods, of great qualities and sons of Aditi, and Aditi, the seer serves for welfare with oblations and excellent praises.

##### English translation
The gods, who, kings over all, and most exalted, have come to the sacrifice, who, uuassailable, abide in heaven : them, the mighty Adityas, (the sage) worships with reverence, and with praises, and also Aditi, for his well-being.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिर्देवान्प्रति बहुधा वितर्कयति । हे देवाः वो युष्माकं कः स्तोतास्तोमं त्रिवृत्पंचदशादिलक्षणं राधति । संसाधयति । न कश्चिदस्तीत्यर्थः । यद्वा ।
> मदन्यः को वो युष्मभ्यं स्तोमं करोति । यूयं यं स्तोतारं जुजोषथ
> सेवध्वे ॥ जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । लेटि शवः श्लुः । अडागमः ॥ किं च हे मनुषो
> मंतारो ज्ञातारो हे विश्वे देवासो देवाः यूयं यति यत्संख्याः स्थन भवथ॥
> यच्छब्दादपि छांदसो डतिद्र्रष्टव्यः ॥ हे तुविजाता धात्रादिविभागेन बहुजनना हे
> देवाः युष्मदर्धं को वा यजमानोऽध्वरं यज्ञमरं करत् । अलंकरोति स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिश्च । मदन्यो नास्तीत्यर्थः । यो यज्यो नोऽस्मान् स्वस्तयेऽविनाशाया०हः पापरूपं मार्गमवैदिकमति पर्षत् अतिपारयति तं यज्ञं को वालंकरोतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer reflects in many ways about the gods. O gods, which praiser of yours offers the stoma, of the trivṛt, pañcadaśa and other kinds? None does. Or else: who other than I makes a stoma for you, the praiser whom you favour? Further, O मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*), thinkers, knowers, O all-gods, how many of you are there? The suffix of यति (*yati*) is to be seen as Vedic, from the word यत् (*yat*). O तुविजाता (*tuvijātā*), of many births through the division into Dhātṛ and the rest: which sacrificer adorns, makes sufficient, for you the sacrifice with praises and oblations? None but I. The sacrifice that carries us, for welfare, beyond अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*), the path of sin, the non-Vedic way: who adorns that sacrifice?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O gods) यं (*yaṃ*)—which praiser
- जुजोषथ (*jujoṣatha*)—you favour, such
- कः (*kaḥ*)—which praiser
- वः (*vaḥ*)—addressing you
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the stoma, trivṛt and the rest
- राधति (*rādhati*)—offers (who but I can offer it?)
- विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)—O all-gods
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—you, excellent knowers
- यति स्थन (*yati sthana*)—how many are you
- तुविजाताः (*tuvijātāḥ*)—O gods of many kinds of birth
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrifice
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our welfare
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—the boundary of sin
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—carries across, such
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—the sacrifice
- वः (*vaḥ*)—for you
- कः (*kaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- अरं करत् (*araṃ karat*)—adorns with oblations and the like

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, who but I offers to you the stoma of trivṛt and the rest, being the praiser whom you favour? O all-gods, excellent knowers, how many of you are there? O gods of many births, which sacrificer adorns for you with oblations and the like (performs) the sacrifice that carries us across the boundary of sin for our welfare?

Who offers you the praise which you like, you wise, universal deities, however many you may be ? Deities from whom many are born, who can

prepare for you such worship as may bear us safe beyond iniquity for our well-being ?

> त आ॑दित्या॒ अभ॑यं॒ शर्म॑ यच्छत सु॒गा नः॑ कर्त सु॒पथा॑  ॒॑

> होतृभिः ।  
> ते । आदित्याः । अभयं । शर्म । यच्छत । सुगा । नः । कर्त । सुपथा । स्वस्तये ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समिद्दाग्निर्हविर्भिः सम्यग्ग्रीप्ताग्निर्मनुर्वैवस्वतो मनुष्याणां प्रथमभावी
> श्रद्दधानेन मनसा सप्त सप्तसंख्याकैर्होतृभिर्वषट्कर्तृभिर्युत्विग्भिश्च सह येभ्यो
> युष्मभ्यं प्रथमां द्रथमं मुख्यं यद्वा सर्वॆषां मनुष्याणामग्रे क्रियमाणत्वादाद्यं होत्रां । हूयंते हवींष्यत्रेति होत्रा यज्ञः । तं । यद्वा ।
> आहूयंते देवाः स्तुतिभिरत्रेति । तं यज्ञमायेजे अभिमुख्यनेष्टवान् ॥ यजेर्लिटि रूपं । यद्वा । लिटि लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः । यजिवपोरलिट्येत्वं
> वक्तव्यं । का. ६-४-१२०-४ । इति वचनादेकारः ॥ हे आदित्या अदितेः पुत्रा हे देवाः
> ते यूयं नोस्मभ्यमभयं शर्म च सुखं प्रयच्छत । किंच नोऽस्माकं स्वस्तये क्षेमाय सुपथा सुपथानि शोभनान्वैदिकमार्गान् सुगा सुष्टु गंतव्यान्
> कर्त । कुरुत ॥ करोतेर्लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । तबादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

समिद्धाग्निः (*samiddhāgniḥ*) is Manu Vaivasvata, first of men, whose fire is well kindled with oblations. With a mind full of faith and with seven hotṛs, the performers of the vaṣaṭ, and priests, he performed for you the होत्रां (*hotrāṃ*), the sacrifice, which is first, chief, or, being performed before all men, foremost. होत्रा (*hotrā*) is the sacrifice in which oblations are offered; or else, in which the gods are invoked with praises. आयेजे (*āyeje*) means he sacrificed facing them. O Ādityas, sons of Aditi, O gods, give us fearlessness and शर्म (*śarma*), happiness. And for our welfare make fair Vedic paths, easy to travel.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनुः (*manuḥ*)—Manu
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with meditation
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven
- होतृभिः (*hotṛbhiḥ*)—together with hotṛs
- येभ्यः (*yebhyaḥ*)—addressing which of you
- होत्रां (*hotrāṃ*)—the sacrifice

- ते (*te*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अभयं (*abhayaṃ*)—fearlessness
- शर्म (*śarma*)—and happiness

- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for welfare
- सुपथा (*supathā*)—good Vedic paths
- सुगा (*sugā*)—easy to travel
- कर्त (*karta*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adityas, sons of Aditi, you to whom Manu, having made the fire blaze with oblations, then with meditation and together with the seven Hotṛs, offered the sacrifice: grant us fearlessness and happiness. For our welfare, make the good Vedic paths easy to travel (so that we may follow them).

##### English translation
Adityas, to whom Manu, having kindled the fire, offered the first sacrifice with (reverent) mind, (aided) by the seven ministrant priests, bestow upon us prosperity, free from peril; provide for us pleasant paths easy to travel for our well-being.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The matter of the seven Hotṛs is explained in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 15, page 693.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods who are far-knowing (प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*)) and all-knowing (मंतवः (*maṃtavaḥ*)) are lords of the whole world, of the immovable and the moving. Addressing them directly: O gods, you who have these qualities, from sin committed (by the body)….

### Printed p. 471

> पात् अकृतात्करचरणादिभिरकृतादेनसः किंतु मानसात्पापाच्चाद्यास्मिन्निने स्वस्तयेऽविनाशायायुषोऽभिवृद्धये पिपृत । पारयत पापरहितान्कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…from sin committed, and from sin not committed by hands, feet and the like, but mental sin; today, for our welfare, i.e. for non-destruction and the increase of life, carry us across (पिपृत (*pipṛta*)), that is, make us free from sin.

- ये (*ye*)—you who
- स्थातुः (*sthātuḥ*)—of the immovable
- जगतः (*jagataḥ*)—and the moving
- विश्वस्य भुवनस्य (*viśvasya bhuvanasya*)—of the entire world
- ईशिरे (*īśire*)—are lords; such
- ते (*te*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- कृतात् (*kṛtāt*)—from what we have done
- अकृतात् (*akṛtāt*)—and what is not done with the hands and the like
- एनसः परि (*enasaḥ pari*)—from sin
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our good
- पिपृत (*pipṛta*)—carry across

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, of excellent knowledge and knowing all, you who are lords of the entire world, immovable and moving: release us from all our sins. Bring about our welfare.

##### English translation
May the wise and omniscient deities, who rule over the whole world both stationery aud moveable, deliver us to-day from committed and uncommitted sin, for our well-being.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We call upon Indra, the liberator from sin (अंहोमुचं (*aṃhomucaṃ*)), well-invoked (सुहवं (*suhavaṃ*)), in the भरेषु (*bhareṣu*): bharas are battles, since in them (people) destroy enemies. In them we call him for protection…

> णायाह्वयामः । किंच सुकृतं सुकर्माणं दैव्यं देवसंबंधिनमन्यं जनं चाह्वयामहे । तं जनमुद्दिशति । अग्निं मित्रं वरुणं भगं भजनीयमेतन्नामानं
> देवं द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्य मरुतश्च सातयेऽन्नलाभाय स्वस्तयेऽविनाशाय रक्षणायाह्वयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…for protection. Further, we call also another person who is of good deeds and belongs to the gods (दैव्यं जनं (*daivyaṃ janaṃ*)); he points to that group: Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bhaga (the adorable god so named), Heaven and Earth, and the Maruts; we call them for the gaining of food (सातये (*sātaye*)) and for welfare, i.e. non-destruction and protection.

- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- भरेषु (*bhareṣu*)—in battles
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call for help
- सुकृतं (*sukṛtaṃ*)—the doer of excellent deeds
- दैव्यं जनं (*daivyaṃ janaṃ*)—belonging to the group of gods
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—Mitra
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuṇa
- भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—Bhaga
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—Heaven and Earth
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the gaining of food
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our welfare we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We call in battles for help Indra, who releases from sin and is worthy of excellent invocation. Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bhaga, Heaven and Earth and the Maruts, who are doers of excellent deeds and belong to the company of the gods, we too call with prayer for the gaining of food and for our welfare.

##### English translation
We call in battles upon the well-invoked Indra, the liberator from sin, and upon the virtuous folk of heaven, Agni, Mitra, Varuna, Bhaga, Heaven and Earth, the Maruts, for the acquisition (of food), for well-being.

> अदितिदेवताकस्य पशोः सुत्रामाणमित्येषा वपायागस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं
> च । अदितिर्ह्यजनिष्ट सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं । आ-३-८ । इति ॥ प्रायणीयेष्वावादित्यस्य हविष एष्यॆवानुवाक्या सैवोदयनीयाया याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।

> सुप्रणीतिं सुप्रणयनां सुष्टु प्रणेत्रि दैवीं देवसंबंधिनीं स्वरित्रां शोभनारित्रां जलाहरणशीलदारुयुक्तामनागसं पापरहितामस्रवंतीमगच्छंतीमविनश्वरीं नावं नावमिव स्थितां द्यां स्वस्तयेऽविनाशाय देवत्वप्राप्त्यय आ रुहेम ।
> वयमारोहेम ॥ रोहतेर्लिजि लिज्याशिष्यज्जित्यज् प्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk सुत्रामाणं (*sutrāmāṇaṃ*) is the yājyā of the vapā offering in the animal sacrifice to Aditi; it is stated in the sūtra: अदितिर्ह्यजनिष्ट सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं (*aditirhyajaniṣṭa sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8). In the Prāyaṇīya offerings, for the oblation to Āditya, this is the anuvākyā, and the same is the yājyā of the Udayanīya; stated in the sūtra सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं महीमू षु मातरं सुव्रतानां (*sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasaṃ mahīmū ṣu mātaraṃ suvratānāṃ*) (Ā. 4-3). On a journey one should board a boat with it; stated in सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसमिति नावं (*sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasamiti nāvaṃ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 2-6-8).
The heaven-world is praised in the form of a boat. सुत्रामाणं (*sutrāmāṇaṃ*): one that protects well; पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*): the vast one; अनेहसं (*anehasaṃ*): free from sin; सुशर्माणं (*suśarmāṇaṃ*): possessed of excellent happiness; अदितिं (*aditiṃ*): the undiminished; सुप्रणीतिं (*supraṇītiṃ*): the good leader; दैवीं (*daivīṃ*): belonging to the gods; स्वरित्रां (*svaritrāṃ*): with good oars, furnished with wood for drawing water; अनागसं (*anāgasaṃ*): sinless; अस्रवंतीं (*asravaṃtīṃ*): not leaking, not perishing; नावं (*nāvaṃ*): standing as a boat. We would board heaven for welfare, that is non-destruction and the attainment of divinity (आ रुहेम (*ā ruhema*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुत्रामाणं (*sutrāmāṇaṃ*)—easily protected
- प्रथिवीं (*prathivīṃ*)—vast
- अनेहसं (*anehasaṃ*)—free from sin
- सुशर्माणं (*suśarmāṇaṃ*)—possessed of excellent happiness
- अनागसं (*anāgasaṃ*)—free from fault
- अदितिं (*aditiṃ*)—undivided
- सुप्रणीतिं (*supraṇītiṃ*)—a good guide
- दैवीं (*daivīṃ*)—belonging to the gods
- स्वरित्रं (*svaritraṃ*)—having excellent oars
- अस्रवंतीं (*asravaṃtīṃ*)—indestructible
- नावं (*nāvaṃ*)—carrying across like a boat
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heaven-world
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our welfare
- आ रुहेम (*ā ruhema*)—let us ascend

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us ascend, for our welfare, the heaven-world, which is easily protected, vast, free from sin, giver of excellent happiness, faultless, undivided, a good guide, belonging to the gods, with excellent oars, indestructible, and carrying across like a boat.

##### English translation
May we for our well-being ascend the well-oared, defectless, unyielding, divine vessel, the safe-sheltering expansive heaven, exempt from evil, replete with happieess, exalted and right-directing.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice made to the deity Aditi, when the vapā offering is made, this Ṛk सुत्रामाणं (*sutrāmāṇaṃ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra—

### Printed p. 474
अदितिर्ह्यजनिष्ट सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं (*aditirhyajaniṣṭa sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8). In the Prāyaṇīya offering, in the oblation made to Āditya, this Ṛk is to be recited as anuvākyā, and in the Udayanīya offering as yājyā, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं महीमू षु मातरं सुव्रतानां (*sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasaṃ mahīmū ṣu mātaraṃ suvratānāṃ*) (Ā. 4-3). At the time of a journey, when crossing a river met on the way, one should recite this Ṛk and board the boat, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसमिति नावं (*sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasamiti nāvaṃ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 2-6-8).

> स्तस्तये ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यजत्रा यजनीया हे विश्वे सर्वॆ देवाः यूयमूतये रक्षणार्थमधि वोचत। अस्मानधिब्रूत । अभाष्य चाभिह्रुतोऽभिहिंसित्रा दुरेवाया दुर्गतेर्नोऽस्मांस्त्रात्रायध्वं । यद्येवं कुरुथ तर्हि हे देवाः शृण्वतः स्तोत्राण्यस्माभिरुक्तानि तादृशान्वो युष्मान् सत्यया यथार्थभूतया देवहूत्या । देवा
> हूयंतेऽनयेति देवहूतिः स्तुतिः । तया वयं हुवेम । आह्वयेम । किमर्थ० ।
> अवसे रक्षणाय शत्रुभ्यः स्वस्तये क्षेमाय जीवनाभिवृद्धये च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O adorable (यजत्रा (*yajatrā*)) all-gods, speak for us (अधि वोचत (*adhi vocata*)) for our protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)), and protect us from the evil course (दुरेवायाः (*durevāyāḥ*)) that afflicts us (अभिह्रुतः (*abhihrutaḥ*): the one who injures). If you do so, then, O gods who listen to the praises we have uttered, we would invoke you with a true (सत्यया (*satyayā*)) invocation of gods (देवहूत्या (*devahūtyā*): that by which gods are called, i.e. praise), for protection from enemies and for welfare (स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)), i.e. well-being and increase of life.

- अभि ह्रुतः (*abhi hrutaḥ*)—(from) that which injures us

- देवहूत्या (*devahūtyā*)—praise that extols the gods

- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O venerable gods, for our protection speak in our favour with graciously inclined praise. Protect us from the evil power that afflicts us. O gods who hear our praises, we call upon you with a true praise that extols the gods, for our protection and our welfare.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, put far from us (*apa kuruta*, separate) the disease (अमीवां (*amīvāṃ*)) and the like, or the enemy who afflicts like disease. Likewise separate all (विश्वां (*viśvāṃ*)) the अनाहुतिं (*anāhutiṃ*), the thought of not invoking the gods, or the great enemy of the gods. Further, drive away the अरातिं (*arātiṃ*), the non-giving, the miserly thought, or the enemy who is of the nature of not giving oblations to the gods. And also (the one) who desires evil (अघयतः (*aghayataḥ*))…

### Printed p. 476

> शत्रुर्दुर्विदत्रां दुर्विज्ञानं दुष्टां बुद्धिं इत्थं च द्वेषो द्वेष्टान् सर्वाञ्छतूनस्मदस्मत्त आरे दूरे युयोतन । पृथक्कुरुत । एवं सति यूयं नोऽस्मभ्यमुरु विस्तीर्णं शर्म सुखं स्वस्तये कल्याणाय प्रयच्छत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the construction begun in the preceding verse: gods, remove far from us the enemy, the evil-minded one दुर्विदत्रां (*durvidatrāṃ*) (bad understanding), and in this way all those who hate us; keep them far away from us. This being so, grant us wide, extensive happiness for our well-being.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- अमीवां (*amīvāṃ*)—disease
- अप (*apa*)—remove from us
- विश्वां (*viśvāṃ*)—all
- अनाहुतिं (*anāhutiṃ*)—the attitude opposed to sacrifice
- अप (*apa*)—destroy
- अरातिं (*arātiṃ*)—the enemy
- अप (*apa*)—drive far away
- अघयतः (*aghayataḥ*)—of the enemy who wishes us harm
- दुर्विदत्रां (*durvidatrāṃ*)—destroy the evil mind
- द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)—our enemies
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- आरे (*āre*)—far away
- युयोतन (*yuyotana*)—drive away
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our welfare
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- उरु (*uru*)—wide
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छत (*yacchata*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, destroy our diseases. Let no attitude opposed to sacrifice cling to us. Drive far away our enemies, who wish us harm and are of evil mind. For our welfare give us wide happiness.

##### English translation
(Remove far) from us disease, remove all neglect of oblations, remove illiberaliiy, the malevolence of those who wish to do us harm ; remove far from us, gods, those who hate us ; grant us ample happiness for our well-being.

> समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Viśvedevas, every mortal, unharmed by anyone, prospers with cattle and the like; and after the sustaining rite he is born forth with offspring, sons and the rest, that is, he becomes manifest in a distinguished way. O Ādityas, the man whom you lead by good guidance beyond all evils (or enemies) for his welfare, you lead over them along the good path; he prospers. This is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*)—O Ādityas
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which man
- सुनीतिभिः (*sunītibhiḥ*)—by excellent guidance
- विश्वानि दुरितानि (*viśvāni duritāni*)—all evil powers
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for his welfare
- अति नयथ (*ati nayatha*)—you cause to cross over
- सः (*saḥ*)—such
- विश्वः मर्तः (*viśvaḥ martaḥ*)—every man
- अरिष्टः (*ariṣṭaḥ*)—without suffering any harm
- विधते (*vidhate*)—attains growth
- धर्मणस्परि (*dharmaṇaspari*)—after the sacrificial rites that sustain the world
- प्रजाभिः (*prajābhiḥ*)—in the form of sons and the rest
- प्र जायते (*pra jāyate*)—increases his lineage

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, the man whom you, by your excellent guidance, cause to cross over all evil powers for his welfare—every such man attains growth without suffering any harm. After performing the sacrificial rites that sustain the world, he comes into manifestation in the form of sons and the rest and gains increase.

##### English translation
Unharmed prospers every mortal, after performing his duties, he flourishes with posterity, whom you Adityas guide with good counsels safe over all misfortunes to well-beings,

> मुख्यत्वादिंद्रमेवाभिलक्ष्य वदत्युत्तरार्धेन । हे इंद्र सर्वेषां मुख्य प्रातयार्वाणं प्रातरेव युद्धं प्रति गंतारं सानसिं संभजनीयमरिष्यंतं कैश्चिदप्यहिंसितं । यद्वा। इंद्रसहायानां मरुतामबाधकं। तं रथं स्वस्तयेऽस्माकं रक्षणाय
> वयमारुहेम । आरोहेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, the chariot which you protect in the winning of food (वाजसाता (*vājasātā*)); O Maruts, the chariot which you protect in शूरसाता (*śūrasātā*), a name for battle (the place where heroes are weary or are destroyed by warriors), with a view to the wealth laid down there—the seventh case is by निमित्तात्कर्मसंयोगे । पा. २-३-३६-६ । (*nimittātkarmasaṃyoge | pā. 2-3-36-6 |*). Since Indra is chief of all the gods, the second half is addressed to him: O Indra, chief of all, we would mount that chariot, which goes forth to battle at early morning, is to be shared in, is unharmed by anyone—or, alternatively, does not hinder the Maruts who are Indra's helpers—for our protection and welfare.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—for the winning of food
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which chariot
- अवध (*avadha*)—you protect
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- शूरसाता (*śūrasātā*)—in the battle that conquers heroes
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which chariot
- हिते धने (*hite dhane*)—you protect for the wealth in it
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- प्रातरावाणं (*prātarāvāṇaṃ*)—setting out to battle early in the morning
- सानसिं (*sānasiṃ*)—worthy of honour
- अरिष्यंतं (*ariṣyaṃtaṃ*)—not liable to harm
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—that chariot
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our welfare
- आ रुहेम (*ā ruhema*)—may we mount

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, the chariot you protect for the winning of food; O Maruts, the chariot you protect, for the wealth in it, in the battle that conquers heroes; O Indra, that chariot which sets out to battle in the early morning, is worthy of honour and not liable to harm—may we mount it for our welfare.

##### English translation
(The chariot) which, deities, you protect for the supply of food ; that which, Maruts, (you protect) in battle for the sake of the deposited spoil ; may we mount, Indra, the early-moving desirable irresistible chariot for our weil-being.
