> दृष्टांतः । पयसेव धेनुं नवप्रसूतिकां गां क्षीरेण यथाप्याययंति तद्वत्
> किंच । गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतीरधि रथ आत्मीये रथे कुविद्बहुवारं वहाथ । प्राप्ताः
> स्थ । स्तुतेषु सत्तु यज्ञं प्रत्यागमनाय रथारूढा भवथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the Maruts, Indra, the gods, Varuṇa and Mitra: the thought (धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)), that is, the rite, which you have given to me, that you must fill with its fruit. The example: as people fill a newly calved cow with milk, so do you. He says that in मरुत (*maruta*) the accent is not lowered because of a break in the sentence, and that the first syllable keeps the high accent because no preceding word exists. Further, you carry (वहाथ (*vahātha*)) our praises many times (कुवित् (*kuvit*)) on your own chariot, that is, you have received them; when praised, you mount your chariots to come to the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- यां धियं (*yāṃ dhiyaṃ*)—which rite
- मे (*me*)—to me
- अददात (*adadāta*)—you have granted
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that rite
- पयसेव धेनुं (*payaseva dhenuṃ*)—as one fills a cow with milk
- पीपयत (*pīpayata*)—fill with fruit
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—our praises
- आधि रथे (*ādhi rathe*)—on your chariots
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—many times
- वहाथ (*vahātha*)—you take up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, O Indra, O gods, O Varuṇa, O Mitra, the rite that you have granted me, fill it with fruit, as a cow is filled with milk. You take up our praises on your chariots many times; that is, you hear our praises.

### Printed p. 501

##### English translation
Maruts, Indra, gods, Varuna and Mitra, reward the worship,
which you have given as (men fatten) the (newly-delivered) cow with milk,
you have repeatedly put my praises on your car.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कु॒विदं॒ग प्रति॒ यथा॑ चिद॒स्य नः॑ सजा॒त्य॑स्य मरुतो॒ बुबो॑धथ।  
> नाभा॒ यत्र॑ प्रथ॒मं सं॒नसा॑महे॒ तत्र॑ जामि॒त्वमदि॑तिर्दधातु  
> नः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कुवित् । अंग । प्रति । यथा । चित् । अस्य । नः । सजात्यस्य । मरुतः । बुबोधथ ।  
> नाभा । यत्र । प्रथमं । संनसामहे । तत्र । जामित्वं । अदितिः । दधातु । नः ॥१३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंगेति संबुद्धौ । हे मरुतः यूयं नोऽस्मान्कुविद्बहुवारं प्रति बुबोधथ।तथा प्रतिबुध्यध्वं ॥ कुविच्छब्दयोगादनिघातः ॥ यथा नोऽस्मान्सजात्यस्यास्य
> बांधवस्य विषयभूतान्कुरुथ तथा जानीथ । ततो नाभा पृथिव्या नाभिस्थाने यत्र
> यस्मिन्नुत्तरवेदिलक्षणे देशे प्रथममेव संनसामहे हविषा यत्र संगच्छेमहि
> तत्त्रैव देशेदितिर्देवानां माता नोऽस्माकं जामित्वं मनुष्यैः सह बांधवं
> दधातु । विदधातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अंग (*aṃga*) is a vocative particle. O Maruts, you must take notice of us many times (कुवित् (*kuvit*)); the accent is not lowered because of the word कुवित् (*kuvit*). As you make us the object of this kinship, so you know us. Then, at the navel of the earth, in the place called the Uttaravedi where we first of all assemble with the oblation, there may Aditi, mother of the gods, establish for us kinship with men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंग मरुतः (*aṃga marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अस्य सजात्यस्य (*asya sajātyasya*)—as you make us fit to attain your kinship
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—many times
- प्रति बुबोधथ (*prati bubodhatha*)—take notice, favouring us
- नाभा (*nābhā*)—at the navel of the earth
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which sacrificial place
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—first
- संनसामहे (*saṃnasāmahe*)—we are ready, together with oblations and the rest
- तत्र (*tatra*)—in that place
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi, mother of the gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- जामित्वं (*jāmitvaṃ*)—kinship with men
- दधातु (*dadhātu*)—may she grant

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, in the manner in which you make us fit objects of your kinship, favour us many times. In the sacrificial place, the navel of the earth, where we are ready beforehand together with oblations and the rest, in that place may Aditi, mother of the gods,

### Printed p. 502
grant us kinship with men.

##### English translation
Maruts, repeatedly acknowledge us, so that (you may make us the
objects) of this relationship ; and may Aditi grant us affinity (with men)
on the navel of the earth, where we first assemble (to offer oblations).

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते हि द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी मा॒तरा॑ म॒ही दे॒वी दे॒वाञ्जन॑ना य॒ज्ञि॑ -  ॒
> ये इतः ।  
> उ॒भे बि॑भृत उ॒भयं॒ भरी॑मभिः पु॒रू रेतां॑सि पि॒तृभि॑श्च  
> सिंचतः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते इति । हि । द्यावापृथिवी इति । मातरा । मही इति । देवी इति । देवान् । जन्मना ।  
> यज्ञिये इति । इतः ।  
> उभे इति । बिभृतः । उभयं । भरीमभिः । पुरु । रेतांसि । पितृभिः । च । सिंचतः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मातरा सर्वस्य जगतो निर्मात्र्यौ आत एव मही महत्यौ देवी देवनशीले
> यज्ञिये यज्ञार्हे ते द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ देवानिंद्रादीज्जननैवेतो
> हि । प्राप्नुतः खलु ॥ इण् गत् । लिटि रूपं ॥ किंचोभे द्यावापृथिव्यौ भरीमभिर्भरणैर्नानाविधैरुभयं जनं देवान्मनुष्यांश्च बिभृतः । धारयतः । पोषयतः । तथा
> पितृभिः पालकैर्देवैः संगते ते पुरु पुराण्यात्मीयानि रेतांस्युदकानि सिंचतः ।
> क्षरतः । प्रत्यक्षेण धारयतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Heaven and Earth are the mothers, makers of the whole world, and therefore great, divine and worthy of sacrifice. By their very birth they reach (इतः (*itaḥ*), from the root इण् (*iṇ*) "to go", perfect form) the gods, Indra and the others. Both, with manifold supports, bear and nourish both peoples, gods and men. Joined with the protecting gods, the fathers, they pour abundant waters (रेतांसि (*retāṃsi*)), their own; that is, they sustain them visibly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मातरा (*mātarā*)—the two makers of the world
- मही (*mahī*)—of great nature
- देवी (*devī*)—divine
- यज्ञिये (*yajñiye*)—worthy of sacrifice
- ते द्यावापृथिवी (*te dyāvāpṛthivī*)—those Heaven and Earth
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and others
- जन्मना (*janmanā*)—at the very birth
- इतः हि (*itaḥ hi*)—they join
- उभे (*ubhe*)—both Heaven and Earth
- भरीमभिः (*bharīmabhiḥ*)—with many materials that support the world
- उभयं (*ubhayaṃ*)—gods and men
- बिभृतः (*bibhṛtaḥ*)—they nourish
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—they, together with the protecting gods
- पुरु (*puru*)—abundant
- रेतांसि (*retāṃsi*)—waters
- सिंचतः (*siṃcataḥ*)—make flow

### Printed p. 503

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and Earth, makers of the world, of great nature, divine and worthy of sacrifice, join the gods Indra and the rest at their very birth. Both Heaven and Earth nourish gods and men with the many materials that support the world. Together with the gods who protect the world, they make abundant waters flow.

##### English translation
They two, the maternal heaven and earth, mighty, divine, adorable, attain to the gods upon their birth ; they both cherish tho two (races, human and divine) with various nutriments : (associated) with the paternal (gods), they shed abundant moisture.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि षा होत्रा॒ विश्व॑मश्नोति॒ वार्यं॒ बृह॒स्पति॑र॒रम॑तिः॒ पनी॑यसी ।  
> ग्रावा॒ यत्र॑ मधु॒षुदु॒च्यते॑ बृ॒हदवी॑वशंत म॒तिभि॑र्मनी॒षिणः॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । सा । होत्रा । विश्वं । अश्नोति । वार्यं । बृहस्पतिः । अरमतिः । पनीयसी ।  
> ग्रावा । यत्र । मधुसुत् । उच्यते । बृहत् । अवीवशंत । मतिभिः । मनीषिणः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> होत्रा । वाज्ञामैतत् आहूयंतेऽनया देवा इति । सा वाग्वार्यं वरणीयं विश्वं सर्वं पश्वादिसहितं धनं व्यश्नोति । विविधं व्याप्नुते । कीदृशी ।
> बृहस्पतिर्बृहतां महतां पालयित्रि आरमतिः पर्याप्तस्तुतिः यद्वा कुत्राप्यनुपरता पनीयस्य अत्यंतं देवानां स्तोत्रकारिणी । यत्र यस्यां होत्रायां
> मधुषुत् सोममभिषुण्वन्बृहद्महान्गावोच्यते अभिधीयते। स्तूयत इत्यर्थः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

होत्रा (*hotrā*) is a name of speech: "by it the gods are invoked". That speech obtains (व्यश्नोति (*vyaśnoti*), pervades in various ways) all desirable wealth, together with cattle and the like. What kind is it? बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*): protectress of the great; अरमतिः (*aramatiḥ*): of sufficient praise, or, alternatively, never ceasing anywhere; पनीयसी (*panīyasī*): one who greatly praises the gods. In that invocation in which the great grinding-stone (ग्रावा (*grāvā*)), pressing the sweet Soma, is spoken of, that is, praised,

### Printed p. 504
*Gist (continued):* the wise gods (मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*)) desire that sacrifice full of praise together with the praises (मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)). अवीवशंत (*avīvaśaṃta*) means "they desire". Alternatively: the wise praisers, by their praises, make the gods desirous of the sacrifice.

> तं स्तुतिमंतं यज्ञं मनीषिणो देवा मतिभिः स्तुतिभिः सहावीवशंत । काम
> यंते॥ वष्टीर्ण्यंतस्य लुजि रूपं यद्वा। मनीषिणः स्तोतारः स्तुतिभिर्देवान्यज्ञं
> कामयमानान्कुर्वंति ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—that which protects the gods of great nature
- अरमतिः (*aramatiḥ*)—that which is pervasive
- पनीयसी (*panīyasī*)—that which praises the gods
- होत्रा (*hotrā*)—that which praises the gods and calls them to the sacrifice
- सा (*sā*)—that praise
- वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—desired
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all wealth
- व्यश्नोति (*vyaśnoti*)—obtains
- यत्र (*yatra*)—at what time of praise
- मधुसुत् (*madhusut*)—that which presses Soma
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great
- ग्रावा (*grāvā*)—the pressing stone
- उच्यते (*ucyate*)—is praised; that sacrifice full of praise
- मनीषिणिः (*manīṣiṇiḥ*)—the wise gods
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with praises
- अवीवशंत (*avīvaśaṃta*)—desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praise that protects the gods of great nature, is pervasive, praises the gods and calls them to the sacrifice, causes all desired wealth to be obtained. At the time of praise in which the great stone that presses the Soma is praised, that sacrifice full of praise the wise gods desire together with the praises.

##### English translation
That voice of invocation, the protectress of the mighty, never ceasing, the panegyrist (of the gods), obtains all desirable wealth : on uttering which, the great grinding-stone expressing the sweet Soma is eulogized ; the pious, by their praises, make the god desirous (of the sacrifice).

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा क॒विस्तु॑वी॒रवा॑ ऋत॒ज्ञा द्र॑विण॒स्युद्रर्वि॑णसश्चका॒नः ।  
> उ॒क्षेभि॒रत्र॑ म॒तिभि॑श्च॒ विप्रोऽपी॑पय॒द्गयो॑ दि॒व्यानि॒ जन्म॑ ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । कविः । तुविरवान् । ऋतज्ञाः । द्रविणस्युः । द्रविणसः । चकानः ।  
> उक्षेभिः । अत्र । मतिभिः । च । विप्रः । अपीपयत् । गयः । दिव्यानि । जन्म ॥ १६ ॥

### Printed p. 505

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कविः क्रांतप्रज्ञस्तुवीरवान् ॥ मत्त्वर्थीयप्रत्ययावृत्तिः ॥ बहुस्तुतियुक्तऋतज्ञा यज्ञस्य वेदिता द्रविणस्युद्धनकामः ॥ सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यो लालसायामिति
> सुगागमः ॥ तस्यैव विशदवचनं । द्रविणसश्च कान इति। पश्वादिधनं कामयमान इत्यर्थः।
> विव्रो मेधावी गयो नामर्षिरेवमुक्तप्रकारेणात्र सूक्त उक्तेभिः शस्त्रैर्मतिभिः
> स्तुतिभिश्च दिव्यानि दिवि जातानि जन्म जननानि देवानपीपयत् । अवर्धयत् ।
> अस्तावीदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

कविः (*kaviḥ*) is one of far-reaching wisdom; तुवीरवान् (*tuvīravān*) is one with much praise (the possessive affix is repeated); ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*) is a knower of the sacrifice; द्रविणस्युः (*draviṇasyuḥ*) is one desiring wealth (the augment *suk* in the sense of longing). The phrase द्रविणसश्च कानः (*draviṇasaśca kānaḥ*) is its explanation: one desiring cattle and the like. The sage, the wise गय (*gaya*) by name, in the way described, here in this hymn, with recitations (उक्षेभिः (*ukṣebhiḥ*), the Śastras) and praises, caused the gods, born in heaven (दिव्यानि जन्म (*divyāni janma*)), to thrive (अपीपयत् (*apīpayat*)), that is, he made them grow, he praised them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the wise
- तुविरवान् (*tuviravān*)—one with many praises
- ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*)—one who knows the truth of the sacrifice
- द्रविणस्युः (*draviṇasyuḥ*)—one who desires wealth
- द्रविणसश्चकानः (*draviṇasaścakānaḥ*)—one who wishes for cattle and the like
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the learned
- गयः (*gayaḥ*)—the seer Gaya
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this hymn
- उक्तेभिः (*uktebhiḥ*)—with the Śastra mantras
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with praises
- एव (*eva*)—in this manner
- दिव्यानि जन्म (*divyāni janma*)—the gods who have an excellent birth
- अपीपयत् (*apīpayat*)—has made to thrive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seer Gaya, wise, full of many praises, knowing the truth of the sacrifice, desiring wealth, wishing for cattle and the like, and learned, has in this hymn, with Śastra mantras and praises, in this manner made the gods of excellent birth thrive.

##### English translation
The pious sage, Gaya, eloquent in laudation, conversant with sacred rites, wishing for wealth, eager for wealth, propitiates the celestial people with prayers and praises.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा प्ल॒तेः सू॒नुर॑वीवृधद्वो॒ विश्व॑ आदित्या अदिते मनी॒षी ।  
> ई॒शा॒नासो॒ नरो॒ अम॑र्त्ये॒नास्ता॑वि॒ जनो॑ दि॒व्यो गये॑न ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । प्लतेः । सूनुः । अवीवृधत् । वः । विश्वे । आदित्याः । अदिते । मनीषी ।  
> ईशानासः । नरः । अमर्त्येन । अस्तावि । जनः । दिव्यः । गयेन ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 506

> इयं व्याख्याता ॥ 482ने पेजन्नु नोडि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says only that this Ṛk has already been explained, and refers the reader to page 482.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वे आदित्याः (*viśve ādityāḥ*)—O all gods, sons of Aditi
- अदिते (*adite*)—O Aditi, mother of the gods
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- मनीषी (*manīṣī*)—the wise praiser
- प्लतेः सूनुः (*plateḥ sūnuḥ*)—Gaya, the son of Plati
- एव (*eva*)—thus
- अवीवृधत् (*avīvṛdhat*)—has made (you) thrive through his praises
- अमर्त्येन (*amartyena*)—through the favour of which deathless divine people
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—men
- ईशानासः (*īśānāsaḥ*)—become lords of wealth
- दिव्यः जनः (*divyaḥ janaḥ*)—such a host of gods
- गयेन (*gayena*)—by Gaya
- अस्तावि (*astāvi*)—has been praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O all gods, sons of Aditi, O Aditi, mother of the gods, Gaya, the wise praiser and son of Plati, has thus made you thrive through his praises. The host of gods, the deathless divine people, through whose favour men become lords of wealth, has been praised by Gaya.

##### English translation
Universal deities and Aditi, thus has the prudent son of Plati magnified you; the celestial people, the immortal (company of the gods)through whom (when praised) men become the bonds (of wealth), have been glorified by Gaya.

## Sūkta 65 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The deity of this sūkta is the Viśvedevas. We have explained the matter of the Viśvedevas at length earlier, but not separately. Some of the deities who appear in the first Ṛk of this sūkta we have explained here and there: Agni on pages 612 of Part 1; Indra (11-665), Vāyu (5-598), Pūṣan (15-394), Sarasvatī (15-444 and 447). Now we shall explain briefly here the deities Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman.

**Introduction**
Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are regarded as separate deities, but here they seem to be described as the many forms of Sūryas, that is, as partial deities of that name among the twelve Ādityas. Moreover, in some places these three deities are said to be other forms of Agni.

### Printed p. 507
In the Ṛks
त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः (*tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1)
त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन् गुह्यं बिभर्षि । (*tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvan guhyaṃ bibharṣi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-2)
it is said that Agni has these three names: Varuṇa when he is born, Mitra when he is well kindled and blazes brightly, and Aryaman in the homas and other rites connected with a maiden. Moreover in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:
मित्रोऽसि वरुणोसीत्याह । मैत्रं ना अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः । आहोरात्राभ्यामेवैनमुपावहरति ॥ ( (*mitro 'si varuṇosītyāha | maitraṃ nā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ | āhorātrābhyāmevainamupāvaharati ‖ (*) (Tai. Brā. 1-7-10-1)
Mitra is said to be lord of the day and Varuṇa lord of the night. It must therefore be noted that these three deities are said in some places to be partial deities of the Sun, and in others different names of Agni.

In the Purāṇas and similar works Mitra is one of the twelve Ādityas. In the Ṛgveda, though Mitra is another name of the Sun, Mitra has a distinct character of his own, that is, an individual prominence. The Ṛgveda also says that Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are sons of Aditi; therefore they are called Ādityas in many places. As to these Ādityas, the sons of Aditi, being six in number: in the Ṛk
इमा गिर आदित्थेभ्यो धृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥ (*imā gira āditthebhyo dhṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi | śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1)
only the names of six are given: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa.
In the Ṛk
देवा आदित्या ये सप्त तेभिः सोमाभि रक्ष न इंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव । (*devā ādityā ye sapta tebhiḥ somābhi rakṣa na iṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3)
the sons of Aditi are said to be seven.
अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्वं स्परि (*aṣṭau putrāso aditerye jātāstanvaṃ spari*)
देवा उपप्रैत्सप्तभि; परा मार्तांडमास्यत् (*devā upapraitsaptabhi; parā mārtāṃḍamāsyat*)
सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप प्रैत्सूर्व्यं युगं (*saptabhiḥ putrairaditirupa praitsūrvyaṃ yugaṃ*)
प्रजाय्य मृत्युवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तांडमाभरत् (*prajāyya mṛtyuve tvatpunarmārtāṃḍamābharat*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8, 9)

### Printed p. 508
In these Ṛks it is said that Aditi had in all eight sons: first seven, and afterwards Mārtaṇḍa. Moreover in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:
अष्टा पुत्रासो अदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वः परि । देवा उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तांडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उपप्रैत्सूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्युवे तत् । परा मार्तांडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चेत्येते ॥ (*aṣṭā putrāso aditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥ pari | devā upapraitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtāṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upapraitsūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyuve tat | parā mārtāṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgścetyete ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 1-13-3)
The names of the eight sons of Aditi are given: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, Aryaman, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān are those eight. The same matter is stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:
अदितिः पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौदनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यै धाता चार्यमा चाजायेतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यै मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अगंंशश्च भगश्चाजायेतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्ंश्चाजायेतां ॥ (*aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmaudanamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatrāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyai dhātā cāryamā cājāyetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyai mitraśca varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā agaṃṃśaśca bhagaścājāyetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatrāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivasvāgṃścājāyetāṃ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1,2,3)
Here the matter of Aditi's obtaining eight sons is clearly described. Of these eight, only the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, are specially famous in the Ṛgveda. In Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 2-7 there is an extensive description of the beneficent heroic deeds of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. **NOTE**

Mitra: Yāska has given the etymology of the word Mitra in his Nirukta as follows:
मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते । संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । मेदयतेर्वा । (*mitraḥ pramītestrāyate | saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | medayatervā |*) (Ni. 10-21)
What is the meaning of the word Mitra? मित्रः कस्मात् । स हि प्रमितेः त्रायते । प्रमितिः मरणं । ततः सर्वलोकं त्रायते वर्षद्वारेण । (*mitraḥ kasmāt | sa hi pramiteḥ trāyate | pramitiḥ maraṇaṃ | tataḥ sarvalokaṃ trāyate varṣadvāreṇa |*) Pramiti means death. Because he produces rain for people in the world, thereby provides food and the like, averts the fear of death that may arise from hunger, and so protects, this deity is called Mitra.
समंततो मिन्वानः उदकेन द्रवति अंतरिक्षलोके (*samaṃtato minvānaḥ udakena dravati aṃtarikṣaloke*) This deity, being lord of water and staying in the atmosphere, through the clouds makes all around, that is, the whole region, flow with water, that is, become drenched; therefore this deity is called Mitra.

### Printed p. 509
Or: स्नेहनार्थस्य सर्वं ह्यसावुदकेन स्नेहयति (*snehanārthasya sarvaṃ hyasāvudakena snehayati*) This deity makes everything cling together, that is, unite into one, with water; therefore this deity is called Mitra. After stating three such etymologies, he has given as example, in support of it, the Ṛk
मित्रो जनान् यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । मित्रः कृष्टीरसिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जु होत ॥ (*mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ | mitraḥ kṛṣṭīrasimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ dhṛtavajju hota ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-1)
In this Ṛk Mitra, helping the works of agriculture and the like, pours rain and so on, provides people with food and the like, and sustains, that is, nourishes, the people of the earth and the dwellers in heaven. "O men, offer oblations mixed with ghee to such a god Mitra": thus his extraordinary qualities and his beneficence to the world are very well described. The only sūkta in the Ṛgveda in praise of Mitra is this sūkta of 9 Ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59); elsewhere Mitra is praised together with other deities such as Varuṇa. Since the heroic acts of Mitra and Varuṇa are very many, the sūkta with Mitra alone as deity is, as said before, only one in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59), and even there the part praising that deity is indistinct. Only in the first Ṛk, however, is Mitra's distinctive character well stated. In the fifth Ṛk of the same sūkta:
महा आदित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गृणते सुशेवः (*mahā ādityo namasopasadyo yātayajjano gṛṇate suśevaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-5)
this Mitra is called the great Āditya who unites all men together. The word यातयज्जन (*yātayajjana*), which gives this meaning, is used in the Ṛk
व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातॆयज्जना (*vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātèyajjanā*)
(printed reference: Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-72-2) **NOTE**
with reference to Mitra and Varuṇa, and in the Ṛk
मित्रस्तयोर्वरुणो यातयज्जनोऽर्यमा यातयज्जनः (*mitrastayorvaruṇo yātayajjano 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-3)
with reference to the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. According to the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59 mentioned above, Mitra is the support of heaven and earth. The five tribes of men (पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*) ) are obedient to him; he is the sustainer of life for all other deities: so his qualities are described. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-4 Savitṛ and Mitra are said to be one; in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Vā. Saṃ. 4-3) Viṣṇu is said to have taken his three steps in accordance with Mitra's ordinances; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8.4 Agni, established before dawn, himself brings forth Mitra for himself **NOTE**; and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-4, when the blazing Agni is born, he is Mitra, that is,

### Printed p. 510
मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत्समिद्दो मित्रो होता वरुणो चातवेदाः । मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिंधूनामुत पर्वतानां ॥ (*mitro agnirbhavati yatsamiddo mitro hotā varuṇo cātavedāḥ | mitro adhvaryuriṣiro damūnā mitraḥ siṃdhūnāmuta parvatānāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-4)
In this verse the well-kindled Agni is called Mitra; this Mitra is in the sacrifice the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, Varuṇa and Agni called Jātavedas; and he is the friend (benefactor) of the rivers and the mountains: thus Mitra's qualities are described.

Varuṇa: वरुणो वृणोतीति सतः (*varuṇo vṛṇotīti sataḥ*) (Ni. 10-2). Yāska's etymology is that, because he is covered by a mass of clouds, this deity is called Varuṇa.
Varuṇa is a most eminent deity, equal to Indra in power and the like. There are twelve sūktas in the Ṛgveda addressed to Varuṇa; but the sūktas praising Mitra and Varuṇa together are twenty-four.
Varuṇa has a human body and human activities. But more than his physical body and activities, the description of his moral activities and works is what is chiefly indicated. He has a face, eyes, arms, hands and feet. His bodily activities are described: he drives a chariot, sits, eats, drinks, and so on. That the Sun is the eye of Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa is stated plainly in the Ṛks
चित्रं देवनामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः (*citraṃ devanāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1)
उदुत्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धं । (*udutyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdhaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1)
उद्वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान् । (*udvāṃ cakṣurvaruṇa supratīkaṃ devayoreti sūryastatanvān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-61-1)
चुक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक् तमांसि । (*cukṣurmitrasya varuṇasya devaścarmeva yaḥ samavivyak tamāṃsi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-63-1)
नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत । (*namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase maho devāya tadṛtaṃ saparyata |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-1)
Since the matter of the Sun being like an eye to them stands in the very first Ṛk of the sūktas addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa, it seems that this is the point that first presents itself whenever Mitra and Varuṇa are mentioned; and in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-10

### Printed p. 511
Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa are said to have the Sun as their eye. That Varuṇa is far-seeing (उरुचक्षसं (*urucakṣasaṃ*)) is said in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-5; 1-25-16 and other Ṛks.
आ नो बर्हि रिशादसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । सीदंतु मनुषो यथा ॥ व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ॥ (*ā no barhi riśādaso varuṇo mitro aryamā | sīdaṃtu manuṣo yathā ‖ vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātayajjanā | ni barhiṣi sadataṃ somapītaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-72-2)
In such Ṛks, for the drinking of soma, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are prayed to come and sit on the darbha grass spread on the sacrificial altar.
यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादय्यते ॥ (*yadī sakhāyā sakhyāya somaiḥ sutebhiḥ suprayasā mādayyate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-41-3)
In such Ṛks it is said that Varuṇa drinks soma together with Indra and other gods.
बिभ्रद्दापिं हिरण्ययं वरुणो वस्त्र निर्णिजं (*bibhraddāpiṃ hiraṇyayaṃ varuṇo vastra nirṇijaṃ*)
परिस्पशो निषेदिरे (*parispaśo niṣedire*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-13)
In this Ṛk there is the description that Varuṇa wears a golden mantle or robe and a shining garment. Varuṇa's chariot is golden and radiant like the Sun, and has whips that urge the horses. Mitra and Varuṇa mount their chariot in a very high region of the sky (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-1); such descriptions are found. The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is golden and is in the upper world; and Varuṇa, seated in his palace,
नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्ता ३ स्वा । साम्राज्याय सुक्रतुः । अतो विश्वन्याद्भुता चिकित्वा अभि पश्यति । कृतानि या च कर्त्वा ॥ (*ni ṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastā 3 svā | sāmrājyāya sukratuḥ | ato viśvanyādbhutā cikitvā abhi paśyati | kṛtāni yā ca kartvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-10, 11)
sees all that goes on in the world. The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is very large, very high, firm, resting on a thousand pillars, and their house has a thousand doors (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-5). There are also descriptions that the all-seeing Sun, setting out from his own abode, goes to the house of Mitra and Varuṇa to report the doings of men, and enters their dear house.
Varuṇa, alone or together with Mitra, is called king in many places, like other gods.

### Printed p. 512
In the Ṛks अबुध्ने राजा वरुणो वनस्योर्ध्वं स्तूपं ददते पूतदक्षः । (*abudhne rājā varuṇo vanasyordhvaṃ stūpaṃ dadate pūtadakṣaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-7), त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः । (*tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23.10) and तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूम । (*tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaṃ na vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūma |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3), and in others like them, Varuṇa is called king not only of men but also of the gods and of all the worlds. Besides Varuṇa, the gods Indra, Yama, Soma and others also bear the honorific name of king.

There are many stories connected with Indra, but in the case of Varuṇa the situation is quite the opposite: there is not a single story. Varuṇa is praised greatly as the regulator of the physical and moral ordinances (वरुणस्य व्रतानि (*varuṇasya vratāni*)). The divine power of Mitra and Varuṇa is described by the word Māyā. Applied to the gods, it means a hidden power they have to do good; in contexts where it is applied to demons, the same word means a harsh power they have to do evil. In the good sense this word suits Mitra and Varuṇa; in the bad sense it applies to the demons. Like the word Asura, the word Māyā is used in both senses. By this Māyā-power hidden in himself, Varuṇa, standing in the atmosphere, measures out the earth with the sun as with a measuring rod. He makes the sun cross the firmament and makes it dim with rain-clouds. Then honey-mixed (sweet) drops fall (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-4). He makes the sky pour rain. Therefore this word Māyā is said chiefly of Varuṇa among the gods in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-14; 7-28-4; 10-99-10; 10-147-5 and others.

Varuṇa is the one who lays down the laws of nature. It was he who established earth and heaven, and in the Ṛk आसीदद्विश्वा भुवनानि संराड्विश्वेत्तानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि । (*āsīdadviśvā bhuvanāni saṃrāḍviśvettāni varuṇasya vratāni |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-42-1) it is said that Varuṇa dwells in all the worlds and that his ordinances are observed everywhere; in तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अंतरस्मिन् तिस्रो भूमीरुसराः षड्विधानाः । (*tisro dyāvo nihitā aṃtarasmin tisro bhūmīrusarāḥ ṣaḍvidhānāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-87-5) it is said that the three upper worlds and the three earths (lower worlds) are under his control. Varuṇa and Mitra rule the whole world (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-7). They are the protectors of the whole universe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-4). Varuṇa is the support of heaven, earth and sky

### Printed p. 513
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-1, 4). He has placed fire in the waters, the sun in the sky, and Soma upon the stone. He has made a broad path for the sun. Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman open the way for the sun (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-60-4). In many such Ṛks Varuṇa's authority is described.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-8-4) it is said मित्रोऽहरजनयद्वरुणो रात्रिं (*mitro 'harajanayadvaruṇo rātriṃ*), that is, Mitra created the day and Varuṇa the night. Therefore मैत्रं वा अहः ।वारुणी रात्रिः (*maitraṃ vā ahaḥ |vāruṇī rātriḥ*) — that is, in many places it is said that Mitra is the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-4). In one place it is said that Varuṇa divided the seasons. In वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते । (*veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-8) it is said that Varuṇa knows the twelve months; and in the Ṛk वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञ मक्तुं चादृचं । अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥ (*vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajña maktuṃ cādṛcaṃ | anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-11) it is said that Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman divided the autumn, the month, the day and the night.

In many places it is said that he too is the one who regulates the waters. He is the one who made the rivers flow; by his command they flow continuously (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4). That the rivers, though swiftly pouring water into the ocean, do not fill it, is due to his hidden power (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-6). Varuṇa and Mitra are lords of the rivers. That Varuṇa is lord of the oceans is a well-known point, yet it occurs very rarely in the Ṛgveda; perhaps the reason is that it was unimportant. In the Purāṇas and similar works Varuṇa is famed as lord of the waters, and that Varuṇa, as one of the eight guardians of the quarters, is lord of the west is what the Purāṇas say; the Ṛgveda gives no support for it. In general all that concerns Varuṇa relates to the water that is with the atmosphere. Among the gods prayed to for rain, Varuṇa and Mitra are the chief. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3, 4 it is said that when all the mountains are covered with clouds, Varuṇa pours water from the overturned vessel (the cloud) for heaven, earth and sky and makes the whole earth moist. One whole sūkta (that is, Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63) points to their rain-pouring power. In the Yajurveda Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-4-1) आपो वरुणस्य पत्न य आसन्— (*āpo varuṇasya patna ya āsan—*)

### Printed p. 514
the waters are said to be Varuṇa's wives, and (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-2) मित्रा वरुणौ ना अपां नेतारौ— (*mitrā varuṇau nā apāṃ netārau—*) Mitra and Varuṇa are the leaders of the waters.

Varuṇa's ordinances are said again and again to be well established. For this reason he is called Dhṛtavrata ("of firm ordinances"). This epithet is fitting for both Mitra and Varuṇa.
परि धामानि मर्मशद्वरुणस्य पुरो गये विश्वे देवा अनु व्रतं नभंतामन्यके समे ॥ (*pari dhāmāni marmaśadvaruṇasya puro gaye viśve devā anu vrataṃ nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-7)
न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनंति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ॥ (*na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minaṃti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-4)
In such Ṛks it is said that the gods themselves obey the commands of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, and that even the primeval gods cannot transgress their firm ordinances. Mitra and Varuṇa are the regulators of law (Ṛta) and of light. It is by the power of these ordinances that they are able to support the laws. This quality is found especially in these two, and sometimes in the Ādityas or in other ordinary gods. They advance truth (Ṛta) and justice. The epithet ऋतस्य गोपाः (*ṛtasya gopāḥ*), "guardians of the laws" (or "those who make them be kept"), is seen to be applied often to Mitra and Varuṇa.

Varuṇa's power is immeasurable. Neither flying birds nor flowing rivers can reach the boundary of his realm, nor surpass his power, nor stop his anger. Neither the sky nor the rivers have reached the limit of the boundary of Mitra and Varuṇa. Everything is contained in Varuṇa. The dwellings of all creatures, the three heavenly worlds and the three earthly worlds, are placed in him. Varuṇa is all-knowing. The flight of birds in the sky, the passage of ships on the sea, the course of the far-travelling wind, all this he knows. He sees all things, past and future. He is witness of the true and false deeds of men. The deeds, thoughts and devices of every man are all known to Varuṇa. He can grasp all that is in heaven and earth and beyond them. However far one runs beyond the sky, no one can leave the range of Varuṇa's sight.

Being the regulator of morality, Varuṇa is much angered by sin, and angered also by the transgression of his ordinances; for both he imposes very cruel punishment. Varuṇa's noose that binds sinners is mentioned in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-15; 1-25-11; 6-74-4 **NOTE**; 10-85-24. That noose binds the speaker of untruth and releases the speaker of truth.

### Printed p. 515
युवो राष्ट्रं बृहदिन्वति द्यौर्यौ सेतृभिररज्जुभिः सिनीथः । परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इंद्रः कृणवदु लोकं ॥ (*yuvo rāṣṭraṃ bṛhadinvati dyauryau setṛbhirarajjubhiḥ sinīthaḥ | pari no heḷo varuṇasya vṛjyā uruṃ na iṃdraḥ kṛṇavadu lokaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-84-2)
In this Ṛk it is said that Varuṇa, accompanied by Indra, binds with bonds that are not ropes. In the whole Ṛgveda this word "noose" (pāśa) occurs only once in a mantra addressed to Agni, and that in a context where he is asked to loosen the noose binding his worshippers. Therefore it may be said that these acts of binding with the noose and of releasing belong to Varuṇa alone. Varuṇa together with Mitra drives away, hates and punishes untruth. Mitra and Varuṇa punish those who are negligent in their worship; but Varuṇa spares the repentant and shows compassion to those who have transgressed his commands through forgetfulness. Varuṇa has hundreds and thousands of medicines. He removes death and takes away sin. He can take away life and can also give life; he is very skilled in protecting immortality. Such descriptions of Varuṇa's qualities occur in many Ṛks. Here we have explained it very briefly; we shall explain it on a suitable occasion.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā — फल्गु नीनक्षत्रमर्यमा देवता............ अनूराधानक्षत्रं मित्रो देवता............ । (*phalgu nīnakṣatramaryamā devatā............ anūrādhānakṣatraṃ mitro devatā............ |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 4-4.9-2) — that is, Aryaman is said to be lord of the Pūrvaphalgunī constellation and Mitra of the Anurādhā constellation.

Aryaman: In the sūktas addressed to the Ādityas, the Ādityas generally meant are Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. As we said before, in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1) only six names are given: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa. In the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3 **NOTE** the number of the Ādityas is seven, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8 it is said that Aditi first presented seven sons to the gods and afterwards bore the eighth, Mārtāṇḍa. In Atha. Ve. 8-9-21 and Tai. Ā. 1-13-3 it is said that Aditi had eight sons: Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Dhātṛ, Indra, Vivasvān. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 6-1-2-8 and Śa. Brā. 11-6-3-8) the Ādityas are twelve, one for each month. In the Purāṇas too the Ādityas are twelve. Although the name of the deity Aryaman occurs in the Ṛgveda in about a hundred places, since he has no complete personality, Yāska in his Nirukta (Nighaṇṭu) has omitted the name of this deity Aryaman when explaining the derivation of the names of the deities. Outside the mantras, Aryaman is mentioned everywhere only together with other deities, and mostly together with Mitra and Varuṇa. When Agni is addressed in winning over maidens,

### Printed p. 516
त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन्‌गुह्यं बिभर्षि । (*tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvanguhyaṃ bibharṣi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-2)
it is said "you are Aryaman".
In the Ṛk भगो अर्यमा सविता पुरंधिर्मह्यं त्वादुर्गार्हपत्याय देवाः । (*bhago aryamā savitā puraṃdhirmahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-36) the bridegroom says: O gods, Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Purandhi gave me this bride to help my householder's life.
न तमंहो न दुरितं देवासो अष्ट मर्त्यं । सजोषसो यमर्यमा मित्रो नयंति वरुणो अति द्विषः ॥ (*na tamaṃho na duritaṃ devāso aṣṭa martyaṃ | sajoṣaso yamaryamā mitro nayaṃti varuṇo ati dviṣaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126-1)
शुनमस्मभ्यमूतये वरुणो मित्रो आर्यमा । शर्म यच्छंतु सप्रथ आदित्यासो यदीमहे अति द्विषः ॥ (*śunamasmabhyamūtaye varuṇo mitro āryamā | śarma yacchaṃtu sapratha ādityāso yadīmahe ati dviṣaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126-7)
Although in the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126 the deities are called Viśvedevas, from the Ṛks quoted above it is chiefly the Ādityas who are praised here. Moreover, देवासः अष्ट (*devāsaḥ aṣṭa*) in the first Ṛk refers to the eight Ādityas (the Veda nowhere gives the number of Ādityas as more than eight). Besides, in the 7th Ṛk the word आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*) also makes this plain. In every Ṛk of this sūkta (except the last) the names Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, वरुणो, मित्रो, अर्यमा (*varuṇo, mitro, aryamā*), are recited again and again like a refrain, which indicates that these three hold the principal place among the Ādityas. Since Aryaman is not much described in the Ṛgveda, a special account is not possible.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निरिंद्र इति पंचदशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं । वसुक्रपुत्रस्य वसुकर्णस्यार्षं
> वैश्वदेवं। पंचदशी त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा जगत्यः। तथा चानुक्रम्यते। अग्निरिंद्रः पंचोना
> वासुक्रो वसुकर्णस्त्रिष्टुबंतं त्विति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अग्निरिंद्र (*agniriṃdra*) has fifteen Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta. Its seer is Vasukarṇa, son of Vasukra; its deity is the Viśvedevas. The fifteenth Ṛk is Triṣṭubh and the rest are Jagatī. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: अग्निरिंद्रः पंचोना वासुक्रो वसुकर्णस्त्रिष्टुबंतं त्विति ॥ (*agniriṃdraḥ paṃconā vāsukro vasukarṇastriṣṭubaṃtaṃ tviti ‖*)

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta अग्निरिंद्रः (*agniriṃdraḥ*) is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has fifteen Ṛks. Its seer is Vasukarṇa, son of Vasukra; the deities are the Viśvedevas; the fifteenth Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre, and the remaining Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अग्निरिंद्रः पंचोना वासुक्रो वसुकर्णस्त्रिष्टुबंतं तु (*agniriṃdraḥ paṃconā vāsukro vasukarṇastriṣṭubaṃtaṃ tu*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निरिंद्रो॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा वा॒युः पू॒षा सर॑स्वती स॒जोष॑सः ।  
> आ॒दि॒त्या विष्णु॑र्म॒रुतः॒ स्व॑र्बृ॒हत्सोमो॑ रु॒द्रो अदि॑ति॒ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । इंद्रः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । वायुः । पूषा । सरस्वती । सजोषसः ।  
> आदित्याः । विष्णुः । मरुतः । स्वः । बृहत् । सोमः । रुद्रः । अदितिः । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्न्यादय आदित्यादयो बृहद्बृहती स्वद्यौश्च सोमादय एते देवाः
> सजोषसः संहत्य ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni and the others, the Ādityas and the others, the great (Bṛhat), the Bṛhatī, Svar and Dyaus, and Soma and the others — these gods, being united (सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)), together…

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अरमा (*aramā*)—Aryaman **NOTE**
- वायुः (*vāyuḥ*)—Vāyu
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī
- आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)—the Ādityas
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—the great
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the heavenly world
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- रुद्रः (*rudraḥ*)—Rudra
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (*brahmaṇaspatiḥ*)—Brahmaṇaspati
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—being united (they pervade the atmosphere and shine)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Vāyu, the god Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the great heavenly world, Soma, Rudra, Aditi and Brahmaṇaspati, united, pervade the atmosphere and shine.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इं॒द्रा॒ग्नी वृ॑त्र॒हत्ये॑षु॒ सत्प॑ती मि॒थो हि॑न्वा॒ना त॒न्ना॒३॒॑३समो॑कसा।  
> अं॒तरि॑क्षं॒ मह्या प॑पु॒रोज॑सा॒ सोमो॑ धृत॒श्रीर्म॑हि॒मान॑मी॒रय॑न् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । वृत्रहत्येषु । सत्पती इति सत्पती । मिथः । हिन्वाना । तन्ना ।  
> संओकसा ।  
> अंतरिक्षं । महि । आ । पपुः । ओजसा । सोमः । धृतश्रीः । महिमानं । ईरयन् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृत्रहत्या युद्धानि । तेषु मिथः परस्परं तन्ना शरीरेण तत्रस्थेन बलेन
> शत्रुन्हिन्वाना प्रेरयंतौ सत्पती सतां पती समोकसा समानस्थानविंद्राग्नी । धृतश्रीरुदकं वसतीवर्याख्यं श्रयमाणो महिमानमात्मीयमीरयन् सर्वत्रोदीरयन्नुद्गमयन् सोमश्च । एते सर्वे च महि महदंतरिक्षमोजसा स्वबलेना
> पपुः । आपूरयंति । प्रा पूरणे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The *Vṛtra-slayings* are battles. In them Indra and Agni, urging (हिन्वाना (*hinvānā*)) their enemies on, each with the strength present in his own body, are lords of the good (सत्पती (*satpatī*)) and of one common abode (समोकसा (*samokasā*)). Soma, called धृतश्रीः (*dhṛtaśrīḥ*), resorts to the water called Vasatīvarī and sends forth his own greatness everywhere. All these fill the vast firmament with their own strength: आ पपुः (*ā papuḥ*) means "they fill" (root प्रा पूरणे (*prā pūraṇe*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहत्येषु (*vṛtrahatyeṣu*)—at the time of slaying Vṛtra
- मिथः (*mithaḥ*)—one another
- तन्ना (*tannā*)—joined with a body full of power
- हिन्वाना (*hinvānā*)—those who harm enemies (who urge each other on to destroy enemies)
- सत्पती (*satpatī*)—protectors of the good
- समोकसा (*samokasā*)—having a common abode
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—Indra and Agni
- धृतश्रीः (*dhṛtaśrīḥ*)—he who bears the water such as Vasatīvarī
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—his greatness
- ईरयन् (*īrayan*)—urging forth and manifesting
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma

### Printed p. 519
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with their own strength
- आ पप्पुः (*ā pappuḥ*)—pervade and shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of slaying Vṛtra, Indra and Agni, who, joined with a body full of power, urge one another on to destroy enemies, who protect the good and share a common abode, and the god Soma, who bears the water such as Vasatīvarī and sends forth and manifests his greatness, pervade and shine over the vast firmament with their own strength.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, the lords of the virtuous, standing in the same place, mutually invigorating each other with might in the Vritra-slaying battles, and the ghi-glorified Soma putting forth his greatness have filled the vast firmament with their strength.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तेषां॒ हि म॒ह्ना म॑ह॒ताम॑न॒र्वणां॒ स्तोमा॒ इय॑र्मि त॒ज्ञा  
> ऋ॑त॒वृधां॑ ।  
> ये अ॑प्स॒वम॑र्ण॒वं चि॒त्ररा॑धस॒स्ते नो॑ रासंतां म॒हये॑  ॒
> सुमित्राः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तेषां । हि । मह्ना । महतां । अनर्वणां । स्तोमान् । इयर्मि । ऋतज्ञाः ।  
> ऋतवृधां ।  
> ये । अप्सवं । अर्णवं । चित्रराधसः । ते । नः । रासंतां । महये । सुमित्राः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मह्ना स्वमहत्वेन महतामनर्वणामन्यस्मिन्नप्रत्यृतानां शत्रुभिरनभिगंतव्यानामृतावृधां सत्यभूतेन यज्ञेन वृद्धानां तेषामग्न्यादीनां देवानामेवार्तज्ञा यज्ञस्य ज्ञाताहं स्तोमानियर्मि । प्रेरयामि ॥ ऋ गतिप्रापणयोः ।
> जौहोत्यादिकः ॥ चित्रराधसश्चायनीयधनोपेता यद्वा पश्वादिलक्षणबहुधना

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Through their own greatness": I, who know the rite (ऋतज्ञा (*ṛtajñā*)), send forth (इयर्मि (*iyarmi*), root ऋ गतिप्रापणयोः (*ṛ gatiprāpaṇayoḥ*), of the Johotyādi class) praises of those gods, Agni and the rest, who are great, अनर्वणां (*anarvaṇāṃ*) (not to be approached by enemies, not opposed by another), and ऋतावृधां (*ṛtāvṛdhāṃ*) (grown by the true sacrifice). चित्रराधसः (*citrarādhasaḥ*) means possessed of wealth to be sought, or else rich in wealth of cattle and the like.

### Printed p. 520

> ये देवा अप्सवं । अप्स इति रूपनाम । रूपवंतमर्णवं ॥ अर्णसः सलोपश्च ।
> का. ५-२-१०९-३ । इति मत्त्वर्थीयो वप्रत्ययः ॥ उदकवंतं मेघं वर्षंति ते
> सुमित्र्याः शोभनसखिकर्माणस्ते देवा नोऽस्मभ्यं महये जनेषु मध्यॆ
> पूजार्थं धनं रासंतां । प्रयच्छंतु । रास्य दाने ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those gods who rain down the अप्सवं (*apsavaṃ*) cloud—अप्स (*apsa*) is a name for form, so a cloud having form (अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*), with the affix va in the sense of "possessing"), full of water—those सुमित्र्याः (*sumitryāḥ*), whose actions are those of good friends, those gods, may they give us wealth महये (*mahaye*), for honour among men (root रास्य दाने (*rāsya dāne*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतावृधां (*ṛtāvṛdhāṃ*)—those who have grown strong through sacrifice
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—through their own majesty
- महतां (*mahatāṃ*)—those who have power
- अनर्वणां (*anarvaṇāṃ*)—those not subject to the harm of enemies
- तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—of those deities, Agni and the rest
- ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*)—I, who know the truth of sacrifice
- स्तोमान् (*stomān*)—praises
- इयर्मि (*iyarmi*)—I offer
- चित्रराधसः (*citrarādhasaḥ*)—possessed of attractive wealth
- ये (*ye*)—which deities
- अप्सवं (*apsavaṃ*)—full of water (of attractive form)
- अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*)—the cloud, which they squeeze and shower rain
- ते (*te*)—such
- सुमित्राः (*sumitrāḥ*)—deities who are excellent friends
- नः महये (*naḥ mahaye*)—among people, for honour
- रासंतां (*rāsaṃtāṃ*)—may they give us wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, who know the sacrificial truth of the gods Agni and the rest, who have grown strong through sacrifice, have by their own majesty great power, and are not subject to the harm of enemies, offer them praises. May those excellent friends among the gods, rich in attractive wealth, who squeeze the cloud filled with attractive water and shower rain, give us wealth among the people for the sake of honour.

##### English translation
Skilled in pious rites, I recite the praises of these (deities), mighty through (their own) might, unassailable, exalted by sacrifice ; may those (gods) who, possessed of various wealth, (rain down) the beautiful water-cloud, acting in friendly wise, grant us (wealth) for our honour (among men).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्व॑र्णरमं॒तरि॑क्षाणि रोच॒ना द्यावा॒भूमी॑ पृथि॒वीं स्कं॑भु॒रोज॑सा ।  
> पृ॒क्षा इ॑व म॒हयं॑तः सुरा॒तयो॑ दे॒वाः स्त॑वंते॒ मनु॑षाय  ॒॑
> सूरयः ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 521

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वःनरं । अंतरिक्षाणि । रोचना । द्यावाभूमी इति । पृथिवीं । स्कंभुः । ओजसा ।  
> पृक्षाःइव । महयंतः । सुरातयः । देवाः । स्तवंते । मनुषाय । सूरयः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वर्णरं सर्वस्य स्वस्वकर्मणि नेतारमादित्यमंतरिक्षाणि । द्यावापृथिव्योरंतरा
> मध्ये क्षियंति निवसंतीत्यंतरिक्षाणि । मध्यस्थितानि रोचना रोचमानानि तेजांसि
> द्यावाभूमिा द्यावापृथिव्यौ पृथिवीं विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षं च एतानादित्यादीनोजसा
> स्वबलेनैव देवाः स्कंभुः । धारयंति ॥ स्कंभ इति सौत्रो धातुः । लिटि रूपं ॥ किंच
> पृक्षा इव दरिद्रेषु धनानि संपर्चयंत इव अत एव महयंतः स्तोत्थन्थनादिभिः
> पूजयंतः सुरातयः सुदाना मनुषाय मनुष्याय सूरयो धनावां प्रेरका
> एते देवाः स्तवंते । अस्मिन्यज्ञे स्तूयंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

स्वर्णरं (*svarṇaraṃ*) is the sun, the leader of all in their several actions. अंतरिक्षाणि (*aṃtarikṣāṇi*) are those that dwell between heaven and earth: the shining luminaries standing in the middle. The gods sustain (स्कंभुः (*skaṃbhuḥ*)—स्कंभ (*skaṃbha*) is a sautra root; the form is perfect) these, the sun and the rest, heaven and earth, and the wide firmament, by their own strength. Further: like पृक्षाः (*pṛkṣāḥ*), as if bringing wealth to the poor, and therefore honouring (their worshippers) with praises and the like, these gods, generous givers (सुरातयः (*surātayaḥ*)), सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) who impel wealth to man (मनुषाय (*manuṣāya*)), are praised at this sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वर्णरं (*svarṇaraṃ*)—the sun, guide of all actions
- अंतरिक्षाणि (*aṃtarikṣāṇi*)—those that lie between heaven and earth
- रोचना (*rocanā*)—all luminaries
- द्यावाभूमी (*dyāvābhūmī*)—heaven and earth
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the wide firmament
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with their strength
- स्कंभुः (*skaṃbhuḥ*)—the gods have sustained
- पृक्षा इव (*pṛkṣā iva*)—like those who give food to the poor
- महयंतः (*mahayaṃtaḥ*)—those who give wealth and the like to worshippers
- सुरातयः (*surātayaḥ*)—generous givers
- मनुषाय (*manuṣāya*)—to man
- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—impellers
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—gods
- स्तुवंते (*stuvaṃte*)—are praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods have sustained by their power the sun, guide of all actions, all the luminaries between heaven and earth, heaven and earth, and the wide firmament. The gods, who give wealth and the like to worshippers as one gives food to the poor, who are generous givers and impellers of man, are praised.

##### English translation
They have sustained by their strength the leader of all (the sun), the luminaries of the firmament, heaven and earth, the outstretched (firmament); honouring (their worshippers) like those who give food (to the poor), the generous gods bestowing wealth on man are glorified (at this sacrifice).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मि॒त्राय॑ शिक्ष॒ वरु॑णाय दा॒शुषे॒ या स॒म्राजा॒ मन॑सा॒ न प्र॒युच्छ॑तः ।  
> ययो॒र्धाम॒ धर्म॑णा॒ रोच॑ते बृ॒हद्ययो॑रु॒भे रोद॑सी॒ ॒॑ ॑
> नाधसी वृत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मित्राय । शिक्ष । वरुणाय । दाशुषे । या । संराजा । मनसा । न । प्रयुच्छतः ।  
> ययोः । धाम । धर्मणा । रोचते । बृहत् । ययोः । उभे इति । रोदसी  
> इति । नाधसी इति । वृता ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दाशुषे धनानि स्तोतृभ्यः प्रयच्छते मित्राय वरुणाय च शिक्ष । हवींषि
> प्रयच्छ । शिक्षतिर्दानकर्मा । सम्राजा सम्राजौ सर्वस्य या यौ मित्रावरुणौ मनसांतःकरणेनापि न प्रयुच्छतः न प्रमाद्यतः किमुत वाह्येन व्यापारेण ॥ युच्छ
> प्रमादे । भौवादिकः ॥ ययोर्मित्रावरुणयोर्बृहद्महद्दाम शरीरं धर्मणात्मीयेन लोकप्रकाशनादिलक्षणेन कर्मणा रोचते सम्यग्धीप्यते । ययोश्च नाधसी ॥
> णाधृ याच्चोपतापैश्वर्याशीषु ॥ याचमाने उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ वृत्
> वर्तमाने भवतः । यद्वा । नाधसी देवमनुष्यैः समृद्धे द्यावापृथिव्यौ । तयोर्वृत् वर्तमाने भवतः । तदधीने भवत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To Mitra and Varuna, who give wealth to the worshippers, शिक्ष (*śikṣa*): offer oblations (शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) is a verb of giving). Those two, सम्राजा (*samrājā*), rulers of all, who do not न प्रयुच्छतः (*na prayucchataḥ*) lapse even in thought, much less in outward action (root युच्छ प्रमादे (*yuccha pramāde*), Bhūvādi class). Their great body (धाम (*dhāma*)) shines brightly through धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*), their own action such as illuminating the world. In them the two worlds, heaven and earth, नाधसी (*nādhasī*) (root णाधृ याच्चोपतापैश्वर्याशीषु (*ṇādhṛ yāccopatāpaiśvaryāśīṣu*)) imploring, abide (वृत् (*vṛt*)). Or else: नाधसी (*nādhasī*) means heaven and earth enriched by gods and men; they abide in them, that is, are dependent on them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सम्राजा (*samrājā*)—sovereigns of the whole world
- या (*yā*)—which Mitra and Varuna
- मनसा (*manasā*)—even in mind
- न प्रयुच्छतः (*na prayucchataḥ*)—do not forget their duty
- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—of which Mitra and Varuna
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great
- धाम (*dhāma*)—body
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—through excellent action
- रोचते (*rocate*)—shines
- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—in whom
- नाधसी (*nādhasī*)—full of devotion
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- वृत् (*vṛt*)—are established; such are they
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—who give wealth to the sacrificer
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—to Mitra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to Varuna
- शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)—offer oblation

### Printed p. 523

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Offer oblation to Mitra and Varuna, sovereigns of the whole world, who do not forget their duty even in mind, whose great body shines through excellent action, in whom both heaven and earth, full of devotion, are established, and who give wealth to the sacrificer.

##### English translation
Worship the liberal Mitra and Varuna, the two royal deities who are never negligent in their thoughts, whose vast body is resplendent through their functions, upon whom the two solicitous worlds (heaven and earth) remain (dependent)

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या गौर्व॑त॒निं प॒र्येति॑ निष्कृ॒तं पयो॒ दुहा॑ना व्रत॒नीर॑वा॒रतः॑ ।  
> सा प्र॑ब्रुवा॒णा वरु॑णाय दा॒शुषे॑ दे॒वेभ्यो॑ दाशद्ध॒ विषा॑ वि॒वस्व॑ते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । गौः । वर्तनिं । परिएति । निःकृतं । पयः । दुहाना । व्रतनीः । अवारतः ॥  
> सा । प्रब्रुवाणा । वरुणाय । दाशुषे । देवेभ्यः । दाशत् । हविषा । विवस्वते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> येयं मदीया पयः क्षीरादिकं दुहाना व्रतनीराश्रयणपयःप्रदानेन कर्मणो नेत्री गौर्निष्कृतं संस्कृतं वर्तनिमावासस्थानं यज्ञमवारतोऽवरणेनाप्रार्थनेनैव पर्योति परिगच्छति स्वयमेवागच्छति प्रब्रुवाणा मया
> प्रस्तूयमाना सा गौर्दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते वरुणाय देवेभ्योऽन्येभ्य इंद्रादिभ्यत्त्व हविषान्नेन विवस्वते देवान्परिचरते मह्यं मां रक्षितुं दाशत् । पयः प्रयच्छतु ॥ दाश्य दाने । लेट्यडागमः॥ यद्वा गौरिति माध्यमिका वाक् या पय ऊर्ज०
> दुहाना सा नो मंद्रॆषमूर्ज० दुहाना । ऋ. ८-१००-११ । इत्यादिषु दृष्टत्वात् । तत्परतया पूर्ववद्योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This cow of mine, milking milk and the like, leader of the rite (व्रतनीः (*vratanīḥ*)) by giving milk for the support of the vow, goes round (पर्येति (*paryeti*)) the prepared (निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)) place of abode, the sacrifice, of her own accord, unsought (अवारतः (*avārataḥ*)). Praised (प्रब्रुवाणा (*prabruvāṇā*)) by me, may that cow give (दाशत् (*dāśat*), root दाश्य दाने (*dāśya dāne*), leṭ with aṭ-augment) milk to me, to protect me, for Varuna who has given oblation, for the other gods Indra and the rest, and for the one who serves the gods with the oblation of food (विवस्वते (*vivasvate*)). Or else: गौः (*gauḥ*) is the middle-realm Speech, who milks milk and strength; this is seen in सा नो मंद्रॆषमूर्ज० दुहाना (*sā no maṃdrèṣamūrja0 duhānā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-100-11) and similar; the verse is to be construed as before with that reference.

### Printed p. 524

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- दुहाना (*duhānā*)—milking
- व्रतनीः (*vratanīḥ*)—therefore the accomplisher of the rite
- या गौः (*yā gauḥ*)—which cow
- निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)—consecrated with the implements
- वर्तनिं (*vartaniṃ*)—the sacrifice
- अवारतः (*avārataḥ*)—of her own impulse (unasked by anyone)
- पर्येति (*paryeti*)—comes and joins
- सा (*sā*)—such
- प्रब्रुवाणा (*prabruvāṇā*)—the cow praised by me
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the giver
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to Varuṇa
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods, Indra and the rest
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblation
- विवस्वते (*vivasvate*)—to me, who worship the gods
- दाशत् (*dāśat*)—may she give milk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that cow which yields milk, and is therefore the accomplisher of the rite, which of her own impulse comes and joins the sacrifice consecrated with the implements, being praised by me, give milk to the generous Varuṇa, to the gods Indra and the rest, and to me who worship the gods with oblation.

##### English translation
May that cow, the leader of the rite, which yielding her milk proceeds uncalled to the consecrated place(of sacrifice), may she, propitiated by me, yield her milk to (me), the offerer of oblations to liberal Varuna and the (other) gods.

> दि॒वक्ष॑सो अग्निजि॒ह्वा ऋ॑ता॒वृध॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ योनिं॑ विमृ॒शंत॑ आसते ।  
> द्यां स्क॑भि॒त्त्वग१॒॑प आ च॑क्रु॒रोज॑सा य॒ज्ञं ज॑नि॒त्वी त॒न्वी॒३॒॑३नि  ॑
> मामृजुः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवक्षसः । अग्निजिह्वा । ऋतवृधः । ऋतस्य । योनिं । विमृशंतः । आसते ॥  
> द्यां । स्कभित्वी । अपः । आ । चक्रुः । ओजसा । यज्ञं । जनित्वी । तन्वि । नि । ममृजुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवक्षसः स्वतेजसा दिवं व्याप्नुवंतः ॥ अक्षू व्याप्तौ । असुनि रूपं ॥ यद्वा ।
> दिवो वोढारः आग्निजिह्वा अग्न्यास्याः । अग्निना हवींषि लिहंत्यास्वादयंतीति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

दिवक्षसः (*divakṣasaḥ*): those who pervade heaven with their own radiance (root अक्षू (*akṣū*), to pervade). Or else: bearers of heaven. अग्निजिह्वा (*agnijihvā*): having Agni as mouth, since they lick up, that is, taste, the oblations through Agni.

### Printed p. 525

> तन्मुखाः । ऋतावृधो यज्ञवृद्धा यज्ञस्य वर्धयितारो देवा वर्तस्य सत्यभूतस्य
> यज्ञस्य योनिं स्थानं विमृशंतो विचारयंतः प्रतीक्षमाणाः संत आसते । सर्वत्र
> तिष्यंति । त इमे द्यां द्युलोकं स्वभित्वा स्वभित्वा तां धारयित्वाजसा स्वबलेनापोऽपेक्षितान्युदकान्या चक्रुः । आकुर्वंति । ततो यज्ञं यजनीयं हविश्च जनित्वी
> जनयित्वा तन्नि स्वशरीरे नि मामृजुः । निम्मृजंति । नितरामलंकुर्वंति । हविर्भक्षयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*): the gods who increase the sacrifice. They sit watching, contemplating the place of the true sacrifice, and abide everywhere. Having sustained heaven they bring about by their own strength the waters that are needed. Then, having produced the sacrifice and the oblation, they adorn their own bodies with it; that is, they eat the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवक्षसः (*divakṣasaḥ*)—pervading the heavenly world with their radiance
- अग्निजिह्वाः (*agnijihvāḥ*)—having a tongue in the form of Agni
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—the gods, increasers of the sacrifice
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice, which is truth
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—the place
- विमृशंतः (*vimṛśaṃtaḥ*)—looking with the eye of meditation
- आसते (*āsate*)—sit
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heavenly world
- स्कभित्वी (*skabhitvī*)—having sustained
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by their power
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- आ चक्रुः (*ā cakruḥ*)—produce
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice (the oblation)
- जनित्वी (*janitvī*)—having produced
- तन्नि (*tanni*)—their own body
- नि मामृजुः (*ni māmṛjuḥ*)—adorn themselves with it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, who pervade heaven with their radiance, have Agni as their tongue and increase the sacrifice, sit contemplating with the eye of meditation the place of the sacrifice, which is truth. Having sustained heaven, they produce the waters by their power. Having produced the sacrifice, they adorn their bodies with it.

##### English translation
Pervading heaven (with their radiance), having Agni as their tongue, the augmenters of sacrifice, (these deities) sit contemplating the place of sacrifice ; sustaining heaven they have produced the waters by their power; having generated sacrifice, they have decorated their persons (with it).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒रि॒क्षिता॑ पि॒तरा॑ पूर्व॒जाव॑री ऋ॒तस्य॒ योना॑ क्षयतः॒ समो॑कसा ।  
> द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी वरु॑णाय॒ सव्र॑ते घृ॒तव॒त्पयो॑ महि॒षाय॑ पिन्वतः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परिक्षिता । पितरा । पूर्वजावरी इति पूर्वजावरी । ऋतस्य । योना । क्षयतः ।  
> संओकसा ।

### Printed p. 526

> द्यावापृथिवी इति । वरुणाय । सव्रते इति सव्रते । धृतवत् । पयः । महिषाय । पिन्वतः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परिक्षिता परितो निवसंत्यौ सर्वत्र व्यापिन्यौ पितरा सर्वेषां मातापितृभूते
> आत एव पूर्वजावरी पूर्वं जाते समोकसा समाननिवासस्थाने एते द्यावापृथिव्यावृतस्य यज्ञस्य योना योन् स्थाने क्षयतः। आहुत्यधिकरणत्वेन निवसतः। हविर्धानरूपे ना क्षियतः । किंच सव्रते समानकर्मणी ते महिषाय महते पूज्याय वा
> वरुणाय । तं यष्टुं । उपलक्षणमेतत् । अन्यान्धेवानपि । घृतवत्क्षरणवत् पय
> उदकं पिन्वतः । सिंचतः । उदकेन ह्यन्नं जायते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

परिक्षिता (*parikṣitā*): dwelling all around, pervading everywhere; पितरा (*pitarā*): the mother and father of all; therefore पूर्वजावरी (*pūrvajāvarī*): born first; समोकसा (*samokasā*): having a common dwelling-place. These, Heaven and Earth, dwell in the place of the sacrifice, as the support of the oblation, in the form of the receptacle of the oblation. Further, सव्रते (*savrate*): of common work, they sprinkle water that flows like ghee for the great, or adorable, Varuṇa, to worship him. This is indicative; the other gods too are meant. For by water food is produced.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- परिक्षिता (*parikṣitā*)—pervading everywhere
- पितरा (*pitarā*)—mother and father of the world
- पूर्वजावरी (*pūrvajāvarī*)—born before everything
- समोकसा (*samokasā*)—having a common abode
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—Heaven and Earth
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- योना (*yonā*)—in the place
- क्षयतः (*kṣayataḥ*)—dwell
- सव्रते (*savrate*)—they, of common work
- महिषाय (*mahiṣāya*)—adorable
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to worship Varuṇa
- धृतवत् (*dhṛtavat*)—flowing
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—water
- पिन्वतः (*pinvataḥ*)—pour out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and Earth, who pervade everywhere, are the mother and father of the world, were born before everything and have a common abode, dwell in the place of the sacrifice. Having common work, they pour out flowing water to worship the adorable Varuṇa.

##### English translation
The encompassing parents (heaven and earth), born of old, having a common dwelling, sit down upon the place of sacrifice ; engaged in a common observance they sprinkle upon the adorable Varuna water mixed with butter.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒र्जन्या॒वाता॑ वृष॒भा पु॑री॒षिणें॑द्रवा॒यू वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो  ॒॑
> अर्यमा ॥

### Printed p. 527

> देवा आदित्या अदितिं हवामहे ये पार्थिवासो दिव्यासो  
> अप्सु ये ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पर्जन्यावाता । वृषभा । पुरीषिणा । इंद्रवायू इति । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा ॥  
> देवान् । आदित्यान् । अदितिं । हनामहे । ये । पार्थिवासः । दिव्यासः । अप्सु । ये ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पर्जन्यावाता पर्जन्यावातौ पर्जन्यानायू वृषभा वृषभौ कामानां सेक्तारौ
> पुरीषिणा पुरीषिणौ । पुरीषमुदकं । कर्तृत्वेन तद्वंतौ ताविंद्रवायू वरुणादयश्च एते स्वमहिम्ना सर्वत्र वर्तंते । वायोः पर्जन्येनेंद्रेण च तत्कार्या.
> पेक्षया सहोपादानं । एतानादित्यान्देवानदितिं तेषां मातरं च हवामहे ।
> अस्मिन्ज्ञे वयमाह्वयामः । किंच ये देवाः पार्थिवासः पार्थिवाः पृथिव्यां
> भवा ये च दिव्या दिवि जाता ये चाप्स्यंतरिक्षे समुत्पन्नाः तानाह्वयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पर्जन्यावाता (*parjanyāvātā*): Parjanya and Vāta; वृषभा (*vṛṣabhā*): showerers of desires; पुरीषिणा (*purīṣiṇā*): possessing पुरीष (*purīṣa*), water, as agents. These two, Indra and Vāyu, and Varuṇa and the others, exist everywhere by their own greatness. Vāyu is taken together with Parjanya and Indra because of the relation of their functions. We invoke these Ādityas, the gods, and Aditi, their mother, in this sacrifice. Further, we invoke those gods who are पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*), born on earth, those who are दिव्या (*divyā*), born in heaven, and those born अप्सु (*apsu*), in the atmosphere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभा (*vṛṣabhā*)—granters of desires
- पर्जन्यावाता (*parjanyāvātā*)—Parjanya and Vāyu
- पुरीषिणा (*purīṣiṇā*)—possessors of water
- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—the deities Indra and Vāyu
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman; they pervade everywhere
- ये (*ye*)—who
- पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*)—are on earth
- ये (*ye*)—who
- दिव्यासः (*divyāsaḥ*)—are in the heavenly world
- अप्पु (*appu*)—who are in the atmosphere
- देवान् (*devān*)—those gods
- आदित्यान् (*ādityān*)—the Ādityas
- अदितिं (*aditiṃ*)—Aditi, the mother of the gods
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Parjanya and Vāyu, granters of desires, Indra and the Vāyu deity, possessors of water, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman pervade everywhere. All the gods, those on earth, those in the heavenly world and those in the atmosphere, the Ādityas, and Aditi, the mother of the gods, we call with prayer.

##### English translation
The two showerers (of desires), Parjanya and Vata, the two senders of water, Indra and Vayu, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman; we invoke the divine Adityas, Aditi and the gods, who dwell on the earth, or in heaven, or in he waters.
