> ईमह इति याच्छाकर्मा ॥ ईज् गत् दैवादिकः । बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक्॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*): they shine by ऋत (*ṛta*), truth; or they shine abundantly by their own radiance. O wise ones, the Soma which, for your welfare and your delight, brings Tvaṣṭṛ and the others (root ओह (*oha*), to go, of the bhū class) – brings, reaches – likewise reaches Bṛhaspati, the very wise, and Indra, the eater (destroyer) of the asura Vṛtra. We, sharing wealth, ask for that Soma, dear to Indra; we beg for wealth. ईमहे (*īmahe*) is a verb meaning "to ask" (root ईज् (*īj*) of the divādi class).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*)—O Ṛbhus
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for your welfare
- त्वष्टारं (*tvaṣṭāraṃ*)—Tvaṣṭṛ
- वायुं (*vāyuṃ*)—Vāyu
- देव्यौ होतार् (*devyau hotār*)—the Aśvin deities, divine Hotṛs
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—the goddess Uṣas
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- वृत्रखादं (*vṛtrakhādaṃ*)—the destroyer of Vṛtra
- सुमेधसं (*sumedhasaṃ*)—Indra, possessed of excellent wisdom
- ओहते (*ohate*)—brings to the sacrifice
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—the friend of Indra
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- धनसाः (*dhanasāḥ*)—we who desire wealth
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—ask for wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ṛbhus, the Soma who, for your welfare, brings to the sacrifice Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, the Aśvin deities who are divine Hotṛs, the goddess Uṣas, Bṛhaspati, the destroyer of Vṛtra, and Indra, possessed of excellent wisdom,

### Printed p. 529

that Soma, the friend of Indra, we who desire wealth ask for wealth.

##### English translation
Desirous of wealth, we solicit that Soma, the friend of Indra, who for your welfare, Ribhus, brings (hither) Twashtri, Vayu, the two divine sacrificers. (the Ashwins), Dawn, Brihaspati, and the wise slayer of the Vritra.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब्रह्म॒ गामश्वं॑ ज॒नयं॑त॒ ओष॑धी॒र्वन॒स्पती॑न्स्पृथि॒वीं पर्व॑ता  ॒
> असः ।  
> सूर्यं॑ दि॒वि रो॒हयं॑तः सु॒दान॑व॒ आर्या॑ व्र॒ता वि॑सृ॒जंतो॒ ॒ ॑
> अधि क्षमि ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ब्रह्म । गां। अश्वं। जनयंतः। ओषधीः। वनस्पतीन्। पृथिवीं। पर्वतान्। अपः॥  
> सूर्यं । दिवि । रोहयंतः । सुदानवः । आर्या । वृता । विस्पृजंतः । अधि । क्षमि॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रह्म वर्धनसाधनमन्नं । अन्नेन हि सर्वाः प्रजाः वर्धंते । गामश्वमेतत्पृथ्वीन्यशून् तथौषधीर्वनस्पतींश्च तथा पृथिवीं विस्तीर्णां भूमिं पर्वताइलैलोच्चयान् वृष्टा जगदापूरकान्मेघान्वा अप उदकान्यंतरिक्षं वा एताज्ञानयंत उत्पादयंतः किंच दिवि द्युलोके सूर्यमादित्यं रोहयंतः सुदानवः शोभनदानास्तेऽमी देवा अधि क्षमि ॥ आत इति योगविभागात् । पा-६-४-१४० ।
> अकार लोपः ॥ क्षमायां पृथिव्यामार्या श्रेष्ठानि कल्याणानि व्रतानि कर्माणि
> यागादीनि विसृजंतः प्रसारयंतः सर्वत्र वर्तंते । तान्वयं धनं याचामह इति
> शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ब्रह्म (*brahma*): food, the means of growth; for by food all creatures grow. They produce the cow and the horse, these animals; likewise the herbs and the trees; likewise the earth, the broad land; the mountains, the heaps of rock; and अपः (*apaḥ*), the waters, or the clouds that fill the world with rain, or the atmosphere. Further, those generous gods who make the sun, Āditya, rise in heaven अधि क्षमि (*adhi kṣami*), on the earth, send forth and spread excellent, auspicious rites (व्रतानि (*vratāni*)), sacrifices and the like, and exist everywhere. We ask wealth of them; this is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—nourishing food
- गां (*gāṃ*)—the cow
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—the horse
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the herbs
- वनस्पतीन् (*vanaspatīn*)—the trees
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- पर्वतान् (*parvatān*)—the mountains

### Printed p. 530
**Pratipadārtha** (continued)
- गळन्नू (*gaḷannū*)—mountains (the word continues from the previous page)
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—waters
- जनयंतः (*janayaṃtaḥ*)—producing
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heavenly world
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- रोहयंतः (*rohayaṃtaḥ*)—establishing on high
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—the gods, generous givers
- अधि क्षमि (*adhi kṣami*)—upon the earth
- आर्य व्रता (*ārya vratā*)—auspicious rites such as sacrifices
- विसृजंतः (*visṛjaṃtaḥ*)—they perform extensively

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The generous giver-gods, who produce nourishing food, horses, plants, trees, the earth, mountains and waters, and who establish the sun on high in the heavenly world, extensively carry out upon the earth auspicious rites such as sacrifices.

##### English translation
Generating food, cows, horses, plants, trees, the earth mountains and waters, elevating the sun in heaven, munificent, promoting sacred observances upon the earth, (they abide everywhere).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भु॒ज्युमंह॑सः पिपृथो॒ निर॑श्विना॒ श्यावं॑ पु॒त्रं व॑ध्रिम॒त्या अ॑जिन्वतं ।  
> क॒म॒द्युवं॑ विम॒दायो॑हथुर्यु॒वं वि॑ष्णा॒ष्ट्वं१॒॑विश्व॑का॒याव॑  
> सृजथः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भुज्युं । अंहसः । पिपृथः । निः । अश्विना । श्यावं । पुत्रं । वध्रिमत्याः । अजिन्वतं ।  
> कमद्युवं । विमदाय । ऊहथुः । युवं । विष्णाष्ट्वं । विश्वकाय । अव। सृजथः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्ववंतौ सर्वं व्याप्प्नुवंतौ वैतन्नामकौ हे देवौ अंहस उपद्रवकारिणः समुद्राद्भुज्यं तुग्रपुत्रमेतन्नामानं निः पिपृथः । निष्पारयथः । नितरां
> रक्षथः ॥ पृ पालनपूरणयोः । जौहोत्यादिकः ॥ निष्पौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात् ।
> ऋ. १-११८-६ । इति निगमः । तथा श्यावं हिरण्यहस्तनामानं पुत्रं वध्रिमत्या एतन्ना
> मिकाया अजिन्वतं । अप्रीणयतं । अदत्तं। हिरण्यहस्तमश्विना रराणा। ऋ. १-११७-२४।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, the two horse-possessing, all-pervading gods: you rescued Bhujyu, son of Tugra, from the distressing sea (अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)), protecting and carrying him across. Sāyaṇa cites the Nigama Ṛ. 1-118-6 (निष्पौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात् (*niṣpaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrāt*)). The root पृ (*pṛ*) is in the sense of protecting and filling (Jauhotyādi class). You also gratified Vadhrimatī (so named) by giving her her son Śyāva, called Hiraṇyahasta; he cites the Nigama Ṛ. 1-117-24 (अदत्तं हिरण्यहस्तमश्विना रराणा (*adattaṃ hiraṇyahastamaśvinā rarāṇā*)).

### Printed p. 531

> इत्यादि निगमः । तथा कमद्युवं कामस्य दीपनीं वेनपुत्रीं जायां विमदायर्षये युवमूहथुः। प्रापयथः। युवं रथेन विमदाय । ऋ. १०-३९-७ । इति
> निगमः। तथा विष्णाप्वमेतन्नामानं विनष्टं पुत्रं विश्वकायर्षय आनीयाव सृजथः ।
> अदत्तं । पशुं न नष्टमिव दर्शनाय । ऋ. १-११६-२३ । इति निगमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

So too you brought to the seer Vimada his wife Kamadyu, the kindler of desire, daughter of Vena (Ṛ. 10-39-7). And you restored to the seer Viśvaka his lost son Viṣṇāpu, as one restores a lost animal for sight (Ṛ. 1-116-23).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin gods
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from the sea, the seat of harm
- भुज्युवं (*bhujyuvaṃ*)—Bhujyu
- नि पिपृथः (*ni pipṛthaḥ*)—you protected
- वध्रिमत्याः (*vadhrimatyāḥ*)—to Vadhrimati
- श्यावं पुत्रं (*śyāvaṃ putraṃ*)—the son named Śyāva
- अजिन्वतं (*ajinvataṃ*)—you graciously gave
- विमदाय (*vimadāya*)—to the seer named Vimada
- कमद्युवं (*kamadyuvaṃ*)—the wife named Kamadyu
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you
- ऊहथुः (*ūhathuḥ*)—you provided
- विश्वकाय (*viśvakāya*)—to the seer named Viśvaka
- विष्णाप्वं (*viṣṇāpvaṃ*)—the son named Viṣṇāpta
- अव सृजथः (*ava sṛjathaḥ*)—you searched out and gave

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, you protected Bhujyu from the sea, the seat of harm. You graciously gave Vadhrimati her son Śyāva. You provided the seer Vimada with the wife Kamadyu. You searched out and gave the seer Viśvaka his son Viṣṇāpta.

##### English translation
You, Ashwins, extricated Bhujyu from calamity, you gave to Vadhrimati her son Shyava ; you gave Kamadyu (as a wife) to Vimada : you restored (the lost) Vishnapu to Vishwaka.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For Bhujyu, see the Ṛks beginning निष्टौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात् (*niṣṭaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrāt*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-6) and others; for Vadhrimati, see Bhāga 9 p. 408 and Bhāga 27 p. 954; for Viśvaka and Viṣṇāpu, see 9 p. 298; for Vimada, see the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-7 and others, where it is written.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पावी॑रवी तन्य॒तुरेक॑पाद॒जो दि॒वो ध॒र्ता सिंधु॒रासः॑ समु॒द्रियः॑ ।  
> विश्वे॑ दे॒वासः॑ शृणव॒न्वचां॑सि मे॒ सर॑स्वती स॒ह धी॒भिः पुरं॑ध्या ॥

### Printed p. 532

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पावीरवी । तन्यतुः । एकपात् । अजः । दिवः । धर्ता । सिंधुः । आपः । समुद्रियः ।  
> विश्वे । देवासः । शृणवन् । वचांसि । मे । सरस्वती । सह । धीभिः । पुरंध्या ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पावीरव्यायुधवती तन्यतुः स्तनयित्री वाग्माध्यमिका तथा दिवो द्युलोकस्य
> धर्ता धारयिताज एकपात् एक एव पद्यते गच्छतीति न जायत इत्येत्संज्ञको
> देवः सिंधुश्च समुद्रियः । समुद्रमंतरिक्षं । तत्र भवा आपश्च ॥ समुद्राभ्राद्ध इति
> भावार्थे घप्रत्ययः ॥ विश्वे देवाश्च धीभिः कर्मभिर्युक्ताः पुरंध्या बहुविधया
> प्रज्ञया सहिता सरस्वती च मे मदीयानि वचांसि वक्तव्यानि स्तोत्राणि शृणवन् ।
> शृण्वंतु । पविः शल्यो भवति यद्विपुनाति कायमित्यादि निरुक्तमनुसंधेयं ।
> नि- १२-३० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pāvīravī is the weapon-bearing voice of the middle region, thundering (तन्यतुः (*tanyatuḥ*)). Aja Ekapād is the upholder of heaven, a god so named because he alone moves and is not born. Sindhu (the sea deity) and the waters of the sea, i.e. of the atmosphere, born there (the affix gha in the sense of the state, by समुद्राभ्राद्ध (*samudrābhrāddha*)). The All-gods, endowed with rites, and Sarasvatī, with manifold wisdom, are to hear my words, the praises to be uttered. Pavi is a spear, or "that which purifies the body", and so on, according to the Nirukta, Ni. 12-30.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पावीरवी (*pāvīravī*)—the weapon-bearing
- तन्यतुः (*tanyatuḥ*)—the sounding Vāg-devī of the middle region
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—the upholder
- अज एकपात् (*aja ekapāt*)—the god named Aja Ekapāt
- सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*)—the sea deity
- समुद्रियः (*samudriyaḥ*)—born of the atmosphere
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)—the All-gods
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—endowed with rites
- पुरंध्या सह (*puraṃdhyā saha*)—endowed with excellent knowledge
- मे (*me*)—my
- वचांसि (*vacāṃsi*)—words of praise
- शृण्वन् (*śṛṇvan*)—may they hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the weapon-bearing, sounding Vāg-devī of the middle region, the god Aja Ekapāt who upholds the heavenly world, the sea deity, the waters born of the atmosphere, the All-gods and Sarasvatī, all these deities, endowed with rites and excellent knowledge, hear my words of praise.

##### English translation
May the armed and thundering (voice of mid-heaven); the upholder of heaven, Aja Ekapad, the ocean, the waters of the firmament, the universal gods and Saraswati, accompanied by sacred rites and abundant wisdom, hear my words.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वे॑ दे॒वाः स॒ह धी॒भिः पुरं॑ध्या॒ मनो॒र्यज॑त्रा अ॒मृता॑  ॒
> ऋत॒ज्ञाः ।

### Printed p. 533

> रातिषाचो अभिषाचः स्वर्विदः स्वर्गिरो ब्रह्मसूक्तं जुषेरत ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वे । देवाः । सह । धीभिः । पुरंध्या । मनोः । यजत्राः । अमृताः । ऋतज्ञाः ।  
> रातिसाचः। अभिसाचः। स्वःविदः । स्वः । गिरः । ब्रह्म । सुउक्तं । जुषेरत ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धीभिः कर्मभिः सहिताः पुरंध्या प्रज्ञानेन युक्ता मनोर्मनुष्यस्य यज्ञे
> यजत्रा यष्टव्या अमृता मरणधर्मरहिता ऋतज्ञाः सत्यविदो रातिषाचो दीयमानं हविः सेवमाना अभिषाच अभिमुख्यन यज्ञं समवयंतः संगतवंतः स्वर्विधः
> सर्वस्य लंभका विश्वे सर्व इंद्रादयो देवाः स्वः सर्वा गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतीब्रह्म महच्चान्नं सूक्तं सुष्टु वक्तव्यं स्तोमं यद्वा सुष्टु मंत्रेण सह दत्तमन्नं जुषेरत । सेवंतां ॥ जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । तौदादिकः । अनुदात्तेत् ।
> लिजि झस्य रनादेशाभावश्चांदसः । बहुलं छंदसीति रुडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The All-gods, Indra and the rest, accompanied by rites (धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)) and endowed with wisdom (पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)), are to be worshipped in the sacrifice of man (Manu); they are immortal, knowers of truth, partakers of the oblation offered, coming together facing the sacrifice, and obtainers of all. May they enjoy all our praises, and the great food (ब्रह्म (*brahma*)), the well-spoken hymn (सूक्तं (*sūktaṃ*)); or else the food given together with a well-spoken mantra. जुषेरत (*juṣerata*) means "may they enjoy".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनोः (*manoḥ*)—in man's sacrifice
- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—worthy of worship
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—free from mortality
- ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*)—knowers of truth
- रातिषाचः (*rātiṣācaḥ*)—partakers of the oblation
- अभिषाचः (*abhiṣācaḥ*)—those who come together to the sacrifice
- स्वर्विदः (*svarvidaḥ*)—omniscient
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—endowed with rites
- पुरंध्या सह (*puraṃdhyā saha*)—endowed with excellent knowledge
- सूक्तं (*sūktaṃ*)—well recited
- स्वः गिरः (*svaḥ giraḥ*)—all our praises
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the oblation
- जुषेरत (*juṣerata*)—may they enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, worthy of worship in man's sacrifice, immortal, knowers of truth, partakers of the oblation, coming together to the sacrifice, omniscient, endowed with rites and excellent knowledge, enjoy all our well-recited praises and the oblations.

##### English translation
May the universal gods, accompanied by sacred rites and abundant wisdom, adorable (at the sacrifice) of men, immortal, the knowers of truth,

### Printed p. 534
waiting on the oblation to be given, arriving together (at the sacrifice) omniscient, graciously accept all our praises and abuudant food with well-suug hymns.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वान्वसि॑ष्ठो अ॒मृता॑न्ववंदे॒ ये विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒भि प्र॑त॒स्थुः ॥  
> ते नो॑ रासंतामुरुगा॒यम॒द्य यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑  
> नः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवान् । वसिष्ठः । अमृतान् । ववंदे । ये । विश्वा । भुवना । अभि । प्रतस्थुः ।  
> ते । नः । रासंतां । उरुगायं । अद्य । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसिष्ठो वसिष्ठकुलजोऽयमृषिरमृतान्मरणरहितान्देवान्ववंदे । एवमस्तावीत् । ये देवा विश्वा विश्वानि भुवनानि लोकानभि प्रतस्थुः स्वतेजसाभिभवंति ।
> अभितः प्रतिष्ठंतीति वा ॥ प्रपूर्वात्तिष्ठतेर्लिटि रूपं । समासस्वरः ॥ ते देवा अद्यास्मिन्निने नोऽस्मभ्यमुरुगायं प्रभूतयशस्कमन्नं रासंतां । प्रयच्छंतु । हे
> देवाः यूयं स्वस्तिभिः कल्याणीभिरूतिभिर्नोऽस्मान्सदा सर्वदा पात । रक्षत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vasiṣṭha, this seer born in the Vasiṣṭha family, has praised the immortal gods who pervade all worlds with their own splendour, or who stand all around. प्रतस्थुः (*pratasthuḥ*) is the perfect of the root with the prefix pra. May those gods today give us widely famed food. O gods, protect us always with auspicious aids.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which gods
- विश्वा भुवना (*viśvā bhuvanā*)—all worlds
- अभि प्रतस्थुः (*abhi pratasthuḥ*)—those who have pervaded with their splendours
- अमृतान् (*amṛtān*)—immortal
- देवान् (*devān*)—gods
- वसिष्ठः (*vasiṣṭhaḥ*)—this seer born in the Vasiṣṭha line
- ववंदे (*vavaṃde*)—has saluted with praise
- ते (*te*)—those same gods
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- उरुगायं (*urugāyaṃ*)—highly renowned, excellent food
- रासंतां (*rāsaṃtāṃ*)—may they give
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you (O gods)
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with auspicious protections
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This seer, born in the Vasiṣṭha line, has saluted with praise the immortal gods who pervade all worlds with their splendours. May those same gods today give us most excellent and renowned food. O gods, protect us always with your auspicious protections.

### Printed p. 535

##### English translation
(Descendant of ) Vasishtha, I have glorified the immortal gods who preside over all worlds : may they this day bestow upon us widely-famed food ; do you always cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 66 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवान्हुव इति पंचदशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । ऋष्या द्याः पूर्ववत् । देवान्हुव इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ पृष्ठाभिप्लवषडहयोः पंचमेऽहनीदं वैश्वदेवनिविद्धानं ।
> सूत्रितं च । इहेह व इति चतस्रो देवान्हुव इति वैश्वदेवं । आ-७-५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning देवान्हुव (*devānhuva*) has fifteen Ṛks and is the sixth hymn. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says देवान्हुव (*devānhuva*). On the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas this is the Vaiśvadeva nivid-dhāna. It is prescribed in the sūtra इहेह व इति चतस्रो देवान्हुव इति वैश्वदेवं । (*iheha va iti catasro devānhuva iti vaiśvadevaṃ |*) (Ā. 7-5).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn, देवान् हुवे (*devān huve*), is the sixth hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has fifteen Ṛks. Its seer, deity and metre are the same as for the previous hymn. The Anukramaṇī says देवान् हुवे (*devān huve*). On the fifth day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, this hymn is to be recited as the Vaiśvadeva-nivid-dhāna hymn, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, इहेह व इति चतस्रो देवान् हुव इति वैश्वदेवं (*iheha va iti catasro devān huva iti vaiśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 7-5).

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 66. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 2; Vargas 12, 13, 14. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 15.
Ṛṣi: Vasukarṇa Vāsukra.
Deity: Viśvedevas.
Metre: 1–14 Jagatī; 15 Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वान्हु॑हे बृ॒हच्छ्र॑वसः स्व॒स्तये॑ ज्योति॒ष्कृतो॑ अध्व॒रस्य॒  ॑
> प्रचे॑तसः ।  
> ये वा॑वृ॒धुः प्र॑त॒रं वि॒श्ववे॑दस॒ इंद्र॑जेष्ठासो अ॒मृता॑  ॒॑
> ऋतावृधः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 536

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवान् । हुवे । बृहत्श्रवसः । स्वस्तये । ज्योतिःकृतः । अध्वरस्य । प्रचेतसः ।  
> ये । ववृधुः । प्रततरं । विश्ववेदसः । इंद्रज्येष्णासः । अमृताः । ऋतवृधः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहच्छवसः प्रभूताना इत्योतिष्कृत आदित्याख्यस्य तेजसः कर्त्यान्प्रचेतसः
> प्रकृष्टज्ञानांस्तान्देवानध्वरस्यास्य यज्ञस्य स्वस्तयेऽविनाशाय निर्विघ्नेन यज्ञपरिसमाप्तये हुवे । आह्वयामि । विश्ववेदसः सर्वधना इंद्रज्येष्णासः । इंद्रो
> ज्येष्णः प्रधानो येषां । इंद्रनेतृका इत्यर्थः । अमृता मरणधर्मरहिता ऋतावृधो यज्ञेन प्रवृद्धा ये देवाः प्रतरमत्यंतं ववृधुः वर्धंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses बृहच्छवसः (*bṛhacchavasaḥ*) as "those of abundant (food or fame)", and ज्योतिष्कृतः (*jyotiṣkṛtaḥ*) as the makers of the light called Āditya, the solar brilliance. प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*) he glosses as those of excellent knowledge. The poet says: "I invoke those gods for the welfare, the indestructibility, of this sacrifice (अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)), that is, for its completion free of obstacles." हुवे (*huve*) means "I call". विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*) means those who have all wealth. इंद्रज्येष्णासः (*iṃdrajyeṣṇāsaḥ*) means those whose chief and foremost is Indra, that is, those led by Indra. अमृता (*amṛtā*) means free from mortality, and ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*) means grown strong through the sacrifice. These are the gods who grow exceedingly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—those who possess all wealth
- इंद्रज्येष्ठासः (*iṃdrajyeṣṭhāsaḥ*)—those who have Indra himself as leader
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—those free from mortality
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—those who obtain growth through the sacrifice
- ये (*ye*)—which gods
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—exceedingly
- ववृधुः (*vavṛdhuḥ*)—who have obtained strength (such gods)
- बृहच्च्रवसः (*bṛhaccravasaḥ*)—those possessing abundant food
- ज्योतिष्कृतः (*jyotiṣkṛtaḥ*)—those who create and spread radiance
- प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*)—those of excellent knowledge
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for a faultless completion
- हुवे (*huve*)—I pray and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I pray and call, that the sacrifice may be completed without obstacle, those gods who possess all wealth, have Indra himself as leader, are free from mortality, and obtain growth through the sacrifice, and who are exceedingly strong: those who possess abundant food, who create and spread radiance, and who are of excellent knowledge.

##### English translation
I invoke for the success of the sacrifice the gods who bestow abundant food, the diffusers of light, the extremely wise who flourish mightily, abounding in all riches, having Indra as their chief, immortal, augmented by sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑प्रसूता॒ वरु॑णप्रशिष्टा॒ ये सूर्य॑स्य॒ ज्योति॑षो भा॒गमा॑न॒शुः ।  
> म॒रुद्ध॑णे वृ॒जने॒ मन्म॑धीमहि॒ माघो॑ने य॒ज्ञं ज॑नयंत  ॒॑
> सूरयः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रप्रसूताः । वरुणप्रशिष्टाः । ये । सूर्यस्य । ज्योतिषः । भागं । आनशुः ।  
> मरुत्गणे । वृजने । मन्म । धीमहि । माघोने । यज्ञं । जनयंत । सूरयः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रप्रसूता इंद्रेण तत्कार्येषु प्रेरिता वरुणप्रशिष्ठा वरुणेनानुशिष्टा
> अनुमोदिता ये मरुतो ज्योतिषो द्योतमानस्य सूर्यस्य स्वस्वकर्मणि सर्वस्य
> प्रेरकस्यामुष्यादित्यस्य भागं भजनीयं लोकमानशुः आनशिरे व्याप्तवंतः। सूर्यमधिष्ठाय वर्तंत इत्यर्थः । वृजने शत्रूणां छेदके माघोने मघवत इंद्रस्य
> संबंधिनि मरुद्धणे। तेषां मरुतां गणे मन्म मननीयं स्तोत्रं धीमहि। दध्मः ।
> कुर्मः । किंच । सूरयः प्राज्ञा यजमानास्तन्निमित्तमेव यज्ञं जनयंत । जनयंति । तेषां हविष्ट्रदानाय कुर्वंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts are "impelled by Indra", urged by him in his tasks, and "instructed by Varuṇa", that is, approved by him. They have obtained a portion, a world fit to be shared, of the shining Sun (ज्योतिषः (*jyotiṣaḥ*)), the impeller of all in their respective works, that is, the Āditya. This means that they abide resting on the Sun. "In the company of the Maruts" (मरुद्धणे (*maruddhaṇe*)), which is cutter of enemies (वृजने (*vṛjane*)) and belongs to Maghavan, that is Indra, "we offer (धीमहि (*dhīmahi*), दध्मः (*dadhmaḥ*), "we place") a hymn (मन्म (*manma*)) worthy of reflection". Moreover, the wise (सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)) sacrificers produce (जनयंत (*janayaṃta*)) the sacrifice for this very purpose, in order to give oblations to them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रप्रसूताः (*iṃdraprasūtāḥ*)—those impelled by Indra
- वरुणप्रशिष्टाः (*varuṇapraśiṣṭāḥ*)—those who have obtained Varuṇa's permission
- ये (*ye*)—which Maruts
- ज्योतिषः (*jyotiṣaḥ*)—of the shining
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of Āditya
- भागं (*bhāgaṃ*)—the venerable portion of radiance
- आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*)—who obtain (such)
- वृजने (*vṛjane*)—those who cut down enemies
- माघोने (*māghone*)—those who are Indra's kinsmen
- मरुद्धणे (*maruddhaṇe*)—addressing the Maruts
- मन्मथ (*manmatha*)—a meditative hymn **NOTE**
- धीमहि (*dhīmahi*)—I offer
- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the wise sacrificers
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- जनयंत (*janayaṃta*)—they procure (perform)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We offer a meditative hymn to those Maruts who are impelled by Indra and have obtained Varuṇa's permission, and who obtain the venerable share of radiance of the shining Āditya. These Maruts are cutters of enemies and kinsmen of Indra.

### Printed p. 538

The wise sacrificers offer (perform) the sacrifice for this very purpose.

##### English translation
We offer praise to the company of the Maruts, the attendants upon Maghavan, who, encouraged by Indra, and instructed by Varuna, have acquired a portion of the light of the sun ; the wise worshippers beget the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॒ वसु॑भिः॒ परि॑ पातु नो॒ गय॑मादि॒त्यैनर्नो॒ अदि॑तिः॒ ॑ 
> शर्म॑ यच्छतु ।  
> रु॒द्रो रु॒द्रेभि॑र्दे॒वो मृ॑ळयाति न॒स्तृष्टा॑ नो॒ ग्नाभिः॑ सुवि॒ताय॑ जिन्वतु ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । वसुभिः । परि । पातु । नः । गयं । आदित्यैः । नः । अदितिः । शर्म । यच्छतु ।  
> रुद्रः । रुद्रेभिः । देवः । मृळयाति । नः । त्वष्टा । नः । ग्नाभिः । सुविताय । जिन्वतु ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसुभिरेतन्नामकैरष्टभिर्देवैः सहित इंद्रो नोऽस्मदीयं गयं । गृहनामैतत् प्राप्तव्यं गायते शब्द्यतेऽत्रेति वा गृहं गयं । परि पातु । परिरक्षतु ।
> तथादितिर्देवमातादित्यैर्देवैः सह नोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं प्रयच्छतु । किंच
> देवो दीप्यमानो रुद्रो रुद्रेभिः स्वपुत्रैर्मरुद्भिः सह नोऽस्मान्मृळॆयाति ।
> सुखयतु ॥ मृड सुखने । लेट्यडागमः । अपि च त्वष्टा प्रजापतिर्गाभिर्देवपत्निभिश्चंदोभिः सुविताय सुष्टु प्राप्तव्यायाभ्युदयाय नोऽस्माइज्वॆन्वतु । प्रीणयतु॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, together with the Vasus, that is, the eight gods of that name, is to protect all around our "gaya" (गयं (*gayaṃ*)). Sāyaṇa says that this is a name for the house; it is what is to be reached, or else the place where one sings or where sound is made. Aditi, mother of the gods, with the Ādityas, is to grant us शर्म (*śarma*), happiness. The shining Rudra, with his sons the Maruts, is to make us happy (मृळयाति (*mṛḷayāti*), "let him gladden"). Tvaṣṭṛ, that is Prajāpati, is to please us (जिन्वतु (*jinvatu*)) for our well-being (सुविताय (*suvitāya*)), a good prosperity to be attained. He is accompanied by the wives of the gods, whom Sāyaṇa names with ग्नाभिः (*gnābhiḥ*) and then चंदोभिः (*caṃdobhiḥ*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—together with the gods called Vasus
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गयं (*gayaṃ*)—house
- परि पातु (*pari pātu*)—may he protect

- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—together with the Ādityas
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छतु (*yacchatu*)—may she give
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining
- रुद्रः (*rudraḥ*)—Rudra
- रुद्रेभिः (*rudrebhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळयाति (*mṛḷayāti*)—may he make happy
- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—Tvaṣṭṛ (Prajāpati)
- ग्नाभिः (*gnābhiḥ*)—together with the wives of the gods
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—so that good fortune may come to us
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- जिन्वतु (*jinvatu*)—may he gladden

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, together with the gods called Vasus, protect our house. May Aditi, together with the Ādityas, give us happiness. May the shining Rudra, together with the Maruts, make us happy. May Prajāpati, together with the wives of the gods, gladden us so that good fortune may come to us.

##### English translation
May Indra with the Vasus guard our dwelling ; may Aditi with the Adityas grant us felicity ; may the divine Rudra with the Rudras make us happy : may Twashtri with the wives of the gods be favourable to us for our prosperity.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अदि॑ति॒र्दार्यवा॑पृथि॒वी ऋ॒तं म॒हदिंद्रा॒विष्णू॑ म॒रुतः॒ स्व॑र्बृ॒हत् ।  
> दे॒वा आ॑दि॒त्या अव॑से हवामहे॒ वसू॑न्द्रा॒द्रान्त्स॑वि॒तारं॑ सु॒दंस॑सं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अदितिः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । ऋतं । महत् । इंद्राविष्णू इति । मरुतः । स्वः। बृहत् ।  
> देवान् । आदित्यान् । अवसे । हवामहे । वसून् । रुद्रान् । सवितारं । सुदंससं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अदितिदर्त्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ महद्महानृतं सत्यभूतोऽग्निरिंद्राविष्णू
> मरुतश्च बृहत्परिवृढः स्वरादित्यः एते देवाः सर्वत्र स्वमहिम्मा वर्तंते। एतान्देवानादित्यादीन्सदंससं सुकर्माणं सवितारमेतन्नामानं चावसे रक्षणाय हनामहे।
> वयमाह्वयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Aditi, heaven and earth, the great ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*) (that is, Agni, who is the embodiment of truth), Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the vast, all-encompassing स्वः (*svaḥ*), that is, Āditya: all these gods abide everywhere by their own greatness. These gods, the Ādityas and the rest, and Savitṛ, who bears this name and is of good works (सुदंससं (*sudaṃsasaṃ*)), "we invoke (हवामहे (*havāmahe*)) for protection (अवसे (*avase*))".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- महत् (*mahat*)—the great one
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—Agni, who is of the nature of truth
- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—Indra and Viṣṇu
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts

### Printed p. 540

- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—of great nature
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—Āditya; all of them together shine, pervading
- देवान् (*devān*)—these gods
- वसून् (*vasūn*)—the Vasu gods
- रुद्रान् (*rudrān*)—the Rudras
- आदित्यान् (*ādityān*)—the Ādityas
- सुदंससं (*sudaṃsasaṃ*)—the doer of excellent works
- सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*)—Savitṛ
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Aditi, heaven and earth, Agni who is great and of the nature of truth, Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and Āditya of great nature all together pervade and shine. These gods, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas, and Savitṛ, the doer of excellent works, we pray and call for protection.

##### English translation
Aditi, heaven and earth, the mighty truth (Agni), Indra, Vishnu, the Maruts, the great sun—(these) we invoke for our protection, as well as the divine Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras and Savitri, the accomplisher of good works.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सर॑स्वान्थी॒भिर्वरु॑णो धृ॒तव्र॑तः पू॒षा विष्णु॑र्महि॒मा वा॒युर॒श्विना॑ ।  
> ब्र॒ह्म॒कृतो॑ अ॒मृता॑ वि॒श्ववे॑दसः॒ शर्म॑ नो यंसन् त्रि॒वरू॑थ॒मंह॑सः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सरस्वान् । धीभिः । वरुणः । धृतव्रतः । पूषा । विष्णुः । महिमा । वायुः । अश्विना ।  
> ब्रह्मकृतः । अमृताः । विश्ववेदसः । शर्म । नः । यंसन् । त्रिवरूथं । अंहसः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धीभिः प्रज्ञाभियुक्तः सरस्वानेतन्नामा धृतव्रतो धृतकर्मा वरुणश्च
> पूषा महिमा महत्वेन युक्तो विष्णुश्च वायुरश्विनाश्विन् बृहकृतः कर्मकृतः
> स्तोतृणामन्नदातारो ना विश्ववेदसः सर्वथना व्याप्तज्ञाना वा०हसः पापरूपाणां
> शत्रूणां हंतारोऽमृता एते देवा नोऽस्मभ्यं त्रिवरूथं त्रिष्कंभं त्रिकक्ष्यं शर्म

### Printed p. 541

> गृहं । यद्वा । त्रिवरूथं । द्रोणाधवनीयपूतभृत्संज्ञकानि त्रीणि पात्राणि यत्र
> व्रियंते संभज्यंते तद्यज्ञसाधनं गृहं । यंसन् । प्रयच्छंतु ॥ यच्छतेर्लॆटि
> सिष्यडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sarasvān, so named, is endowed with धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*), intelligences. Varuṇa is the upholder of vows (धृतव्रतः (*dhṛtavrataḥ*)), the bearer of rites. Then come Pūṣan, Viṣṇu who is endowed with greatness (महिमा (*mahimā*)), Vāyu, and the two Aśvins. These are ब्रह्मकृतः (*brahmakṛtaḥ*), doers of rites, givers of food to the praisers. **NOTE** They are विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*), possessors of all wealth, or of pervasive knowledge. They are destroyers of the enemies that take the form of sin (अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)), and they are immortal. May these gods give us त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*), which Sāyaṇa glosses as threefold-pillared and as three-chambered. शर्म (*śarma*) is the house. Or else त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*) is the house, the means of the sacrifice, where the three vessels called Droṇa, Adhavanīya and Pūtabhṛt are kept. यंसन् (*yaṃsan*) means "let them give".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—the one endowed with intelligence
- सरस्वान् (*sarasvān*)—Sarasvān
- धृतव्रतः (*dhṛtavrataḥ*)—the vow-bearing
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- महिमा (*mahimā*)—the one endowed with greatness
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- वायुः (*vāyuḥ*)—Vāyu
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin gods
- ब्रह्मकृतः (*brahmakṛtaḥ*)—givers of food
- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—the all-knowing
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—destroyers of sin
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—all the gods, free from death
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)—furnished with three kinds of supporting pillars (protections)
- शर्म (*śarma*)—the house (or the sacrificial house having the three vessels such as the Droṇa-kalaśa)
- यंसन् (*yaṃsan*)—may they graciously give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, Sarasvān endowed with intelligence, Varuṇa the vow-bearer, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu endowed with greatness, Vāyu, the Aśvins, who give food, are all-knowing, destroy sin and are free from death, bestow on us a house furnished with threefold protections.

##### English translation
May Saraswat, (endowed) with intelligences, Varuna the observer of oblations, Pushan, Vishnu, the mighty Vayu, the Ashwins (may these) the bestowers of food upon worshippers, immortal, the possessors of all wealth, grant us a habitation triply-guarded from evil.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॑ य॒ज्ञो वृष॑णः संतु य॒ज्ञिया॒ वृष॑णो दे॒वा वृष॑णो  ॒॑
> हवि॒ष्कृतः॑ ।  
> वृष॑णा॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ऋ॒ताव॑री॒ वृषा॑ प॒र्जन्यो॒ वृष॑णो वृष॒स्तुभः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । यज्ञः । वृषणः । संतु । यज्ञियाः । वृषणः । देवाः । वृषणः । हविःकृतः ।

### Printed p. 542

> वृषणा । द्यावापृथिवी इति । ऋतवरी इत्यृतवरी । वृषा । पर्जन्यः । वृषणः । वृषस्तुभः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यज्ञ एषोऽस्मदीयो वृषा कामानां वर्षितास्तु । तथा यज्ञिया
> यज्ञार्हा देवाश्च वृषणः संतु । किंच देवाः स्तुतिकारिण ऋत्विजो वृषणो धनवर्षणे कारणानि संतु साधुस्तुतिकरणेन । तथा हविष्कृतो हनिषां कर्तारोऽध्वर्यादयो वृषणोऽव्यग्रतया मंत्रसाहित्येन च हविष्णुदानेन । अपि चर्तावरी यज्ञवत्यौ द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ वृषणा हविरुत्पादनेन कामानां वर्षयित्र्यौ भवतां। तथा पर्जन्य इंद्रो वृषापां वर्षिता भवतु । वृषस्तुभो वर्षणशीलस्तुतिभिर्देवान्सुवंतः सर्व ऋत्विजो वृषणो भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this sacrifice of ours be a showerer (वृषा (*vṛṣā*)) of desires. May the gods who are worthy of sacrifice (यज्ञिया (*yajñiyā*)) be showerers. May the praising priests, the gods of the verse, be causes of the showering of wealth by praising well. May the offerers of oblations, the Adhvaryu and the others, be showerers by their unflagging attention, by accompanying the mantras, and by the giving of oblations. May heaven and earth, both possessed of sacrifice (ऋतावरी (*ṛtāvarī*)), be showerers of desires by producing the oblation. May Parjanya, that is Indra, be the showerer of waters. May all the priests who bring the gods near with showering praises (वृषस्तुभः (*vṛṣastubhaḥ*)) be showerers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—our sacrifice
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—let it be the giver of desired ends
- यज्ञियाः (*yajñiyāḥ*)—the gods worthy of worship
- वृषणः संतु (*vṛṣaṇaḥ saṃtu*)—let them be those who shower our desire
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the priests who are praisers
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—let them be givers of desired ends
- हविष्कृतः (*haviṣkṛtaḥ*)—the priests who offer the oblation
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—let them be the procurers of desires
- ऋतावरी (*ṛtāvarī*)—possessed of sacrifice
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—let them be givers of desired ends
- पर्जन्यः (*parjanyaḥ*)—Parjanya (Indra)
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—let him be the giver of desires (let him shower rain)
- वृषस्तुभः (*vṛṣastubhaḥ*)—the priests who offer praises that procure the desired end
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—let them be those who shower the desired things

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May our sacrifice be the giver of desired ends. May our gods, who are worthy of worship, fulfil our wish; may the praising priests be givers of desired ends. May heaven and earth, which possess sacrifice, and Parjanya, each according to his own nature, provide our desired ends. May the praising priests too help them.

##### English translation
May (our) sacrifice be the showerer (of benefits); may the gods who are worthy of sacrifice be the showerers (of beeefits); may the priests, may the presenters of the oblation, be the showerers (of benefits); may heaven and earth receiving adoration be the showerer (of benefits); may Parjanya be the showerer (of rain), may those who praise (the gods) with showers be showerers.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्नीषोमा॒ वृष॑णा॒ वाज॑सातये पुरुप्रश॒स्ता वृष॑णा॒ उप॑  
> ब्रुवे ।  
> यावी॑जि॒रे वृष॑णो देवय॒ज्यया॒ ता नः॒ शर्म॑ त्रि॒वरू॑थं॒ वि  ॑
> यंसतः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्नीषोमा । वृषणा । वाजसातये । पुरुप्रशस्ता । वृषणौ । उप । ब्रुवे ।  
> यौ । ईजिरे । वृषणः । देवयज्यया । ता। नः । शर्म । त्रिवरूथं । नि । यंसतः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषणा वर्षणशीलौ पुरुप्रशस्ता बहुभिः प्रशस्तावग्नीषोमौ वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभायोप ब्रुवे । अहमुपस्तौमि । पुनर्वृषणावित्यादरार्थं । यौ देवौ वृषण
> ऋत्विजो देवयज्यया । देवा इज्यंतेऽत्रेति देवयज्या यज्ञः ॥ छंदसि निष्टर्कैति निपातितः ॥ तेनेजिरे यजंते हविर्भिः पूजयंति ता त् प्रसिद्धौ नोऽस्मभ्यं
> त्रिवरूथं त्रिष्कंभं शर्म गृहं वि यंसतः । विशेषेण प्रयच्छतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I address, for the gaining of food, Agni and Soma, the two showerers (वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)), praised by many (पुरुप्रशस्ता (*purupraśastā*)). उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*) means "I praise"; the repetition वृषणौ (*vṛṣaṇau*) is for emphasis. The two gods whom the priests (वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)) worship with देवयज्यया (*devayajyayā*) — the sacrifice in which the gods are worshipped, the word being irregularly formed in the Veda — that is, worship with oblations: those famous two, may they specially give to us a dwelling (शर्म (*śarma*)) with three supports (त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—the givers of desired ends
- पुरुप्रशस्ता (*purupraśastā*)—those who are praised abundantly
- अग्निषोमा (*agniṣomā*)—the deities Agni and Soma
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gaining of food
- उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*)—I praise
- यौ (*yau*)—which Agni and Soma
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—the priests
- देवयज्यया (*devayajyayā*)—with the sacrifice that worships the gods
- ईजिरे (*ījire*)—who worship
- ता (*tā*)—those same deities
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)—having protection in three ways
- शर्म (*śarma*)—a dwelling
- वि यंसतः (*vi yaṃsataḥ*)—let them provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise, for the gaining of food, Agni and Soma, the givers of desired ends, who are praised abundantly. Those famous deities, Agni and Soma, whom the priests worship with the sacrifice that worships the gods, may they provide us a dwelling furnished with three kinds of protection.

### Printed p. 544

##### English translation
I glorify for the obtaining of food the two showerers (of benefits), Agni and Soma, the many-lauded showerers (of beuefits), may these two whom the priests have worshipped with divine worship bestow upon us a triply-guarded dwelling.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धृ॒तव्र॑ताः क्ष॒त्रिया॑ यज्ञनि॒ष्कृतो॑ बृहद्दि॒वा अ॑ध्व॒राणा॑मभि॒त्रियः॑ ।  
> अ॒ग्निहो॑तार ऋत॒सापो॑ अ॒द्रुहो॒पो अ॑सृज॒न्ननु॑ वृत्र॒तूर्ये॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धृतव्रताः । क्षत्रियाः । यज्ञनिःकृतः । बृहत्दिवाः । अध्वराणां । अभिश्रियः ।  
> अग्निहोतारः । ऋतसापः । अद्रुहः । अपः । असृजन् । अनु । वृत्रतूर्ये ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धृतव्रता धृतकर्माणो जात्या क्षत्रियाः। यद्वा। क्षत्रं बलं। तदर्हाः। यज्ञनिष्कृतः । यज्ञं प्रति निर्गमनं यज्ञनिः । तस्य कर्तारो बृहद्दिवा महातेजस्का
> अध्वराणां रक्षोभिरहिंसितानां यज्ञानामभिश्रियोऽभिसेवका अग्निहोतारोऽग्निर्होताह्वाता येषां तादृशा ऋतसापः ॥ षप समवाये ॥ सत्यभाजः अत एवाद्रुहः केषांचिदप्यद्रोग्धारः । यद्वा ॥ द्रुहेः कर्मण्याणादिकः क्विप् ॥ कैश्चिदप्यहिंस्याः। एवंप्रभावा देवा वृत्रतूर्ये। वृत्रस्तूर्यते हिंस्यतेऽत्रेति वृत्रतूर्यः
> संग्रामः । तस्मिन्नपामावरकशत्रुवधेऽप उदकान्यन्वसृजन् । अन्वसारयन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods are धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*), upholders of their rites, and by birth क्षत्रियाः (*kṣatriyāḥ*); or else क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*) is strength and they are worthy of it. यज्ञनिष्कृतः (*yajñaniṣkṛtaḥ*): यज्ञनिः (*yajñaniḥ*) is going forth to the sacrifice, and they are its makers. They are बृहद्दिवा (*bṛhaddivā*), of great splendour; अभिश्रियः (*abhiśriyaḥ*), attendants of the sacrifices (अध्वराणां (*adhvarāṇāṃ*)) that are not injured by demons; अग्निहोतारः (*agnihotāraḥ*), having Agni as their invoking priest; ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*), partakers of truth; and therefore अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*), not harming even any others. Or else, अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*) is formed from the root *druh* with क्विप् (*kvip*), meaning those who cannot be harmed by anyone. Gods of such power, in वृत्रतूर्ये (*vṛtratūrye*) — the battle in which Vṛtra is slain — released (असृजन् (*asṛjan*)) the waters after him (अनु (*anu*)), that is, made them flow, when the enemy that obstructed the waters was slain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृतव्रताः (*dhṛtavratāḥ*)—those who firmly perform their appointed rites
- क्षत्रियाः (*kṣatriyāḥ*)—the powerful
- यज्ञनिष्कृतः (*yajñaniṣkṛtaḥ*)—those who go together for the sacrifice
- बृहद्दिवाः (*bṛhaddivāḥ*)—those of very great splendour
- अध्वराणां (*adhvarāṇāṃ*)—to the sacrifices
- अभिश्रियः (*abhiśriyaḥ*)—those who give shining protection
- अग्निहोतारः (*agnihotāraḥ*)—those who have Agni himself as invoking priest
- ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*)—protectors of truth
- अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—those who wish harm to no one; such are the gods
- वृत्रतूरै (*vṛtratūrai*)—in the battle that destroys Vṛtra
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- अनु असृजन् (*anu asṛjan*)—let them produce and pour out

### Printed p. 545

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, who firmly perform their appointed rites, who are powerful, go together for the sacrifice, have very great splendour, give shining protection to the sacrifices, have Agni himself as invoking priest, are protectors of truth and wish harm to no one — may they, in the battle that destroys Vṛtra, pour out the waters and make them flow.

##### English translation
The (gods) observing obligations endowed with vigour, developers of sacrifice, possessed of abundant brightness, the defenders of sacrifices, having Agni for their priest, enjoying truth, unassailable, set free the waters at the combat with the Vritra.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ज॑नयन्न॒भि व्र॒ताप॒ ओष॑धीर्व॒निना॑नि य॒ज्ञिया॑ ।  
> अं॒तरि॑क्षं॒ स्व१॒॑रा प॑पुरू॒तये॒ वशं॑ दे॒वास॑स्त॒न्वी॒३॒॑३नि मा॑मृजुः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्यावापृथिवी इति । जनयन् । अभि । व्रता । आपः । ओषदीः । वनिनानि । यज्ञिया ।  
> अंतरिक्षं । स्वः । आ । पपुः । ऊतये । वशं । देवासः । तन्नि । नि । ममृजुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवासो देवा इंद्रादयो द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यावभ्यभिलक्ष्य व्रता
> व्रतेन स्वेन कर्मणापः ॥ सुब्बत्ययः ॥ अप उदकान्योषधीश्च तथा यज्ञिया
> यज्ञार्हान्वनिनानि वने भवान्सलाशादीन्वृक्षाञ्जनयन् । उदपादयन् । किंच ते
> देवाः स्वः सर्वमंतरिक्षमा पपुः । तेजसापूरयंति । किमर्थं । ऊतये रक्षणाय
> शत्रुभ्यो बाधाभावाय । अपि च वशं काम्यमानं ॥ वशिरण्योरुपसंख्यानं ।
> पा-३-३-५८-३ । इत्यकर्तरि कारकेऽप् ॥ तं यज्ञं तन्नि स्वशरीरे नि ममृजुः । नितरां
> शुद्धमलंकृतं चक्रुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, Indra and the others (देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)), with their own proper work (व्रता (*vratā*)) directed towards heaven and earth, brought forth the waters and the plants, and likewise the trees (वनिनानि (*vanināni*)) of the forest, such as the palāśa, which are fit for sacrifice (यज्ञिया (*yajñiyā*)). Moreover those gods filled the whole firmament (अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)) with their lustre, for protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)), that is, so that there may be no hindrance from enemies. And they thoroughly purified and adorned in their own bodies that sacrifice which is desired (वशं (*vaśaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- अभि व्रता (*abhi vratā*)—by their respective individual works
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the creepers and the like

### Printed p. 546
- यज्ञिया (*yajñiyā*)—fit for sacrifice
- वनिनानि (*vanināni*)—the trees
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—they produced
- स्वः अंतरिक्षं (*svaḥ aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the whole firmament
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- आ पपुः (*ā papuḥ*)—they have filled with their lustre
- वशं (*vaśaṃ*)—the attractive sacrifice
- तन्नि (*tanni*)—in their own bodies
- नि ममृजुः (*ni mamṛjuḥ*)—they take it within and adorn themselves

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, Indra and the others, by their respective individual works, produced heaven and earth, the waters, the creepers and the like, and the trees fit for sacrifice. They have filled the whole firmament with their lustre for protection. They take the attractive sacrifice within their bodies and adorn themselves.

##### English translation
The gods engendered the heaven and earth with their respective functions, the waters, the plants, the sacred trees; they filled the whole firmament (with lustre) for its protection; they graced the desirable (sacrifice) in their own persons.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ध॒र्तारो॑ दि॒व ऋ॒भवः॑ सु॒हस्ता॑ वातापर्ज॒न्या म॑हि॒षस्य॑ तन्य॒तोः ।  
> आप॒ ओष॑धीः॒ प्र ति॑रंतु नो॒ गिरो॒ भगो॑ रा॒तिर्वा॒जिनो॑ यंतु ॒ ॑
> मे हवं ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धर्तारः । दिवः । ऋभवः । सुहस्ताः । वातापर्जन्या । महिषस्य । तन्मतोः ।  
> आपः । ओषधीः । प्र । तिरंतु । नः । गिरः । भगः । रातिः । वाजिनः । यंतु । मे । हवं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो द्युलोकस्य धर्तारो धारयितार ऋभवः सत्येन भासमानाः सुहस्ताः
> शोभनवज्राद्यायुधयुक्तहस्ता देवास्तथा महिषस्य महतस्तन्यतोः शब्दस्य ॥ तनु
> विस्तारे । ऋतन्यंजीति यतुच्छत्ययः ॥ शब्दस्य कर्तार् वातापर्जन्या वातश्च पर्जन्यश्च तत्कार्या अप ओषधीरोषधयश्च नोऽस्माकं गिरः स्तुतीः प्रतिरंतु । प्रवर्ध-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods are upholders (धर्तारः (*dhartāraḥ*)) of the world of heaven, the Ṛbhus shining with truth, with fine hands (सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*)), that is, hands furnished with fine weapons such as the thunderbolt. Vāta and Parjanya, makers of the great (महिषस्य (*mahiṣasya*)) sound (तन्यतोः (*tanyatoḥ*), from the root तनु (*tanu*), "to extend"), and the waters and plants that are their effects, let them make our praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) prosper (प्रतिरंतु (*pratiraṃtu*)). The sentence goes on in the next block.

### Printed p. 547

> यंतु । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वृद्ध्यर्थः । तथा रातिर्दाता भगो भजनीयोऽर्यमा च
> वाजिनः । अग्निर्वायुः सूर्यस्ते वै वाजिन इति तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणं । १-६-३-९ ।
> एते देवाश्च मे मदीयं हवमाह्वानं यंतु । अभिगच्छंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

प्रतिरंतु (*pratiraṃtu*) is the root तिर (*tira*) with the prefix प्र (*pra*), in the sense of increase. Likewise the giver (रातिः (*rātiḥ*)), Bhaga the adorable, that is Aryaman, and the Vājins — Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya: "Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, they are the Vājins" (अग्निर्वायुः सूर्यस्ते वै वाजिन इति (*agnirvāyuḥ sūryaste vai vājina iti*)), Tai. Brā. 1-6-3-9. May these gods come to my invocation (हवं (*havaṃ*)), that is, approach it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the world of heaven
- धर्तारः (*dhartāraḥ*)—the upholders
- ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*)—those who shine with their true nature
- सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*)—those having excellent hands
- महिषस्य (*mahiṣasya*)—of the great
- तन्यतोः (*tanyatoḥ*)—to the sound, the makers
- वातापर्जन्या (*vātāparjanyā*)—Vāyu and Parjanya
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the plants
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises
- प्रतीरंतु (*pratīraṃtu*)—let them make them grow
- रातिः (*rātiḥ*)—the generous
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—the god Bhaga
- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—Agni, Vāyu and Sūra
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—having regard to the invocation
- यंतु (*yaṃtu*)—let them come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vāyu and Parjanya, who are upholders of the world of heaven, shine with their true nature, have excellent hands and are makers of the great sound, let them make the waters and plants make our praises grow. May the generous god Bhaga, and Agni, Vāyu and Sūra, come having regard to my invocation.

##### English translation
May the upholders of the sky, the radiant with truth, the well-armed deities, Vata and Parjanya, (the utterers) of the mighty thunder, the waters, the plants, amplify our praises ; may the liberal Bhaga and the Vajins come to my invocation.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒मु॒द्रः सिंधू॒ रजो॑ अं॒तरि॑क्षम॒ज एक॑पात्तनयि॒त्र॑ुर्ण॒वः ।  
> अहि॑र्बु॒ध्न्यः॑ शृणव॒द्वचां॑सि मे॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वास॑ उ॒त सू॒रयो॒  ॑
> मनु ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समुद्रः । सिंधुः । रजः । अंतरिक्षं । अजः । एकपात् । तनयित्नुः । अर्णवः ।  
> अहिः । बुध्न्यः । शृणवत् । वचांसि । मे । विश्वे । देवासः । उत । सूरयः । मम ॥

### Printed p. 548

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समुद्रः समुंदनशीलः स्यंदमानोदकः सिंधुरेतन्नामकोऽंतरिक्षं द्यावा
> पृथिव्योरंतरा मध्ये क्षितमुषितं रजो मध्यमलोकमज एकपात् अजायमान
> एक एव पद्यते । एतत्संज्ञको देवोऽर्णव उदकवांस्तनयित्नुः स्तनयित्नुर्मोघो बुध्योऽंतरिक्षे भवोऽहिरेतत्संज्ञकः एते देवा मे मम वचांसि
> वक्तव्यानि स्तोत्राणि शृणवत् । प्रत्येकं शृणोतु उतापि च सूरयः प्राज्ञा विश्वे
> देवासो देवा मम स्तोत्राणि शृण्वंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses the nouns of the verse one by one. समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*) is the one of flowing waters, named Sindhu. अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*) is रजः (*rajaḥ*), the middle world that lies between heaven and earth. अज एकपात् (*aja ekapāt*) is the god who goes as the one unborn, on one foot. अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*) is the watery one, तनयित्नुः (*tanayitnuḥ*), the thundering one.**NOTE** *ahiḥ budhyaḥ* is the god of that name who has his being in the atmosphere. These gods are to hear, each one, the words (the praises to be spoken) of the poet, and likewise all the wise gods are to hear his praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*)—the one with flowing water
- सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*)—Sindhu
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—lying between heaven and earth
- रजः (*rajaḥ*)—the middle world
- अज एकपात् (*aja ekapāt*)—the god named Aja Ekapād
- अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*)—the one possessing water
- तनयित्नुः (*tanayitnuḥ*)—the maker of sound
- आहिर्बुध्न्यः (*āhirbudhnyaḥ*)—the god Ahirbudhnya
- मे (*me*)—my
- वचांसि (*vacāṃsi*)—words of praise
- शृणवत् (*śṛṇavat*)—let him hear
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the wise
- विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)—all the gods
- मम (*mama*)—let them hear my praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Sindhu with flowing waters, the middle world that lies between heaven and earth, the god named Aja Ekapād, the watery one, and the god Ahirbudhnya, the maker of sound, hear my words of praise; and may the wise Viśvedevas hear my praises.

##### English translation
May the flowing Sindhu, the atmosphere, the firmament, Aja
Ekapad, the rain-bearing thunder-cloud, and Ahirbudhnya hear my words;
may the wise universal gods (listen to) my (praises).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्याम॑ वो॒ मन॑वो दे॒ववी॑तये॒ प्रांचं॑ नो य॒ज्ञं प्र ण॑यत साधु॒या ।  
> आदि॑त्या॒ रुद्रा॒ वस॑वः॒ सुदा॑नव इ॒मा ब्रह्म॑ श॒स्यमा॑नानि जिन्वत ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्याम । वः । मनवः । देववीतये । प्रांचं । नः । यज्ञं । प्र । नयत । साधुया।

### Printed p. 549

> आदित्याः । रुद्राः । वसवः । सुदानवः । इमा । ब्रह्म । शस्यमानानि । जिन्वत ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाः मनवो मनुष्या वयं वो यष्मदीयाय देवनीतये ।
> देवानां नीतिर्भक्षणं यस्मिन् स यज्ञः । तस्यै यज्ञाय स्याम । यज्ञकर्तारो
> भवेम । ततो नोऽस्मदीयं यज्ञं साधुया ॥ सुप्रो याजादेशः ॥ साधु
> कल्याणं प्रांचं प्राचीनं प्र णयत । प्रकृष्णांचनं कुरुत । हे आदित्या हे रुद्रा
> रुद्रपुत्रा मरुतो हे सुदानवः शोभनदाना हेवसवः इमेमानि शस्यमानानि ब्रह्म
> ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि जिन्वत । प्रीणयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O gods, we men may become performers of the sacrifice that is yours": the sacrifice is that in which there is the *devanīti*, the consuming of the gods.**NOTE** Then, he says, conduct our sacrifice well (साधुया (*sādhuyā*) means साधु (*sādhu*), auspicious) प्रांचं (*prāṃcaṃ*), forward or ancient; make it go forward.**NOTE** Addressed are the Ādityas, the Rudras (the Maruts, Rudra's sons), the Vasus, who are generous givers. Gratify these hymns that are being recited.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O gods) मनवः (*manavaḥ*)—we men
- वः (*vaḥ*)—who worship you
- देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—for the performance of the sacrifice
- स्याम (*syāma*)—we are intent
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- प्रांचं (*prāṃcaṃ*)—ancient
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—sacrifice
- साधुया (*sādhuyā*)—so that it yields auspicious fruit
- प्रणयत (*praṇayata*)—help
- आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)—O Ādityas
- रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*)—O Rudras
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—generous
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—O Vasus
- इमा शस्यमानानि (*imā śasyamānāni*)—which are recited here
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the praises
- जिन्वत (*jinvata*)—accept with regard

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, we men are intent on performing the sacrifice that worships you. Help our ancient sacrifice so that it yields auspicious fruit. O Ādityas, O Rudras, and O generous Vasus, accept with regard the praises recited here.

##### English translation
May we men be (deligent in providing) for your food, (O gods); conduct our ancient sacrifice to a successful end, Adityas, Rudras, and generous Vasus, graciously accept these hymns whieh are being recited.

> साधुया ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दैव्या । होतारा । प्रथमा । पुरःहिता । ऋतस्य । पंथां । अनु । एमि। साधुया ।  
> क्षेत्रस्य । पतिं । प्रतिवेशं । ईमहे। विश्वान् । देवान् । अमृतान्! अप्रयुच्छतः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्तोर्यामेच्छावाकातिरिक्तोक्षस्य दैव्या होतारेत्येषा परिधानीया ।
> सूत्रितं च । उभा उ नूनं दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहितेति परिधानीया ।
> आ-९-११ । इति ॥
> प्रथमा मुख्य पुरोहिता पुरोहितौ पुरतो निहितौ दैव्या देवसंबंधिनौ
> होतारा होतारावेतन्नामानावग्न्यादित्यावन्नेमि । हविर्भिरनुगच्छामि। तत ऋतस्य
> यज्ञस्य पंथां पंथानं साधुया कल्याणं विघ्नराहित्येनान्वेमि । अनुगच्छामि ।
> अनंतरं प्रतिवेशं समीपे वर्तमानं क्षेत्रस्य पतिं पालयितारमेतन्नामानममृतान्नरणधर्मरहितानप्रयुच्छतोऽप्रमाद्यतो विश्वान्सर्वान्देवांश्चेमहे । धनं
> याचामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Aptoryāma, in the atirikta uktha of the Acchāvāka, this verse "दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*)" is the Paridhānīyā.**NOTE** It is so laid down in the sūtra: उभा उ नूनं दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहितेति परिधानीया (*ubhā u nūnaṃ daivyā hotārā prathamā purohiteti paridhānīyā*) (Ā. 9-11). Sāyaṇa explains: the two divine hotṛs, प्रथमा (*prathamā*) (chief) and पुरोहिता (*purohitā*) (placed in front), are Agni and Āditya by name; "I follow them with oblations." Then "I follow the path of the sacrifice (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)) well, without obstruction." Next, प्रतिवेशं (*prativeśaṃ*) is the one who stays near; the क्षेत्रस्य पतिं (*kṣetrasya patiṃ*) is the protector of that name; and all the gods, immortal (free from the nature of dying) and unheedless (अप्रयुच्छतः (*aprayucchataḥ*), not negligent), we ask for wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—the chief
- पुरोहिता (*purohitā*)—those established before all
- दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*)—the worshippers of the gods, Agni and Āditya
- अन्वेमि (*anvemi*)—I follow
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- पंथां (*paṃthāṃ*)—the path
- साधुया (*sādhuyā*)—well
- अन्वेमि (*anvemi*)—I follow
- प्रतिवेशं (*prativeśaṃ*)—who is near us
- क्षेत्रस्य पतिं (*kṣetrasya patiṃ*)—the god called Lord of the Field
- अमृतान् (*amṛtān*)—the deathless
- अप्रयुच्छतः (*aprayucchataḥ*)—the not idle
- विश्वान् देवान् (*viśvān devān*)—all the gods
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask for wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I follow Agni and Āditya, the chief, established before all, the worshippers of the gods; I follow the path of the sacrifice well. We ask for wealth from the god called Lord of the Field, who is near us, and from the Viśvedevas (all the gods), who are deathless and not idle.

##### English translation
I follow the two chief priests, the divine offerers of burnt sacrifices ;
(I follow) successfully the path of sacrifice; we solicit (wealth of ) the
contiguous lord of the field, and the immortal and not unheeding universal
deities.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifice called Aptoryāma, when the officiant called Acchāvāka recites the mantras called atirikta, this Ṛk दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) is to be recited as the last Ṛk. This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, उभा उ नूनं दैन्व्या होतारा पुरोहितेति परिधानीया (*ubhā u nūnaṃ dainvyā hotārā purohiteti paridhānīyā*) (Ā. 9-11).

> स्वजनस्य धनं प्रेरयंति तद्वद्धविर्दानेन स्तुतिकरणेन च बंधुष्टस्मासु धनं प्रेरयतेति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Vasiṣṭhas, the ṛṣis born in Vasiṣṭha's family, praising the gods like the ṛṣis of old and like their father Vasiṣṭha, have made a hymn (वाचं (*vācaṃ*)) for their welfare, for freedom from destruction. "O gods, come to our desire and bestow wealth, of the kind of cattle and the like, upon us." The illustration is प्रीता इव (*prītā iva*): as delighted kinsmen send wealth to their own people, so, he says, you are to send wealth to us who offer oblations and praise, as to kin.**NOTE**

## Sūkta 67 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Introduction**
Bṛhaspati is the deity of this hymn and of the next. Yāska, explaining the derivation of the word Bṛhaspati in his Nirukta, says: बृहस्पतिः बृहतः पाता वा पालयिता ना । (*bṛhaspatiḥ bṛhataḥ pātā vā pālayitā nā |*) (Ni. 10-11). On this the commentator Durgācārya says: बृहस्पतिः कस्मात् ? बृहतः पाता ना पालयिता ना । बृहतः महतोऽस्य जगतः उदकस्य ना पाता रक्षिता पालयिता अपि रक्षितैव धात्वन्यत्वमर्थैकत्वं ॥ (*bṛhaspatiḥ kasmāt ? bṛhataḥ pātā nā pālayitā nā | bṛhataḥ mahato 'sya jagataḥ udakasya nā pātā rakṣitā pālayitā api rakṣitaiva dhātvanyatvamarthaikatvaṃ ‖*) That is: the protector, the guardian, of the great world or of water. To indicate the meaning of the word पति (*pati*) there are words formed from different roots, पाता (*pātā*) and पालयिता (*pālayitā*), but the meaning is only one. In many places, when explaining बृहतः पाता (*bṛhataḥ pātā*), Sāyaṇa has given for the word बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*) the meaning बृहतः यज्ञकर्मणः (*bṛhataḥ yajñakarmaṇaḥ*) or वृष्ट्याख्यकर्मणः (*vṛṣṭyākhyakarmaṇaḥ*), that is, of the work in the form of sacrifice, or of the work in the form of the bestowal of rain. Since Bṛhaspati, as priest of the gods, carries out the sacrificial work, and since he brings about the rain that men need, these two kinds of epithets are natural to him.

To illustrate Bṛhaspati's priesthood and his bestowal of rain, Yāska has given as example the Ṛk यद्देवापिः शंतनवे पुरोहितो होत्राय वृतः कृपयन्नदीधेत् । देवश्रुतं वृष्टिवनिं रराणो बृहस्पतिर्वाचमस्मा अयच्छत् ॥ (*yaddevāpiḥ śaṃtanave purohito hotrāya vṛtaḥ kṛpayannadīdhet | devaśrutaṃ vṛṣṭivaniṃ rarāṇo bṛhaspatirvācamasmā ayacchat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-98-7). In the explanation of this Ṛk, बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मासीत् सोऽस्मै वाचमयच्छत् (*bṛhaspatirbrahmāsīt so 'smai vācamayacchat*) — that is, Bṛhaspati was the Brahman priest at the sacrifice made by the king named Śantanu and taught him a mantra in the form of words; and when the sacrificer praised with that mantra, rain came — is described. Besides this, in the Yajurveda and other texts: बृहस्पतिर्देवानां पुरोहित आसीच्छंडामर्कावसुराणां । (*bṛhaspatirdevānāṃ purohita āsīcchaṃḍāmarkāvasurāṇāṃ |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-10-1).

### Printed p. 554
It is said that Bṛhaspati was the purohita of the gods, and that Śaṇḍa and Marka were the purohitas of the asuras.
ब्रह्म वै देवानां बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मण्यैवैनमभिचरति । (*brahma vai devānāṃ bṛhaspatirbrahmaṇyaivainamabhicarati |*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-9-1)
It is said that Bṛhaspati, in the sacrifice performed by the gods, acted as the ṛtvij called Brahmā and brought the sacrifice to completion.
तस्मै विशः स्वयमेवा नमंते यस्मिन् ब्रह्मा राजनि पूर्व एति । (*tasmai viśaḥ svayamevā namaṃte yasmin brahmā rājani pūrva eti |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-50-8)
अवस्यवे यो वरिवः कृणोति ब्रह्मणे राजा तमवंति देवाः । (*avasyave yo varivaḥ kṛṇoti brahmaṇe rājā tamavaṃti devāḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-50-9)
सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे । आदित्यान्विष्णुं सूर्यं ब्रह्माणं च बृहस्पतिं ॥ (*somaṃ rājānamavase 'gniṃ gīrbhirhavāmahe | ādityānviṣṇuṃ sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca bṛhaspatiṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-141-3)
In these and other Ṛks Bṛhaspati is described as the ṛtvij called Brahmā.

In the Ṛgveda Bṛhaspati holds an important place. Besides being praised in eleven sūktas, he is also praised in two sūktas (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-49; 7-97) as a dual deity together with Indra. The word Bṛhaspati occurs about 120 times in the Ṛgveda. In many contexts the deities Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are praised interchangeably in one and the same mantra. Even so, Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are different deities.

Some Western scholars, and some modern scholars too, have expressed the opinion that because Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are praised interchangeably in Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 2-23, the two are one deity. But the ancient Veda commentators such as Yāska, Śaunaka and Sāyaṇa have stated clearly that Bṛhaspati is one and Brahmaṇaspati another. Of the 19 Ṛks of the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23 mentioned above, only 6, namely Ṛks 1, 5, 9, 11, 17 and 19, praise Bṛhaspati. The remaining 13 Ṛks are addressed to Brahmaṇaspati. Yāska too has given separate etymologies for the word Bṛhaspati and for the word Brahmaṇaspati. Therefore Bṛhaspati is one and Brahmaṇaspati another.

Bṛhaspati has a distinction wholly different from the other deities. While the other deities are all particular forms of nature or of a natural power, Bṛhaspati appears to belong to the sphere of man's moral and religious life. There are many examples in the Ṛgveda that this deity, protector of praise-hymns and prayer, exerts his influence on the resolve, intention or power of the gods' minds. In the 98th sūkta of the 10th maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda there is a historical account concerning the princes of the Kuru line, Devāpi and Śantanu.

### Printed p. 555
The Nirukta-author describes how very important Bṛhaspati's role in it is, as follows:
अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । देवापिश्चार्ष्टिषेणः शंतनुश्च कौरवा भ्रातरा बभूवतुः । स शंतनुः कनीयानभिषेचयांचक्रे । देवापिस्तपः प्रतिपेदे । ततः शंतनो राज्ये द्वादशवर्षाणि देवो न ववर्ष । तमूचु र्ब्राह्मणा अधर्मस्त्वयाचरितो ज्येषं भ्रातरमंतरित्याभिषेचितं तस्मात्ते देवो न वर्षतीति । स शंतनुर्देवापिं शिशिक्ष राज्येन । तमुवाच देवापिः पुरोहितस्तेऽसानि याजयानि च त्वेति ॥ (*atretihāsamācakṣate | devāpiścārṣṭiṣeṇaḥ śaṃtanuśca kauravā bhrātarā babhūvatuḥ | sa śaṃtanuḥ kanīyānabhiṣecayāṃcakre | devāpistapaḥ pratipede | tataḥ śaṃtano rājye dvādaśavarṣāṇi devo na vavarṣa | tamūcu rbrāhmaṇā adharmastvayācarito jyeṣaṃ bhrātaramaṃtarityābhiṣecitaṃ tasmātte devo na varṣatīti | sa śaṃtanurdevāpiṃ śiśikṣa rājyena | tamuvāca devāpiḥ purohitaste 'sāni yājayāni ca tveti ‖*)
(Ni. 2-11)
In former times, in the Kuru line, King Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa had two sons, Devāpi and Śantanu. Of them Devāpi was the elder and Śantanu the younger. After their father Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa died, his elder son Devāpi wished to become king. But his younger brother Śantanu, not allowing it and wishing to be the ruler of the kingdom himself, drove away his elder brother Devāpi and began to rule the kingdom himself. The elder brother Devāpi, distressed, went to the forest and passed his time practising austerities. While matters stood so, no rain fell in his country for 12 years and a great famine came. Then King Śantanu, wondering what to do about it, asked the Brāhmaṇas for advice. The Brāhmaṇas said to the king: "According to the dharmaśāstra the king's eldest son is the one entitled to the kingdom. So your elder brother Devāpi ought to have ruled. But you did not allow that; you drove him away and seized the kingdom. Since you are thus practising adharma, the rain-god does not rain in your kingdom." King Śantanu repented of the wrong he had done, summoned his elder brother Devāpi, who was practising austerities in the forest, and handed the kingdom over to him. But Devāpi said that he did not want the kingdom, that he would practise austerities in the forest and rely on the path of withdrawal; and he said that Śantanu should perform a sacrifice to remove the drought in the kingdom, and that he himself would take on the priesthood in it and help bring about rain. When the king agreed, Devāpi took the part of the ṛtvij called hotṛ in his sacrifice. Bṛhaspati became the ṛtvij called Brahmā. In that sacrifice, performed for the sake of bringing rain, the hotṛ Devāpi addressed Bṛhaspati the Brahmā: "O Bṛhaspati, you have great influence over the minds of the gods; therefore teach me the mantras that win them over." Being so asked, Bṛhaspati said "So be it" and taught the hotṛ Devāpi mantras containing prayers to the gods needed for bringing rain. When offerings were made with those mantras, addressed to the gods, rain fell as much as desired,

### Printed p. 556
so it is said. Therefore this sūkta is also called the Vṛṣṭikāma-sūkta ("rain-desiring" hymn). This matter, with some differences, is also told in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4-20-7, the Mahābhārata Ādiparvan, the Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9-22-14 to 17, and other Purāṇa works.

In the 10th maṇḍala of the Ṛ. Saṃ., in sūkta 108, there is another episode. The asuras called Paṇis had stolen the cows of the gods (the water-bearing clouds) and hidden them in an impregnable fort. Indra sent Saramā, the divine bitch, to search for them. Saramā came to the Paṇis, entered into a dispute with them and asked them to give back the stolen cows. The Paṇis said: "What is Indra's strength? We are great heroes and our weapons are very sharp. The gods therefore cannot defeat us, and the gods cannot even learn the place where the cows are kept. So if Saramā leaves the gods' side and joins our company, we shall give her the wealth and so on that she wants." Though urged in many ways, Saramā did not agree, returned from there and told the gods all of it. Then Bṛhaspati by his power found out the place where the cows had been hidden. After that the gods subdued them and brought the cows back. Such is the episode.

In many such deeds of daring Bṛhaspati's role is very important. In particular, when men need rain, Bṛhaspati's help is indispensable. This kind of prayer is seen especially in the sūktas addressed to Bṛhaspati.

Let us examine closely what Bṛhaspati's qualities and achievements are, as described in the Ṛgveda. Bṛhaspati was born of heaven and earth and is nourished by their greatness (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-97-8). But in one place (2-23-17) it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ produced him. He has the name father of the gods (6-26-3); it is also said (10-72-8) that the gods were produced from him as sparks of fire fly from the blow of a smith's hammer. He has the name Brahmā (the ṛtvij called Brahmā) (10-141-3). He is connected with the ṛtvijs (7-10-4; 10-14-3). He has also the name Aṅgirasa (4-40-1; 4-23-1; 10-47-6). He composes and utters praise-words, is their lord and impeller (2-23-1, 2; 1-40-5; 10-98-7); he accomplishes all his aims by mantra alone (2-24-3); mounting the shining chariot called sacrifice he sets out to conquer the enemies of the gods and the praisers (2-23-3). He is the nourisher and protector of the faithful, their guide; he rescues them from calamities (2-23-4) and grants them wealth and the like (2-23-9). He is held to be the father of all the gods and is endowed with all divine qualities (3-62-4; 4-50-6). He is of all forms; all things that everyone desires are in him (7-10-4; 7-97-4).

### Printed p. 557
He bears a golden spear (7-97-7). Together with Indra he too is leader of the armies (10-103-8). He increases life (10-100-5); plants arose from him (10-97-15 and 19); tawny horses are his vehicle (Ni. 2-28). Such descriptions occur.

It is said that, hearing the cry of distress of Trita, who had been thrown into a well by rākṣasas and was calling the gods for help, Bṛhaspati released him from that perilous state (10-105-17); and that together with Indra Bṛhaspati made the water, enveloped in darkness, flow again (2-23-18; 1-56-5).

Bṛhaspati by his power broke open the stone door of the well full of honey. The gods drank that honey and rained abundantly (2-24-3, 4). When Bṛhaspati pierced the forts of Vala with fire-spitting rays, the herds of cows became visible; he drove the cows out as one breaks an egg; seeing the water enclosed by rock, he split it with his lion's roar and brought it out (10-68-4 to 9). Bṛhaspati brought the cows out from the place covered with rocks; he seized the cows of Vala and made them his own (10-68-5). Bṛhaspati is distinguished by divinity (2-23-2); he is one's own to all the gods (3-62-4; 4-50-6) and the most divine among the gods. In the form of a god he gathers into himself all the gods and all things (2-24-11; 8-61-8). Being capable, he keeps the two ends of the earth far apart (4-50-1). That the sun and moon rise one after the other is his exemplary deed (10-68-10). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (of the Yajurveda) a connection between Bṛhaspati and certain constellations is stated. Bṛhaspati is the deity of the constellation Puṣya (Tai. Saṃ. 4-4-10-1). In the Purāṇas and elsewhere Bṛhaspati is described as Vācaspati and as the presiding deity of the planet Bṛhaspati (Jupiter).

Some scholars have held that the deities Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are modifications of Agni. The scholar M. Langlois, in Part I, pp. 249, 254, 578 of his work, a translation of the Ṛgveda, supports with many examples that these two deities are modifications of Agni. The scholar Wilson also expressed the same opinion in the introduction to the first part of his translation of the Ṛgveda. The scholar Max Müller too (the Kannada prints this in English): "Brihaspati and Brahmanaspati are both varieties of Agni, the priest and the purohit of the Gods and men and as such he is invoked together with the Maruts." That is, Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are both modifications of Agni, standing in the place of ṛtvij and purohita to gods and men. It is from this point of view that they are invoked together with the Marut deities

### Printed p. 558
in many places, he says. We give one or two examples stating this identity of Agni with Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati.
त्वमग्न इंद्रो वृषभः सतामसि त्वं विष्णुरुरुगायो नमस्यः । त्वं ब्रह्मार्यिविद्ब्रह्मणस्पते त्वं विधर्तः सचसे पुरंध्या ॥ (*tvamagna iṃdro vṛṣabhaḥ satāmasi tvaṃ viṣṇururugāyo namasyaḥ | tvaṃ brahmāryividbrahmaṇaspate tvaṃ vidhartaḥ sacase puraṃdhyā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-3)
"O Agni, you are Indra, the most excellent among the good; you are Viṣṇu, worshipful and of very great body; O Brahmaṇaspati, you are the wealthy ṛtvij named Brahmā." Thus Agni is described as the form of many deities.
तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यं । बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवतातये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदं ॥ (*taṃ śubhramagnimavase havāmahe vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvānamukthyaṃ | bṛhaspatiṃ manuṣo devatātaye vipraṃ śrotāramatithiṃ raghuṣyadaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ.
We invoke for our protection the bright Agni, friend of the human race. We invoke Mātariśvan, fit to be spoken of in mantras, and Bṛhaspati, the wise one who praises with the gods in view, who stands in the place of a guest and is swift-going, to come to the sacrificial rites connected with men.**NOTE**

Sāyaṇācārya, when writing the commentary on Ṛk 5-43-12, for the word Bṛhaspati says:
अथवा इयमाग्नेयी । बृहतः परिवृढस्य कर्मणः स्वामीति बृहस्पतिरग्निरुच्यते । तथा नीलवर्णधूमपृष्टत्वसदनसादनहिरण्यवर्णत्वादिलिंगैरप्यग्निरेव बृहस्पतिः ॥ (*athavā iyamāgneyī | bṛhataḥ parivṛḍhasya karmaṇaḥ svāmīti bṛhaspatiragnirucyate | tathā nīlavarṇadhūmapṛṣṭatvasadanasādanahiraṇyavarṇatvādiliṃgairapyagnireva bṛhaspatiḥ ‖*)
That is: "Or else this mantra may be said to set forth Agni as its deity. Because he is lord of the great work, the sacrifice now in hand, Agni is called Bṛhaspati. Likewise, by marks such as the black smoke being his back, the sacrificial altar being his seat, and golden colour, Bṛhaspati too must be called Agni."

Now let us examine examples that state a difference between Agni and Bṛhaspati-Brahmaṇaspati.
सोषामविंदत्स स्वः १ सो अग्निं सो अर्केण वि बबाधे तमांसि । बृहस्पतिर्गोवपुषो वलस्य निर्मज्ञानं न पवर्णो जभार ॥ (*soṣāmaviṃdatsa svaḥ 1 so agniṃ so arkeṇa vi babādhe tamāṃsi | bṛhaspatirgovapuṣo valasya nirmajñānaṃ na pavarṇo jabhāra ‖*)
In this Ṛk it is said that Bṛhaspati obtained Uṣas, heaven and Agni, and by a mantra dispelled the darkness; thus Bṛhaspati and Agni are said to be different.

### Printed p. 559
इंद्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषा रुद्रं रुद्रेभिरा वहा बृहंतं । आदित्येभिरदितिं विश्वजन्यां बृहस्पतिमृक्वभिर्विश्ववारं ॥ (*iṃdraṃ no agne vasubhiḥ sajoṣā rudraṃ rudrebhirā vahā bṛhaṃtaṃ | ādityebhiraditiṃ viśvajanyāṃ bṛhaspatimṛkvabhirviśvavāraṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-10-4)
In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to bring Indra together with the Vasus, Rudra together with the Rudras (Marut deities), Aditi, mother of all, together with the Ādityas (gods), and Bṛhaspati together with the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis who are praising. Besides, Ṛks which indicate that Bṛhaspati or Brahmaṇaspati is one and Agni another, namely 3-20-5; 4-40-1, 5-51-12, 7-41-1, 7-44-1, 9-5-11, 10-35-11, 10-65-1, 10-130-4, 10-141-3 and other mantras, are very many in the Ṛgveda. Therefore the doctrine that Agni is one and Bṛhaspati-Brahmaṇaspati another is the one supported in the Ṛgveda.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमां धियमिति द्वादशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तमांगिरसस्यायस्यस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं।
> इदमुत्तरं च बृहस्पतिदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इमां धियं द्वावशायास्यो
> बार्हस्पत्यं त्विति ॥ आभिप्लविकेपूक्ष्येषु स्तोमवृदौ ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इदं सूक्तमावापार्थं । सूत्रितं च। इमां धियमिति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी विष्णोर्नु कमिति सूक्ते ।
> आ-७ ९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta इमां धियं (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ*) is a twelve-Ṛk seventh sūkta; its ṛṣi is Ayāsya of the Āṅgirasa line, its metre is Triṣṭubh. This sūkta and the next have Bṛhaspati as deity. He cites the Anukramaṇī: इमां धियं द्वावशायास्यो बार्हस्पत्यं त्विति (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ dvāvaśāyāsyo bārhaspatyaṃ tviti*). In the Abhiplava ukthya rites, for the increase of the stoma, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites this sūkta as an āvāpa. It is also laid down in the sūtra: इमां धियमिति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी विष्णोर्नु कमिति सूक्ते (*imāṃ dhiyamiti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī viṣṇornu kamiti sūkte*) (Ā. 7-9).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta इमां धियं (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ*) is the seventh sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Ayāsya of the Aṅgirasa gotra; the metre is Triṣṭup. Bṛhaspati is the deity of this sūkta and of the next. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: इमां धियं द्वादशायास्को बार्हस्पत्यं तु (*imāṃ dhiyaṃ dvādaśāyāsko bārhaspatyaṃ tu*). In the ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, the ṛtvij called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite this sūkta as an āvāpa for increase of the stoma, as expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism इमां धियमिति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी विष्णोर्नु कमिति सूक्ते (*imāṃ dhiyamiti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī viṣṇornu kamiti sūkte*) (Ā. 7-9).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 67. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 2; Vargas 15, 16. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12. Ṛṣi: Ayāsya. Deity: Bṛhaspati. Metre: Triṣṭup.

> देवानां हितोपदेशनायेंद्रस्य पुरोहितोऽभवत् । कदाजित्तस्य गावः पणिनामकैरसुरैरपहृत्य वलपुरं प्रापय्य त्रिषु स्थानेषु तमसावृतेषु स्थापिता आसन् । अथ
> तासामन्वेषणायेंद्रेण प्रेरितो बृहस्पतिर्मरुद्भिः सह तत्रागत्य गवां गुहा
> स्थितानां दर्शनाय सूर्यं जनयित्वा वलनामानमसुरं तदनुचरान्पणींश्च हत्वा
> गा आजहारेति । तदत्र दर्शयिष्यते । तथा चास्या ऋचोऽयमर्थः। धियं कर्मणां
