> तुरीयं स्विन्नप्तारमपि जनयत् अजनयत् विश्वजन्यः सर्वजनहित इंद्रायेश्वराय
> बृहस्पतय इंद्राय वोक्तं स्तोत्रं शंसन्नयमयास्को नामर्षिः । पूर्वमेव
> नोऽस्माकं पिताकार्षिदित्याह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that an itihāsa is told here. Long ago the ṛṣi Aṅgiras obtained a son, Bṛhaspati, who became Indra's priest (purohita) in order to give the gods beneficial counsel. Once his cows were carried off by Asuras called Paṇis, brought to the city of Vala and kept in three places covered with darkness. Sent by Indra to seek them, Bṛhaspati came there with the Maruts, produced the sun so that the cows hidden in the cave could be seen, slew the Asura named Vala and his followers the Paṇis, and brought the cows back. This will be shown in the hymn. The meaning of the Ṛk is then given: धियं (*dhiyaṃ*) is the supporter of rites; सप्तशीर्ष्णीं (*saptaśīrṣṇīṃ*) is "seven-headed", furnished with seven groups of Maruts standing as heads, the principal ones; or else, having heads made of the seven metres. ऋतप्रजातां (*ṛtaprajātāṃ*) is born for the sake of the sacrifice. Our father Aṅgiras obtained this great body of ours, that is, he obtained Bṛhaspati, the meditator on rites, as a son. He quotes the Brāhmaṇa: those who were embers became the Aṅgirasas; the embers that, having cooled, blazed up again became Bṛhaspati (Ai. Brā. 3-34). Likewise Ayāsya, the ṛṣi, benevolent to all people, reciting praise to Indra, that is, to Bṛhaspati, begot also a fourth (descendant); he says that our father had acted even before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—the supporter of rites
- सप्तशीर्ष्णीं (*saptaśīrṣṇīṃ*)—having seven heads
- ऋतप्रजातां (*ṛtaprajātāṃ*)—that which was born for the sake of sacrifice
- बृहतीं (*bṛhatīṃ*)—of great form
- इमां (*imāṃ*)—this (Bṛhaspati-formed) body
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पिता (*pitā*)—father Aṅgiras
- अविंदत् (*aviṃdat*)—obtained
- तुरीयं स्वित् (*turīyaṃ svit*)—a grandson
- जनयत् (*janayat*)—begot
- विश्वजन्यः (*viśvajanyaḥ*)—beneficial to all

### Printed p. 561
- अयास्यः (*ayāsyaḥ*)—the ṛṣi named Ayāsya
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressing Indra
- उक्तं (*uktaṃ*)—a hymn
- शंसन् (*śaṃsan*)—offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Our father Aṅgiras obtained this body (of the form of Bṛhaspati), the supporter of rites, seven-headed, born for the sacrifice, of great form. He also obtained a grandson. The ṛṣi Ayāsya, beneficial to all, offered praise addressing Indra.

##### English translation
This great seven-headed ceremony, born of truth, our father (Angiras) discovered ; Ayasya, the friend of all races, engendered the fourth (generation), reciting a hymn to Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the bhāṣya of this Ṛk Sāyaṇa tells an itihāsa: अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । पुरा किलांगिरा नामर्षिर्बृहस्पतिं पुत्रमलभत । स तु देवानां हितोपदेशनायेंद्रस्य पुरोहितोऽभवत् । कदाजित्तस्य गावः पणिनामकैरसुरैरपहृत्य वलपुरं प्रापय्य त्रिषु स्थानेषु तमसावृतेषु स्थापिता आसन् । अथ तासामन्वेषणायेंद्रेण प्रेरितो बृहस्पतिर्मरुद्भिः सह तत्रागत्य गवां गुहा स्थितानां दर्शनाय सूर्यं जनयित्वा वलनामानमसुरं तदनुचरान्पणींश्च हत्वा गा आजहारेति । तदत्र दर्शयिष्यते । (*atretihāsamācakṣate | purā kilāṃgirā nāmarṣirbṛhaspatiṃ putramalabhata | sa tu devānāṃ hitopadeśanāyeṃdrasya purohito 'bhavat | kadājittasya gāvaḥ paṇināmakairasurairapahṛtya valapuraṃ prāpayya triṣu sthāneṣu tamasāvṛteṣu sthāpitā āsan | atha tāsāmanveṣaṇāyeṃdreṇa prerito bṛhaspatirmarudbhiḥ saha tatrāgatya gavāṃ guhā sthitānāṃ darśanāya sūryaṃ janayitvā valanāmānamasuraṃ tadanucarānpaṇīṃśca hatvā gā ājahāreti | tadatra darśayiṣyate |*) In the past the ṛṣi Aṅgiras had a son named Bṛhaspati. Because that Bṛhaspati, a well-wisher of the gods, gave them beneficial counsel, he was Indra's priest. At one time Asuras called Paṇis carried off Bṛhaspati's cows, took them to the city of their chief, the Asura named Vala, and hid them in a mountain cave covered on three sides and enveloped in pitch darkness. Sent by Indra with the intention of finding the cows, Bṛhaspati came with the Marut deities near Vala's city; as he searched for the cows, darkness had spread in the cave and nothing could be seen, so he set up the sun there to give light and made everything visible. Then he slew the Asura Vala who had carried off the cows and his followers the Paṇis, freed his cows and brought them back. This very matter is told in this hymn.
The carrying off of the cows of the gods (of Bṛhaspati) by the Paṇis, their hiding in a mountain cave, and their recovery by Bṛhaspati and the other gods with Indra's help, are described in many places in detail.

### Printed p. 562
In the 108th hymn of this same Maṇḍala it is said that, in order to learn who had carried off these cows and where they were, Indra first sent Saramā, the bitch of the gods; she crossed many rivers, mountains and hills, went a very long way, discovered the secret place where the Paṇis had hidden the cows, held a conversation with the Paṇis, and reported to Indra what had passed there; and that Indra and the other gods went there, conquered the Asuras and brought the cows back. The detailed explanation written on this subject can be seen there.
Concerning Bṛhaspati: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passages such as येऽज्ञारा आसंस्थेऽङ्गि रसोऽभवन् यदांगाराः पुनरवशांता उददीप्यंत तद्बृहस्पतिरभवत् (*ye 'jñārā āsaṃsthe 'ṅgi raso 'bhavan yadāṃgārāḥ punaravaśāṃtā udadīpyaṃta tadbṛhaspatirabhavat*) (Ai. Brā. 3-34) we have explained at length in the introduction to this hymn. (Part 20, p. 680)

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तं शंसं॑त ऋ॒जु दीध्या॑ना दि॒वस्पु॒त्रासो॒ असु॑रस्य वी॒राः ।  
> विप्रं॑ प॒दमंगि॑रसो॒ दधा॑ना य॒ज्ञस्य॒ धाम॑ प्रथ॒मं म॑नंत ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋतं । शंसंतः । ऋजु । दीध्यानाः । दिवः । पुत्रासः । असुरस्य । वीराः ।  
> विप्रं । पदं । अंगिरसः । दधानाः । यज्ञस्य । धाम । प्रथमं । मनंत ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋतं सत्यभूतं स्तोत्रं शंसंतः स्तुवंत ऋजु कल्याणं दीध्यानाः कर्माणि
> ध्यायंतो दिवो दीप्तस्यासुरस्य प्रज्ञानवतोऽग्नेरंगिरसः पुत्राः । अंगिरसो
> ह्यं गारेभ्यो जाता इत्युक्तं। अंगारेष्टंगिराः। नि. ३-१७-१ इति। वीरा विक्रांतप्रज्ञा
> एतेऽंगिरसो विप्रं प्रज्ञापकं यज्ञस्य धाम धारकं पदं बृहस्पत्याख्यं दधानाः
> कर्मणा धारयंतः संतः प्रथममादित एव मनंत । स्तुवंति । प्रज्ञापकं ह्येतत्स्थानं यद्बृहस्पतिरिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sons of the shining Asura (the wise Agni), the Aṅgirasas, recite true praise (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)), and meditate on rites (दीध्यानाः (*dīdhyānāḥ*)) auspiciously (ऋजु (*ṛju*)). He notes that the Aṅgirasas are said to be born from embers, and quotes अंगारेष्टंगिराः (*aṃgāreṣṭaṃgirāḥ*) (Ni. 3-17-1). Being valiant (वीराः (*vīrāḥ*), of heroic wisdom), these Aṅgirasas, bearing by their rite the place called Bṛhaspati, which makes known (विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)) and supports (धाम (*dhāma*)) the sacrifice, praise it from the very beginning (मनंत (*manaṃta*) = they praise). For this station, Bṛhaspati, is one that makes known.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—true praise
- शंसतः (*śaṃsataḥ*)—those who recite
- ऋजु (*ṛju*)—the welfare of the world
- दीध्यानाः (*dīdhyānāḥ*)—those who meditate
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—the shining one
- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—the wise
- पुत्रासः (*putrāsaḥ*)—sons of Agni
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—the Aṅgirasas
- वीराः (*vīrāḥ*)—being valiant

### Printed p. 563
- विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)—that which makes known to the world
- यज्ञस्य धाम (*yajñasya dhāma*)—that which supports the sacrifice
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—the station called Bṛhaspati
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—having borne it by their rite
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—from the beginning
- मनंत (*manaṃta*)—they praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirasas, sons of the shining and wise Agni, who recite true praise and meditate for the welfare of the world, being valiant, having borne by their rite the station called Bṛhaspati, which makes known to the world and supports the sacrifice, praise it from the beginning.

##### English translation
Reciting sincere praise, reflecting correctly, the Agirasas, the pious sons of the brilliant and powerful (Agni), upholding the intelligent base, the supporter of the sacrifice, praise from the beginning.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हं॒सैरि॑व॒ सखि॑भि॒र्वाव॑दद्भिरश्म॒न्मया॑नि॒ नह॑ना॒ व्यस्य॑न् ।  
> बृह॒स्पति॑रभि॒कनि॑क्रद॒द्दा उ॒त प्रास्तौ॒दुच्च॑ वि॒द्वा अ॑गायत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हंसैः इव । सखिभिः । वावदत्भिः । अश्मन्मयानि । नहना । विअस्यन् ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । अभिकनिक्रदत् । गाः । उश । प्र । अस्तौत् । उत । च । विद्वान् । अगायत् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवसुवां हविःषु बृहस्पतॆये वाचस्पतय इत्यस्य याज्या हंसैरिवेत्येषा।
> सूत्रितं च । बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावदद्भिः । आ. ४-११ ।
> इति ॥
> हंसैरिव मधुरवाद्भिः सखिभिः सखिभूतैर्वावदभ्यिरत्यंतं शब्दायमानैर्मरुद्धिरश्मन्मयान्यश्ममयानि नहना गवां बंधकान्यावरकाण्यसुराणां स्थानानि
> व्यस्यन् विक्षिपञ्चथिलयन्नभिकनिक्रददाभिमुख्येन शब्दयन् गाः पणिभिरपहृतान्पशूनाजिहीर्षुः स बृहस्पतिर्वर्तते । यद्वा । वावदद्धिरत्यंतं स्तुवद्धिः स्तोतृभिः सह

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the offerings to the Devasuvas (the gods called Devasuvaḥ), for the oblation to बृहस्पतॆये वाचस्पतय (*bṛhaspatèye vācaspataya*) the yājyā is this Ṛk हंसैरिव (*haṃsairiva*). It is also given in the sūtra: बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावदद्भिः (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ haṃsairiva sakhibhirvāvadadbhiḥ*) (Ā. 4-11). Explanation: Bṛhaspati, with the Maruts as friends, sounding sweetly like geese and sounding greatly (वावदद्भिः (*vāvadadbhiḥ*)), throwing open (व्यस्यन् (*vyasyan*), loosening) the stone-made (अश्मन्मयानि (*aśmanmayāni*)) fastenings (नहना (*nahanā*)), the enclosing places of the Asuras that bind the cows, and calling out (अभिकनिक्रदत् (*abhikanikradat*)) toward them, is intent on bringing back the cattle carried off by the Paṇis. Or else: with the worshippers who praise greatly he utters the speech-form of praise toward the cows.

### Printed p. 564
Moreover, प्रास्तौत् (*prāstaut*): when the rite begins, sitting with his friends at the sacrifice he begins the sāman to sing. Knowing all (विद्वान् (*vidvān*)), he became the Udgātṛ and sang (उदगायत् (*udagāyat*)); he sings to the gods, he praises.

> गाः स्तोत्रलक्षणा वाचोभिकनिक्रददाभिमुख्येनोच्चारयन् । उतापि च प्रास्तौत् ।
> कर्मणि प्रवृत्तौ यज्ञस्य सखिभिः सहासीनः साम गातुं प्रस्तौति । विद्वान् सर्वं
> जानानः स उद्गाता भूत्वोदगायत् । देवानुद्गायति । अभिष्टौति ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हंसैः इव (*haṃsaiḥ iva*)—like geese
- वावदद्भिः (*vāvadadbhiḥ*)—sounding sweetly
- सखिभिः (*sakhibhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts, who are friends
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- अश्मन्मयानि (*aśmanmayāni*)—made of stone
- नहना (*nahanā*)—cow-binding places of the Asuras
- व्यस्यन् (*vyasyan*)—loosening
- अभिकनिक्रदत् (*abhikanikradat*)—sounding
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—wished to free the cows
- उत (*uta*)—and
- प्रास्तौत् (*prāstaut*)—praised the gods
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—he who knows everything
- उद गायत् (*uda gāyat*)—praised in the form of song

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Together with the Maruts, who sound sweetly like geese and are his friends, Bṛhaspati, loosening the stone-made, cow-binding places of the Asuras and sounding aloud, wished to free the cows. Knowing everything, he praised the gods in song.

##### English translation
With his friends (the Maruts) clamouring like geese, throwing open the (Asuras') cattle-folds made of stone, Brihaspati calling aloud (desires to carry off) the cows; knowing all things he praises (the gods), and chants (their laudation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the homa performed to the eight deities called Devasuvas, when the oblation offered to the deity बृहस्पतये वाचस्पतये (*bṛhaspataye vācaspataye*) is offered, this Ṛk हंसैरिव (*haṃsairiva*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावदद्भिः (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ haṃsairiva sakhibhirvāvadadbhiḥ*) (Ā. 4-11).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒वो द्वाभ्यां॑ प॒र एक॑या॒ गा गुहा॒ तिष्ठं॑ती॒रनृ॑तस्य॒ सेत् ॑।  
> बृह॒स्पति॒स्तम॑सि॒ ज्योति॑रि॒च्छन्नुदु॒स्रा आक॒र्वि हिति॒स्र आवः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> आवरित्यावः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पणयो गा आहृत्य त्रिपु स्थानेषु निदधुः । अवोऽवस्तात्स्थिता अनृतस्य तमसः
> सेत्वा स्थाने गुहा गुहायां तिष्ठंतीर्गा द्वाभ्यां स्थानाभ्यामुदाजत् । ततः परः
> परस्तादवस्थिता गा एकयैकेन स्थानेनोदगमयत् । तदेवाह । बृहस्पतिस्तस्मिंस्तमसि
> ज्योतिः कर्तुमिच्छंस्तत्र स्थिता उस्रा गा उदाकः । उदकार्षित् । प्रादुर्भूता
> अकार्षित् । इत्थमयं तिस्रोऽसुराणां द्वारो न्यावः । विवृतवान्खलु ॥ वृणोतेर्लुजि मंत्रे घसेति चेर्लुक् । बहुलं छंदसीत्यडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Paṇis, having carried off the cows, placed them in three places. The cows standing below (अवः (*avaḥ*)), in a cave in a place of darkness (अनृतस्य । सेता (*anṛtasya | setā*)), he led out by two places; those standing above (परः (*paraḥ*)) he brought out by one place (एकया (*ekayā*)). Bṛhaspati, wishing to make light in that darkness, brought forth (उदाकः (*udākaḥ*)) the cows (उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)) standing there, made them appear. Thus he opened (न्यावः (*nyāvaḥ*)) the three doors of the Asuras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनृतस्य (*anṛtasya*)—dark
- सेत् (*set*)—in the place
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in the cave
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—that were in the lower region
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- द्वाभ्यां (*dvābhyāṃ*)—he drove out by two places (ways)
- परः (*paraḥ*)—the cows that were in the upper place
- एकया (*ekayā*)—he drove out by one way
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- तमसि (*tamasi*)—in the darkness
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—producing light
- इच्छन् (*icchan*)—wishing to free the cows
- उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)—the cows
- उदाकः (*udākaḥ*)—brought out
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—the three doors of the Asuras
- व्यावः (*vyāvaḥ*)—split open

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The cows that were in the lower region, in a cave in a place covered with darkness, he drove out by two ways; the cows that were in the upper place he drove out by one way. Bṛhaspati, producing light in the darkness and wishing to free the cows, brought the cows out. He split open the three doors of the Asuras' pen.

##### English translation
Brihaspati purposing to bring light into the darkness drove out the cows standing in the cave in the place of darkness below by two (ways), and those above by one (way) ; he opened the three (doors of the Asuras).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स बृहस्पतिः शयथोपशयेन स्थित्वापाचीं पराङ्मुखीमीमिमामसुरपुरीं
> विभिद्य विदार्योदधेर्वलाद्मेघरूपादसुरात्साकं सह युगपत् त्रीण्युषसं
> सूर्यं गामेतानि त्रीणि निरकृंतत् । निर्गतमकार्षित् । तमसावृतेषु स्थानेषूषःकालतः पश्चाद्भाविनं सूर्यं च जनयित्वा पशून्निरगमयदित्यर्थः । सोऽयमर्कमर्चनीयं मंत्रं सूर्यं विवेद। प्रज्ञापयति । कथमिव । यथा स्तनयन्
> शब्दं कुर्वन् द्यौरिव स्थितः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Bṛhaspati, abiding by lying close beside it, split open this western, that is backward-facing, city of the Asura. Together, at one and the same time, he brought out from Vala, the Asura in the form of a cloud (उदधेः (*udadheḥ*)), these three: Uṣas, Sūrya and the cow. That is, having produced the dawn and the sun that comes after the dawn-time in the places covered with darkness, he made the cattle come out. This same one made known the adorable mantra, the sun (अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)), like thundering heaven making a sound.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- शयथा (*śayathā*)—standing leaning right beside it
- अपाचीं (*apācīṃ*)—facing west
- ईं पुरं (*īṃ puraṃ*)—the city of the Asura
- विभिद्य (*vibhidya*)—having destroyed
- त्रीणि (*trīṇi*)—the three means of light
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—Uṣas
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- गां (*gāṃ*)—the cow
- उदधेः (*udadheḥ*)—from the Asura Vala, in the form of a cloud
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- नि अकृंतत् (*ni akṛṃtat*)—made come out
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—like the heaven
- स्तनयन्निव (*stanayanniva*)—making a sound
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—the adorable sun
- विवेद (*viveda*)—made manifest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Bṛhaspati, standing leaning right beside it, destroyed the west-facing city of the Asura and brought out together, from the Asura named Vala in the form of a cloud, the three kinds of means of light: Uṣas, the sun and the cow. Making a sound like the heaven, he caused the adorable sun to shine.

### Printed p. 567

##### English translation
Resting near it, demolishing the western city, Brihaspati wrestled at once from Vala the three, the dawn, the sun, the cow ; thundering like the heaven, he proclaimed the adorable (sun).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॑ व॒लं र॑क्षि॒तारं॒ दुघा॑नां क॒रेणे॑व॒ वि च॑कर्ता॒ रवे॑ण ।  
> स्वेदां॑जिभिरा॒शिर॑मि॒च्छमा॒नोऽरो॑दयत्प॒णिमा गा अ॑मुष्णात् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । वलं । रक्षितारं । दुघानां । करेण इव । वि । चकर्त । रवेण ।  
> स्वेदांजिभिः । आशिरं । इच्छमानः । अरोदयत् । पणिं । आ । गाः । अमुष्णात् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्र ईश्वरो बृहस्पतिर्दुघानां क्षीरस्य दोग्धीणां गवां रक्षितारं वलमसुरं करेणेव सायुधकर इव स्थितेन रवेण शब्देन वलं वि चकर्त। विचिच्छेद। किंच
> स्वेदांजिभिः । स्वेदांजयो मरुतः क्षरदाभरणाः। तैः सहाशिरमाश्रयणं संयोगमिच्छमानः कामयमानः पणिं वलस्यानुचरमेतन्नामानमसुरमरोदयत् ।
> व्यनाशयत् । ततस्तेनापहृता गा आमुष्णात् । आजहार ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the lord Bṛhaspati, with a sound that was like an armed hand, split Vala the Asura, the guardian of the milk-yielding cows. Further, desiring association (आशिरं (*āśiraṃ*), refuge) with the Maruts, the स्वेदांजिभिः (*svedāṃjibhiḥ*), whose ornaments are streaming sweat, he destroyed Paṇi, the follower of Vala, an Asura of that name, and then carried off the cows that had been taken away by him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra (the lord Bṛhaspati)
- दुघानां (*dughānāṃ*)—of the cows that yield milk
- रक्षितारं (*rakṣitāraṃ*)—who had hidden them
- वलं (*valaṃ*)—the Asura named Vala
- करेणेव (*kareṇeva*)—like a hand bearing a weapon
- रवेण (*raveṇa*)—by sound alone
- वि चकर्त (*vi cakarta*)—tore apart
- स्वेदांजिभिः (*svedāṃjibhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts who have sweat itself as their ornament
- आशिरं (*āśiraṃ*)—Soma mixed with curds and the like
- इच्छमानः (*icchamānaḥ*)—Indra (Bṛhaspati), desiring
- पणिं (*paṇiṃ*)—the Asura named Paṇi
- अरोदयत् (*arodayat*)—destroyed
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- अमुष्णात् (*amuṣṇāt*)—carried off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra (Bṛhaspati) tore apart the Asura Vala, who had hidden the milk-yielding cows, by a sound that was like an armed hand. Desiring Soma mixed with curds and the like together with the Maruts, who had sweat itself as their ornament, Indra destroyed the Asura named Paṇi. He carried off the cows.

### Printed p. 568

##### English translation
Indra with his voice as with an (armed) hand clove Valva the defender of the milch cows; desirous of the mixture (of milk and Soma) he with (the Maruts), who were shining with perspiration, destroyed Pani and liberated the cows.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स ईं॑ स॒त्येभिः॒ सखि॑भिः शु॒चद्भि॒गोर्धा॑यसं॒ वि ध॑न॒सैर॑दर्दः ।  
> ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पति॒र्वृष॑भिर्व॒राहै॑र्घ॒र्मस्वे॑देभि॒र्द्रवि॑णं॒ व्या॑नट् ॥७॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः। ईं। सत्येभिः । सखिभिः। शुचत्ऽभिः। गोऽधायसं । वि। धनऽसैः। अदर्दरित्यदर्दः।  
> ब्रह्मणः । पतिः । वृषऽभिः । वराहैः । घर्मऽस्वेदेभिः । द्रविणं । वि । आनट् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स बृहस्पतिः सत्येभिर्यथार्थबलैः सखिभिः । सखिभूतैः शुचद्भिर्दिप्यमानैर्धनसैर्धनस्य संभक्तृभिर्मरुद्भिः सह गोधायसं गवां धारकमीमेनं वलं
> व्यदर्दः । व्यदारयत् । ततो ब्रह्मण ऋग्यजुःसामलक्षणस्य स्तोत्रस्य पतिरधिपतिः स
> वृषभिर्वर्षितृभिर्वराहैर्वराहारैर्वरस्य वरणीयस्योदकस्याहर्तृभिर्घर्मस्वेदेभिर्दिप्तागमनैः यद्वा क्षरदुदकैः । अथवा! घर्मो यज्ञः। तं प्रति गंतृभिर्मरुद्भिर्द्रविणं गोलक्षणं धनं व्यानट् । व्याप्नोत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Bṛhaspati, with the Maruts, who are true, that is, of real strength, friendly, shining (शुचद्भिः (*śucadbhiḥ*)) and sharers of wealth (धनसैः (*dhanasaiḥ*)), split open this Vala, the holder of the cows. Then Brahmaṇaspati, lord of the praise-hymn that has the form of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, obtained the wealth in the form of cows with the Maruts who are showerers, वराहैः (*varāhaiḥ*), that is, bringers of choice (desirable) water, and घर्मस्वेदेभिः (*gharmasvedebhiḥ*), of blazing approach, or else streaming water. Or else: *gharmaḥ* is the sacrifice, and they are the Maruts who go to it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः (*saḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- सत्येभिः (*satyebhiḥ*)—possessed of true strength
- सखिभिः (*sakhibhiḥ*)—friendly
- शुचद्भिः (*śucadbhiḥ*)—shining
- धनसैः (*dhanasaiḥ*)—together with the Maruts who possess wealth
- गोधायसं (*godhāyasaṃ*)—who had hidden the cows
- ईं (*īṃ*)—Vala
- व्यदर्दः (*vyadardaḥ*)—tore apart
- ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (*brahmaṇaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati, lord of praises
- वृषभिः (*vṛṣabhiḥ*)—granters of desired ends
- वराहैः (*varāhaiḥ*)—pourers of the desired water
- घर्मस्वेदेभिः (*gharmasvedebhiḥ*)—with the Maruts, who go to the sacrifice
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—the wealth in the form of cows
- व्यानट् (*vyānaṭ*)—obtained

### Printed p. 569

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Together with the Maruts, who possess true strength, are friends, shine and hold wealth, Bṛhaspati tore apart Vala, who had hidden the cows. Bṛhaspati, lord of praises, together with the Maruts, who grant desired ends, pour the desired water and go to the sacrifice, obtained the wealth in the form of cows.

##### English translation
Together with his true brilliant wealth-winning friendly (Maruts) he destroyed the detainer of the cows; Brahmanaspati, with the showerers (of benefits), the conveyers of desirable (water). the frequenters of sacrifice, acquired wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वराहैः (*varāhaiḥ*)—In explaining the word वराह (*varāha*), Yāska says:
अंगिरसोऽपि वराहा उच्यंते । ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्वृषभिर्वराहैः । (*aṃgiraso 'pi varāhā ucyaṃte | brahmaṇaspatirvṛṣabhirvarāhaiḥ |*) (Ni. 5-4).
The Aṅgirā ṛṣis are also called Varāhas. For वराहैर्वराहारैः (*varāhairvarāhāraiḥ*): because they partake only of the best, sattvic food, they get the name Varāha; or else वरस्य वरणीयस्योदकस्याहर्तृभिः (*varasya varaṇīyasyodakasyāhartṛbhiḥ*): because they cause to rain down (by the performance of sacrifices and other rites) the rain-water desired by all, the Aṅgirases are called Varāhas. This is how he explains the meaning. The various meanings of the word वराह (*varāha*) (as Yāska explains them in the Nirukta) we have set out at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 25, p. 175, and Part 26, p. 762.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते स॒त्येन॒ मन॑सा॒ गोप॑तिं॒ गा इ॑या॒नास॑ इषणयंत धी॒भिः ।  
> बृह॒स्पति॑र्मि॒थोअ॑वद्यपेभि॒रुदु॒स्रिया॑ असृजत स्य॒युग्भिः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । सत्येन । मनसा । गोऽपतिं । गाः । इयानासः । इषणयंत । धीभिः ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । मिथःऽअवद्यपेभिः । उत् । उस्रियाः । असृजत । स्वयुक्ऽभिः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 570

> गाः पणिभिरपहृतान्पशूनियानासोऽभिगच्छंतः सत्येन यथार्थभूतेन मनसा
> युक्तास्ते मरुतो धीभिरात्मीयैः कर्मभिरेतं बृहस्पतिं गोपतिं तदाहरणेन
> गवां स्वामिनं कुर्म इतीषणयंत । ऐच्छन् । बृहस्पतिश्च मिथोअवद्यपेभिः ॥
> पातेः कर्मण्यौणादिकः प्रत्ययः ॥ अवद्यरूपादसुराद्रक्षितव्या गावो येषु मरुत्तु
> परस्परं संगच्छंत इति ते तथोक्ताः । तैः स्वयुग्भिः स्वयमेव युक्तैर्मरुद्धिरुस्रिया गा उदसृजत । पर्वतान्निरगमयत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Maruts, going towards the cows, the cattle carried off by the Paṇis, and endowed with a true, that is real, mind, desired by their own deeds (धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)) to make this Bṛhaspati the lord of the cows (गोपतिं (*gopatiṃ*)) by their recovery. And Bṛhaspati, with the मिथोअवद्यपेभिः (*mithoavadyapebhiḥ*): the word is formed with an Uṇādi affix in the sense of the object from the root पा (*pā*) (to protect). They are those Maruts among whom the cows are to be protected from the Asura who is in the form of blame, and who come together with one another; so they are so called. With those स्वयुग्भिः (*svayugbhiḥ*), the Maruts yoked of their own accord, he let the cows go forth (उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*)); he made them come out from the mountains.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्येन (*satyena*)—with a trustworthy
- मनसा (*manasā*)—mind
- ते (*te*)—the Maruts
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- इयानासः (*iyānāsaḥ*)—searching
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—by their deeds
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- गोपतिं (*gopatiṃ*)—to make him the lord of the cows
- इषणयंत (*iṣaṇayaṃta*)—desired
- मिथोअवद्यपेभिः (*mithoavadyapebhiḥ*)—who give one another protection from the Asura
- स्वयुग्निः (*svayugniḥ*)—together with the Maruts who come and join of their own accord
- उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*)—the cows
- उदसृजत (*udasṛjata*)—made come out
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, with trustworthy minds, searching for the cows, desired by their deeds to make Bṛhaspati the lord of the cows. Bṛhaspati, together with the Maruts, who give one another protection from the Asura and who come and join of their own accord, made the cows come out.

##### English translation
They with truthful mind searching for the cows resolved by their exploits to make him the lord of cattle; Brihaspati with his self-yoked (allies) mutually defending each other from reproach, set free the cows.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं व॒र्धयं॑तो म॒शिभिः॑ शि॒वाभिः॑ सिं॒हमि॑व॒ नान॑दतं स॒दस्ये॑ ।  
> बृह॒स्पतिं॒ वृष॑णं॒ शूर॑सात्॒ भरे॑भरे॒ अनु॑ मदेम जि॒ष्णुं ॥९॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । वर्धयंतः । मतिभिः । शिवाभिः । सिंहं इव । नानदतं । सधस्थे ।

### Printed p. 571

> बृहस्पतिं । वृषणं । शूरसात् । भरेऽभरे । अनु । मदेम । जिष्णुं ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सधस्थे । सह तिष्ठंत्यत्र देवा इति सधस्थमंतरिक्षं । तस्मिन् सिंहमिव नानदतं
> पुनःपुनः शब्दायमानं वृषणं कामानां वर्षितारं जिष्णुं जयशीलं तं बृहस्पतिं
> वर्धयंतो मरुतो वयं शूरसात् शूरैः संभजनीये भरे भरे संग्रामे
> शिवाभिः कल्याणीभिः स्तुतिभिरनु मदेम। अनुष्टुमः। स्तोतृपरत्वेन वा योजनीयं॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*): the gods abide together here, hence *sadhasthaṃ* is the atmosphere. In it Bṛhaspati roars again and again like a lion; he is the showerer of desires and victorious by nature. We Maruts, magnifying him, rejoice in him with auspicious, that is, propitious, praises in every battle (भरे भरे (*bhare bhare*)), where heroes win the prize (शूरसात् (*śūrasāt*)). Alternatively the verse is to be construed as referring to the praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)—in the atmosphere
- सिंहमिव (*siṃhamiva*)—like a lion
- नानदतं (*nānadataṃ*)—roaring again and again
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—granter of desired ends
- जिष्णुं (*jiṣṇuṃ*)—victorious
- तं बृहस्पतिं (*taṃ bṛhaspatiṃ*)—that Bṛhaspati
- वर्धयंतः (*vardhayaṃtaḥ*)—we who strengthen
- शूरसात् (*śūrasāt*)—where heroes win victory
- भरेभरे (*bharebhare*)—in battle
- शिवाभिः (*śivābhiḥ*)—auspicious
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—by praises
- अनु मदेम (*anu madema*)—we gladden

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We who strengthen Bṛhaspati, who roars in the atmosphere again and again like a lion, who grants desired ends and is victorious, gladden him with auspicious praises in battle where heroes win victory.

##### English translation
Magnifying the victorious Brihaspati, the showerer (of benefits), roaring in mid-heaven like a lion, let us praise him in the conflicts where heroes win. with auspicious praises.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒दा वाज॒मस॑नद्वि॒श्वरू॑प॒मा द्यामरु॑क्ष॒दुत्त॑राणि॒ सद्म॑ ।  
> बृह॒स्पतिं॒ वृष॑णं व॒र्धयं॑तो॒ नाना॒ संतो॒ भिभ्र॑तो॒  ॒॑
> ज्योतिरासा ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यदा । वाजं । असनत् । विश्वरूपं । आ । द्यां । अरुक्षत् । उत्तराणि । सद्म ।  
> बृहस्पतिं । वृषणं । वर्धयंतः । नाना । संतः । बिभ्रतः । ज्योतिः । आसा ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 572

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स बृहस्पतिर्यदा यस्मिन्काले विश्वरूपं नानारूपं वाजं गोलक्षणमन्नमसनत् भजते यदा वाहृतपशुकः सन् द्यां द्युलोकमरुक्षत् आरोहति । अथवोत्तराणि वा सद्म स्थानान्यारोहति ॥ रुहेर्लुजि च्छेः शल इगुपधादनिटः क्सः पा. ३-१-४५॥
> तदानीं वृषणं वर्षितारं बृहस्पतिमासास्येन देवा वर्धयंतो भवंति । तथा नाना
> दिक्षु संतो भवंतो ज्योतिर्बिभ्रतो धारयंतो देवाश्च स्तुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that Bṛhaspati, when he enjoys विश्वरूपं (*viśvarūpaṃ*) food of many forms (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), meaning food in the form of cows, ascends the sky (द्यां (*dyāṃ*)), the heavenly world. Or he ascends *uttarāṇi sadma*, the higher stations, having had his cattle brought back. **NOTE**
At that time the gods increase Bṛhaspati, the showerer, with their mouths. The gods who are in various quarters and bear light also praise him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- विश्वरूपं (*viśvarūpaṃ*)—having forms of many kinds
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- आसनत् (*āsanat*)—Bṛhaspati obtains
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the world of heaven
- अरुक्षत् (*arukṣat*)—when he ascends
- उत्तराणि ना सद्म (*uttarāṇi nā sadma*)—when he joins the regions of the northern direction, then
- नाना संतः (*nānā saṃtaḥ*)—those who are in many directions
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—light
- बिभ्रतः (*bibhrataḥ*)—the gods who bear (it)
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—the granter of desired things
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- आसा (*āsā*)—with their mouths
- वर्धयंतः (*vardhayaṃtaḥ*)—praise and make thrive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Bṛhaspati obtains food of many forms (cows), and when he ascends either the regions of the heavenly world or the region of the northern direction, then the gods, who are in many directions and bear radiance, praise with their mouths Bṛhaspati, the granter of desired things, and make him thrive.

##### English translation
When he acquires food of various kinds, when he ascends the sky or
the northern stations, (the gods are) extolling Brihaspati, the showerer (of
benefits), with their mouth, being in various (quarters), bearing light.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒त्यामा॒शिषं॑ कृणुता वयो॒ध्यै की॒रिं चि॒द्द्यव॑थ॒ स्वेभि॒रेवैः॑ ।  
> प॒श्चा मृधो॒ अप॑ भवंतु॒ विश्वा॒स्तद्रो॑दसी शृणुतं विश्वमि॒न्वे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्यां । आशिषं । कृणुत । वयःधैः । कीरिं । चित् । हि । अवथ । स्वेभिः । एवैः ।

### Printed p. 573

> पश्चा । मृढः । अप । भवंतु । विश्वाः । तत् । रोदसी इति । शृणुतं । विश्वमिन्वे इति  
> विश्वं इन्वे ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे बृहस्पतिप्रभृतयो देवा वयोधा अन्नस्य धानायास्मदीयामाशिषं
> स्तुतिं सत्यां यथार्थां कृणुत । कुरुत । तथा यूयं स्वेभिरात्मीयैरेवैर्गमनैः
> कीरिं स्तोतारं मामवथ । रक्षथ । हिरवधारणे । पश्चा ॥ पश्चा च छंदसि । पा. ५ ३-३३ ।
> इति निपातितः ॥ पश्चादिश्वाः सर्वा मृधो हिंसित्र्योप भवंतु । नश्यंतु । तदिदमस्माभिरुक्तं वचनं हे विश्वमिन्वे विश्वस्य प्रीणयित्र्यौ हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ शृणुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O gods, Bṛhaspati and the rest, givers of sustenance (वयोधा (*vayodhā*)), make our praise (आशिषं (*āśiṣaṃ*)) true, that is, as it should be, so that food may be bestowed. Protect me, the singer (कीरिं (*kīriṃ*)), by your own goings (एवैः (*evaiḥ*)). Here हि (*hi*) is used in the sense of emphasis. पश्चा (*paścā*) is a form fixed by rule. Afterwards may all harming enemies (मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)) perish. O heaven and earth, delighters of all (विश्वमिन्वे (*viśvaminve*)), hear this word spoken by us."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O gods, Bṛhaspati and the rest)
- वयोध्यॆ (*vayodhyè*)—in order to offer food
- आशिषं (*āśiṣaṃ*)—our praise
- सत्यां (*satyāṃ*)—as true
- कृणुत (*kṛṇuta*)—make
- स्वेभिः (*svebhiḥ*)—your
- एवैः (*evaiḥ*)—by goings
- कीरिं (*kīriṃ*)—me, the praiser
- अवथ (*avatha*)—protect
- विश्वाः मृधः (*viśvāḥ mṛdhaḥ*)—all enemies, harmful (to us) **NOTE**
- पश्चा (*paścā*)—at the end
- अप भवंतु (*apa bhavaṃtu*)—may they perish
- विश्वमिन्वे (*viśvaminve*)—you who gladden the whole world
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—O heaven and earth
- तत् (*tat*)—our praise
- शृणुतं (*śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, Bṛhaspati and the rest, make our praise true, in order to offer food in the form of oblation. Protect me, the praiser, by your goings. May all our harming enemies perish. O heaven and earth, who gladden the whole world, hear our praise.

##### English translation
Make good our prayer for the bestowal of food; you protect through
your movements even (me) your worshipper; may all our enemies he driven
back again; heaven and earth, the delighters of all, hear this (our prayer).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॑ म॒ह्ना म॑ह॒तो अ॑र्ण॒वस्य॒ वि मू॒र्धान॑मभिनदर्बु॒दस्य॑ ।  
> अह॒न्नहि॒मरि॑णात्स॒प्त सिंधू॑न्दे॒वैर्द्या॑वापृथिवी॒ प्राव॑तं नः ॥

### Printed p. 574

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । मह्ना । महतः । अर्णवस्य । वि । मूर्धानं । अभिनत् । अर्बुदस्य ।  
> अहन् । अहिं । अरिणात् । सप्त । सिंधून् । देवैः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । प्र । अवतं ॥  
> नः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्र ईश्वरो मह्ना महत्त्वेन युक्तो बृहस्पतिर्महतो अर्णवस्योदकवर्तोऽर्बुदस्यांबुदस्य मेघस्य मूर्धानं शिरो व्यभिनत् । व्यच्छिनत् । तदुच्यते ।
> अहिमहंतव्यमपामावरकं शत्रुमहन् । अवधीत् । अतः सप्त सर्पणशीलाः सिंधून्
> स्यंदमाना अपः । यद्वा । सप्तसंख्याका गंगाद्या नदीः । अरिणात् । समुद्रं प्रत्यगमयत् । अथ प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ देवैः सह नोऽस्मान्प्रावतं ।
> प्ररक्षतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the lord, that is Bṛhaspati, endowed with greatness (मह्ना (*mahnā*)), split (व्यभिनत् (*vyabhinat*), cut) the head of the great watery (*udakavarto*) cloud (अर्बुदस्य (*arbudasya*)). Further it is said that he slew Ahi, the enemy who is to be slain and who obstructs the waters. Therefore he made the seven flowing rivers (सिंधून् (*siṃdhūn*)), the waters that move, go (अरिणात् (*ariṇāt*)) to the sea; or else the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā. Then, addressing directly: O heaven and earth, protect us (प्रावतं (*prāvataṃ*)) together with the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—he who is filled with greatness
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Bṛhaspati, the lord
- महतः (*mahataḥ*)—of the great one, endowed with majesty
- अर्णवस्य (*arṇavasya*)—and endowed with water
- अर्बुदस्य (*arbudasya*)—of the cloud
- मूर्धानं (*mūrdhānaṃ*)—the head
- व्यभिनत् (*vyabhinat*)—he split
- अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—the enemy
- अहन् (*ahan*)—he destroyed
- सप्त सिंधून् (*sapta siṃdhūn*)—the seven rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest
- अरिणात् (*ariṇāt*)—he made flow towards the sea
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—O heaven and earth, you
- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—together with the gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- प्रावतं (*prāvataṃ*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Bṛhaspati, filled with greatness and a lord, split the head of the cloud, which is endowed with majesty and with water. He destroyed the enemy, and made the seven rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest, flow towards the sea. O heaven and earth, protect us together with the gods.

##### English translation
Indra by his might has cleft the brow of the vast watery cloud, he has
has slain Ahi; he has made the seven rivers flow; do you, heaven and earth,
along with the gods, protect us.

## Sūkta 68 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उदपुत इति द्वादशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं । ऋष्या द्याः पूर्ववत् । उदपुत
> इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ उक्ते ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । प्र मंहिष्ठायोदपुतोऽच्छा म इंद्रं । आ. ६-१ । इति ॥

### Printed p. 575

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning उदपुत (*udaputa*) has twelve verses and is the eighth sūkta (of the anuvāka). Its seer and the rest (deity, metre) are as before. The Anukramaṇī says उदपुत (*udaputa*) and so on. In the ukta recitation this sūkta belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. It is also stated in the sūtra: प्र मंहिष्ठायोदपुतोऽच्छा म इंद्रं (*pra maṃhiṣṭhāyodaputo 'cchā ma iṃdraṃ*) (Ā. 6-1).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, उदपुतः (*udaputaḥ*), is the eighth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has twelve ṛks. Its seer, deity and metre are as in the preceding sūkta. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated beginning with उदपुतः (*udaputaḥ*). That the officiating priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite this sūkta in the recitation of the ukta mantras is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, प्र मंहिष्ठायोदपुतोऽच्छा म इंद्रं (*pra maṃhiṣṭhāyodaputo 'cchā ma iṃdraṃ*) (Ā. 6-1).

Maṇḍala 10. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 68. Aṣṭaka 8. Adhyāya 2. Varga 17, 18. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 12. Seer: Ayāsya. Deity: Bṛhaspati. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒द॒पुतो॒ न वयो॒ रक्ष॑माणा॒ वाव॑दतो अ॒भिय॑स्येव॒  ॑
> घोषाः ।  
> गि॒रि॒भ्रजो॒ नोर्मयो॒ मदं॑तो॒ बृह॒स्पति॑म॒भ्य१॒॑र्का अ॑नावन्॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उदप्रुतः । न । वयः । रक्षमाणाः । वावदतः । अभ्रियस्य इव । घोषाः ।  
> गिरिभ्रजः । न । ऊर्मयः । मदंतः । बृहस्पतिं । अभि । अर्काः । अनावन् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उदपुत उदकस्योद्गमयितारो वयः पक्षिणः पक्षात्सस्याद्रक्षमाणाः
> कृषीवलाः । न उपमार्थे । यथा शब्दायंते । यथा च वावदतः पुनःपुनः शब्दायमानस्याभ्रियस्येवाभ्रसमूहस्य घोषाः शब्दा यथा भवंति । किंचगिरिभ्रजो गिरिभ्यो
> मेघेभ्यो भ्रष्टा निर्गता ऊर्मयोऽप्समूहा यथा मदंतः शब्दायमाना
> भवंति । तथार्का अर्चकाः स्तोतारो बृहस्पतिमभ्यनावन् । अभिष्णुवंति ॥ नु स्तवने ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

उदपुत (*udaputa*) are the raisers of water; वयः (*vayaḥ*) are birds; farmers (कृषीवलाः (*kṛṣīvalāḥ*)) who guard the crop from birds make sound as they drive them; न (*na*) is in the sense of comparison. Just as the sounds (घोषाः (*ghoṣāḥ*)) of a cloud-mass (अभ्रियस्य (*abhriyasya*)) that thunders again and again come to be, and just as the torrents (ऊर्मयः (*ūrmayaḥ*)) of water that have fallen from the mountains, the clouds, rejoice and resound, so the worshippers (अर्काः (*arkāḥ*)), the singers, praise Bṛhaspati (अभ्यनावन् (*abhyanāvan*), from the root नु स्तवने (*nu stavane*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उदप्रुतः (*udaprutaḥ*)—sprinkling water
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—driving away birds
- रक्षमाणाः न (*rakṣamāṇāḥ na*)—as farmers who protect the crops from birds make a noise when driving the birds away
- वावदतः (*vāvadataḥ*)—repeatedly thundering **NOTE**
### Printed p. 576
- अभ्रियस्य (*abhriyasya*)—of the cloud
- घोषा इव (*ghoṣā iva*)—like the sound
- गिरिभ्रजः (*giribhrajaḥ*)—falling from the cloud
- ऊर्मयः (*ūrmayaḥ*)—the flood of rain-water
- मदंतः न (*madaṃtaḥ na*)—as it makes a noise
- अर्काः (*arkāḥ*)—the worshippers, the praisers
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- अभ्यनावन् (*abhyanāvan*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As farmers, guardians of the crops, make a noise when they sprinkle water and drive birds away, as the cloud thunders again and again, and as the flood of rain-water falling from the cloud makes a noise, so the worshippers, the praisers, praise Bṛhaspati.

##### English translation
Like birds swimming in water when keeping watch, like the sound of
the roaring thunder-cloud, like sounding torrents falling from the clouds,
the worshippers glorify Brihaspati.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं गोभि॑रांगिर॒सो नक्ष॑माणो॒ भग॑ इ॒वेद॑य्॒रमणं॑  
> निनाय ।  
> जने॑ मि॒त्रो न दंप॑ती अनक्ति॒ बृह॑स्पते वा॒जया॒शूरि॑वा॒जौ ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । गोभिः । अंगिरसः । नक्षमाणः । भगः इव । इत् । अर्यमणं । निनाय ।  
> जने । मित्रः । न । दंपती इति दंपती । अनक्ति । बृहस्पते । वाजय । आशून् इव  
> आजौ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आंगिरसोऽंगिरसः पुत्रो नक्षमाणः स्वतेजसा व्याप्पुवन् भग इवेद्भगो
> देव इव स्थितो बृहस्पतिरेवार्यर्मणं स्तुतेः प्रेरकं स्तोतारं गोभिः सह सं
> निनाय । नयति । संयोजयति । मित्रो न मित्रो यथा जनपदे स्वरश्मीन्संयोजयति तद्वद्दंपती जायापती अनक्ति । संगमयति । स्वसामर्थ्यं तत्र स्थापयतीत्यर्थः । हे बृहस्पते आशून्वाप्तान्स्वरश्मीन्वाजय । तव स्तोतृषु गमय ।
> स्थापय । आशूनिव व्याप्तानश्वानाजौ संग्रामे योद्धारो यथा संगमयंति
> तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Āṅgirasa, the son of Aṅgiras, pervading (नक्षमाणः (*nakṣamāṇaḥ*)) with his own brilliance, standing like the god Bhaga, Bṛhaspati himself, unites (सं निनाय (*saṃ nināya*): leads, joins) Aryaman, the impeller of praise, the singer, with cows. As Mitra unites his own rays in the realm, so he unites (अनक्ति (*anakti*)) husband and wife (दंपती (*daṃpatī*)); that is, he places his own power there. O Bṛhaspati, send (वाजय (*vājaya*)) your pervading rays to your worshippers and place them there, as warriors in battle (आजौ (*ājau*)) bring together swift horses.

### Printed p. 577

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नक्षमाणः (*nakṣamāṇaḥ*)—he who pervades with his own radiance
- भग इवेत् (*bhaga ivet*)—he who shines like the god Bhaga
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—the son of Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati
- आर्यमणं (*āryamaṇaṃ*)—the praiser, the impeller of praise
- गोभिः (सह) (*gobhiḥ (saha)*)—with cows
- सं निनाय (*saṃ nināya*)—joins
- जने (*jane*)—among all
- मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—as the Sun-god brings together his rays
- दंपती (*daṃpatī*)—husband and wife
- अनक्ति (*anakti*)—he joins together
- बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*)—O Bṛhaspati
- आजौ (*ājau*)—in battle
- आशूनिव (*āśūniva*)—as one brings horses together
- वाजय (*vājaya*)—send your rays to the praisers and join them to them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Bṛhaspati, who pervades everywhere by his radiance, shines like Bhaga and is the son of Aṅgiras, joins the praiser, the impeller of praise, with cows. As the Sun-god brings together his rays among all, he joins husband and wife together. O Bṛhaspati, as horses are brought together in battle, join your rays to the praisers.

##### English translation
The son of Angiras pervading him with his brightness, has, like
Bhaga, brought Aryaman to the cows; as Mitra (unites his radiance) with
the people, so has he united husband and wife, Brihaspati, send (your wide-
spread rays to your worshippers) ar (a warrior sends his) his horses to battle.

> बृह॒स्पतिः॒ पर्व॑तेभ्यो वि॒तूर्या॒ निर्गा ऊ॑पे॒ यव॑निव  ॒॑
> स्थिविभ्यः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> साधुऽआर्याः । अत्तिथिनीः । इषिराः । स्पार्हाः । सुवर्णाः । आनवद्यरूपाः ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । पर्वतेभ्यः । वृतूर्य । निः । गाः । ऊपे । यवंइव । स्थिविभ्यः ॥ ३ ॥

> एषणीयाः स्पार्हाः स्पृहणीयाः सुवर्णाः शोभनशुक्लादिवर्णोपेता अनवद्य-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

साध्वर्याः (*sādhvaryāḥ*) are the leaders (*netrīḥ*) of good, auspicious milks; अत्तिथिनीः (*attithinīḥ*) those that go constantly; इषिराः (*iṣirāḥ*) those to be sought; स्पार्हाः (*spārhāḥ*) those to be desired; सुवर्णाः (*suvarṇāḥ*) those endowed with beautiful colours, white and the like; अनवद्य (*anavadya*)-

### Printed p. 578

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रूपाः प्रशस्य रूपा एता गाः पर्वतेभ्यो वलसंबंधिभ्यो वितूर्य निर्गमय्योपे।
> देवसमीपे निर्वपति । प्रापयति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । यवमिव यथा यवं स्थिविभ्यः
> कुसिदेभ्य आदाय निर्वपति॥ डुवप् बीजसंताने । लिटि रूपं ॥ यद्वा। साधुनयनादि
> गुणयुक्ता गा अपः पर्वतेभ्यो मेघेभ्य आहृत्य सर्वत्र वर्षति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The cows are of excellent form, praised for it. Brihaspati draws them out from the mountains belonging to Vala and brings them to the gods' side. The example is barley, which a man takes from the granaries and pours out. Alternatively: the cows (the waters), endowed with good leading and other qualities, he fetches from the mountains, that is, the clouds, and rains everywhere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्थि विभ्यः (*sthi vibhyaḥ*)—from the granaries
- यवमिव (*yavamiva*)—as barley grain is brought, filled up
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Brihaspati
- साध्वराः (*sādhvarāḥ*)—those that give beneficial milk
- अतिथिनीः (*atithinīḥ*)—those of continuous movement
- इषिरः (*iṣiraḥ*)—those to be sought
- स्पार्हाः (*spārhāḥ*)—desired
- सुवर्णाः (*suvarṇāḥ*)—those of excellent colour
- अनवद्यरूपाः (*anavadyarūpāḥ*)—those of praised form
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—cows
- पर्वतेभ्यः (*parvatebhyaḥ*)—from the mountains in which Vala had hidden them
- वितूर्‍य (*vitūrya*)—bringing out
- निः ऊपे (*niḥ ūpe*)—leads them to the gods' side

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As barley grain is filled up from the granaries and brought out, Brihaspati brings out the cows, the givers of beneficial milk, of continuous movement, to be sought, desired, of excellent colour and of praised form, from the mountains where Vala is hidden, and leads them to the gods' side.

##### English translation
Brihaspati brings to (the gods), after extricating them from the mountains, the cows that are the yielders of pure (milk), ever in motion, the objects of search and of desire, well-coloured and of unexceptionable form, (as men bring) barley from the granaries.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒प्रु॒षा॒यन्मधु॑न ऋ॒तस्य॒ योनि॑मवक्षि॒पन्न॒र्क उ॒ल्कामि॑व॒ द्योः ।  
> बृह॒स्पति॑रु॒द्धर॒न्नश्म॑नो॒ गा भूम्या॑ उ॒द्वेव॒ वि त्वचं॑ बिभेद ॥४॥

### Printed p. 579

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मधुनोदकेनाप्रुषायन् पृथिवीमाभिमुख्येन सिंचन्॥ प्रुष प्लुष स्नेहनसेचनपूरणेषु। व्यत्ययेन विकरणस्य शायजादेशः॥ ऋतस्कोदकस्य योनिं मेघमवक्षिपन् वृष्ट्यर्थमवकिरन्नर्कोऽर्चनीयो बृहस्पतिर्द्योर्दुलोकादुल्क्यामिमिवोल्कां यथोद्धरति तद्वदश्मनः शिलोच्चयाद्वलेनाधिष्ठिताद्दाः पणिभिरपहृतान्वशूनुद्धरन्नूर्ध्व० गमयन्भूम्यास्त्वचं तेषां शफैर्वि बिभेद ! विभिन्नामकार्षित् । सर्वत्र गा वितता अकार्षिदित्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । उद्भव यथा
> वृष्टु दकेन पर्जन्यो भूमित्वचं विभिनत्ति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Brihaspati, the adorable, sprinkling the earth with मधुना (*madhunā*), that is, water, directing it towards the earth, and scattering the cloud, the source of the water, for the sake of rain, draws up from the rock (the mass of stone held by Vala) the cattle carried off by the Paṇis, bringing them upward, as one draws out a meteor from the sky. With their hoofs he split the skin of the earth; that is, he made the cattle spread everywhere. The example: as Parjanya splits the skin of the earth with the water of rain, so he does.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मधुना (*madhunā*)—with water
- आ प्रुषायन् (*ā pruṣāyan*)—making the earth wet
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—the source, the cloud
- अवक्षिपन् (*avakṣipan*)—scattering for rain
- अर्कः (*arkaḥ*)—the adorable
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Brihaspati
- द्योः (*dyoḥ*)—from the sky
- उल्कामिव (*ulkāmiva*)—as one brings a meteor out
- अश्मनः (*aśmanaḥ*)—from the mountain
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—cows
- उद्धरन् (*uddharan*)—bringing out
- उद्वेव (*udveva*)—as Parjanya makes the regions of the earth into hollows and pits by rain
- भूम्याः (*bhūmyāḥ*)—of the earth
- त्वचं (*tvacaṃ*)—the upper part
- वि बिभेद (*vi bibheda*)—makes it split with hoofs

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The adorable Brihaspati, making the earth wet with water, scattering for rain the cloud that is the source of the water, bringing the cows out of the mountain as one brings a meteor out of the sky, makes the upper part of the earth split with the hoofs of the cows, as Parjanya pours rain and splits the regions of the earth.

##### English translation
Saturating (the earth) with water, scattering the receptacle of rain, the adorable Brihaspati, raising up the cattle from the rock as (he raises) a meteor from the sky, rent the skin of the earth (with the hoofs of the cattle) as (Parjanya rends it) with rain.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अप॒ ज्योति॑षा॒ तमो॑ अं॒तरि॑क्षादु॒द्नः शीपा॑लमिव॒ वात॑ आजत् ।  
> बृह॒स्पति॑रनु॒मृश्या॑ व॒लस्या॒भ्रमि॑न॒ वात॒ आ च॑क्र॒ आ गाः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 580

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आप । ज्योतिषा । तमः । अंतरिक्षात् । उद्यः । शीपालंऽइव । वातः । आजत् ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । अनुमृश्य । वलस्य । अभ्रंऽइव । वातः । आ । चक्रे । आ । गाः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स बृहस्पतिर्जोयतिषा तमसावृते पर्वतविवरे कृतेन सूर्येणांतरिक्षात्तत्तमोऽपाजत् । अपागमयत् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । उद्यः शीपालमिव । यथोदकाद्वातो वायुः शीपालं शैवालमपगमयति तद्वत् । ततः सोऽयमनुमृश्यात्र
> गावस्तिष्ठंतीति विचार्य निश्चित्य वलस्य स्वभूतस्य पर्वतस्यांतर्गता गा आ चक्रे । आ
> समंतादकार्षित् । कथमिव । अभ्रमिव यथा वायुरंतरिक्षस्थितमभ्रं मेघमाकिरति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Brihaspati, by the light of the sun made in the mountain cave enveloped in darkness, drove that darkness away from the atmosphere. The example: as the wind drives शीपालं (*śīpālaṃ*), moss, away from the water. Then, reflecting that the cows must be there, and deciding so, he brought together on all sides the cows lying inside the mountain that belonged to Vala. The example: as the wind scatters the cloud standing in the atmosphere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- उदृः (*udṛḥ*)—from water
- शीपालमिव (*śīpālamiva*)—as it separates moss
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Brihaspati
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—by his radiance
- अंतरिक्षात् (*aṃtarikṣāt*)—from the atmosphere
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—darkness
- अपाजत् (*apājat*)—scattered
- अभ्रमिव (*abhramiva*)—as it scatters a cloud
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—Brihaspati
- अनुमृश्य (*anumṛśya*)—guessing that the cows must be there
- वलस्य (*valasya*)—hidden in Vala's mountain
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- आ चक्रे (*ā cakre*)—brought out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the wind scatters moss from water, Brihaspati with his radiance scattered the darkness from the atmosphere. Guessing that the cows must be in Vala's mountain, he brought out the cows hidden there, as the wind scatters a cloud.

##### English translation
Brihaspati drove away the darkness from the firmament with light as the wind (blows) the shipala from the water, guessing (them to be there) he swept the Vala's cows together to himself as the wind (sweeps) the clouds.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒दा व॒लस्य॒ पीय॑तो॒ जसुं॒ भेद्बृह॒स्पति॑रग्नि॒तपो॑भिर॒र्कैः ।  
> द॒द्भिर्न जि॒ह्वा परि॑विष्ट॒माद॑दा॒विर्नि॒धीर॑कृणोदु॒स्रिया॑णां ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 581

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यदा । वलस्य । पीयतः । जसुं । भेत् । बृहस्पतिः । अग्नितपःभिः । अर्कैः ।  
> दत्थभिः । न । जिह्वा । परिऽविष्टं । आदत् । आविः । निधीन् । आकृणोत् । उस्रियाणां॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पीयतः । पीयतिर्हिंसाकर्मा। हिंसकस्य वलस्य जसुमायुधं यदा यस्मिन्काले भेत् भिनत्ति । केन साधनेन । अग्नि तपोभिरग्नि वत्तपनशीलैरर्कैरर्चनीयै रश्मिभिः
> अपि वा मंत्रैर्भिनत्ति । किंच दद्भिः ॥ पद्दन्नोमासित्यादिना दंतशब्दस्य दद्भावः ॥
> यथा दंतैः परिविष्टं भक्ष्यं जिह्वा भक्षयति तद्वत्स परिविष्टं पर्वते पणिभिः परिवृतं
> वलनामानं यदादत् अभक्षयत् अवधीत् तदानीं तैरपहृतानामुस्रियाणां गवां
> निधीनाविरकृणोत् । आविर्भूतमकरोत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पीयतः (*pīyataḥ*): the root पीयति (*pīyati*) means injuring; so, of the injuring Vala. When Brihaspati split Vala's weapon जसुं (*jasuṃ*): by what means? By rays, अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*), adorable and burning like fire (अग्नि तपोभिः (*agni tapobhiḥ*)); or he splits it with mantras. Further, दद्भिः (*dadbhiḥ*) (the word for tooth takes the form दत् (*dat*)). As the tongue consumes food surrounded by the teeth, so, when he consumed (killed) the one named Vala, surrounded by the Paṇis in the mountain, then he made manifest the treasures of the cows, उस्रियाणां (*usriyāṇāṃ*), carried off by them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दद्भिः (*dadbhiḥ*)—the food lying between the teeth
- जिह्वा आदत् न (*jihvā ādat na*)—as the tongue tastes
- पीयतः (*pīyataḥ*)—of the injurer
- वलस्य (*valasya*)—of the Asura named Vala
- परिविष्टं (*pariviṣṭaṃ*)—covered by the weapons of other Asuras
- जसुं (*jasuṃ*)—the weapon (of Vala)
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- अग्नि तपोभिः (*agni tapobhiḥ*)—burning like fire
- अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—with rays, adorable
- बृहस्पतिः भेत् (*bṛhaspatiḥ bhet*)—Brihaspati destroyed, then
- उस्त्रियाणां (*ustriyāṇāṃ*)—of the cows
- निधीन् (*nidhīn*)—the herds
- आविरकृणोत् (*āvirakṛṇot*)—made visible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the tongue tastes food enclosed by the teeth, when Brihaspati destroyed, with rays burning like fire and adorable, the weapon of the injuring Asura Vala, which was enclosed by the weapons of other Asuras, then he made the herds of cows visible.

##### English translation
When Brihaspati demolished with rays burning like fire the weapon of the malignant Vala, he devoured him (encompassed by his followers) as the tongue (consumes) that which is encompassed by the teeth; he made manifest the hiding-place of the cows.

> बृह॒स्पति॒रम॑त॒ हि त्यदा॑सां॒ नाम॑ स्व॒रीणां॒ सद॑ने॒ गुहा॒ यत् ।

### Printed p. 582

> आंडेव भित्वा शकुनस्य गर्भमुदुस्रियाः पर्वतस्य त्मनाजत् ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बृहस्पतिः । अमत । हि । त्यत् । आसां । नाम । स्वरीणां । सदने । गुहा । यत् ।  
> आंडाऽइव । भित्ता । शकुनस्य । गर्भं । उत् । उस्रियाः । पर्वतस्य । त्मना । आजत् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहस्पतिर्गुहा गुहायां सदने स्थाने स्वरीणां शब्दायमानानामासां
> गवां त्यत्तत्पसिद्धं नाम नामधेयं यद्यदामत हि ज्ञातवान्खलु ॥ मनु अवबोधने। लुजि तनादिभ्यस्तथासोः । पा. २-४-७९ । इति सिचो लुक् ॥ तदानीं पर्वतस्यांतःस्थिता उस्रिया गास्त्मनात्मनैवासहायेन पर्वतं भित्तोदाजत् । उदगमयत् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । आंडेव यथा शकुनस्य पक्षिण आंडानि भित्वा तत्र स्थितं गर्भमुद्गमयति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When Brihaspati knew गुहा (*guhā*), in the cave, in the place, that well-known name of these lowing cows, then the cows (उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*)) standing inside the mountain he brought out by himself, without help, splitting the mountain. The example: as one splits the eggs of a bird and brings out the embryo lying within.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गुहा (*guhā*)—of the mountain cave
- सदने (*sadane*)—in the place
- स्वरीणां (*svarīṇāṃ*)—that make sound
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of these cows
- त्यत् (*tyat*)—the well-known
- नाम (*nāma*)—name
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Brihaspati
- अमत हि (*amata hi*)—knew; then
- शकुनस्य (*śakunasya*)—of the bird
- आंडेव गर्भं (*āṃḍeva garbhaṃ*)—as one breaks an egg and brings out the substance within
- पर्वतस्य (*parvatasya*)—from the mountain
- उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*)—the cows
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—without the help of others
- भित्वा (*bhitvā*)—breaking (the rocks)
- उदाजत् (*udājat*)—brought out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Brihaspati knew the well-known name of the cows that were hidden in the mountain cave and making sound, then, as one breaks a bird's egg and brings out the substance within, he broke the rocks of the mountain and by himself, without the help of others, brought out the cows that were inside.

##### English translation
When Brihaspati had discovered that name of the lowing cows in their place in the cave; by his own strength he extricated the cattle from the rock as (breaking) the eggs of a bird (one extricates) the embryo.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अश्नापि॑नद्धं॒ मधु॒ पर्य॑पश्य॒न्मत्स्यं॒ न दी॒न उ॒दनि॑ क्षि॒यंतं॑ ।  
> निष्टज्ज॑भार चम॒सं न वृ॒क्षाद्बृह॒स्पति॑र्विर॒वेणा॑ वि॒कृत्य॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्ना । अपिनद्धं । मधु । परि । अपश्यत् । मत्स्यं । न दीने । उदनि । क्षियंतं ।  
> निः । तत् । जभार । चमसं । न । वृक्षात् । बृहस्पतिः । विरवेण । विकृत्य ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहस्पतिरश्नात्मना व्याप्या शिलयापिनद्धं पिहितं मधु गोलक्षणं पर्यपश्यत् । परितोऽद्राक्षीत् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । मत्स्यं न यथा दीने शुष्क उदनि ॥
> उदकशब्दस्योदन्नादेशः । उदके क्षियंतं निदसंतं मत्स्यं यथा पश्यति तद्वत् ॥
> दृष्ट्वा च तद्दोलक्षणं मधु विरवेण विविधेन शब्देन विकृत्य वलं छित्वा निर्जभार ।
> कथमिव । चमसं न । चमंति भक्षयंत्यत्रेति चमसः सोमपात्रं । तं यथा वृक्षान्निर्हरति तद्वत् ॥ हरतेर्लिटि रूपं । हृग्रहोर्भः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Bṛhaspati saw all round मधु (*madhu*), that is, the cows, covered by a pervading rock (अश्ना (*aśnā*)). The example: as one sees a fish living in a dried-up pool. Having seen it, he split Vala with a varied sound (विरवेण (*viraveṇa*)) and drew out that cow-form honey. The example: चमसं न (*camasaṃ na*); चमसः (*camasaḥ*) is the Soma vessel, in which they drink; as one takes it out of a tree.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दीने उदनि (*dīne udani*)—in a pool of dried-up water
- क्षियंतं (*kṣiyaṃtaṃ*)—living
- मत्स्यं न (*matsyaṃ na*)—like a fish
- अश्ना (*aśnā*)—by the rock spread all round
- आपिनद्धं (*āpinaddhaṃ*)—covered
- मधु (*madhu*)—the cow
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- पर्यपश्यत् (*paryapaśyat*)—saw
- वृक्षात् (*vṛkṣāt*)—cutting a tree, from it
- चमसं न (*camasaṃ na*)—as one prepares a Camasa vessel
- विरवेण (*viraveṇa*)—with his own sound
- विकृत्य (*vikṛtya*)—splitting Vala
- तत् (*tat*)—that honey in cow-form
- निर्जभार (*nirjabhāra*)—brought out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As one easily sees a fish living in a pool of dried-up water, Bṛhaspati saw the cow covered all round by rock. As one cuts a tree and prepares a Camasa vessel from it, he split Vala with his roaring sound and brought out the honey in cow-form.

##### English translation
Bṛhaspati looked round upon the cows shut up in the cave like fish in a dried-up pool, he seized Vala with a shout, cutting him off like a bowl from a tree.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The meaning Sāyaṇa has given for this Ṛk differs from the meaning Yāska has given. Explaining the etymology of the word Bṛhaspati, Yāska says: बृहस्पतिर्बृहतः पाता वा पालयिता वा (*bṛhaspatirbṛhataḥ pātā vā pālayitā vā*). Of him there is this Ṛk. अश्नापिनद्धं मधु पर्यपश्यन्मत्स्यं न दीन उदनि क्षियंतं । निष्कज्जभार चमसं न वृक्षा (*aśnāpinaddhaṃ madhu paryapaśyanmatsyaṃ na dīna udani kṣiyaṃtaṃ | niṣkajjabhāra camasaṃ na vṛkṣā*)-

### Printed p. 584

द्बृहस्पतिर्विरवेणा विकृत्य ॥ अशनवता मेघेनापिनद्धं मधु पर्यपश्यन्मत्स्यमिव दीन उदके निवसंतं निर्जहार तच्चमसमिव वृक्षात् । चमसः कस्मात् चमंत्यस्मिन्निति । बृहस्पतिर्विरवेण शब्देन विकृत्य ॥ (*dbṛhaspatirviraveṇā vikṛtya ‖ aśanavatā meghenāpinaddhaṃ madhu paryapaśyanmatsyamiva dīna udake nivasaṃtaṃ nirjahāra taccamasamiva vṛkṣāt | camasaḥ kasmāt camaṃtyasminniti | bṛhaspatirviraveṇa śabdena vikṛtya ‖*) (Ni. 10-12) **NOTE**

That is: because he protects this vast world, or the water, he is called Bṛhaspati. The explanation of the Ṛk "अश्नापिनद्धं (*aśnāpinaddhaṃ*)", which describes his deed, is as follows. Bṛhaspati saw the water (madhu) that was bound (within or in the middle of) this all-pervading cloud, that is, covered so that no one could see it. He saw it as easily as one can see a fish in shallow water; he saw the water in the middle of the cloud. And as one fashions a cup (camasa) from a tree and brings it, so he brought the water that was in the middle of the cloud down to the earth with a terrible sound (a roar, or mantras recited in a loud voice); that is, he made it fall as rain. If it is asked what "camasa" means here: the word camasa is formed from the root cam, "to eat". Because Soma juice is eaten, that is, drunk, from this cup, it has come to be called camasa. This is the meaning of the etymology.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोषाम॑विंद॒त्सः स्व१॒॑गःसो अ॒ग्निं सो अ॒केण॒ वि ब॑बाधे॒ तमां॑सि।  
> बृह॒स्पति॒र्गोव॑पुषो व॒लस्य॒ निर्म॒ज्ञानं॒ न पर्व॑णो जभार ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । उषां । अविंदत् । सः । स्वंरिति स्वः । सः । अग्निं । सः । अर्केण । वि । बबाधे ।  
> तमांसि ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । गोऽवपुषः । वलस्य । निः । मज्जनं । न । पर्वणः । जभार ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स बृहस्वतिस्तत्र पर्वतविवरे गवां दर्शनायोषामुषसमविंदत् । अलभत ।
> स एव स्वरादित्यं सोग्निं लब्ध्वार्केणार्चनीयेन तेजसा तमांसि वि बबाधे ।
> अत्यर्थं बाधितवान् । ततः स गोवपुषो गोरूपशरीरस्य पशुभिः परिवृतस्य वलस्य
> पर्वणः पर्वतात्ता गा निर्जभार । बलेन निर्जहार । बलवादाहरणे दृष्टांतः ।
> मज्ञानं न पर्वणः अस्नो मज्ञानं यथातिक्लेशेन निर्हरंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Bṛhaspati, in that cavity of the mountain, found Uṣas, the dawn, so that the cows might be seen. Having obtained also Svar, the sun, and Agni, he drove the darknesses away with worshipful radiance (arka), hindering them utterly. Then he carried those cows out by force from the mountain of Vala, whose body is of cow-form and who is surrounded by cattle. The illustration for the forcible carrying off: as men with great toil extract the marrow of a bone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः बृहस्पतिः (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*)—that Bṛhaspati
- उषां (*uṣāṃ*)—Uṣas
- अविंदत् (*aviṃdat*)—obtained
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the sun
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni, having obtained
- अर्कॆण (*arkèṇa*)—with worshipful radiance
- तमांसि (*tamāṃsi*)—the darknesses
- वि बबाधे (*vi babādhe*)—destroyed
- पर्वणः (*parvaṇaḥ*)—by the entry into the inside of the bones
- मज्जनं न (*majjanaṃ na*)—as the fat is made to come out
- गोवपुषः (*govapuṣaḥ*)—of him pervaded by a body of cow-form
- वलस्य (*valasya*)—of Vala
- पर्वणः (*parvaṇaḥ*)—from the mountain
- निर्जभार (*nirjabhāra*)—made the cows come out with toil

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To help in seeing the cows, Bṛhaspati obtained Uṣas, the sun and Agni, and with their worshipful radiance destroyed the darknesses. As fat is made, with difficulty, to come out from the inside of the bones, so he made the cows come out with toil from the mountain of Vala, who was pervaded by a body of cow-form.

##### English translation
Brihaspati found the dawn, the sun, Agni; he dispersed the gloom with light; he seized (the cattle from the rock) of Vala surrounded by the cows as (one extracts) marrow from a bone.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As lotus leaves are plundered by frost, so the desirable cow-wealth was plundered by Vala. Then, because Bṛhaspati had come in search of the cows, Vala showed favour: he gave those plundered cows back to him. And Bṛhaspati did there a deed that cannot be imitated and cannot be repeated, that is, one done in such a way that it need not be done again afterwards.

### Printed p. 586

> णीयं न भवति यथा पुनरकरणीयं तथाकार्षिदिर्थः । किं तदिति आह । सूर्यामासा सूर्यचंद्रमसौ मिथः परस्परमहोरात्रयोरुच्चरात उच्चरत इति यात्
> तच्चकार ॥ यादिति दीर्घश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

What was that deed? Sun and moon move up in turn, as day and night: that is what he did.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पर्णा (*parṇā*)—the leaves of a tree
- हिमेव मुषिता (*himeva muṣitā*)—as they are carried off by frost
- बृहस्पतिना (*bṛhaspatinā*)—by Bṛhaspati
- वनानि (*vanāni*)—the attractive cows were carried off (by Vala)
- बृहस्पतिना (*bṛhaspatinā*)—as soon as Bṛhaspati came
- वलः (*valaḥ*)—Vala
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—those cows
- अकृपयत् (*akṛpayat*)—handed over to him
- यात् (*yāt*)—by whose power
- सूर्यमासा (*sūryamāsā*)—sun and moon
- मिथः (*mithaḥ*)—alternately
- उच्चरातः (*uccarātaḥ*)—move
- अननुकृत्यं (*ananukṛtyaṃ*)—not imitated by another
- अपुनः (*apunaḥ*)—that which cannot be done again, that deed
- चकार (*cakāra*)—accomplished

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the leaves of a tree are carried off by frost, so the attractive cows were carried off (by Vala) by Bṛhaspati. As soon as Bṛhaspati came, Vala handed those cows over to him. Bṛhaspati has accomplished a work that cannot be imitated by another and cannot be done again, by whose power sun and moon have come to move in turn.

##### English translation
As the trees (bemoan) their leaves carried off by the winter, so Vala bemoaned his cows (carried off) by Brihaspati; he did that which cannot be imitated, which cannot be repeated, whereby sun and moon mutually rise (day and night).

> अभितोऽदीपयन् ॥ पिश आवयवे । अयं दीपनायां वर्तते ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> श्यावं न यथा श्याववर्णमश्वं कृशनेभिः सौवर्णैराभरणैरलंकुर्वंति तद्वत् । तथा
> रात्र्यां तमो निहितवंतः । किंचाहन्न ह्नि ज्योतिरादित्याख्यमदधुः ॥ अदधुरित्युत्तरवाक्येन संबंधः करणीयः । अन्यथा स्वरो न घटीत । अत्र तु वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥ यदा बृहस्पतिरद्रिं वलेनाधिष्ठितं शिलोच्चयं भिनत् अभिनत् विभिद्य च तत्र
> स्थितान्गाः पशून्विदत् अविदत् अलभत ॥ विदेर्लुजि ल्बुद्धित्वादज् ॥ तदा देवा एवमकार्षुरित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Fathers, the protecting gods, adorned the heaven all around with the constellations beginning with Aśvinī; the root पिश (*piśa*) is used here in the sense of illuminating. The illustration: as men decorate a brown horse with golden ornaments. Likewise they placed darkness in the night, and in the day they placed the light called the sun. (The word "placed" is to be connected with the following sentence.) When Bṛhaspati split the rocky mass held by Vala and found the cattle that stood there, then the gods acted in this way.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्यावं (*śyāvaṃ*)—golden-brown
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—horse
- कृशनेभिः न (*kṛśanebhiḥ na*)—as one decorates with golden ornaments
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—the gods, protectors of the world
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heavenly world
- नक्षत्रेभिः (*nakṣatrebhiḥ*)—with the constellations beginning with Aśvinī
- अभ्यपिंशन् (*abhyapiṃśan*)—have decorated
- रात्र्यां (*rātryāṃ*)—in the night
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—have established thick darkness
- अहन् (*ahan*)—in the day
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—light
- अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—have established
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- आद्रिं (*ādriṃ*)—the mountain
- भिनत् (*bhinat*)—split
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cattle
- विदत् (*vidat*)—obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a golden-brown horse is decorated with golden ornaments, so the gods, protectors of the world, have decorated the heavenly world with the constellations beginning with Aśvinī. They have established darkness in the night and light in the day. With the help of this light Bṛhaspati split the mountain and obtained the cattle.

##### English translation
The protecting (deities) have decorated the heaven with constellations as (men decorate) a brown horse with golden trappings: they established darkness in the night and light in the day; Brihaspati fractured the rock and recovered the cows.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दम॑कर्म॒ नमो॑ अभ्रि॒याय॒ यः पू॒र्वीरन्वा॒नोन॑वीति ।  
> बृह॒स्पतिः॒ स हि गोभिः॒ सो अश्वैः॒ स वी॒रेभिः॒ स नृभि॑नो॒ ॑ 
> वयो धात् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । अकर्म । नमः । अभ्रियाय । यः । पूर्वीः । अनु । आनोनवीति ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । सः । हि । गोभिः । सः । अश्वैः । सः । वीरेभिः । सः । नृभिः । नः । वयः ।  
> धात् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभ्रियायाभ्रेषु भवायांतरिक्ष्याय मध्यमाय बृहस्पतय इदमुक्तं नमः
> स्तोत्रमकर्म । वयमकार्ष्म । यो बृहस्पतिः पूर्विर्बह्वीर्युचोऽन्वनुक्रमेणानोनवीति अत्यर्थमाभिमुख्येन ब्रवीति स बृहस्पतिरेव गोभिरश्वैश्च युक्तं
> वीरेभिः पुत्रैर्नृभिर्भृत्यादिभिश्च सहितं वयोऽन्नं नोऽस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यो धात् ।
> दधातु । प्रयच्छतु । तच्छब्दावृत्तिरादरार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To Bṛhaspati, the one "of the clouds", that is, born in the clouds, belonging to the atmosphere, the middle region, we have made this homage, this praise. The Bṛhaspati who recites many Ṛks in order, vigorously and facing us, may that same Bṛhaspati give to us, the praisers, food together with cows and horses, together with sons (vīras) and with men, that is, servants and the like. The repetition of the word तच्छब्द (*tacchabda*) ("that") is for respect.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अभ्रियाय (*abhriyāya*)—addressed to Bṛhaspati who dwells in the atmosphere
- इदं नमः (*idaṃ namaḥ*)—this praise
- अकर्म (*akarma*)—we offer
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Bṛhaspati who
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—many mantras
- अनु (*anu*)—in order
- आनोनवीति (*ānonavīti*)—recites
- सः बृहस्पतिः (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*)—that same Bṛhaspati
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with cows
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with horses
- वीरेभिः (*vīrebhiḥ*)—with heroic sons
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—with servants and the like
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- धात् (*dhāt*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We offer this praise addressed to Bṛhaspati who dwells in the atmosphere. May that Bṛhaspati who recites many mantras in order give us food together with cows, with horses, with heroic sons and with servants and the like.

##### English translation
We have offered this homage to Brihaspati, who lives in mid-heaven, who recites in order many (sacred stanzas); may he bestow upon us food, with cows, with horses, with sons, with dependants.

## Sūkta 69 (Maṇḍala 10)

> षष्ठेऽनुवाके षोडश सूक्तानि। भद्रा इति द्वादशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं वध्र्यश्वपुत्रस्य सुमित्रस्यार्षं । आदितो द्वे जगत्यावथ दश त्रिष्टुभः । अग्निर्देवता । तथा
> चानुक्रम्यते ॥ भद्राः सुमित्रो वाध्र्यश्व आग्नेयं द्विजगत्यादीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the sixth anuvāka there are sixteen sūktas. The first, "भद्राः (*bhadrāḥ*)", of twelve Ṛks, has as seer Sumitra, son of Vadhryaśva; its first two Ṛks are in Jagatī and the following ten in Triṣṭubh; the deity is Agni. So the Anukramaṇī says: भद्राः सुमित्रो वाध्र्यश्व आग्नेयं द्विजगत्यादीति (*bhadrāḥ sumitro vādhryaśva āgneyaṃ dvijagatyādīti*). The viniyoga has been stated already.

### Printed p. 589

##### Anuvāda

In the sixth anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā there are sixteen sūktas. Of these the sūkta "भद्रा अग्नेः (*bhadrā agneḥ*)" is the first; it has twelve Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Sumitra, the son of Vadhraśva. The first two Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Jagatī metre; the following ten Ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre; Agni is the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: Bhadrāḥ Sumitro Vādhraśva Āgneyaṃ dvijagatyādi. The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 69
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 69.
Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 2; Varga 19, 20.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12.
Ṛṣi: Sāmitra Vādhraśva.
Devatā: Agni.
Chandas: 1, 2 Jagatī; 3-12 Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒द्रा अ॒ग्नेर्व॑ध्र॒श्वस्य॑ सं॒दृशो॑ वा॒मी प्रणी॑तिः सु॒रणा॒ उपे॑तयः ।  
> यदीं॑ सुमि॒त्रा विशो॒ अग्र॑ इं॒धते॑ घृ॒तेनाहु॑तो जरते॒  ॑
> दविद्युतत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भद्राः । अग्नेः । वध्रिऽश्वस्य । संऽदृशः । वामी । प्रनीतिः । सुरणाः । उपइतयः॥  
> यत् । ईं । सुमित्राः । विशः । अग्रे । इंधते । घृतेन । आहुतः । जरते ।  
> दविद्युतत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्नेर्वक्ष्यमाणगुणस्य संदृशः संदृष्टयो वध्रश्वस्यैतन्नामकस्य मम॥
> पितुर्भद्राः कल्याणकारिण्यो भवंतु । यद्वा । वध्रश्वस्य वध्रश्वकुले जातस्याग्नेः
> संदृष्टयो भजनीया भवंतु । प्रणीतिस्तस्य प्रणयनं वामी कल्याणं च भवतु ।
> तथोपेतयो यज्ञं प्रत्युपगतयः सुरणाः शोभनरमणा भवंतु । सुमित्रा
> एतन्नामधेया विशोऽमी मनुष्या ईमेनमग्निमग्रे प्रथमं यद्यदेंधते

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the sights (saṃdṛśaḥ) of Agni, whose qualities will be told, be auspicious for my father, who bears the name Vadhryaśva. Or else: may the sights of Agni, born in the family of Vadhryaśva, be worthy of being served; may his leading forward (praṇīti) and his welfare be there; and may the approaches (upetayaḥ) to the sacrifice be of good delight. The men named Sumitra, who kindle this Agni first, whenever they kindle him.

### Printed p. 590

> हविर्भिर्दिर्पयंति तदा धृतेनाहुतो हविर्भिश्च दविद्युतद्भृशं द्योतमानः ॥
> दाधर्तिदर्धर्तित्यादिना निपातितः । सोग्निर्जरते । अस्माभिः स्तूयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes his gloss of the preceding verse. Agni, fed with oblations and with ghee, is "brilliantly blazing", shining intensely. The word जरते (*jarate*) is explained as "he is praised by us", the form being derived by the rule that treats it as an irregularly formed word.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- संदृशः (*saṃdṛśaḥ*)—the benevolent glances
- वध्र्यश्वस्य (*vadhryaśvasya*)—to my father named Vadhryaśva
- भद्राः (*bhadrāḥ*)—may they be beneficent
- प्रणीतिः (*praṇītiḥ*)—his excellent guidance
- वामी (*vāmī*)—may it be auspicious
- उपेतयः (*upetayaḥ*)—his approach towards the sacrifice
- सुरणाः (*suraṇāḥ*)—may it be favourable
- सुमित्राः (*sumitrāḥ*)—those named Sumitra
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—people
- ईं (*īṃ*)—Agni
- अग्रे (*agre*)—first
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- इंथते (*iṃthate*)—they cause to blaze, then
- घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)—with ghee
- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—honoured
- दविद्युतत् (*davidyutat*)—and shining, Agni
- जरते (*jarate*)—is praised by us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni's benevolent glances be beneficent to my father Vadhryaśva. May his excellent guidance be auspicious. May his approach towards the sacrifice be favourable. When the people named Sumitra first cause Agni to blaze, then Agni, honoured with ghee and shining, is praised by us.

##### English translation
May Agni's regards be benevolent to Vadhryashwa, may his guidance be auspicious, his approaches (to the sacrifice) favourable; when the Sumitra people first kindle Agni, then fed with butter and brilliantly blazing, he is glorified.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> घृ॒तम॒ग्नेर्व॑ध्र्य॒श्वस्य॒ वर्ध॑नं घृ॒तमन्नं॑ घृ॒तम्व॑स्य॒ मेद॑नं ।  
> घृ॒तेनाहु॑त उर्वि॒या वि प॑प्रथे॒ सूर्य॑ इव रोचते स॒र्पिरा॑सुतिः ॥ २ ॥

> मेदनं ।  
> घृतेन । आहुतः । उर्विया । वि । पप्रथे । सूर्यः इव । रोचते । सर्पि आसुतिः॥

### Printed p. 591

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वध्र्यश्वस्य संबंधिनोऽग्नेर्घृतं दीयमानं हनिर्वर्धनं भवतु । तथा
> घृतमन्नमदनीयं भवतु । तथास्याग्नेर्घृतमु घृतमेव मेदनं पुष्टिकरं भवतु।
> येनाग्निः पुष्टो भवति तन्नेदनं । तेन घृतेनाहुतोऽग्निरुर्वियोर्वत्यंतं वि
> पप्रथे । स्वतेजसा विप्रथितो भवति । तथा सर्पिरासुतिः सर्पिरासूयते यस्मिन्निति
> सोऽग्निः सूर्य इव रोचते । दीप्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ghee offered to Agni of Vadhryaśva is to be his augmenter; ghee is to be his food; ghee alone is his मेदनं (*medanaṃ*), the nourishing thing, that by which Agni becomes nourished. Fed with that ghee, Agni spreads out widely with his own radiance. And Agni, in whom the ghee is poured, shines like the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वध्र्यश्वस्य (*vadhryaśvasya*)—worshipped by Vadhryaśva
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)—the oblation
- वर्धनं (*vardhanaṃ*)—may it grow
- घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)—the oblation
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—may it be fit for his eating
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- घृतमु (*ghṛtamu*)—the oblation in the form of ghee itself
- मेदनं (*medanaṃ*)—may it be nourishing
- घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)—with ghee
- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—Agni honoured
- उर्विया (*urviyā*)—exceedingly
- वि पप्रथे (*vi paprathe*)—spreads out with his radiance
- सर्पिरासुतिः (*sarpirāsutiḥ*)—Agni praised with hymns
- सूर्य इव (*sūrya iva*)—like the sun
- रोचते (*rocate*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the oblation offered to Agni, who is worshipped by Vadhryaśva, grow. May the oblation be fit for his eating. May this oblation in the form of ghee be nourishing. Agni, worshipped with ghee, spreads out exceedingly with his radiance. Agni, praised with hymns, shines like the sun.

##### English translation
May ghi be the augmenter of the Agni of Vadhryashwa; may ghi be his food; may ghi be his nutriment; sacrificed to with ghi he expands excee- dingly; he shines like the sun, when the clarified butter is poured out for him.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्ते॒ मनु॒र्यदनी॑कं सुमि॒त्रः स॑मी॒धे अ॑ग्ने॒ तदि॒दं नवी॑यः।  
> स रे॒वच्छो॑च॒ स गिरो॑जुषस्व॒ स वाजं॑ दर्षि॒ स इ॒ह श्रवो॑ धाः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ते । मनुः । यत् । अनीकं । सुमित्रः । संईधे । अग्ने । तत् । इदं ।  
> नवीयः ।

### Printed p. 592

> सः । रेवत् । शोच । सः । गिरः । जुषस्व । सः । वाजं । दर्षि । सः । इह । श्रवः । धाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ते त्वदीयं यदनीकं रश्मिसंघं मनुरेतन्नामको यथा
> समीधे हविर्भिः सम्यग्दीपयति सुमित्र एतन्नामकोऽहं समीपे। सम्यग्दीपयामि॥
> इइंधी दीप्तौ । लिटींधिभवतिभ्यां चेति कित्वान्नलोपः ॥ तदिदं सोऽयं रश्मिसंघो नवीयो नवतरो भवतु । स त्वं रेवद्धनयुक्तं यथा भवति तथा शोच ।
> प्रज्वल । स एव त्वं गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतीर्जुषस्व । सेवस्व । स त्वं वाजं शत्रुबलं
> दर्षि । विदारय । तथेह मयि श्रवोऽन्नं धाः । धेहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, that host of your rays which Manu kindled, as I, Sumitra, also kindle it nearby, igniting it well with oblations: may this same host be newer. You, shine wealthily, that is, blaze so as to bring wealth. Accept our praises. Break the strength of the enemy. Place food in me here." He explains समीधे (*samīdhe*) from the root इइंधी (*iiṃdhī*) in the sense of kindling.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—your
- यत् अनेकं (*yat anekaṃ*)—which mass of flames

- सुमित्रः (*sumitraḥ*)—I, named Sumitra, whichever flames of yours I caused to blaze
- तदिदं (*tadidaṃ*)—that mass of your flames
- नवीयः (*navīyaḥ*)—may it attain a new form
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- रेवत् (*revat*)—so as to bestow wealth
- शोच (*śoca*)—shine
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—our praises
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—the strength of enemies
- दर्षि (*darṣi*)—destroy

- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, may that mass of your flames which Manu caused to blaze, and which I, named Sumitra, caused to blaze, attain a new form. Shine so as to bestow wealth. Accept our praises. Destroy the strength of enemies. Establish food in me.

##### English translation
May that your army of flame, Agni, which Manu, which Sumitra has kindled, be the newest; do you shine wealthily, do you grociously accept our praises; do you destroy the might (of our foes); do you grant us abundance.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं त्वा॒ पूर्व॑मीळि॒तो व॑ध्र्य॒श्वः स॑मी॒धे अ॑ग्ने॒ स इ॒दं जु॑षस्व ।  
> स नः॑ स्ति॒पा उ॒त भ॑वा तनू॒पा दा॒त्रं र॑क्षस्व॒ यदि॒दं ते॑ अ॒स्मे ॥४॥

### Printed p. 593

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । त्वा । पूर्वं । ईळितः । वध्रिऽअश्वः । संईधे । अग्ने । सः । इदं । जुषस्व ।  
> सः । नः । स्तिपाः । उत । भव । तनूपाः । दात्रं । रक्षस्व । यत् । इदं । ते । आस्मे इति ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ईळितः ॥ व्यत्ययेन कर्तरि क्तः ॥ स्तोता वध्यश्वो मम पिता पूर्वं पूर्वस्मिन्काले संजातं यं त्वा समीधे हविर्भिः सम्यगदीपयत् स त्वमिदानीं मया
> क्रियमाणमिदं स्तोत्रं जुषस्व । सेवस्व । यद्वा । वध्यश्वस्तस्य पुत्रोऽहं सम्यग्दीपितवानस्मि । स त्वं नोऽस्माकं स्तिपाः ॥ पृषोदरादिः ॥ पस्त्र्यं गृहं । तस्य रक्षको
> भव । यद्वा । उपस्थिताइष्टोमादीन्यागान्पालयतीति स्तिपाः । अस्मदीयानां
> यज्ञानां पालयिता भव । उतापि च तनूपाः स्वांगानां रक्षको भव । किंच दात्रं
> तद्धनं रक्षस्व यदिदं धनं ते तव स्वभूतेष्वस्मे अस्मासु तिष्ठति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ईळितः (*īḷitaḥ*) has the suffix kta in the active sense by variation. My father Vadhryaśva, the praiser, in former time kindled you well with oblations; you now accept this hymn made by me. Or else: I, his son, have kindled you well. You, be our स्तिपाः (*stipāḥ*), an irregular form: पस्त्र्यं (*pastryaṃ*) is the house, so be its protector. Or else: स्तिपाः (*stipāḥ*) is one who guards the sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma that are at hand; so be the guardian of our sacrifices. And be the protector of our own bodies. Further, guard that wealth which stands with us, belonging to you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ईळितः (*īḷitaḥ*)—the praiser
- वध्र्यश्वः (*vadhryaśvaḥ*)—Vadhryaśva
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—formerly
- यं त्वा (*yaṃ tvā*)—you whom
- समीधे (*samīdhe*)—he caused to blaze with oblations
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same you
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this hymn of mine
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- स्तिपाः (*stipāḥ*)—as house-protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- उत (*uta*)—and
- तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)—be the protector of our bodies
- यदिदं (*yadidaṃ*)—which wealth
- ते (*te*)—your
- अस्मे (*asme*)—is established among us, your worshippers
- दात्रं (*dātraṃ*)—such wealth
- रक्षस्व (*rakṣasva*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you whom the praiser Vadhryaśva formerly caused to blaze with oblations, that same you accept this hymn of mine. Be the protector of our house. Be also the protector of our bodies. Protect the wealth given by you and established among us.

##### English translation
Do you, Agni, whom Vadhryshwa propitiating you formerly kindled, accept this; be the protector of our sacrifices, be the protector of our bodies; preserve this wealth which has been given to us by you.
