> शूरःइव । धृष्णुः । च्यवनः । सुमित्रः । प्र । नु । वोचं । वाध्रिअश्वस्य । नाम ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वाध्र्यश्व वध्यश्वकुले जाताग्ने द्युम्नी । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो
> वान्नं ना । तद्वान्भव । उतापि च गोपा गोपायिता भव । किंच त्वा त्वां कश्चिदसि
> मा तारीत् । मा हिनस्तु । यतो जनानां शत्रूणामभिमातिरभिभवनशीलमानयुक्तोऽभिभविता भवसि । किंच शूर इव बलवानिव धृष्णुः शत्रुधर्षणशीलः तस्माच्च्यवनस्तेषां च्यावयिता भवसि । अथ वाध्र्यश्वस्याग्नेस्तव नामाग्निर्जातवेदा
> वैश्वानर इत्यादीनि नामानि नु क्षिप्रं सुमित्रोऽहं प्र वोचं । प्रब्रवीमि । तस्मान्मेऽन्नादियुक्तो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, born in the family of Vadhryaśva, be द्युम्नी (*dyumnī*); द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*) from the root द्योतते (*dyotate*) means fame or food, so be possessed of it. Be also our protector. Let no one harm you, for you are the overcomer of the enemies, one who overpowers with pride. Like a hero, a strong one, you are bold against enemies and so their dislodger. Now I, Sumitra, quickly proclaim the names of you, Agni of Vadhryaśva: *agnirjātavedā vaiśvānara* and the like. Therefore be possessed of food for me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाध्र्यश्व (*vādhryaśva*)—O Agni, belonging to Vadhryaśva

- उत (*uta*)—and
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—be our protector
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मा तारीत् (*mā tārīt*)—let no one harm
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of all
- अभिमातिः (*abhimātiḥ*)—you are the one who brings defeat
- शूर इव (*śūra iva*)—like a hero
- धृष्णुः (*dhṛṣṇuḥ*)—you crush enemies
- च्यवनः (*cyavanaḥ*)—and are their destroyer
- सुमित्रः (*sumitraḥ*)—named Sumitra
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- वाध्र्यश्वस्य (*vādhryaśvasya*)—of you, belonging to Vadhryaśva
- नाम (*nāma*)—the names such as Vaiśvānara
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- प्र वोचं (*pra vocaṃ*)—I recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, belonging to Vadhryaśva, be possessed of food. Be our protector. Let no one harm you. You bring defeat to all. Like heroes you crush enemies and destroy them. I, named Sumitra, quickly recite your names, such as Vaiśvānara, you who belong to Vadhryaśva.

##### English translation
Kinsman of Vadhryashwa, be the possessor of food and our protector; let one assail you, (for you are) the overcomer of men; like a resolute warrior (you are) the overthrower (of enemies); I, Sumitra, celebrate the names of the kinsmen of Vadhryashwa,

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सम॒ज्र्या॑ पर्व॒त्या॒३॒॑शिवसू॑नि॒ दासा॑ वृ॒त्राण्यार्या॑ जिगेथ ।  
> शूर॑ इव धृ॒ष्णुश्च व॑नो॒ जना॑नां॒त्वम॑ग्ने पृतना॒यूर॒भि ष्याः॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । अज्र्या । पर्वत्या । वसूनि । दासा । वृत्राणि । आर्या । जिगेथ ।  
> शूरःइव । धृष्णुः । च्यवनः । जनानां । त्वं । अग्ने । पृतन्वायून् । अभि । स्याः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अज्रा । अजंति गच्छंतीत्यज्रयो जनाः । तेभ्यो हितानि पर्वत्या
> पर्वतभवानि वसूनि गवादिलक्षणानि सं जिगेथ । शत्रुभ्यः संजितवानसि । तथार्या बलवद्भिः कृतान्दासा दासैरसुरैः कृतान्वृत्राण्युपद्रवान्सं जिगेथ । तान्हतवानसीत्यर्थः ॥
> जि जये । लिटि रूपं ॥ शूर इव धृष्णुर्जनानां च्यवनस्त्वं पृतनायून्संग्रामकामानभि ष्याः । अभिभव ॥ पृतनायूनित्यत्र लोपाभावश्चांदसः । अश्वाघस्यादित्यात्वं
> विधीयमानमस्मादपि व्यत्ययेन भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, अज्रा (*ajrā*): those who go are *ajrayaḥ*, people. For them you have conquered the mountain-born riches पर्वत्या वसूनि (*parvatyā vasūni*), such as cattle, from the enemies. Likewise you have conquered the वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*), the afflictions, caused by the strong (आर्या (*āryā*)) and by the दासा (*dāsā*), the Asura servants; that is, you have slain them. जिगेथ (*jigetha*) is a perfect-tense form of the root जि (*ji*) "to conquer". Like a hero, bold, the dislodger of men, you overcome those who desire battle. The non-elision in पृतनायून् (*pṛtanāyūn*) is Vedic; the ending ā prescribed for अश्वाघस्य (*aśvāghasya*) occurs here too by variation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अज्रा (*ajrā*)—beneficial to men
- पर्वत्या (*parvatyā*)—and mountain-born
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—riches
- सं जिगेथ (*saṃ jigetha*)—you have wrested from enemies
- आर्या (*āryā*)—produced by Āryas
- दासा (*dāsā*)—and produced by Dāsas
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—all the afflictions
- (सं (*saṃ*)) जिगेथ (*jigetha*)—you have destroyed together
- शूर इव (*śūra iva*)—like a hero
- धृष्णुः (*dhṛṣṇuḥ*)—one who overpowers enemies
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of enemy people
- च्यवनः (*cyavanaḥ*)—and their destroyer
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- पृतनायून् (*pṛtanāyūn*)—enemy warriors
- अभि ष्याः (*abhi ṣyāḥ*)—you defeat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you have wrested from enemies the riches that are beneficial to men and mountain-born (or hidden in the mountain). You have destroyed together all the afflictions produced by Āryas and by Dāsas. You, who like a hero overpower enemies and destroy enemy people, defeat enemy warriors.

##### English translation
You have gained mountain-treasures beneficial to men, (you have defeated ihe hostilities) of strong men, Dasas and Vritras, like are solute

##### English translation
warrior, do you Agni, the overthrower (of enemies), overeome those who are desirous of battle.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दी॒र्घतं॑तुर्बृ॒हदु॑क्षा॒यम॒ग्निः स॒हस्र॑स्तरीः श॒तनी॑थ॒ ऋभ्वा॑ ।  
> द्यु॒मान् द्यु॒मत्तु॒ नृभि॑र्मृ॒ज्यमा॑नः सुमि॒त्रेषु॑ दीदयो  ॒॑
> देवयत्तु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दीर्घतंतुः । बृहत्उक्षा । अयं । अग्निः । सहस्रस्तरीः । शतनीथः । ऋभ्वा ।  
> द्युमान् । द्युमत्सु । नृभिः । मृज्यमानः । सुमित्रेषु । दीदयः । देवयत्सु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दीर्घतंतुः। यैर्यज्ञं संतनोति ते तंतवः स्तोत्रादयः । प्रभूतस्तुतिमान्बृहदुक्षा । उक्षा सेचको रश्मिः । प्रभूतरश्मियुक्तः सहस्रस्तरीर्हवीरूपबह्वाच्छादनः शतनीथ आहवनीयादिद्वारेण बहुविधनयन ऋभ्या महान्द्युमत्तु दीप्तिमत्तु मध्यॆ द्युमानतिशयेन दीप्तिमानयमग्निर्नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्यत्विग्निर्मृज्यमानोऽलंक्रियमाणो भवति ॥ मृजू शौचालंकारयोः ॥ सत्वं देवयत्तु देवान्कामयमानेषु सुमित्रेष्टस्मासु दीदयः । दीप्यस्व । दीदयतिर्दिप्तिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The "long-threaded" one: the threads are the stotras and the like, by which the sacrifice is stretched out; he has abundant praise. बृहदुक्षा (*bṛhadukṣā*): उक्षा (*ukṣā*) is the sprinkling ray, so he possesses many rays. सहस्रस्तरीः (*sahasrastarīḥ*): he has a thousandfold covering in the form of oblations. शतनीथः (*śatanīthaḥ*): he leads in many ways through the Āhavanīya and the other fires. ऋभ्वा (*ṛbhvā*): great. द्युमत्तु (*dyumattu*): among the radiant, this Agni is exceedingly radiant. He is adorned by the priests, the leaders of the rite; मृजू शौचालंकारयोः (*mṛjū śaucālaṃkārayoḥ*) (the root means cleansing and adorning). Such as you are, shine upon us, the Sumitras, who desire the gods; दीदयति (*dīdayati*) is a word for shining.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दीर्घतंतुः (*dīrghataṃtuḥ*)—one who has abundant praise
- बृहदुक्षा (*bṛhadukṣā*)—one who has abundant rays
- सहस्रस्तरीः (*sahasrastarīḥ*)—one who has many coverings in the form of oblations
- शतनीथः (*śatanīthaḥ*)—guide of many
- ऋभ्या (*ṛbhyā*)—the great one
- द्युमत्तु (*dyumattu*)—among the radiant
- द्युमान् (*dyumān*)—one of great brilliance
- अयं अग्निः (*ayaṃ agniḥ*)—this Agni
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- मृज्यमानः (*mṛjyamānaḥ*)—is adorned
- (O Agni) देवयत्तु (*devayattu*)—who are fond of the worship of the gods
- सुमित्रेषु (*sumitreṣu*)—among us who are called Sumitras
- दीदयः (*dīdayaḥ*)—shine exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who has abundant praise, abundant rays, many coverings in the form of oblations, who is the guide of many, the great one, of great brilliance among the radiant,

### Printed p. 597
is adorned by the priests. O Agni, shine exceedingly among us, the Sumitras, who are devoted to the worship of the gods.

##### English translation
This Agni to whom a long series (of sacrifices has been addressed), who is bright with many rays, covering thousands (in the form of ghi), the leader of hundreds (of burnt offerings), the mighty one, brilliant among the brilliant, (is) heing glorified by the priests ; shine (Agni) upon the devout Sumitras.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वे धे॒नुः सु॒दुघा॑ जातवेदोऽस॒श्चते॑व सम॒ना स॑ ब॒र्धुक् ।  
> त्वं नृभि॒र्दक्षि॑णावद्भिरग्ने सुमि॒त्रेभि॑रिध्यसे देव॒यद्भिः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वे इति । धेनुः । सुदुघा । जातवेदः । असश्चताइव । समना । सबःधुक् ।  
> त्वं । नृभिः । दक्षिणावत्भिः । अग्ने । सुमित्रेभिः । इध्यसे । देवयत्भिः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञाग्ने त्वे त्वयि सुदुघा सुष्टु पयसो दोग्नि
> काचिद्भोमसाधनभूता धेनुरस्ति । कीदृशी । असश्चतेव संगवर्जितेनेवैकत्र स्थित्यभावात्कुत्रापि न संयुक्तेनादित्येन समना संगता सबर्धुगमृतं दुहाना। गोरूपा
> माध्यमिका वाग्वैद्युते त्वय्यस्तीति भावः । तादृशस्त्वं नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्दक्षिणावद्भिर्युत्विग्भो देयत्वेन तद्वद्भिर्देवयद्भिर्देवकाम्यॆः सुमित्रेभिरस्माभिरिध्यसे ।
> हविर्भिर्दिर्प्यसे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, Agni of born wisdom, in you there is a cow that yields milk well, a means of the sacrifice. What kind? Like one free of attachment, since she does not stay in one place and is joined to nothing, she is united with the Āditya; she milks the सबर्धुग (*sabardhuga*) nectar. The meaning is that the cow in the form of the middle-realm Speech, belonging to lightning, is in you. Such as you are, you are kindled by us, the Sumitras, who desire the gods, with the priests, the leaders of the rite, who are endowed with the sacrificial fee (they having it to give). You are made to blaze with oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O one in the form of Jātavedas
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- असश्चतेव (*asaścateva*)—with the Āditya, who is ever moving (not staying fixed anywhere)
- समना (*samanā*)—united (and)
- सबर्धुक् (*sabardhuk*)—like the middle-realm goddess Speech who milks nectar
- त्वे (*tve*)—in you
- सुदुघा (*sudughā*)—who milks excellent milk
- धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*)—a cow is established
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दक्षिणावद्धिः (*dakṣiṇāvaddhiḥ*)—

### Printed p. 598
- by those who are endowed with the sacrificial fee
- देवयद्भिः (*devayadbhiḥ*)—devoted to the worship of the gods
- सुमित्रेभिः (*sumitrebhiḥ*)—called Sumitras
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- इध्यसे (*idhyase*)—you are kindled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, one in the form of Jātavedas, in you a cow that milks excellent milk is established, like the middle-realm goddess Speech who, joined to the Āditya, ever moving and fixed nowhere, milks nectar. You are kindled by the priests who are endowed with the sacrificial fee, devoted to the worship of the gods, and called Sumitras.

##### English translation
In you, Jatavedas, is the milch cow, easy to be milked, yielding ambrosia as it were inexhaustibly in battle, you are kindled, Agni, by the devout Sumitras who are entitled to the sacrificial donation.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वाश्चि॑त्ते अ॒मृता॑ जातवेदो महि॒मानं॑ वाध्र्यश्व॒ प्र  ॑
> वोचन् ।  
> यत्सं॒पृच्छं॒ मानु॑षी॒र्विश॒ आय॒न्त्वं नृभि॑रजय॒स्तावृ॑धेभिः॥९॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवाः । चित् । ते । अमृताः । जातवेदः । महिमानं । वाध्रिऽअश्व । प्र । वोचन् ।  
> यत् । संपृच्छं । मानुषीः । विशः । आयन् । त्वं । नृभिः । अजयः । त्वावृधेभिः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेदो हे वाध्यश्वाग्ने ते तव महिमानममृता देवाश्चिद्देवा अपि
> प्र वोचन् । प्रब्रुवंति। यद्यदा मानुषीर्मनुष्यसंबंधिन्यो विशः प्रजाः संपृच्छं
> देवैः सह को ना असुरान्हंतीत्येवमादिकं संप्रश्नमायन् प्राप्तवंतः तदा त्वं
> नृभिः सर्वस्य नेतृभिस्तावृधेभिस्त्वया वर्धितैर्देवैः सह कर्मविघ्नकारिणस्तनजयः ।
> जितवानसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, O Agni of Vadhryaśva, even the immortal gods proclaim your greatness. When the human tribes, the people connected with men, put the question (संपृच्छं (*saṃpṛcchaṃ*))—"Who, together with the gods, slays the Asuras?"—and the like, then you, with the leaders of all, with the gods who are strengthened by you, conquered those who obstruct the rite. अजयः (*ajayaḥ*): you have conquered.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाध्र्यश्व (*vādhryaśva*)—O one related to Vadhryaśva
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—your
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—greatness
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—deathless
- देवाश्चित् (*devāścit*)—even the gods

### Printed p. 599
- प्र वोचन् (*pra vocan*)—praise
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*)—belonging to the group of humans
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the people
- संपृच्छं (*saṃpṛcchaṃ*)—the question "Who slays the Asuras?"
- आयन् (*āyan*)—ask, then
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—with those who are guides
- त्वावृधेभिः (*tvāvṛdhebhiḥ*)—together with the gods who are nourished by you
- अजयः (*ajayaḥ*)—you conquer them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, related to Vadhryaśva, even the deathless gods praise your greatness. When we humans ask, "Who is the hero who will slay the Asuras?", then you, together with the gods who are guides and are nourished by you, conquer them.

##### English translation
The immortal gods have proclaimed your greatness, Jatavedas, Vadhryashwa (Agni); when human beings came to inquire (who would slay the Asuras), then you with (the gods), the leaders of all, fostered by you overcame (those who impeded the ceremony).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पि॒तेव॑ पु॒त्रम॑बिभरु॒पस्थे॒ त्वाम॑ग्ने वध्र्य॒श्वः स॑प॒र्यन् ।  
> जु॒षा॒णो अ॑स्य स॒मिधं॑ यविष्टो॒त पूर्वा॑ अवनो॒र्व्राध॑तश्चित् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जुषाणः । अस्य । संइथं । यविष्ठ । उत । पूर्वान् । अवनोः । प्राधतः । चित् ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वामुपस्थे पृथिव्या उपस्थान उत्तरवेद्यां सर्पयन् परिचर्याकर्मा परिचरन्वध्र्यश्वो मम पिताबिभः । धृतवान्। हविर्भिः पोषितवान्वा। कथमिव ।
> पितेव यथा पिता समीपे पुत्रं स्थापयति पोषयति वा ॥ डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः । लज्तिपि गुणे कृते हल्ब्यादिना तिपो लोपः ॥ हे यविष्ठ युवतमाग्ने उतापि चास्य वध्र्यश्वस्य पितुर्वा मम ना समिधं जुषाणः सेवमानः सन्
> पूर्वान्प्रत्नान्वाधतश्चिद्बाधकानपि शत्रूनवनोः । अवधीः ॥ वनतिर्हिंसायां भौवादिकः । व्यत्ययेनोप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, Vadhryaśva, serving you on the upastha (lap) of the earth, the Uttaravedi, bore you, or nourished you with oblations, as a father keeps his son near and nourishes him. The root डुभृञ् (*ḍubhṛñ*) means holding and nourishing. O Yaviṣṭha, youngest Agni, enjoying the fuel of this Vadhryaśva, or of my father, you have slain even the former, the obstructing enemies. The root वनति (*vanati*) is of the first class and means injuring.

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, Vadhryaśva, who worshipped you on the Uttaravedi, has nourished you with oblations and the like, as a father seats his child near him and nourishes him. O exceedingly young Agni, you who enjoy my oblations and the like have slain all enemies, those who were before and the injurers.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Agni, together with the priests of Vadhryaśva who have pressed the Soma (सुतसोमवद्भिः (*sutasomavadbhiḥ*): the suffix is anuvādaka, in the sense of "having"), has always conquered the enemies. Now he is addressed directly: O Citrabhānu, of manifold, worshipful radiance, Agni, you

> संग्रामनाम । तमप्यदहः स्वतेजोभिः । अथ तव स्तोता वाध्र्यश्वो वृधश्चित्स्वयं
> वृद्धो भवन्वाधंतं वर्धमानं हिंसकं नावाभिनत् । अवाङ्मुखं कृत्वाच्चिनत् ।
> यद्वा । त्वमेव तमवाभिनत् । अवाङ्मुखं कृत्वाभिनः । अच्छिनः ॥ प्रथममध्यमयोः
> समानमेतद्रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

समनं (*samanaṃ*) is a name for battle. You burned even that with your own splendours. Further, your praiser Vadhryaśva, himself grown strong, cut down the growing, harming foe, turning him face downward. Or else: you yourself cut him down, turning him face downward. This form is common to the first and middle persons.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- वध्र्यश्वस्य (*vadhryaśvasya*)—belonging to Vadhryaśva
- सुत सोमवद्भिः (*suta somavadbhiḥ*)—who offer pressed Soma
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—with the help of the priests
- शश्वत् (*śaśvat*)—always
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—enemies
- जिगाय (*jigāya*)—has conquered
- चित्रभानो (*citrabhāno*)—O Agni of manifold radiance
- समनं चित् (*samanaṃ cit*)—even the battle
- अदहः (*adahaḥ*)—you have burned with your splendour
- (Vadhryaśva, who praises you) वृधश्चित् (*vṛdhaścit*)—though mighty
- प्राधॆंतं (*prādhèṃtaṃ*)—the harming enemy
- अवाभिनत् (*avābhinat*)—has destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

With the help of the priests who belong to Vadhryaśva and offer pressed Soma, Agni has always conquered the enemies. O Agni of manifold radiance, you have burned even the battle with your splendour. Vadhryaśva, who praises you, has conquered the enemy who was mighty and harming.

##### English translation
Agni by means of the priests of Vadhryashwa pouring out libations always conquners his foes; you (Agni) shining with varied splendour, have consumed the battle; (your praiser) self-fostercd has destroyed his powerful (assailant),

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यम॒ग्निर्व॑ध्र्य॒श्वस्य॑ वृत्र॒हा स॑न॒कात्प्रेद्धो॒ नम॑सोपवा॒क्यः॑ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 602

> वृत्रहा शत्रूणां हंतायमग्निः सनकाच्चिरादारभ्य वध्र्यश्वस्य हविषा प्रेद्धः
> प्रकर्षेण दीपितो भवति । तथा तस्य नमसा नमस्कारेण सहोपवाक्य उपस्तोतव्यो
> भवति । हे वाध्र्यश्व वध्र्यश्वकुले मथनेन समुत्पन्नाग्ने स त्वं नोऽस्माकमजामीनज्ञातीञ्त्यत्रून् उत नापि वा शर्धतो हिंसतो विजामीन्विविधाञ्चा तीनप्यभि
> तिष्ठ । अभिभव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses the verse as follows. This Agni, वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*), the slayer of enemies, has been kindled, that is, brilliantly lit, from long ago (सनकात् (*sanakāt*), "beginning from a long time ago") by the oblation of Vadhryaśva. Likewise he is उपवाक्यः (*upavākyaḥ*), to be praised, together with Vadhryaśva's homage (नमसा (*namasā*), "with obeisance"). The poet then addresses Agni: "O Vādhryaśva", that is, O Agni born by churning in the family of Vadhryaśva, "you, नः (*naḥ*), ours, अजामीन् (*ajāmīn*), the unrelated enemies, and also (उत वा (*uta vā*)) विजामीन् (*vijāmīn*), enemies of various kinds who are kinsmen, even those who harm us (शर्धतः (*śardhataḥ*)), अभि तिष्ठ (*abhi tiṣṭha*), overcome them."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the destroyer of enemies
- अयं अग्निः (*ayaṃ agniḥ*)—this Agni
- सनकात् (*sanakāt*)—from a long time
- वध्रश्चश्वस्य (*vadhraścaśvasya*)—by the oblation of Vadhryaśva **NOTE**
- प्रेद्धः (*preddhaḥ*)—has been kindled
- नमसा (*namasā*)—together with his homage
- उपवाक्यः (*upavākyaḥ*)—is praised
- वाध्रश्च (*vādhraśca*)—O Agni, born through the effort of Vadhryaśva **NOTE**
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शर्धतः (*śardhataḥ*)—who inflict harm
- अजामीन् (*ajāmīn*)—the enemies who are not kinsmen
- उत वा (*uta vā*)—and likewise
- विजामीन् (*vijāmīn*)—the enemies who are kinsmen
- अभि तिष्ठ (*abhi tiṣṭha*)—defeat them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Agni, the destroyer of enemies, has for a long time been kindled by the oblation of Vadhryaśva, and is praised together with his homage. O Agni, born through the effort of Vadhryaśva, conquer all the enemies who inflict harm on us, and destroy them, whether they are our kinsmen or not.

##### English translation
From a long period has this Agni the slayer of foes been kindled (by the ohlation) of Vadhryashwa ; (he is) to be addressed with reverence; do you, (Agni, kindled in the) family of Vadhryashwa, overcome our ene-mies, both those who have no kinsmen and those who have many kinsmen.

## Sūkta 70 (Maṇḍala 10)

Seventieth Sūkta

Introduction

The present sūkta is one of the Āprī-sūktas. In the Ṛgveda there are ten Āprī-sūktas in all. In them there are mantras having as deities Idhma (or Samiddha Agni), Narāśaṃsa, Tanūnapāt, Iḷa, Barhis, the Devī Dvāras, Uṣāsānaktā, the two divine Hotṛs who are Pracetasas, the three goddesses Sarasvatī, Iḷā and Bhāratī, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Vanaspati and the Svāhākṛtis. But in respect of the deities Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt, in some sūktas the one deity Narāśaṃsa alone is praised, in others the one deity Tanūnapāt alone,

### Printed p. 603

and in others both deities, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt, are praised. According to this, these Āprī-sūktas have been divided into three kinds. That is, the Āprī-sūktas composed by the seers Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vādhryaśva and Gṛtsamada are:
1. जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने (*juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2 (मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठः (*maitrāvaruṇirvasiṣṭhaḥ*))
2. सुसमिद्धाय शोचिषे (*susamiddhāya śociṣe*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5 (वसुश्रत आत्रेयः (*vasuśrata ātreyaḥ*))
3. इमां मे अग्ने समिधं (*imāṃ me agne samidhaṃ*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70 (सुमित्रो वाध्यश्वः (*sumitro vādhyaśvaḥ*))
4. समिद्धो अग्निर्निहितः (*samiddho agnirnihitaḥ*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3 (गृत्समदः (*gṛtsamadaḥ*))

These four sūktas belong to one group. Each of them has a Ṛk whose deity is Narāśaṃsa. Therefore these four sūktas are named नराशंसवंति सूक्तानि (*narāśaṃsavaṃti sūktāni*), Āprī-sūktas that praise the deity Narāśaṃsa alone.
1. सुसमिद्धो न आ वह (*susamiddho na ā vaha*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13 (मेथातिथिः काण्वः (*methātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ*))
2. समिद्धो अग्न आवह (*samiddho agna āvaha*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142 (दीर्घतमा औचथ्यः (*dīrghatamā aucathyaḥ*))

These two Āprī-sūktas belong to the second group. In them there is one Ṛk each for the two deities Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. Therefore these Āprī-sūktas are known as sūktas with both kinds of deity, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. Since both deities are present in these sūktas, in sūkta 1-142, apart from Indra, there came to be twelve homas in place of the eleven Prayāja homas.
1. समिद्धो अद्य राजसि (*samiddho adya rājasi*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188 (अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः (*agastyo maitrāvaruṇiḥ*))
2. समित्समित्सुमना (*samitsamitsumanā*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4 (गाधिनो विश्वामित्रः (*gādhino viśvāmitraḥ*))
3. समिद्धो विश्वतस्पतिः (*samiddho viśvataspatiḥ*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5 (काश्यपोऽसितो देवलो वा (*kāśyapo 'sito devalo vā*))
4. समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो (*samiddho adya manuṣo*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110 (जमदग्निः भार्गवः (*jamadagniḥ bhārgavaḥ*))

These sūktas belong to the third group. In them there are only Ṛks whose deity is Tanūnapāt (there are no Ṛks with Narāśaṃsa as deity). Therefore they are named तनूनपात्वंति सूक्तानि (*tanūnapātvaṃti sūktāni*), that is, Āprī-sūktas containing mantras whose deity is Tanūnapāt. These Āprī-sūktas are recited in the animal oblation for performing the eleven Prayāja homas. There is a sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: एकादशावदानान्यवद्यति दश वै पशोः प्राणा आत्मैकादशः (*ekādaśāvadānānyavadyati daśa vai paśoḥ prāṇā ātmaikādaśaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-3). In reciting these Āprī-sūktas and performing the animal oblation there is one special rule: sacrificers born in a given gotra must, when performing the sacrifice, recite only the Āprī-sūkta composed by the seer of that gotra (Ā. 3-2). The present Āprī-sūkta is to be recited by those born in the Vādhryaśva gotra.

### Printed p. 606

… a Brāhmaṇa sentence confirms this very view. But some say it is addressed to the metre-deities (Śa. Brā. 1-3-2-9); others, to the deities consisting of the Ṛtus (Śa. Brā. 1-3-2-8); others, to the sacrificial animal (Kau. Brā. 3.4 **NOTE**); some, to the deity consisting of the vital breath (Ai. Brā. 1-11, Śa. Brā. 11-2-7-27); and still others, to the Self (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-5-4). Having gathered together all that these have said, [Kātyāyana] then states his firm view that the sound doctrine is to say that it is addressed to Agni.

In the Sarvānukramaṇikā of Kātyāyana the difference between the words Āpra and Āprī is also indicated (this difference is stated at the end of the Āprī-sūkta, that is, of sūkta 1-142; it shows that Ṛks addressed to the deity Narāśaṃsa are known as Āpra mantras, and Ṛks addressed to the deity Tanūnapāt as Āprī mantras). In the Bṛhaddevatā:
द्वितीये द्वादशर्चॆ तु प्रत्यृचं यास्तु देवताः । सूयंते ह्यग्निना सार्थ० तासां नामानि मे शृणु ॥ (*dvitīye dvādaśarcè tu pratyṛcaṃ yāstu devatāḥ | sūyaṃte hyagninā sārtha0 tāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu ‖*)
प्रथमायां स्तुतश्चेध्मो द्वितीयायां तनूनपात् । नराशंस स्तृतीयायां चतुर्थ्या० सूयते त्विळः ॥ (*prathamāyāṃ stutaścedhmo dvitīyāyāṃ tanūnapāt | narāśaṃsa stṛtīyāyāṃ caturthyā0 sūyate tviḷaḥ ‖*)
बर्हिरेव तु पंचम्यां द्वारो देव्यस्ततोऽन्यया । नक्तोषासा तु सप्तम्यामष्टम्यां संस्तुतौ सह ॥ (*barhireva tu paṃcamyāṃ dvāro devyastato 'nyayā | naktoṣāsā tu saptamyāmaṣṭamyāṃ saṃstutau saha ‖*)
देव्याविति तु होतारौ नवमामृचि संस्तुताः । तिस्रो देव्यो दशम्यां तु ज्ञेयस्त्वष्टैव तु स्तुतः ॥ (*devyāviti tu hotārau navamāmṛci saṃstutāḥ | tisro devyo daśamyāṃ tu jñeyastvaṣṭaiva tu stutaḥ ‖*)
एकादश्यां तु सूक्तस्य स्तुतं विद्याद्वनस्पतिः । द्वादश्यां तु स्तुता देवीर्विद्यात्साहाकृतीरिति ॥ (*ekādaśyāṃ tu sūktasya stutaṃ vidyādvanaspatiḥ | dvādaśyāṃ tu stutā devīrvidyātsāhākṛtīriti ‖*)
सूक्तेऽस्मिन्प्रत्यृचं यासु देवताः परिकीर्तिताः । ता एव सर्वास्वाप्रीषु द्वितीया तु विकल्पते ॥ (*sūkte 'sminpratyṛcaṃ yāsu devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ | tā eva sarvāsvāprīṣu dvitīyā tu vikalpate ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 2-146 to 151).
Thus, having named all the deities beginning with Idhma, it states the order of the sūkta and the particular deity addressed in each single Ṛk. On the question of how many Āprī-sūktas there are, the author of the Nirukta says:
इतीमान्येकादशाप्रीसूक्तानि । तेषां वासिष्ठमात्रेयं वाध्र्यश्वं गार्त्स्मदमिति नाराशंसवंति । मैधातिथं दैर्घतमसं प्रैषितमित्युभयवंत्यतोऽन्यानि तनूनपात्वंति तनूनपात्वंति ॥ (*itīmānyekādaśāprīsūktāni | teṣāṃ vāsiṣṭhamātreyaṃ vādhryaśvaṃ gārtsmadamiti nārāśaṃsavaṃti | maidhātithaṃ dairghatamasaṃ praiṣitamityubhayavaṃtyato 'nyāni tanūnapātvaṃti tanūnapātvaṃti ‖*)
(Ni. 8-22).

### Printed p. 607

Among these sūktas, those seen by Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vadhryaśva and Gṛtsamada are devoted to Narāśaṃsa. Those seen by the seers Medhātithi and Dīrghatamas, and also the Praiṣa-sūkta, are addressed to both deities, Tanūnapāt and Narāśaṃsa; the remaining four sūktas are devoted to the deity Tanūnapāt alone. In all (if the Praiṣa-sūkta is included) there are eleven Āprī-sūktas. The Bṛhaddevatā too gives this same view:
प्रेष्टैः सहाप्रीसूक्तानि तान्येकादश संति च । यजूंषि प्रैषसूक्तं ना दशैतानीतराणि तु ॥ (*preṣṭaiḥ sahāprīsūktāni tānyekādaśa saṃti ca | yajūṃṣi praiṣasūktaṃ nā daśaitānītarāṇi tu ‖*)
सौत्रामण्यानि तु त्रीणि प्राजापत्याश्वमेधिके । पुरुषस्य तु यन्मेधे यजस्वेव तु तानि षट् ॥ (*sautrāmaṇyāni tu trīṇi prājāpatyāśvamedhike | puruṣasya tu yanmedhe yajasveva tu tāni ṣaṭ ‖*)
अत्रैव प्रैषसूक्तं स्यान्न यजुष्वाद्रियेत तत् । तेषां प्रैषगतं सूक्तं यच्च दीर्घतमा जगौ । मेधातिथौ यदुक्तं च त्रिण्येवोभयवंति तु । ऋषौ गृत्समदे यच्च वाध्यश्वे च यदुच्यते ॥ (*atraiva praiṣasūktaṃ syānna yajuṣvādriyeta tat | teṣāṃ praiṣagataṃ sūktaṃ yacca dīrghatamā jagau | medhātithau yaduktaṃ ca triṇyevobhayavaṃti tu | ṛṣau gṛtsamade yacca vādhyaśve ca yaducyate ‖*)
नराशंसवदत्रेश्च ददर्श च यदौर्वशः । तनूनपादगस्त्यश्च जमदग्निश्च यज्जगौ ॥ (*narāśaṃsavadatreśca dadarśa ca yadaurvaśaḥ | tanūnapādagastyaśca jamadagniśca yajjagau ‖*)
विश्वामित्र ऋषिर्यश्च जगौ वै काश्यपोस्ितः । मेधातिथेर्युचां यास्तु प्रोक्ता द्वादशदेवताः ॥ (*viśvāmitra ṛṣiryaśca jagau vai kāśyapositaḥ | medhātitheryucāṃ yāstu proktā dvādaśadevatāḥ ‖*)
संपद्यंते यथाग्निं ताः संपदं तां निबोधत । (*saṃpadyaṃte yathāgniṃ tāḥ saṃpadaṃ tāṃ nibodhata |*)
(Bṛ. De. 2-152 to 157).
In these verses it is said that if the Praiṣa-sūkta is included there are eleven Āprī-sūktas in all, and if not, ten; and following the Nirukta sentence itself it gives the order of the sūktas addressed to the deities Narāśaṃsa, Tanūnapāt and so on, and of those composed by the seers Medhātithi and others.

The Praiṣa-sūkta is orderly and is such as to gather together the substance of all the Āprī-sūktas and give one definite picture. It collects all the individual epithets of the deities addressed in the Āprī-sūktas and sets out separately the nature and the function of each deity. In addressing each deity as well, it first utters a fixed portion of mantra, होता यक्षत् (*hotā yakṣat*), and only then names the deity concerned. By first examining the deity, the epithet of the deity and the function described in the Praiṣa-sūkta, one can afterwards learn the agreement, or the differences of opinion, on the questions: what is the aim of such Āprī-sūktas addressed to deities? What are their characteristics? What benefit results from reciting them?
