Gathering the main points of the Āprī-sūktas, a systematic … the order of their composition, their styles, and in the sacrificial rite … poetic character … at the end it is stated. … regarding their aims the scholar Max Muller first … as a means of satisfying …, and afterwards … to take them up is toil, thus he has said— **NOTE**

### Printed p. 609

… it is well known that this sūkta alone is used. But for the seers who were the seers of the fourth and sixth Maṇḍalas no reason can be given why they have no need of it; or perhaps the descendants of Vāmadeva and of Bharadvāja used to recite some other mantras in this place.

The mantras indicated by the names Āprī and Āpra: Kātyāyana in the Sarvānukramaṇikā says: एतदाप्रीसूक्तं एतेनान्युक्तदैवतानि एकादशकानि तु नाराशंसानि आप्रशब्दोक्तानि आतनूनपात्वंति । (*etadāprīsūktaṃ etenānyuktadaivatāni ekādaśakāni tu nārāśaṃsāni āpraśabdoktāni ātanūnapātvaṃti |*). He has said that the mantras recited addressed to the deity Narāśaṃsa are known by the name Āpra, and the mantras recited addressed to the deity Tanūnapāt are known by the name Āprī. But in the Nirukta and the like there are no sentences showing this distinction. The question also naturally arises whether the name Āprī belongs to the deity or to the sūkta. On close examination one may say that they were first sūkta-wise, and afterwards became mantras pointing out the deity.

Nature of the rite: it may be said that the sacrificial rite prescribed by the Āprī-sūkta did not hold a subordinate position, as the Brāhmaṇas and the like indicate, but held the position of a principal sacrifice. The difference between the Prayāja oblations and the oblations prescribed in this rite is evident in many places: 1-13-8, 1-148-7 **NOTE**, 1-142-8, 3-4-8, 5-5-7, 9-5-8. In these Ṛks the mantra-words इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*); in Ṛks 5-5-2 and 3-4-5 the words नः यज्ञं (*naḥ yajñaṃ*); and in Ṛks 1-13-2, 7-2-7 and 10-110-8 the words अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*asmin yajñe*) show a principal position in the sacrificial rite or in the offering of oblations, and not a subordinate position like the Prayāja oblations.

From the mantras त्रिरादिवोमिमिक्षति (*trirādivomimikṣati*) (1-142-3) and त्रिरहन्नायजंते (*trirahannāyajaṃte*) (3-4-2) it is learned that this rite is to be performed at three times in the day; and from समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे (*samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe*) (10-110-1) it is learned that there is no separate sacrificial house for it, and that the fire may be established in an ordinary house.

In the Ṛk
समित्समित्सुमना बोध्यस्मे शुचाशुचा सुमतिं रासि वस्वः । आ देव देवान्यजथाय वक्षि सखा सखीन्सुमना यक्ष्यग्ने ॥ (*samitsamitsumanā bodhyasme śucāśucā sumatiṃ rāsi vasvaḥ | ā deva devānyajathāya vakṣi sakhā sakhīnsumanā yakṣyagne ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-1)
the seer Viśvāmitra describes poetically the kindling of Agni, and also in
जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने अद्य शोचा बृहद्यजतं धूममृण्वन् । (*juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne adya śocā bṛhadyajataṃ dhūmamṛṇvan |*)

### Printed p. 610
… and the kindling of Agni, which the sage Viśvāmitra describes in poetic form in the Ṛk
*ā deva devānyajathāya vakṣi sakhā sakhīnsumanā yakṣyagne‖* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-1),
and the description, in the Ṛk
उप स्पृश दिव्यं सानु स्तूपैः सं रश्मिभिस्ततनः सूरस्य॥ (*upa spṛśa divyaṃ sānu stūpaiḥ saṃ raśmibhistatanaḥ sūrasya‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-1),
of the rays of Agni and the rays of the sun spreading out together, also show the poetic character of the mantras. These same descriptions also show that this sacrifice is to be begun in the morning.

The mantra पूर्व्यं तंतुं तनुष्प (*pūrvyaṃ taṃtuṃ tanuṣpa*) (1-142-1) shows that this sacrifice is ancient. For this sacrifice to be completed without obstacle the help of Agni, the Hotṛ of the gods, is needed, and therefore the ghee-offering must first be made to Agni. After Agni is satisfied by it, he spreads towards the atmosphere (7-2-1). Then he brings the gods. Because Agni is the friend of men (3-4-1), he does this service.

Skill of composition—Although the Āprī-sūktas were composed at different times, one apart from another, and belong to different lines of seers, all these sūktas have the same style of diction and the same aim; hence their harmony and charm, greater in one way than in all other kinds of sūktas, show their distinctiveness.

In all the sūktas (except two) the number of Ṛks is eleven, and the sūkta begins with the word समिद् (*samid*) and ends with स्वाहा (*svāhā*); this shows a fixed rule from the point of view of both poetry and art. In the matter of metre there is no such restriction. The sūktas 1-13, 1-188, 5-5 and 9-5 are composed in the Gāyatrī metre, the 142nd sūkta of Maṇḍala 1 in the Anuṣṭubh metre, and 2-3, 3-5, 7-2, 10-70 and 10-110 in the Triṣṭubh metre.

Many mantra phrases are repeated, such as देवान् आ वह (*devān ā vaha*), देवान् वक्षि (*devān vakṣi*), विप्रा यज्ञेषु मानवेषु कारुः (*viprā yajñeṣu mānaveṣu kāruḥ*) and the like.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमां म इत्येकादशर्च० द्वितीयं सूक्तं । वाध्र्यश्वस्य सुमित्रस्यार्ष०
> त्रैष्टुभं तनूनपाद्वर्जिताः सनराशंसाः समिदादयः प्रत्यृचं देवताः । शथा
> चानुक्रांतं । इमां म एकादशाप्रमिति ॥ वध्यश्वगोत्राणां पशाविदमाप्रीसूक्तं।
> सूत्रितं च । समिद्धो अद्येति सर्वॆषां यथऋषि ना । आ. ३-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, beginning इमां मे (*imāṃ me*). Its seer is Sumitra of the Vādhryaśva line; the metre is Triṣṭubh. Its deities, for each Ṛk in turn, are the Āprī deities beginning with Samidh, together with Narāśaṃsa, but omitting Tanūnapāt. As the Anukramaṇī says, इमां म एकादशाप्रं (*imāṃ ma ekādaśāpraṃ*): this is the Āprī-sūkta of the Vadhryaśva (Vādhryaśva) gotras for the animal sacrifice. It is also prescribed in the sūtra: समिद्धो अद्येति सर्वॆषां यथऋषि ना (*samiddho adyeti sarvèṣāṃ yathaṛṣi nā*) (Ā. 3-2).

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning इमां मे (*imāṃ me*) is the second sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Its seer is Sumitra, son of Vadhryaśva; the metre is Triṣṭubh. Since it is an Āprī-sūkta, leaving aside the deity Tanūnapāt and in its place including Narāśaṃsa, the eleven deities of the Samidh-and-following Āprī-sūkta are the deities of the Ṛks in order; hence the Anukramaṇī says इमां म एकादशाप्रं (*imāṃ ma ekādaśāpraṃ*).

### Printed p. 611
The use of this Āprī-sūkta in the animal offering for those of the gotra of the seer Vadhryaśva is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the sūtra समिद्दो अद्येति सर्वॆषां यथर्षि वा (*samiddo adyeti sarvèṣāṃ yatharṣi vā*) (Ā. 3-2).

Sūkta—70
Maṇḍala—10 ‖ Anuvāka—6 ‖ Sūkta—70 ‖
Aṣṭaka—8 ‖ Adhyāya—2 ‖ Varga—21, 22 ‖
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—11 ‖
Seer: Sāmitra Vādhryaśva ‖
Deity: Āprī ‖ 1. Idhma, Samiddha, or Agni. 2. Narāśaṃsa. 3. Iḷā. 4. Barhis. 5. The divine Doors. 6. Uṣāsānaktā. 7. The two divine Hotṛs, the wise. 8. The three goddesses Sarasvatī, Iḷā, Bhāratī. 9. Tvaṣṭṛ. 10. Vanaspati. 11. The Svāhākṛtis ‖
Metre: Triṣṭubh ‖

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मां मे॑ अग्ने स॒मिधं॑ जुषस्वे॒ळस्प॒दे प्रति॑ हर्या घृ॒ताचीं॑।  
> वर्ष्म॑न्पृथि॒व्याः सु॑दिन॒त्वे अह्ना॑मू॒र्ध्वो भ॑व सुक्रतो  ॒
> देवयज्या ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमां । मे । अग्ने । संइधं । जुषस्व । इळः । पदे । प्रति । हर्य । धृताचीं ।  
> वर्ष्मन् । पृथिव्याः । सुदिनत्वे । अह्नां । ऊर्ध्वः । भव । सुक्रतो इति सुक्रतो  
> देवयज्या ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने इळस्पद इळायास्पदे । एतद्वा इळायास्पदं यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिः। इति
> ब्राह्मणं । उत्तरवेद्यामिमां मे मदीयां समिधं जुषस्व । सेवस्व । तथा घृताचीं घृतमंचंतीं स्रुचं प्रति हर्य । प्रतिकामयस्व । किंच हे सुक्रतो सुप्रज्ञ
> पृथिव्या वर्षन्वर्षणि सनुच्छ्रिते पूर्वोक्ते देशेऽह्नां सुदिनत्वे तन्निमित्तं देवयज्या देवयागेन हेतुनोर्ध्वो ज्वालाभिरुन्नतो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, इळस्पदे (*iḷaspade*) means "in the place of Iḷā". A Brāhmaṇa says: एतद्वा इळायास्पदं यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिः (*etadvā iḷāyāspadaṃ yaduttaravedī nābhiḥ*) So: on the uttaravedi accept this my fuel-stick (samidh), serve it. Likewise desire the ghee-filled ladle (ghṛtācī, "that which holds ghee"). Further, O very wise one: on the lofty place of the earth, the spot just mentioned, for the good days (sudinatva) of the days, because of the worship of the gods, rise up high with flames.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- इळस्पदे (*iḷaspade*)—established on the uttaravedi
- मे (*me*)—my
- इमां समिधं (*imāṃ samidhaṃ*)—these fuel-sticks
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—serve
- धृताचीं (*dhṛtācīṃ*)—this ladle full of ghee
- प्रतिहर्य (*pratiharya*)—desire
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Agni of excellent wisdom
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- वर्ष्मन् (*varṣman*)—on the lofty uttaravedi
- आह्नां (*āhnāṃ*)—of the days
- सुदिनत्वे (*sudinatve*)—for welfare
- देवयज्या (*devayajyā*)—by means of worship of the gods and the like
- ऊर्ध्वः भव (*ūrdhvaḥ bhava*)—rise up in the form of flame and shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, established on the uttaravedi, accept these my fuel-sticks. Desire this ladle full of ghee. O Agni of excellent wisdom, on the lofty uttaravedi of the earth, for all welfare, by means of worship of the gods and the like, rise up and shine with flame.

##### English translation
Graciously accept, Agni, this my fuel (placed) on the place of libation (the altar); delight in the butter-laden (spoon); most wise, rise up upon the lofty place of the earth for the propitiousness of the days through the worship of the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—सम्यग्दीपितः एतन्नामकः त्वं (*samyagdīpitaḥ etannāmakaḥ tvaṃ*): Sāyaṇa explains it as "famed by the name Samiddha". It is addressed to the kindled Agni, who holds the first place in the Āprī-sūkta.

इध्मो यः सर्वमेवाग्निरयं हीध्मः समिध्यते । ध्मातेर्वै तत्कृतं रूपं ध्मातो हीध्मः समिध्यते ॥ (*idhmo yaḥ sarvamevāgnirayaṃ hīdhmaḥ samidhyate | dhmātervai tatkṛtaṃ rūpaṃ dhmāto hīdhmaḥ samidhyate ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-188)

Here identity is stated between the wooden idhma and the all-pervading Agni. The word idhma is derived from the root ध्मा (*dhmā*). Because it blazes after being blown upon, it has this name: so the author of the Bṛhaddevatā gives the explanation of the words idhma and samiddha. This explanation follows that of the Nirukta-author. In the Nirukta also, concerning the first deity of the Āprī-sūkta, it is said:
तासामिध्मः प्रथमागामी भवति । इद्मः समिंधनात् । (*tāsāmidhmaḥ prathamāgāmī bhavati | idmaḥ samiṃdhanāt |*) (Ni. 8-5)
In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa also, at the beginning of the Praiṣa-sūkta—

### Printed p. 612
(No text of the Kannada page 612 beyond what is given above and below; see the continuation.)

### Printed p. 613
होता यक्षदग्निग्ं समिधा समिद्धं सुषमिधा नाभा प्रथिव्याः संगथे वामस्य । (*hotā yakṣadagnigṃ samidhā samiddhaṃ suṣamidhā nābhā prathivyāḥ saṃgathe vāmasya |*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2.1)

—the Hotṛ is addressed as having sacrificed to Agni, called Samidh and accompanied by the first Aprayāja deity.

Another point must be noted here. The designation idhma does not occur in the Āprī-sūktas; this name is not in the Praiṣa-sūkta either. Only in the Sarvānukramaṇī is it stated: सुसमिद्ध इतीध्र्यः समिद्धो वा अग्नि.................. इति प्रत्यृचं देवताः । (*susamiddha itīdhryaḥ samiddho vā agni.................. iti pratyṛcaṃ devatāḥ |*) Since the word is not used in this context in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa either, it is clear that Śaunaka and Kātyāyana followed the Nirukta-author in using it. Moreover, the epithet samiddha or susamiddha is used in seven sūktas, and the epithet samidh in the remaining three (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-1; 7-2-1; 10-70-1).

The first duty of this Agni called Samiddha is to invoke the gods: in the opening Ṛks of the sūktas 1-13-1, 1-142-1, 3-4-1, 10-110-1, as in the prayer of the Ṛk सुसमिद्धोन आ वह देवा अग्ने हविष्मते (*susamiddhona ā vaha devā agne haviṣmate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-1), Agni's duty is indicated. Not only this, it is also prayed that he carry the oblations and so on.

On the question whether this deity is Agni or not, the Nirukta-author cites the difference of opinion from the beginning and then states his own view. After giving the opinions of the respective sages, यज्ञेध्म इति कात्थक्यः (*yajñedhma iti kātthakyaḥ*) (Ni. 8-5), अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*) (8-5), he gives his own view: आग्नेय इति तु स्थितिः (*āgneya iti tu sthitiḥ*) (Ni. 8-22). In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:
समिधो यजति । प्राणा वै समिधः । प्राणा हीदं सर्वं समिंधते यदिदं किंच प्राणानेव तत्प्रीणाति प्राणान्यजमाने दधाति ॥ (*samidho yajati | prāṇā vai samidhaḥ | prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ samiṃdhate yadidaṃ kiṃca prāṇāneva tatprīṇāti prāṇānyajamāne dadhāti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 2-4)
Although by these sentences identity between samidh and prāṇa is stated, still, on many other grounds, it may be said that this deity must be Agni.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ दे॒वाना॑मग्र॒यावे॒ह या॑तु॒ नरा॒शंसो॑ वि॒श्वरू॑पेभि॒रश्वैः॑ ।  
> ऋ॒तस्य॑ प॒था नम॑सा मि॒येधो॑ दे॒वेभ्यो॑ दे॒वत॑मः सुषूदत् ॥

### Printed p. 614

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । देवानां । अग्रयावा । इह । यातु । नराशंसः । विश्वरूपेभिः । अश्वैः ।  
> ऋतस्य । पथा । नमसा । मियेधः । देवेभ्यः । देवतमः । सुसूदत् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवानामग्रयावाग्रे गंता नराशंसः ॥ उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदिति
> पूर्वोत्तरपदयोर्युगपत्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ नरैः शंसनीय एतन्नामकोऽग्निर्विश्वरूपेभिर्नानारूपैरश्वै रोहिदाख्यैः सहेहास्मिन्यज्ञ आ यातु । अगत्य च मियेधो
> मेध्यो यज्ञहितः स्तुतियोग्यो वा देवतमो देवानां मुख्यः सोऽग्निर्हविर्नयनयोग्येनर्तस्य यज्ञस्य पथा मार्गेण नमसा स्तोत्रेण सह देवेभ्य
> इंद्रादिभ्यः सुसूदत् । हविः प्रेरयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Narāśaṃsa is the one who goes first of the gods (देवानामग्रयावा (*devānāmagrayāvā*)). The name Narāśaṃsa is one to be praised by men; this Agni, with various-formed horses called Rohits, should come here to this sacrifice. And he, मियेधः (*miyedhaḥ*), pure, beneficial to the sacrifice or worthy of praise, देवतमः (*devatamaḥ*), chief of the gods, Agni, fit to carry the oblation, by the path of the sacrifice and with praise, should impel the oblation to the gods, Indra and the others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of all the gods
- अग्रयावा (*agrayāvā*)—who goes in front
- नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*)—Agni called Narāśaṃsa
- विश्वरूपेभिः (*viśvarūpebhiḥ*)—of many kinds of form
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with horses
- इह (*iha*)—to this sacrifice
- आ यातु (*ā yātu*)—may he come
- मियेधः (*miyedhaḥ*)—worshipful
- देवतमः (*devatamaḥ*)—Agni, chief of all gods
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- पथा (*pathā*)—by the path
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with praise
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—toward the gods beginning with Indra
- सुषूदत् (*suṣūdat*)—may he impel the oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni called Narāśaṃsa, who goes in front of all the gods, come to this sacrifice with horses of many kinds of form. May Agni, worthy of worship and chief of all the gods, come along the path of the sacrifice and, accompanied by praise, impel the oblation toward the gods beginning with Indra.

##### English translation
May Narashamsa, the preceder of the gods, come here with his horses of various forms; deserving of adoration, chief of the gods, may he effuse (oblations) to the gods by the path of the sacrifice with praise.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*)—नरैः शंसनीयः (अग्निः) (*naraiḥ śaṃsanīyaḥ (agniḥ)*): Agni, praised by men; this is a name of Agni true to its meaning. Or नराशंसोऽग्निर्यज्ञो वा। (*narāśaṃso 'gniryajño vā|*) — another view is that Narāśaṃsa means either Agni or the sacrifice. The Nirukta passage supports both views.

### Printed p. 615
नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यः । नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसंति । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । नरैः प्रशस्यो भवति ॥ (*narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyaḥ | narā asminnāsīnāḥ śaṃsaṃti | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | naraiḥ praśasyo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 8-7)

That is: Kātthakya says that the sacrifice has the name Narāśaṃsa because men (humans), sitting on the sacrificial altar, praise (the gods); Śākapūṇi says that the name applies to Agni because he is to be praised by men. After indicating these two views, the Nirukta-author cites the Ṛk:
नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः । ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियंधाः स्वदंति देवा उभयानि हव्या ॥ (*narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāmupa stoṣāma yajatasya yajñaiḥ | ye sukratavaḥ śucayo dhiyaṃdhāḥ svadaṃti devā ubhayāni havyā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-2)
In this Ṛk the meaning "Agni" for the word Narāśaṃsa is the apt one. Among the deities listed in the Nighaṇṭu, the deity Narāśaṃsa is said to be one of the other forms of Agni. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā say this very thing:
नराशंसस्त्रितश्चैनमेनमेवाश्रितस्त्वशीलः । बर्हिद्वारश्च देव्योऽग्निमेनमेव तु संश्रिताः ॥ (*narāśaṃsastritaścainamenamevāśritastvaśīlaḥ | barhidvāraśca devyo 'gnimenameva tu saṃśritāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-107)
In this verse it is said that deities such as Narāśaṃsa, Trita, Iḷā and Barhirdvāra rely on this very Agni and are contained in him; and:
पृथक्त्वेन समस्तैस्तु यज्ञे यच्छस्यते नृभिः । स्तुवंत्याप्रीषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः ॥ (*pṛthaktvena samastaistu yajñe yacchasyate nṛbhiḥ | stuvaṃtyāprīṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-28)
Because he is praised separately by all the men gathered at the sacrifice, the poets praise him (Agni) in the Āprī-sūktas by the name Narāśaṃsa; thus they too endorse the view the Nirukta-author states.
नराशंसमिहैके तु अग्निमाहुरथेतरे । नराः शंसंति सर्वेऽस्मिन्नासीना इति नाध्वरे ॥ एतमेवाहुरन्येऽग्निं नराशंसोऽध्वरे ह्ययं । नर्मैः प्रशस्य आसीनैराहुश्चैवर्त्विजो नरः ॥ (*narāśaṃsamihaike tu agnimāhurathetare | narāḥ śaṃsaṃti sarve 'sminnāsīnā iti nādhvare ‖ etamevāhuranye 'gniṃ narāśaṃso 'dhvare hyayaṃ | narmaiḥ praśasya āsīnairāhuścaivartvijo naraḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-2, 3)
Some say Narāśaṃsa is Agni. Others say it is the sacrifice, because men gather at the sacrifice and praise. Because he is praised by the men gathered at the sacrifice, Narāśaṃsa means …

### Printed p. 616
Others hold that it is Agni; the third view is a reconciliation of the first and second views. Along with these two meanings Sāyaṇa has also given a third. In the bhāṣya on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89.9:

नराशंसमेतन्नामकं देवविशेषं । यद्वा अवयवार्थव्युत्पत्ता सदसस्पतिदेवतापरोऽयं शब्दः । अत्र अग्निवत् सदसस्पतेरपि नरैः शस्यमानत्वात् नराशंसस्त्वं । एतमेवाभिप्रायं हृदि निभाय ब्राह्मणमेवमान्न्यायते प्रजा वै नरो वाक् शंसः ॥ (*narāśaṃsametannāmakaṃ devaviśeṣaṃ | yadvā avayavārthavyutpattā sadasaspatidevatāparo 'yaṃ śabdaḥ | atra agnivat sadasaspaterapi naraiḥ śasyamānatvāt narāśaṃsastvaṃ | etamevābhiprāyaṃ hṛdi nibhāya brāhmaṇamevamānnyāyate prajā vai naro vāk śaṃsaḥ ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 6-27)

This is the explanation. Narāśaṃsa may be understood as a particular deity of this name, or as Sadasaspati. Because Sadasaspati too is praised by men, and because the sentence quoted from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa suggests this idea, this meaning is possible too; thus the third meaning has been shown. But it may be said that this word is used of Agni throughout the Ṛksaṃhitā.

नराशंसः प्रति धामान्यंजन् तिस्रो दिवः प्रति मह्ना स्वर्चिः । घृतपुषा मनसा हव्यमुंदन्मूर्धन्यज्ञस्य समनक्तु देवान् ॥ (*narāśaṃsaḥ prati dhāmānyaṃjan tisro divaḥ prati mahnā svarciḥ | ghṛtapuṣā manasā havyamuṃdanmūrdhanyajñasya samanaktu devān ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-2)

In such Ṛks the word Narāśaṃsa is understood as Agni.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒श्व॒त्त॒ममी॑ळते दू॒त्या॑य ह॒विष्मं॑तो मनु॒ष्या॑सो अ॒ग्निं ।  
> वहि॑ष्ठै॒रश्वैः॑ सु॒वृता॒ रथे॒ना दे॒वान्व॑क्षि॒ नि ष॑दे॒ह होता॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शश्वत्तमं । ईळते । दूत्याय । हविष्मंतः । मनुष्यासः । अग्निं ।  
> वहिष्यैः । अश्वैः । सुवृता । रथेन । आ । देवान् । वक्षि । नि । सद । इह । होता ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शश्वत्तममत्यंतं नित्यमग्निं हविष्मंतः संभृतहविष्का मनुष्यासो मनुष्या
> यजमाना दूत्याय ॥ दूतस्य भागकर्मणी इति यश्प्रत्ययाः ॥ दूतकर्मणे हविर्वहनलक्षणाय तन्निमित्तमीळते । स्तुवंति । स त्वमेवं स्तुतो वहिष्ठैर्वोढृतमैरश्चैः सुवृता सुवर्तनेन रथेन च सह देवानिंद्रादीना वक्षि । अस्मदीयं
> यज्ञं प्रत्यावह । प्रापय । तस्त्वं होता भवन्नि हास्मिन्यज्ञे नि सद । निषेद ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: the sacrificers, men bearing oblations, praise Agni, who is शश्वत्तम (*śaśvattama*), that is, utterly eternal, for the office of messenger, namely carrying the oblation (to the gods); for that purpose they praise him. Praised thus, Agni is asked to bring Indra and the other gods to our sacrifice with his best draught horses and his well-rolling chariot, and, being the Hotṛ, to sit down here in this sacrifice.

### Printed p. 617

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)—having an exceedingly eternal state
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—those provided with oblations
- मनुष्यासः (*manuṣyāsaḥ*)—the sacrificers
- दूत्याय (*dūtyāya*)—to perform the office of messenger of the gods
- ईळते (*īḷate*)—praise
- *�vahiṣṭhaiḥ*—fit to draw the chariot
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with horses
- सुवृता (*suvṛtā*)—of excellent movement
- रथेन (*rathena*)—with the chariot
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and the rest
- आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—bring to our sacrifice
- होता (*hotā*)—being in the form of the Hotṛ
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- निषद (*niṣada*)—sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificers, provided with oblations, praise Agni of eternal state, that he may discharge the office of messenger of the gods. O Agni, with a chariot drawn by horses fit to draw it and of excellent movement, bring Indra and the other gods to our sacrifice. Being in the form of the Hotṛ, sit down in this sacrifice.

##### English translation
Men offering oblations adore the eternal Agni to (induce him to perform) the duty of messenger (to the gods); do you with your stalwart draught horses and your well-turning chariots bear (our offering) to the gods, and sit down here as the ministrant priest.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ईळते (*īḷate*)—सर्वैः स्तुयते इळनामकः त्वं (*sarvaiḥ stuyate iḷanāmakaḥ tvaṃ*). It is explained as Agni, praised by all and well known by the name Iḍa. ईळ ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*īḷa īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*); it may be derived either from the root īḍ meaning praise, or from the root ind meaning to blaze (Ni. 8-8). Having shown this derivation of the word, the Nirukta author quotes Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-3 and explains the right meaning of the word.

First, like the word samidh, this word too seems to have had no separate designation as a deity, but to be used only as an epithet of Agni. Since the help and support of Agni had to be complete during the performance of the sacrifice, he was by nature worthy of praise. At the beginning Agni must be (1) kindled. Afterwards, (2) under the name Tanūnapāt or Narāśaṃsa, he must make the oblations of the sacrifice full of honey. Then he must bring the gods to the sacrifice. For this work he must needs be īḍya (praiseworthy). Therefore in this setting he is (3) īḍya (is entreated) by the sacrificers.

### Printed p. 618
In the Āprī hymns this word, derived from the root īḍ, is used of Agni in nine places in all: in eight as an epithet meaning "praised" or "worthy of praise", and in one as an epithet showing Agni's office of messenger. Only in the Ṛk seen by Viśvāmitra,

प्रदीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै । अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वंदध्यै स देवान्यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् ॥ (*pradīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai | acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vaṃdadhyai sa devānyakṣadiṣito yajīyān ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3)

does it mean food in the form of oblation; yet even so it is connected with Agni, the chief deity of that Ṛk. This meaning differs from the tradition of the Āprī hymn. In the Praiṣa hymn, however, it is only a synonym of Agni.

होतायक्षदग्निमिड ईडितो देवो देवाग्ं आवक्षद्दूतो हव्यनाडमूरः । उपेमं यज्ञमुपेमां देवो देवहूतिमवतु नेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥ (*hotāyakṣadagnimiḍa īḍito devo devāgṃ āvakṣaddūto havyanāḍamūraḥ | upemaṃ yajñamupemāṃ devo devahūtimavatu netvājyasya hotaryaja ‖*)
(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1)

On this sentence the commentator says इडेत्येतन्नामकमग्निं तृतीयप्रयाजदेवं (*iḍetyetannāmakamagniṃ tṛtīyaprayājadevaṃ*), taking it as a synonymous name of Agni. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

इळो यजत्यन्नं ना इळोन्नमेव तत्प्रीणात्यन्नं यजमाने दधाति । (*iḷo yajatyannaṃ nā iḷonnameva tatprīṇātyannaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*)
(Ai. Brā. 2-4)

Iḷa is said to be the food in the form of oblation to be offered in the sacrifice, and as the fruit of offering this food the sacrificer too gains food.

As explained above, the connection that Yāska shows between this word and the root indh is not clearly understood. Here Yāska has not stated the view of Kātthakya. In the Bṛhaddevatā:

इळस्तृषिकृतं रूपं ईडेशश्च स्तुतिकर्मणः । इळावांस्तेन वोक्तोग्निरिडिना वृद्धिकर्मणा ॥ (*iḷastṛṣikṛtaṃ rūpaṃ īḍeśaśca stutikarmaṇaḥ | iḷāvāṃstena voktogniriḍinā vṛddhikarmaṇā ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 3-4)

By these words it is shown that this word is of seer-origin and a synonymous name of Agni, and that the word इळावान् (*iḷāvān*) is an epithet of Agni.

गोमा अग्नेऽविमा अश्वी यज्ञो नृवत्सखा सदमिदप्रमृष्यः । इळावा एषो असुर प्रजावान्दीर्घो रयिः पृथुबुध्नः सभावान् ॥ (*gomā agne 'vimā aśvī yajño nṛvatsakhā sadamidapramṛṣyaḥ | iḷāvā eṣo asura prajāvāndīrgho rayiḥ pṛthubudhnaḥ sabhāvān ‖*)

In this Ṛk the word इळावान् (*iḷāvān*) is an epithet of Agni, so the Bṛhaddevatā points to that.

### Printed p. 619
Although such differences of tradition appear in the explanations, it may be said on the whole that the word is a synonymous name of the deity Agni, who holds the third place in the hymn.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि प्र॑थतां दे॒वजु॑ष्टं तिर॒श्चा दी॒र्घं द्रा॒घ्मा सु॑र॒भि भू॑त्व॒स्मे ।  
> अहे॑ळता॒ मन॑सा देव बर्हि॒रिंद्र॑ज्येष्ठा उश॒तो य॑क्षि दे॒वान् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । प्रथतां । देवजुष्टं । तिरश्चा । दीर्घं । द्राघ्मा । सुरभि । भूतु । अस्मे इति ।  
> अहेळता । मनसा । देव । बर्हिः । इंद्रज्येष्ठान् । उशतः । यक्षि । देवान् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे बर्हिर्नामकाग्ने देवजुष्टं देवैः सेवितं तिरश्चा तिरश्चीनं तिर्यगंचनमिदं बर्हिर्वि प्रथतां । विशेषेण विस्त्रतं भवतु । तथा दीर्घं चेदं द्राघ्मा
> दाघिम्ना ॥ दीर्घशब्दस्यॆमनिचि प्रियस्थिरेत्यादिना द्राघिरादेशः । अकारस्यॆकारोवर्णव्यापत्ता । पश्चादल्लोपः ॥ द्राघिम्ना युक्तं भवतु । अस्मे अस्मदीयं बर्हिः सुरभि
> सोमादिहनिर्निधानेन सुगंधं भूतु । भवतु । हे देव स्तोतमान हे बर्हिरेतन्नामकाग्ने अहेळता। हेल इति क्रोधनाम । अक्रुध्यता मनसोषतो हवींषि कामयमानानिंद्रज्येष्ठानिंद्रप्रधानान्देवान्यक्षि । यज । पूजय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa: O Agni, named Barhis, let this Barhis, cherished by the gods and lying crosswise, be spread out widely; let it be long and endowed with length (द्राघ्मा (*drāghmā*) means दाघिम्ना (*dāghimnā*)). Let our Barhis be fragrant through the placing of Soma and the oblations. O shining one, Agni named Barhis, अहेळता (*aheḷatā*): हेल (*hela*) is a name for anger, so with an unangered mind worship the gods who desire the oblations, of whom Indra is chief.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवजुष्टं (*devajuṣṭaṃ*)—cherished by the gods
- तिरश्चा (*tiraścā*)—lying twisted in a curved form
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—the Barhis (the excellent grass seat)
- वि प्रथतां (*vi prathatāṃ*)—let it be spread out
- दीर्घं (*dīrghaṃ*)—of long growth
- द्राघ्मा (*drāghmā*)—of great extent
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our Barhis
- सुरभि (*surabhi*)—fragrant
- भूतु (*bhūtu*)—let it be
- देव (*deva*)—O shining one
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—O Agni named Barhis
- अहेळता (*aheḷatā*)—free from wrath
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind
- उशतः (*uśataḥ*)—those desiring the oblation
- इंद्रज्येष्ठान् (*iṃdrajyeṣṭhān*)—those of whom Indra is chief
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the Barhis (grass seat), cherished by the gods and lying twisted in a curved form, be spread out. Let our Barhis, of long growth, be fragrant.

### Printed p. 620
O shining Agni named Barhis, with an unangered mind worship the gods who desire the oblation and of whom Indra is chief.

##### English translation
May our (sacred grass) acceptable to the gods twining crookedly be stretched out, may it be long, lengthy, and fragrant ; with mind free romf wrath, divine Barhis, offer worship to the gods desiring (the sacrifice), of whom Indra is the chief.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—This instrument has a more concrete form than the notions इध्मः (*idhmaḥ*) and ईळः (*īḷaḥ*). Barhis means simply the grass seat. As the doors are given a divine aspect by the words देवीः द्वारः (*devīḥ dvāraḥ*), no such thing is done for Barhis; only the sense of a seat of the gods is suggested. Moreover, the doors are entreated to open of themselves, without other help, and make a way for the gods' coming. Inanimate doors cannot open of their own accord and make a wide road unless they have divine power; but in the case of Barhis there is no attribution of this power. The priests must spread it. Not in this Ṛk alone, but in the other Ṛks of the Āprī hymns too, it is clearly said that the spreading of the Barhis must be done with the help of the priests and others. For example:

प्राचीनं बर्हिरोजसा सहस्रवीरमस्त्रणन् । यत्रादित्या विराजथ । (*prācīnaṃ barhirojasā sahasravīramastraṇan | yatrādityā virājatha |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-4)

In this Ṛk, and likewise in Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-4, बर्हिः प्राचीनमोजसा पवमानः स्तृणन् हरिः । (*barhiḥ prācīnamojasā pavamānaḥ stṛṇan hariḥ |*), there is the description that the priests spread the Barhis. Likewise in the Ṛks of the other Āprī hymns too the Barhis, though earthly and inanimate, is said to be a sacred seat for the gods. Only in the Praiṣa hymn,

होतायक्षद्बर्हिः सुष्टरीमोर्णंम्रदा अस्मिन्यज्ञे विचप्रच प्रथताग्ं स्वासस्थं देवेभ्यः । एमेनदस्य वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः सदंतु प्रियमिंद्रस्यास्तु वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर‍्यज ॥ (*hotāyakṣadbarhiḥ suṣṭarīmorṇaṃmradā asminyajñe vicapraca prathatāgṃ svāsasthaṃ devebhyaḥ | emenadasya vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ sadaṃtu priyamiṃdrasyāstu vetvājyasya hotaryaja ‖*)
(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1)

is it said, with बर्हिर्नामकं चतुर्थप्रयाजदेवमग्निं (*barhirnāmakaṃ caturthaprayājadevamagniṃ*), to be a seat that is a synonym of Agni and of the nature of a deity. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

बर्हिर्यजति । पशवो वै बर्हिः । पशूनेव तत्प्रीणाति पशून्यजमाने धदाति । (*barhiryajati | paśavo vai barhiḥ | paśūneva tatprīṇāti paśūnyajamāne dhadāti |*)
(Ai. Brā. 2-4.)

### Printed p. 621
it is explained as an animal that grazes on grass and is provided with grass. But it is understood that there is not the slightest room for this meaning.

The Nirukta author says बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् । (*barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt |*): because it grows swiftly, the darbha grass is named Barhis (Ni. 8-8). In the Bṛhaddevatā:

बर्हिरेवायमग्निस्तु सर्वं हि परिबृंहितं । अन्नेन यद्दुतो वा सन्निध्मेन परिबृंहितः ॥ (*barhirevāyamagnistu sarvaṃ hi paribṛṃhitaṃ | annena yadduto vā sannidhmena paribṛṃhitaḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 3-5)

Identity is stated thus: because all the food is pervaded by it, and because after the oblation it is filled up with fuel, Agni himself is present in the form of Barhis.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वो वा॒ सानु॑ स्पृ॒शता॒ वरी॑यः पृथि॒व्या वा॒ मात्र॑या॒ वि  ॑
> श्रयध्वं ।  
> उ॒श॒तीर्द्वा॑रो महि॒ना म॒हध्भि॑र्दे॒वं रथं॑ रथ॒युर्धा॑रयध्वं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवः । वा । सानु । स्पृशत । वरीयः । पृथिव्या । वा । मात्रया । वि । श्रयध्वं ।  
> उशतीः । द्वारः । महिना । महत्भिः । देवं । रथं । रथयुः । धारयध्वं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे द्वार एतन्नामधेया देव्यः यूयं दिवो वा । नाशब्दश्चार्थे । दिवश्च
> सानु समुच्च्रितं वरीय उरुतरं स्थानं स्पृशत । उन्नता भवतेत्यर्थः ॥ चवायोगे
> प्रथमेति न निघातः ॥ पृथिव्याश्च यावती मात्रास्ति तावत्या मात्रया वि श्रयध्वं ।
> विस्त्रता भवत । उशतीर्देवान्कामयमाना यूयं रथयुः ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति जसः
> सुः ॥ रथकामाः सत्यो महिना महिम्ना महद्भिर्देवैरधिष्ठितं अत एव देवं द्योतमानं रथं रमणसाधनं धारयध्वं । धारयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa: O goddesses named Doors, touch the lofty and wider region of heaven (वा (*vā*) here has the sense of "and"); that is, become high. And spread out to the full measure of the earth; become extended. Desiring the gods, being eager for the chariot (रथयुः (*rathayuḥ*)), in your greatness occupied by the great gods, therefore hold the shining chariot, the instrument of delight.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*)—O goddesses named Doors
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the world of the gods
- सानु (*sānu*)—situated on a high place
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—and wide place
- स्पृशत (*spṛśata*)—touch
- वा (*vā*)—

### Printed p. 622
**Pratipadārtha** (continued)
- अथवा (*athavā*)—or (and)
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- मात्रया (*mātrayā*)—according to the measure
- विश्रयध्वं (*viśrayadhvaṃ*)—attain expansion
- उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*)—you who desire the worship of the gods
- रथयुः (*rathayuḥ*)—desiring a chariot
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by your greatness
- महद्भिः (*mahadbhiḥ*)—by the gods of great nature, who have resorted to it
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—shining
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- धारयद्वं (*dhārayadvaṃ*)—sustain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddesses called the Doors, touch the lofty, extensive divine place of the world of the gods. Attain an expansion according to the measure of the earth. You who desire the worship of the gods, desiring a chariot, by your greatness sustain the shining chariot that the gods of great nature have resorted to.

##### English translation
Be in contact, doors, with the lofty height of heaven, or expand according to the measure of the earth; desiring the gods, desiring a chariot, sustain with your might the shining chariot (that is mounted) by the mighty gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-5, when the door-deities of the sacrificial house (दुरः (*duraḥ*)) are prayed to with देवीर्द्वारः (*devīrdvāraḥ*), a further peculiarity is that the names of the four doors, standing in the four directions of the sacrificial house, are indicated there. Other Āprī hymns do not have such names. Even so, it is reasonable to assign etymological meanings to words such as विराट् (*virāṭ*) and to treat them as epithets of the word दुरः (*duraḥ*). The commentator has made both kinds of attempt.

As to who these door-deities of the sacrificial house, द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*), are, Yāska gives this etymology:
द्वारः । द्वारो जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा । गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*dvāraḥ | dvāro javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā | gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-10)
A door is for entering, for going in, or for preventing going in; hence the name "door". The opinion of Kātthakya is that a door is the house-door; that of Śākapūṇi is that it is Agni. It is also said that the house where the oblation is made is the form of Agni, and therefore its doors are special forms of Agni (अग्नि विशेषमूर्तयः (*agni viśeṣamūrtayaḥ*)). "The doors of the chamber in which the oblation is offered are said to be personification of Agni." Sāyaṇa explains them as the presiding deities of the doors of the sacrificial house. There is a difference of opinion whether these doors are really the doors of the sacrificial house or merely a figurative usage.

### Printed p. 623
If the word here does not mean house-doors, then in the case of the deities of the Āprī hymns too, the points just stated apply, and different meanings must be conceived.

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:
दुरो यजति वृष्टिर्वै दुरो वृष्टिमेव तत्रीणाति वृष्टिमन्नाद्यं यजमाने दधाति । (*duro yajati vṛṣṭirvai duro vṛṣṭimeva tatrīṇāti vṛṣṭimannādyaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*)
Here, instead of the meaning "door", the meaning "rain" is given. How this meaning arises is not explained.

The Nirukta-author: द्वारो जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा । (*dvāro javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā |*) It is formed either from the root जु (*ju*) (meaning "press forward"), or from the root द्रु (*dru*) (meaning "advance"), or from the root वृ (*vṛ*) (meaning "separate"). Quoting the Ṛk
व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयंतां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानाः । देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥ (*vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayaṃtāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śuṃbhamānāḥ | devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-5 **NOTE**)
and explaining the word द्वार (*dvāra*), he states the difference of opinion: गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः । (*gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ |*) — according to Kātthakya, the house-door; अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ |*) — according to Śākapūṇi, Agni (Ni. 8-10). In the Bṛhaddevatā:
द्वारस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्ता विश्वेषां तास्तु पत्नयः । अग्नायीमनुवर्तंते तथाग्नाय्यग्निमेव च ॥ अग्नौ ध्रुवं स्थितास्तास्तु संस्तूयंतेऽग्निना सह । प्राधान्यं तासु चैवाग्ने स्तुतिष्टेव हविष्णु च ॥ (*dvārastu devyo yāḥ proktā viśveṣāṃ tāstu patnayaḥ | agnāyīmanuvartaṃte tathāgnāyyagnimeva ca ‖ agnau dhruvaṃ sthitāstāstu saṃstūyaṃte 'gninā saha | prādhānyaṃ tāsu caivāgne stutiṣṭeva haviṣṇu ca ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-6 to 7)
It is said that these doors are wives of the gods; that they follow Agnāyī (Agni's wife), who follows Agni; and that, being firmly established in Agni, they are praised together with Agni. This is consistent.

Concerning the preparation of the four doors of the sacrificial house, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā describes it thus:
प्राचीनवग्‌ंशं करोति देवमनुष्या दिशो व्यभजंत प्राचीं देवा दक्षिणा पितरः प्रतीचीं मनुष्या उदीचीग्‌० रुद्राः ॥ (*prācīnavagṃśaṃ karoti devamanuṣyā diśo vyabhajaṃta prācīṃ devā dakṣiṇā pitaraḥ pratīcīṃ manuṣyā udīcīg0 rudrāḥ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-1-1)
That is: the gods took the eastern door of the sacrificial house, the Pitṛ-deities the southern, men the western, and the (eleven) Rudras the northern.

### Printed p. 624
The names of the doors of this sacrificial house, as given in 1-188-5, are as follows: विराट् (*virāṭ*) may be said to be the eastern door, सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*) the southern door, विभ्वीः (*vibhvīḥ*) the western door, and प्रभ्वीः (*prabhvīḥ*) the northern door. Sāyaṇa has explained the etymological meaning of these words there itself.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वी दि॒वो दु॑हि॒तरा॑ सुशि॒ल्पे उ॒षासा॒नक्ता॑ सदतां॒ नि योन् ॑।  
> आ वां॑ दे॒वास॑ उशती उ॒शंत॑ उ॒रौ सी॑दंतु सुभगे उ॒पस्थे॑ ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवी इति । दिवः । दुहितरा । सुशिल्पे इति सुशिल्पे । उषासानक्ता । सदतां । नि ।  
> योन्सौ ।  
> आ । वां । देवासः । उशती इति । उशंतः । उरौ । सीदंतु । सुभगे इति सुभगे ।  
> उपस्थे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवी द्योतमाने दिवो द्युलोकस्य दुहितरा दुहितरौ सुशिल्पे शोभनरूपे उषासानक्कोषाश्च नक्तं चाहोरात्र्योन् योन् यज्ञस्य स्थाने नि सदतां ।
> निषीदतां । हे उशती उशत्यौ कामयमाने हे सुभगे शोभनधने हे देव्यौ
> वां युवयोरुर् विस्तीर्णं उपस्थे समीपस्थे स्थान उशंतो हवींषि कामयमाना देवासो देवा आ सीदंतु । उपविशंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

देवी (*devī*) means the two shining ones; दिवः दुहितरा (*divaḥ duhitarā*) the two daughters of the heaven-world; सुशिल्पे (*suśilpe*) those of beautiful form; उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) Dawn and Night, that is, the day-and-night pair. Let them sit down in the योन् (*yon*), the place of the sacrifice (नि सदतां (*ni sadatāṃ*) = let them sit down). "O you two who desire (उशती (*uśatī*)), O you of good fortune (सुभगे (*subhage*)), that is, of beautiful wealth, O goddesses: in your spacious (उरौ (*urau*)) lap (उपस्थे (*upasthe*)), your near place, let the gods (देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)), desiring (उशंतः (*uśaṃtaḥ*)) the oblations, sit down (आ सीदंतु (*ā sīdaṃtu*)), take their seats."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवी (*devī*)—shining ones
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heaven-world
- दुहितरा (*duhitarā*)—daughters
- सुशिल्पे (*suśilpe*)—of excellent form
- उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*)—O deities of day and night
- योन्सौ (*yonsau*)—in the place of sacrifice
- नि सदतां (*ni sadatāṃ*)—sit down
- उशती (*uśatī*)—you who desire wealth
- सुभगे (*subhage*)—O deities who possess excellent wealth
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- उरौ (*urau*)—spacious
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—in the near place
- उशंतः (*uśaṃtaḥ*)—desiring the oblation
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- अ सीदंतु (*a sīdaṃtu*)—let them sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities of day and night, shining, daughters of the heaven-world, of excellent form, sit down in the place of sacrifice. O deities who desire wealth and possess excellent wealth, in your spacious

### Printed p. 625
near place let the gods who desire the oblation sit down.

##### English translation
Radiant daughters of heaven, Dawn and Night, sit down on the place of sacrifice; O you, who are desirous and possessed of affluence, may the gods desirous (of oblations) sit down on your spacious lap.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the presiding deities of night and morning, नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*), are invoked. Yāska's explanation of the word नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) is as follows.
उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्कोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा व्याख्याता । नक्तेति रात्रिनामानक्ति भूतन्यवश्यायेनापि ना नक्ताव्यक्तवर्णा ॥ (*uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānakkoṣāśca naktā coṣā vyākhyātā | nakteti rātrināmānakti bhūtanyavaśyāyenāpi nā naktāvyaktavarṇā ‖*)
Whether read नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) or उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), the meaning is one. The explanation of the word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) we have given earlier. नक्ता (*naktā*) is a name of night. For नक्ता (*naktā*) means "of indistinct colour": because of the darkness, things are indistinct, that is, not seen well. So the night accompanied by darkness is called नक्ता (*naktā*), and in the night creatures are unable to do their activities. अनक्ति क्लेदयति भूतानि अवश्यायेन । (*anakti kledayati bhūtāni avaśyāyena |*) Or else अपि वानक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा । यथा अहः सर्वमभिव्यक्तरूपं भवति न तथा रात्रिः ॥ (*api vānaktā avyaktavarṇā | yathā ahaḥ sarvamabhivyaktarūpaṃ bhavati na tathā rātriḥ ‖*) Since the darkness troubles creatures so that their activities cannot proceed properly, the night accompanied by such darkness is called नक्ता (*naktā*); or because everything is indistinct, not seen well, it is called नक्ता (*naktā*). By day the forms of all things are clearly seen; in the night they are not. Therefore the time of night is called नक्ता (*naktā*), so he has explained (Ni. 8-11).

It has been said that the explanation of the word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) was given earlier. That explanation is as follows: sixteen words beginning with विभावरी (*vibhāvarī*), सूनरी (*sūnarī*) are names of Dawn (2-19), and उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥ (*uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ‖*) Because it removes the darkness of the night-time it is called उषाः (*uṣāḥ*); that is, the latter part of the night. To support this meaning he (Yāska) gives an example—

### Printed p. 626
इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा । यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सावाय एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥ (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ sāvāya evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1)
The Nirukta on this quarter-verse:
इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य । एवं रात्रुषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानं । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुत एनां गर्भः ॥ (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasya | evaṃ rātruṣase yonimaricat sthānaṃ | strīyonirabhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 2-19)
The best and most brilliant light of the sun is rising. The Dawn-time, which precedes the sun's light, appears before the light like its banner. How? Just as the sun's light shines all day and at sunset becomes the womb (yoni), that is, the cause, of night, so the night at its end becomes the womb, that is, the cause, of the Dawn-time. योनि (*yoni*) means birthplace. The main idea is that at the end of day comes night, and at the end of night the Dawn-time, each arriving as a change into the next. Therefore उषः (*uṣaḥ*) means the radiance, the light, that spreads over all directions and appears before sunrise, after the night has passed.

The commentator's (Sāyaṇa's) explanation: नक्तशब्द उषश्यब्दश्च लोके कालविशेष वाचिन् । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानिवह्निमूर्तिद्वये प्रयुज्येते । नक्तोषासा नक्तोषोनामिके वह्निमूर्ति (*naktaśabda uṣaśyabdaśca loke kālaviśeṣa vācin | iha tu tatkālābhimānivahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣonāmike vahnimūrti*)—that is, in common usage the two words नक्ता (*naktā*) (night) and उषः (*uṣaḥ*) (morning) denote times; but in this Ṛk, or in the Ṛgveda, these words convey the meaning of the presiding deities of night and morning. Therefore the words नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) or उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) are used in the sense of two forms (mūrti) of Agni, the presiding deities of night and of the Dawn-time. The word सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) (of good form or shape) used in places supports this meaning. For night and morning, being divisions of time, have neither form nor shape; if they are said to be the presiding deities of those times, a form can be assigned to those deities. Since such an indication is found in this Ṛk, it should be understood that the presiding deities of those times are what is meant here. The long vowel in नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) is lengthened for the convenience of the metre.

The epithet ऋतस्य मातणा (*ṛtasya mātaṇā*) in Ṛk Saṃ. 1-142-7 is very important.
द्रवतां त उषसा वाजयंती अग्ने वातस्य पथ्याभिरच्छ । ऋत्सीमंजंति पूर्व्यं हविर्भिरा वंधुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे ॥ (*dravatāṃ ta uṣasā vājayaṃtī agne vātasya pathyābhiraccha | ṛtsīmaṃjaṃti pūrvyaṃ havirbhirā vaṃdhureva tasthaturduroṇe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-14-3)

### Printed p. 627
In this Ṛk their constant relation to the sacrifice is described. In all the Ṛks that invoke them (there are about twenty such Ṛks) the prayer is that they come with the other gods and sit on the darbha seat. Moreover, they have a very close relation with Agni, who is kindled at dawn and at evening. Hence the figurative description that they bear and hold Agni among us.
नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची । द्यावाक्षामा रुक्मो अंतर्वि भाति देवा अग्निं धारयन्द्र विणोदां ॥ (*naktoṣāsā varṇamāmemyāne dhāpayete śiśumekaṃ samīcī | dyāvākṣāmā rukmo aṃtarvi bhāti devā agniṃ dhārayandra viṇodāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-5)
In such Ṛks it is stated that they help Agni, in the form of an infant, to drink the oblation. Because of this relation they are said to be near the sacrificers. In the Āprī hymns generally this point is repeated. For example:
आसुष्वयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योन् । दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥ (*āsuṣvayaṃtī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yon | divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6)
The same matter is stated in this verse of the Āprī hymn.

From this it is understood that the deities Dawn and Night have in the sacrificial rites no subordinate place but a very important one. This principal position is indicated in the mantra of the Praiṣa hymn:
होतायक्षदुषासानक्ता बृहती सुपेशसा नृग्ः पतिभ्यो योनिं कृष्णाने । सग्स् स्मयमाने इंद्रेण देवैरेदं बर्हिः सीदतां वीतामाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (*hotāyakṣaduṣāsānaktā bṛhatī supeśasā nṛgḥ patibhyo yoniṃ kṛṣṇāne | sags smayamāne iṃdreṇa devairedaṃ barhiḥ sīdatāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaraja ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1)
In it the prayer is that Dawn and Night sit on the darbha seat not only with Agni but also with Indra and the other gods. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa they are addressed as अहोरात्रे (*ahorātre*). The Nirukta-author in 8-11 has explained the nature of these deities; the derivation of the two words उषस् (*uṣas*) and नक्ता (*naktā*) and the nature of these deities as stated by the Nirukta-author were given earlier. In the Bṛhaddevatā too they are described thus:
नक्कोषासौ च ये देव्यावाग्नेय्यावेव ते स्मृते । श्यान्याग्नेयी हि कालस्य तस्यैवोषाः कलेव तु ॥ (*nakkoṣāsau ca ye devyāvāgneyyāveva te smṛte | śyānyāgneyī hi kālasya tasyaivoṣāḥ kaleva tu ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-8)
Both deities, Dawn and Night, are well known to be connected with Agni. Of these, त्यावि (*tyāvi*) (the night-deity, 1-71-1) has a close relation with Agni, and

### Printed p. 628
The Nirukta sentence उषः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣaḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*) (Ni. 2-18) shows that Uṣas is the latter part of that night.

तम उच्छत्युषा नक्तानक्तीमां हिमबिंदुभिः । अपि वाव्यक्तवर्णेति नइद् पूर्वांचीरिदं भवेत् ॥ (*tama ucchatyuṣā naktānaktīmāṃ himabiṃdubhiḥ | api vāvyaktavarṇeti naid pūrvāṃcīridaṃ bhavet ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-9)

Of these two, Uṣas drives away the darkness. Night makes everything wet and pervaded with drops of dew. Or else, because she has no distinct colour, the root अञ्ज्न् (*añjn*) joins with the word नञ् (*nañ*) and gives the sense "of indistinct colour".

सा हि दोषा भवत्यादौ निशीथे सा तमस्वती । नाम्ना भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्रागुदयाद्रवेः ॥ (*sā hi doṣā bhavatyādau niśīthe sā tamasvatī | nāmnā bhavatyuṣāścaiva saiṣā prāgudayādraveḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-10)

At the beginning this goddess is called Doṣā, at midnight Tamasvatī, and before sunrise Uṣas. Doṣā, Tamasvatī, Śyāvī and Naktā are all read in the Nighaṇṭu as names of night. (Nighaṇṭu 1-7)

Elsewhere in the Ṛksaṃhitā, with epithets such as तंतुं ततं संवयंती (*taṃtuṃ tataṃ saṃvayaṃtī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-6), the help of Uṣāsānaktā in extending the sacrifice is described.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒र्ध्वो ग्रावा॑ बृ॒हद॒ग्निः समि॑द्धः प्रि॒या धामा॒न्यदि॑तेरु॒पस्थे॑ ।  
> पु॒रोहि॑तावृत्विजा य॒ज्ञे अ॒स्मिन् वि॒दुष्ट॑रा॒ द्रवि॑ण॒मा  ॑
> यजेथां ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊर्ध्वः । ग्रावा । बृहत् । अग्निः । संइद्धः । प्रिया । धामानि । अदितेः । उपस्थे ।  
> पुरःहिता । ऋत्विजा । यज्ञे । अस्मिन् । विदुःतरा । द्रविणं । आ । यजेथां ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ग्रावा सोमाभिषवाय यदोर्ध्व उन्नतो भवति यदा च बृहन्महानग्निः
> समिद्धो हविर्भिः सम्यग्दीपो भवति । तथा प्रियाणि देवानां सोमादिहविष्पदा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: when the pressing-stone is raised up for pressing the Soma, and when the great Agni is well kindled by the oblations, and when the vessels that hold the oblations, dear to the gods because they are made to hold Soma and other offerings, are set down on the lap of Aditi, the earth, that is, in the sacrificial place — then, O two priests, divine, set in front (the two hotṛs), most learned (he notes a Vedic vowel-change in विदुष्टरा (*viduṣṭarā*))...

### Printed p. 629

> नेन प्रीणयित्यणि धामानि हविषां धारकाणि यज्ञपात्राण्यदितेः पृथिव्या उपस्थे
> यज्ञसदने यदासादितानि भवंति तदानीं हे ऋत्विजौ देव्यौ पुरोहितौ होतार्
> पुरतो निहितौ विदुष्टरा ॥ छांदसं संप्रसारणं ॥ विद्वत्तमौ युवामस्मिन्यज्ञे
> द्रविणं धनमा यजेथां । यजिर्दानार्थः । अस्मभ्यमाभिमुख्येन प्रयच्छृतं ॥
> ग्रावा—सोमवन्नु हिंडुव कल्लुगळु । ऊर्ध्वः—यावाग मेल्मुखवागुवुवो आग ।
> बृहत्—महत्स्वरूपवुळ्ळ । अग्निः—अग्नियु । समिद्धः—प्रज्वलितनागुत्तानॆ । प्रिया—
> देवतॆगळिगॆ प्रीतिकरवाद । धामानि—हविस्सन्नु हॊंदिरुव पात्रॆगळु । अदितेः—पृथ्विय ।
> उपस्थे—यज्ञ स्थानदल्लि सिद्धवागुत्तवॆ (आ कूडले) । ऋत्विजा—ऋत्विग्रूपरू । पुरोहिता—
> होतृरूपरू । विदुष्टरा—विद्यावतियरू आद ऎलै देवतॆगळे । (युवां—नीवु) । अस्मिन्
> यज्ञे—ई यज्ञदल्लि । द्रविणं—धनवन्नु । आ यजेथां—कॊडुत्तीरि.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

...in this sacrifice bestow wealth. The root यजि (*yaji*) has the sense of giving: "give it to us, turned towards us."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रावा (*grāvā*)—the stones that press the Soma
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—when they are turned upward, then
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—of great form
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—becomes kindled
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—pleasing to the gods
- धामानि (*dhāmāni*)—the vessels holding the oblation
- अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)—of the earth
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—in the sacrificial place they are made ready (at once)
- ऋत्विजा (*ṛtvijā*)—who are of the nature of priests
- पुरोहिता (*purohitā*)—who are of the nature of hotṛs
- विदुष्टरा (*viduṣṭarā*)—who are most learned, O gods
- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—you
- अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*asmin yajñe*)—in this sacrifice
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—wealth
- आ यजेथां (*ā yajethāṃ*)—you give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the stones that press the Soma are turned upward, the mighty Agni is kindled. The vessels, pleasing to the gods and holding the oblation, are made ready in the sacrificial place. Immediately then, O gods who are priests, hotṛs and learned ones, you give wealth in this sacrifice.

##### English translation
(When) the grinding-stone is uplifted, the mighty Agni kindled, the acceptable vessels (ready) on the lap of earth ; (then), most learned priests, who take the foremost place, bestow wealth upon us at tkis sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

देवसंबंधिनौ होतारौ । अयं च मध्यमस्थानश्च (*devasaṃbaṃdhinau hotārau | ayaṃ ca madhyamasthānaśca*) — Sāyaṇa has explained the two as the two forms of Agni, the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere, both related to the gods and both hotṛs. Some modern scholars give different meanings and differ among themselves. Gelder takes them as the sacrificer-hotṛ and his fire; Haug as the hotṛ and the adhvaryu; Oldenberg as the hotṛ and his assistant the Maitrāvaruṇa. None of these is acceptable.

That the chief duty of these hotṛs is to perform the sacrifice is stated in the Ṛks 1-13-8 and 1-18-7 as यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं । (*yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ |*), and in Ṛk 2-3-2 as देवान्यजंतावृतुथा । (*devānyajaṃtāvṛtuthā |*)

### Printed p. 630
This statement of duty applies to the human hotṛ, and the address to Agni is figurative.

Yāska's explanation of the word दैन्व्या होतारा (*dainvyā hotārā*) is: दैन्व्याहोतारा दैन्व्याहोतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः ॥ (*dainvyāhotārā dainvyāhotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-12). That is, this word indicates Agni; since Agni invokes the gods, Agni stands between gods and men; he gave an example in this matter:

दैन्व्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै । प्रचोदयंता विधथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता ॥ (*dainvyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai | pracodayaṃtā vidhatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśaṃtā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-7)

Durgācārya's commentary on it is:
यावेत् दैन्यौ होतारौ । देवेषु भवौ दैन्यौ देवावेव दैव्यौ । स्वार्थे एव तद्धितः । मनुष्यहोतारौ अपेक्ष्य । दैन्यौ होतारौ होतृमैत्रावरुणौ इति विशेषणं । होतारा होतारौ आह्वातारौ देवानां वाय्वग्नी । प्रथमा प्रथमौ मुख्यौ मनुष्यहोतारावपेक्ष्य । सुवाचा सुवाचौ, प्रशस्तवाचौ, सुस्तुता । मिनीना यज्ञं यज्ञनिर्मातारौ नित्यं । मनुष्यः मनुष्यस्य यजध्यै यजनाम । प्रयोदयंता प्रचोदयमानौ । विदथेषु यज्ञेषु । कारू कर्तारौ । इत्यादि ॥ (*yāvet dainyau hotārau | deveṣu bhavau dainyau devāveva daivyau | svārthe eva taddhitaḥ | manuṣyahotārau apekṣya | dainyau hotārau hotṛmaitrāvaruṇau iti viśeṣaṇaṃ | hotārā hotārau āhvātārau devānāṃ vāyvagnī | prathamā prathamau mukhyau manuṣyahotārāvapekṣya | suvācā suvācau, praśastavācau, sustutā | minīnā yajñaṃ yajñanirmātārau nityaṃ | manuṣyaḥ manuṣyasya yajadhyai yajanāma | prayodayaṃtā pracodayamānau | vidatheṣu yajñeṣu | kārū kartārau | ityādi ‖*)

Its main sense is this: for the gods, Agni and Vāyu are the hotṛs; for men, the priests called Hotṛ and Maitrāvaruṇa are the hotṛs. Since Agni, or Agni and Vāyu, stand between gods and men and connect them, Agni is also said to be the middle one.

The name of the deities दैव्या होतारौ (*daivyā hotārau*) occurs not only in the Āprī hymns but also in these two Ṛks:

त्वष्टारं वायुमृभवो य ओहते दैव्या होतारा उषसं स्वस्तये । (*tvaṣṭāraṃ vāyumṛbhavo ya ohate daivyā hotārā uṣasaṃ svastaye |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-10)

दैन्व्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहित ऋतस्य पंथामन्वेमि साधुया । (*dainvyā hotārā prathamā purohita ṛtasya paṃthāmanvemi sādhuyā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-66 13)

In Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2.7 they are called जादवेदसा (*jādavedasā*) and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30-7 पुरोहितौ (*purohitau*). And since the words in the Ṛks above — मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै (*mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai*), यज्ञेषु मानुषेषु कारू (*yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kārū*) and प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू (*pracodayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū*) — say that these deities carry out the sacrifices made by men, it is natural that they are called purohitas.

### Printed p. 631
Among the gods the hotṛs are Agni and Vāyu; among men the Hotṛ and his assistant priest Maitrāvaruṇa are called the hotṛs. This Maitrāvaruṇa, by the Praiṣa mantras, commands the other priests to do their respective duties. In the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6.1.4 2) it is said: मैत्रावरुणो हि पुरस्तादृत्विग्यो वाचं विभजति (*maitrāvaruṇo hi purastādṛtvigyo vācaṃ vibhajati*).

Thus some epithets are common to the two hotṛs and yet indicate the duty of the human hotṛ; others, also common to both, describe the duties of Agni, the divine hotṛ. For example:

दैव्या होतारा प्रथमान्यृंजे सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदंति । ऋतं शंसंत ऋतमित्त आहुरनु व्रतं व्रतपा दीध्यानाः । (*daivyā hotārā prathamānyṛṃje sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ svadhayā madaṃti | ṛtaṃ śaṃsaṃta ṛtamitta āhuranu vrataṃ vratapā dīdhyānāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-7)

In this Ṛk there is no doubt that the epithet प्रथमा (*prathamā*) refers to Agni, the divine hotṛ. In 1-13-4 होता मनुर्हितः (*hotā manurhitaḥ*) is an epithet of Agni. The exact difference between the two hotṛs is stated in the Praiṣa hymn thus:

होतायक्षद्दैव्या होतारा मंद्रा पोतारा कवी प्रचेतसा । स्विष्टमद्यान्यः करदिषा स्वभिगूर्तमन्य ऊर्जा सतवसेमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धत्तां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥ (*hotāyakṣaddaivyā hotārā maṃdrā potārā kavī pracetasā | sviṣṭamadyānyaḥ karadiṣā svabhigūrtamanya ūrjā satavasemaṃ yajñaṃ divi deveṣu dhattāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaryaja ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

In this passage one hotṛ is asked to make the sacrifice acceptable with the oblation that is food, and the other to establish this sacrifice in heaven among the gods. This division of work shows the difference between the human hotṛ and Agni, the divine hotṛ.

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:
दैव्या होतारा यजति प्राणापानौ वै दैव्या होतारा प्राणापानावेव तत्प्रीणाति प्राणापानौ यजमाने थदाति ॥ (*daivyā hotārā yajati prāṇāpānau vai daivyā hotārā prāṇāpānāveva tatprīṇāti prāṇāpānau yajamāne thadāti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 2-4)
Thus it states the identity of these hotṛs with prāṇa and apāna, and says that whoever recites this mantra secures for the sacrificer a good state of prāṇa and apāna. In the Nirukta, दैव्या होतारा दैव्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः । (*daivyā hotārā daivyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ |*) — with these supporting passages for Sāyaṇa's meaning — they are said to be the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere. The Bṛhaddevatā, too, approving the same view,

### Printed p. 632
दैव्याविति तु होतारावग्नी पार्थिवमध्यम् । दिव्यादग्नेर्हि जज्ञाते दैव्यौ तेनेह जन्मना ॥ (*daivyāviti tu hotārāvagnī pārthivamadhyam | divyādagnerhi jajñāte daivyau teneha janmanā ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-11)
says that the two hotṛs are the Agnis of the terrestrial and middle (atmospheric) station.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तिस्रो॑ देवीर्ब॒हिरि॒दं वरी॑य॒ आ सी॑दत चक्र॒मा वः॑ स्यो॒नं ।  
> म॒नु॒ष्वद्य॒ज्ञं सुधि॑ता ह॒वींषीळा॑ दे॒वी घृ॒तप॑दी जुषंत ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तिस्रः । देवीः । बर्हिः । इदं । वरीयः । आ । सीदत । चक्रम । वः । स्योनं ।  
> मनुष्वत् । यज्ञं । सुधिता । हवींषि । इळा । देवी । धृतपदी । जुषंत ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे तिस्रो देवीरिळाद्यास्तिस्रो देव्यः वरीय उरुतरमिदं बर्हिरा सीदत ॥
> कालाध्वनोरिति द्वितीया ॥ अत्यंतं तस्मिन्निषीदत । कुत एतत् तत्राह। वो युष्मदर्थं
> स्योनं विस्तीर्णमिदं चकृम । वयं कृतवंतः ॥ वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥ इळ्ळैतन्नामिका
> देवी द्योतमाना सरस्वती धृतपदी दीप्तपदोपेता भारती चैता मनुष्टन्मनोर्यज्ञे यथा हवींष्यसेवंत तद्वदस्मदीयं यज्ञं सुधिता सुष्टु निहितानि हवींषि
> च जुषंत । सेवतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O three goddesses, Iḷā and the others, sit on this very broad barhis (the accusative is used in the sense of duration, "sit on it continuously"). Why? Because we have made it spread wide and comfortable for you. The accent is not lowered because the sentences are separate. The goddess named Iḷā, the shining Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī with shining feet — as they enjoyed the oblations in Manu's sacrifice, so let them enjoy our sacrifice and the well-placed oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तिस्रः देवीः (*tisraḥ devīḥ*)—O three goddesses, Iḷā and the others
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—very wide
- इदं बर्हिः (*idaṃ barhiḥ*)—on this seat of darbha grass
- आ सीदत (*ā sīdata*)—sit down
- वः (*vaḥ*)—for you
- स्योनं चक्रम (*syonaṃ cakrama*)—we have spread this seat widely
- इळा (*iḷā*)—the goddess Iḷā
- देवी (*devī*)—the shining Sarasvatī
- धृतपदी (*dhṛtapadī*)—Bhāratī with shining feet
- मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*)—as accepted in Manu's sacrifice
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—in our sacrifice
- सुधिता (*sudhitā*)—well placed
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations
- जुषंत (*juṣaṃta*)—let them enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddesses, Iḷā and the others, sit on this very broad seat of darbha grass. We have spread this seat widely for you. Let the goddess Iḷā, the shining Sarasvatī and Bhāratī with radiant feet enjoy the well-placed oblations in this sacrifice of ours, as they were accepted in Manu's sacrifice.

### Printed p. 633

##### English translation
Sit down, you three goddesses; upon this broad barhis, we have spread it out for you ; Ila, radiant (Saraswati) and bright-footed (Bharati) accept our sacrificee and well-presented oblations as if they were Manu's.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk a group of three goddesses is addressed and prayed to come to the sacrifice. In all the Āprī hymns except the present one and hymn 1-142, these goddesses are together indicated collectively as तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*). The three are Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī. There is much difference of opinion about the nature of these deities. In 1-142 the goddess Bhāratī has the epithets होत्रा (*hotrā*), शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) (मरुत्सु (*marutsu*), देवेषु (*deveṣu*)), अर्पिता (*arpitā*), and the goddess Sarasvatī the epithet मही (*mahī*). In some hymns the word मही (*mahī*) is an epithet used as a substitute for the goddess Bhāratī. Whether the nature of these deities can be ascertained exactly here may be examined with Śruti and similar passages as authority.

On तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*) Yāska says only तिस्रो देवीः । तिस्रो देवीस्तिस्रो देव्यः । (*tisro devīḥ | tisro devīstisro devyaḥ |*) and then explains the Ṛk given as example:

आ नो यज्ञं भारती तेयमेत्विळा मनुष्पदिह चेतयंती । तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्कोनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदंतु ॥ (*ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī teyametviḷā manuṣpadiha cetayaṃtī | tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ skonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadaṃtu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8)

ऐतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यो जर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकर्माण आसीदंतु ॥ (*aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyadiha cetayamānā tisro devyo jarhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu ‖*)

That is: Bhāratī — Bharata is one of the twelve Ādityas. The radiance of the Āditya is called भा (*bhā*). Therefore Bhāratī is the light of the sun, or the Agni present as light in the solar orb. Iḷā — Iḷā is the earth. मनुष्यत् चेतयंती (*manuṣyat cetayaṃtī*) — having the power to impel like men; that is, because she gives food and wealth to men on earth, Iḷā is a particular form of Agni in the earth's station. Sarasvatī — because she is the presiding deity of the thunder and lightning in the atmosphere, Sarasvatī is also said to be a form of Agni in the atmospheric station.

### Printed p. 634
Therefore it is customary to say that the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī are the three forms of Agni, who is in heaven, in the atmosphere and on the earth.

If one examines the mantra that collects the main points of the Āprī hymns:

होतायक्षत्तिस्रो देवीरसामपस्तमा अच्छिद्रमद्येदमपस्तन्वतां । देवेभ्यो देवीर्देवमपो वियंत्वाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (*hotāyakṣattisro devīrasāmapastamā acchidramadyedamapastanvatāṃ | devebhyo devīrdevamapo viyaṃtvājyasya hotaraja ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

In the original text there is only "तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*)" (the three goddesses). While explaining this, the bhāṣya says: इडा सरस्वती, भारतीत्येवं रूपास्ति स्रोऽष्टम प्रयाजदेव्यस्तद्रूपमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (*iḍā sarasvatī, bhāratītyevaṃ rūpāsti sro 'ṣṭama prayājadevyastadrūpamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu*). That is, the three goddesses Iḍā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, the deities of the eighth Prayāja, are said to be deities who reflect Agni. Further, by the epithet अपसां अपस्तमाः । कर्मवतीनां मध्येऽतिशयेन कर्मवत्यः (*apasāṃ apastamāḥ | karmavatīnāṃ madhye 'tiśayena karmavatyaḥ*) they are shown to be the most excellent of the active (women). In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

तिस्रो देवीर्यजति प्राणो ना अपानो व्यानस्ति स्रो देव्यस्ता एव तत्रीणाति ता यजमाने दधाति । (*tisro devīryajati prāṇo nā apāno vyānasti sro devyastā eva tatrīṇāti tā yajamāne dadhāti |*) (Ai. Brā. 2-4)

Thus an identity is stated between the three goddesses and the vital principles prāṇa, apāna and vyāna. The Nirukta-author quotes the Ṛk 10-110-8 beginning आ नो यज्ञं (*ā no yajñaṃ*) and gives its explanation thus: ऐतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं ! भरत आदित्यस्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यवदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्याः बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकर्माण आसीदंतु । (*aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ ! bharata ādityasyastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyavadiha cetayamānā tisro devyāḥ barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu |*) (Ni. 8-13). "May the deity who is the radiance of Bharata (the Sun), and Iḷā and Sarasvatī adorn the barhis." In the Bṛhaddevatā:

तिस्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास्त्रिस्थानैवेह सा तु वाक् । त्रिविधेनोच्यते नाम्ना ज्योतिःषु त्रिषु वर्तिनी ॥ अग्निमेवानुगेळा तु मध्यं प्राप्ता सरस्वती । अमू स्थिताधि लोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ ॥ सैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि च व्योम्मि चेह च । व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजत्यग्नीमानपि ॥ (*tisrastu devyo yāḥ proktāstristhānaiveha sā tu vāk | trividhenocyate nāmnā jyotiḥṣu triṣu vartinī ‖ agnimevānugeḷā tu madhyaṃ prāptā sarasvatī | amū sthitādhi lokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau ‖ saiṣā tu trividhā vāgvai divi ca vyommi ceha ca | vyastā caiva samastā ca bhajatyagnīmānapi ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-12 to 14)

"The three goddesses" are the presiding deities of speech in the three worlds (the three forms of speech are described in Bṛ. De. 2-72 to 82). अयं प्रयोगस्वेतेषां ज्योतिषां त्रिषु वर्ततां । (*ayaṃ prayogasveteṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ triṣu vartatāṃ |*) (Bṛ. De. 1-90).

### Printed p. 635
As is said there, the different deities in the three worlds are forms of one deity of speech. Of these, Iḷā followed the terrestrial Agni, Sarasvatī occupied the middle world, and Bhāratī became resident of the heavenly world. Even so, in the statement

देव्यस्ति स्रः श्रिताश्चैनं त्वष्टा चैवैतदाश्रयः । (*devyasti sraḥ śritāścainaṃ tvaṣṭā caivaitadāśrayaḥ |*) (Bṛ. De. 1-108)

it is said that the deities of these three worlds also serve the terrestrial Agni alone; thus everything is concluded in the end as relating to Agni.

In the Ṛk

इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः । बर्हिः सीदंत्वस्रिधः ॥ (*iḷā sarasvatī mahī tisro devīrmayobhuvaḥ | barhiḥ sīdaṃtvasridhaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1 13-9)

and also in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5-8, which has the same order, the name Bhāratī is not mentioned; therefore Sāyaṇa has said that mahī is a synonym of the goddess Bhāratī. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-8 and in the Ṛk

भारती पवमानस्य सरस्वतीळा मही । इमं नो यज्ञमा गमनिस्तो देवीः सुपेशसः ॥ (*bhāratī pavamānasya sarasvatīḷā mahī | imaṃ no yajñamā gamanisto devīḥ supeśasaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-8)

it is also an epithet.

Iḷā: Since the Bṛhaddevatā says अग्निमेवानुरागेळा (*agnimevānurāgeḷā*) (3-13), that Iḷā followed the terrestrial Agni; and since in the Ṛk

प्रदीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै । अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वंदध्यै स देवान्यक्ष दिषितो यजीयान् ॥ (*pradīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai | acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vaṃdadhyai sa devānyakṣa diṣito yajīyān ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3)

the word इळः (*iḷaḥ*) is explained as food in the form of oblation; and since in Ṛk 7-16-8 the epithet धृतहस्ता (*dhṛtahastā*) and in 10-20-8 the epithet धृतपदी (*dhṛtapadī*) occur, it seems that Iḷā can be explained as oblation. Probably for this reason, in the Ṛk

उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान्त्सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान । अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास्पुत्रो वयुनेऽजनिष्ट ॥ (*uttānāyāmava bharā cikitvāntsadyaḥ pravītā vṛṣaṇaṃ jajāna | aruṣastūpo ruśadasya pāja iḷāyāsputro vayune 'janiṣṭa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-3)

(Agni) is also called the son of Iḷā.

Bhāratī: The Nirukta says she is the radiance of the Āditya (भरतः आदित्यः तस्य भाः (*bharataḥ ādityaḥ tasya bhāḥ*)). The scholar Macdonell, in his book Vedic Mythology, explains her as the oblation offered by the Bharata clan (p. 87), and Grassmann as the goddess of speech; or she may be explained as related to Agni.

### Printed p. 636
In the Ṛk

तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्योक्षश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं । य इंद्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणां ॥ (*tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajyokṣaśyātsūryamuccaraṃtaṃ | ya iṃdrāya sunavāmetyāha nare naryāya nṛtamāya nṛṇāṃ ‖*) (Mṛ. Saṃ. 4-25-4)

भारतः (*bhārataḥ*) is an epithet of Agni; so some others hold that the related goddess may have the name Bhāratī.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> देव॑ त्वष्ट॒र्यद्ध॑ चारु॒त्वमान॒ड्यदंगि॑रसा॒मभ॑वः सचा॒भूः ।  
> स दे॒वानां॒ पाथ॒ उप॒ प्र वि॒द्वानु॒शन्य॑क्षि द्रविणोदः सु॒रत्नः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देव । त्वष्टः । यत् । ह । चारुत्वं । आनट् । यत् । अंगिरसां । अभवः ।  
> सचाभूः ॥  
> सः । देवानां । पाथः । उप । प्र । विद्वान् । उशन् । यक्षि । द्रविणःदः । सुरत्नः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वाष्ट्रस्य पशोर्वपायागस्य देव त्वष्टरिति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । देव त्वष्टर्यद्ध चारुत्वमानट् पिशंगरूपः सुभरो वयोधाः । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> हे देव त्वष्टरेतन्नामक त्वं यच्चारुत्वं हविर्भिः कल्याणरूपत्वमानट्
> प्राप्तवान् ॥ अश्नोतेर्लिटि प्रत्ययस्य लुक् ॥ यच्च त्वमंगिरसामस्माकं सचाभूः
> सहभावी सखाभवः । हे द्रविणोदो धनस्य दातः अव एव सुरत्नः सुधनः स त्वमुशन्नवींषि कामयमानः सन् विद्वान् अस्येदमस्येदमिति प्रजानंदेवानां पाथोऽन्नमुप यक्षि । उपयज । तेभ्यः प्रयच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk देव त्वष्टः (*deva tvaṣṭaḥ*) is the yājyā for the vapā offering of the animal sacred to Tvaṣṭṛ. It is prescribed in the sūtra: देव त्वष्टर्यद्ध चारुत्वमानट् पिशंगरूपः सुभरो वयोधाः । आ. ३-८ । (*deva tvaṣṭaryaddha cārutvamānaṭ piśaṃgarūpaḥ subharo vayodhāḥ | ā. 3-8 |*) O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, you who have attained, through oblations, the state of beauty, and who have become our companion, of us the Aṅgirases: O giver of wealth, whose wealth is good, you, desiring the oblations and knowing "this is for this one, this for that one", offer (उप यक्षि (*upa yakṣi*)) the food of the gods and give it to them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्रविणोदः (*draviṇodaḥ*)—giver of wealth
- देव (*deva*)—O divine one
- त्वष्टः (*tvaṣṭaḥ*)—O Tvaṣṭṛ
- यत् (*yat*)—because of which
- चारुत्वं (*cārutvaṃ*)—the auspicious form
- आनट् (*ānaṭ*)—you have attained
- यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness of yours
- अंगिरसां (*aṃgirasāṃ*)—with the Aṅgirases (with us)
- सचाभूः (*sacābhūḥ*)—united
- अभवः (*abhavaḥ*)—you are; therefore
- सुरत्नः (*suratnaḥ*)—possessed of excellent wealth
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- उशन् (*uśan*)—desiring the oblations
- प्र विद्वान् (*pra vidvān*)—knowing everything
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—food
- उप यक्षि (*upa yakṣi*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Tvaṣṭṛ, giver of wealth and divine in nature, by that greatness of yours by which you have attained a beautiful form, and by which you are united with us, the descendants of Aṅgiras—

### Printed p. 637
because of this, you, possessed of excellent wealth, desiring the oblations and knowing everything, provide food for the gods.

##### English translation
Divine Twashtri, since you have attained to beauty (through our oblations), and have become the associate of the Angirasas, do you, the bestower of wealth, possessed of precious treasure, and knowing (to whom each portion belongs), offer the food of the gods (to them).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk देव त्वष्टः (*deva tvaṣṭaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the vapā sacrifice offered to the deity Tvaṣṭṛ is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: देव त्वष्टर्यद्ध चारुत्वमानट् पिशंगरूपः सुभरो वयोधाः (*deva tvaṣṭaryaddha cārutvamānaṭ piśaṃgarūpaḥ subharo vayodhāḥ*) (Ā. 3-8).

Yāska's explanation regarding the deity Tvaṣṭṛ:
त्वष्टा । त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः ॥ माध्यमिकस्तृष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*tvaṣṭā | tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ ‖ mādhyamikastṛṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-14)
That is: the Nirukta-authors say that the word Tvaṣṭṛ means one who pervades quickly; or one who is resplendent; or one who performs works (craftsmanship). Some say he is Mādhyamika, that is, he who dwells between heaven and earth (in the atmosphere). Śākapūṇi says he is Agni.

Some say that Tvaṣṭṛ, like Viśvakarman, is the craftsman of the gods. For in the Ṛk that Yāska gives as an example,
य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं तृष्णारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥ (*ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā | tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tṛṣṇāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*)
it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of heaven and earth and the cause of the appropriate form, beauty, prosperity, growth and so on of the creatures in all the worlds. Moreover Śruti (Yajurveda) statements such as त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानां रूपकृत् (*tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-8-5), त्वष्टा रूपाणामधिपतिः (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāmadhipatiḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-4-5-1) and त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*) establish Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in making things; and

मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोवृजन्नपि क्रतुं ॥ (*mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajramatakṣadāyasaṃ mayi devāsovṛjannapi kratuṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-48-3)

### Printed p. 638
Indra says that Tvaṣṭṛ made for him a thunderbolt of iron. Many mantras of the Ṛgveda say that he made for the gods the necessary sacrificial materials and many other things.

Tvaṣṭṛ is famed as one of the twelve Ādityas. For that reason Yāska explained the meaning as "resplendent".

Among the Śruti statements that give a personal view of the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, those cited below refer only to the deity of the Āprī hymn.

होतायक्षत्तष्टारमचिष्टुमपाकग्ं रेतोधां विश्रवसं यशोधां । पुरुरूपमकामकर्शनग्ं सुपोषः पोषैः स्यात्सुवीरो वीरैर्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥ (*hotāyakṣattaṣṭāramaciṣṭumapākagṃ retodhāṃ viśravasaṃ yaśodhāṃ | pururūpamakāmakarśanagṃ supoṣaḥ poṣaiḥ syātsuvīro vīrairvetvājyasya hotaryaja ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

In this mantra there are the epithets अचिष्टुं (*aciṣṭuṃ*), अपाकं (*apākaṃ*), रेतोधां (*retodhāṃ*), विश्रवसं (*viśravasaṃ*), यशोधां (*yaśodhāṃ*), पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*), अकामकर्शनं (*akāmakarśanaṃ*). Among these: अचिष्टुं (*aciṣṭuṃ*) is explained as चेष्टनरहितं, चांचल्यरहितं, स्थिरं (*ceṣṭanarahitaṃ, cāṃcalyarahitaṃ, sthiraṃ*), one who stays steady without fickleness; अपाकं (*apākaṃ*) as अबालं प्राज्ञं (*abālaṃ prājñaṃ*), not a child but wise; रेतोधां (*retodhāṃ*) as पुत्रादिबीजस्य यजमाने धारयितारं (*putrādibījasya yajamāne dhārayitāraṃ*), one who sows the seed of sons and the like in the sacrificer; विश्ववसं (*viśvavasaṃ*) as विविधकीर्तियुक्तं (*vividhakīrtiyuktaṃ*), possessed of various fame; यशोधां (*yaśodhāṃ*) as यजमाने यशसः धारयितारं (*yajamāne yaśasaḥ dhārayitāraṃ*), one who makes the sacrificer a sharer of renown; पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*) as बहुरूपं (*bahurūpaṃ*), one of many kinds of form; अकामकर्शनं (*akāmakarśanaṃ*) as कामानां अनाशयितारं (*kāmānāṃ anāśayitāraṃ*), one who fulfils the sacrificer's desires.

These epithets show Tvaṣṭṛ's personal nature. Showing the derivation of the word Tvaṣṭṛ (8-14), the Nirukta-authors say: त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वास्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् करोटिकर्मणः । (*tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervāsyāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syāt karoṭikarmaṇaḥ |*) The view of the Nirukta-authors is that the name arises from pervading quickly; and it may be formed from the root tviṣ, meaning "to shine", or from the root tvakṣ, meaning "to make". From these explanations it is understood that Tvaṣṭṛ is one who pervades swiftly, shines, and makes. To show to which world this deity belongs they say माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । (*mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ |*)

### Printed p. 639
thereby stating the views that he belongs to the group of atmospheric deities according to some, and that he is Agni according to Śākapūṇi. In the Bṛhaddevatā, approving the first view:

त्वष्टा रूपविकर्ता च योऽसौ माध्यमिके गणे । स्तुतः स च निपातेन सूक्तं तस्य न विद्यते ॥ (*tvaṣṭā rūpavikartā ca yo 'sau mādhyamike gaṇe | stutaḥ sa ca nipātena sūktaṃ tasya na vidyate ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-25)

In this verse he is said to belong to the group of deities of the middle world. Before this:

त्वष्टा तु यस्त्वयमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः । पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चः स्युः कस्याप्यक् चार्तवेषु च ॥ त्वषितस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् तूर्णमश्नुत एव ना । कर्मसूत्तारणो वेति तेन नामैतदश्नुते ॥ यः सहस्रतमो रश्मी रवेश्चंद्रमुपाश्रितः । सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं चेह च यन्मधु ॥ (*tvaṣṭā tu yastvayameva pārthivo 'gniriti stutiḥ | pārthivasyāsya varcaḥ syuḥ kasyāpyak cārtaveṣu ca ‖ tvaṣitastvakṣatervā syāt tūrṇamaśnuta eva nā | karmasūttāraṇo veti tena nāmaitadaśnute ‖ yaḥ sahasratamo raśmī raveścaṃdramupāśritaḥ | so 'pi tvaṣṭāramevāgniṃ paraṃ ceha ca yanmadhu ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-15 to 17)

In some places there is an indication that the praise which belongs to the terrestrial Agni is the same, and that Tvaṣṭṛ is a deity connected with the earth. In the hymns concerning the seasons he is described as a portion of Agni. Then the Nirukta's derivation of the word Tvaṣṭṛ is itself given. It also describes that, as the thousand-rayed sun pervading the moon pervades honey, the other world and the earth, so it is in Tvaṣṭṛ too. In this matter the Bṛhaddevatā-authors chiefly approve the view of Śākapūṇi stated in the Nirukta. In the Nighaṇṭu, Tvaṣṭṛ is placed first with the Āprī deities (5-2), then with the atmospheric deities (5-5), and first with the deities of the heavenly world (5-6).

The story of Tvaṣṭṛ and the sage Dadhīci is told in the Special Topics of Sūkta 1-139. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

त्वष्टारं यजति वाग्वै त्वष्टा वाग्भेदं सर्वं । त्वांष्ट्री वाचमेव तत्रीणाति वाचं यजमाने दधाति । (*tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati vāgvai tvaṣṭā vāgbhedaṃ sarvaṃ | tvāṃṣṭrī vācameva tatrīṇāti vācaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*)

By this statement the identity of Tvaṣṭṛ and speech is stated, which is also one view.

य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् । (*ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā | tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9)

In this Ṛk it is praised that this deity has a divine birth, and that for this reason he shows his antiquity even at the times of creation. The view is that Tvaṣṭṛ is extremely ancient.
