इह त्वष्टारमग्रियं विश्वरूपमुपह्वये । अस्माकमस्तु केवलः ॥ (*iha tvaṣṭāramagriyaṃ viśvarūpamupahvaye | asmākamastu kevalaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10)

त्वष्टारमग्रजां गोपां पुरोयानानमा हुवे । इंदुरिंद्रो वृषा हरिः पवमानः प्रजापतिः ॥ (*tvaṣṭāramagrajāṃ gopāṃ puroyānānamā huve | iṃduriṃdro vṛṣā hariḥ pavamānaḥ prajāpatiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-9)

From such Ṛks it is known, through the epithets "agriya" and "agraja" (the foremost, the first-born).

त्वष्टा रूपाणि हि प्रभुः पशून्विश्वान्त्समानजे । तेषां नः स्कातिमा यज । (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi hi prabhuḥ paśūnviśvāntsamānaje | teṣāṃ naḥ skātimā yaja |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-9)

त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-9-2)

Such sentences praise Tvaṣṭṛ's work of fashioning. Moreover he has the epithet *Viśvarūpa* (of all forms) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वन॑स्पते रश॒नया॑ नि॒यूया॑ दे॒वानां॒ पाथ॒ उप॑ वक्षि वि॒द्वान् ।  
> स्वदा॑ति दे॒वः कृ॒णव॑द्ध॒वींष्यव॑तां॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी हवं॑ मे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वनस्पते । रशनया । नियूय । देवानां । पाथः । उप । वक्षि । विद्वान् ।  
> स्वदाति । देवः । कृणवत् । हवींषि । अवतां । द्यावापृथिवी इति । हवं । मे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वनस्पतिस्तोमे निष्केवल्ये वनस्पते रशनयेत्येषा सूक्तमुखीया । सूत्रितं
> च । देवेभ्यो वनस्पते हवींषि वनस्पते रशनया नियूयेति सूक्तमुखीयाः ।
> आ. ९-५ । इति ॥
> हे वनस्पते वनस्पतिविकार यूप विद्वाञ्ज्ञानानस्त्वं रशनया रज्ज्ञा नियूय
> बध्वा परिव्याय पाथोऽन्नं देवानामिंद्रादीनामुप वक्षि । उपवह । प्रापय ।
> ततो देवो वनस्पतिः स्वदाति । हविष्प्रापणेन स्वदयतु । तथा हवींष्यस्माभिर्दत्तानि
> कृणवत् । देवानां करोतु । तथा मे मदीयं हवं देवविषयाह्वानं द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्याववतां । रक्षतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Niṣkevalya-stoma of the Vanaspati, this Ṛk "वनस्पते रशनया (*vanaspate raśanayā*)" is the sūktamukhīya (the opening verse of the sūkta). It is so stated by the sūtra: देवेभ्यो वनस्पते हवींषि वनस्पते रशनया नियूयेति सूक्तमुखीयाः (*devebhyo vanaspate havīṃṣi vanaspate raśanayā niyūyeti sūktamukhīyāḥ*) (Ā. 9-5).

O Vanaspati, modification of the tree, the sacrificial post, you who know: having tied the food with a rope, bound and wrapped it, carry it up to the gods Indra and the rest. Then may the god Vanaspati enjoy it; by conveying the oblation may he make it pleasing. Likewise may he make the oblations given by us reach the gods. And may Heaven and Earth protect my invocation, my calling of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वनस्पते (*vanaspate*)—O deity of the sacrificial post, made from a tree
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—you who know everything
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—the food in the form of oblation
- रशनया (*raśanayā*)—with a rope
- नियूय (*niyūya*)—having tied it into a bundle
- देवानां उप (*devānāṃ upa*)—to the vicinity of the gods, Indra and the rest
- वक्षि (*vakṣi*)—carry (thereafter)
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the god Vanaspati (or the deity of the post)
- स्वदाति (*svadāti*)—may he eat the oblation
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations offered by us
- कृणवत् (*kṛṇavat*)—may he give to the gods
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—invocation directed to the gods
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—Heaven and Earth
- अवतां (*avatāṃ*)—may they protect, that is, approve

### Printed p. 641

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deity of the sacrificial post, made from a tree, you who know everything: tie the food in the form of oblation with a rope into a bundle (as people carry things when travelling) and carry it to the vicinity of the gods. Then may the deity of the post, called Vanaspati, eat that oblation, and give the oblation offered by us to the gods; and may the deities Heaven and Earth approve my invocation, in which I pray and call that the gods should come to this sacrificial ground.

##### English translation
Vanspati, you are intelligent; having fastened it with a rope, convoy the food of the gods ; may the divine (Vanaspati) taste it, may he take the oblations (to the gods); may heaven and earth protect my invocation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited and the deity Vanaspati is praised, this Ṛk "वनस्पते रशनया (*vanaspate raśanayā*)" is to be recited at the beginning; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra: देवेभ्यो वनस्पते हवींषि वनस्पते रशनया नियूयेति सूक्तमुखीयाः (*devebhyo vanaspate havīṃṣi vanaspate raśanayā niyūyeti sūktamukhīyāḥ*) (Ā. 9-5).

Yāska has said in his explanation that the word vanaspati has two kinds of meaning: वनस्पत इत्येनमाहैष हि वनानां पाता ना पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः । (*vanaspata ityenamāhaiṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā nā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ |*) (Ni. 8-3)

What is Vanaspati? The protector of the vanas (forests), that is, the forest-deity called Vanaspati; the meaning is one who protects the trees in the forest. The word vana is formed from the root vana, in the sense "to resort to, obtain". Because people obtain this (the tree) when they need it for their works, that is, bring it, the tree is called vana. The greatest of trees, or the deity of the tree, is called Vanaspati. As an example, the Ṛk beginning उपावसृजन् (*upāvasṛjan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-10), which has this word vanaspati, is cited.

### Printed p. 642

तत् को वनस्पतिः । यूप इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*tat ko vanaspatiḥ | yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*)

It is the view of Kātthakya that the word vanaspati also means the sacrificial post to which animals are tied in the sacrifice. On this point, the Ṛk अजंति त्वामध्वरे (*ajaṃti tvāmadhvare*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1) is given as an example where the word vanaspati has the meaning yūpa. It is the view of Śākapūṇi that the word vanaspati also means Agni. In support of this the mantras देवेभ्यो वनस्पते (*devebhyo vanaspate*) and वनस्पते रशनया (*vanaspate raśanayā*) are given as examples.

Pāthaḥ—Yāska has given three kinds of meaning for the word pātha:

पाथः । पाथोऽन्तरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यातं । श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः । इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*pāthaḥ | pātho 'ntarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyātaṃ | śyeno na dīyannanveti pāthaḥ | ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-8)

(1) The word pātha means the atmosphere. On this point the Śruti sentence श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः (*śyeno na dīyannanveti pāthaḥ*) supports this meaning.

उदकमपि पाथ उच्यते पानात् । आचष्ट आसां पाथो नदीनां । इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*udakamapi pātha ucyate pānāt | ācaṣṭa āsāṃ pātho nadīnāṃ | ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-9)

(2) The word pātha also means water, because it is drunk. The Śruti sentence आचष्ट आसां पाथो नदीनां (*ācaṣṭa āsāṃ pātho nadīnāṃ*) supports this meaning.

अन्नमपि पाथ उच्यते पानादेव । देवानां पाथ उपवक्षि विद्वान् इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*annamapi pātha ucyate pānādeva | devānāṃ pātha upavakṣi vidvān ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-10)

(3) Because people eat food, food too is called pātha. On this point the present Ṛk itself, देवानां पाथ उपवक्षि विद्वान् (*devānāṃ pātha upavakṣi vidvān*), is the example.

Yāska's explanation of the word vanaspati:

वनस्पत इत्येनमाहैष हि वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः । (*vanaspata ityenamāhaiṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ |*) (Ni. 8-3)

तत्को वनस्पतिः । यूप इति कात्कृक्यः । अग्निरितिशाकपूणिः ॥ (*tatko vanaspatiḥ | yūpa iti kātkṛkyaḥ | agniritiśākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-18)

That is, they call Agni himself Vanaspati, because Agni is the protector or guardian of the forests. Though fire is present within the tree, it does not burn it, so he is said to be its protector. Or, because it is useful for the means of sacrifice, such as wood, it is called vana. Vanaspati means

### Printed p. 643

the king of trees, a great tree. Which deity is Vanaspati? It is Kātthakya's opinion that it is the wooden post set up in the sacrifice for tying the animal. It is Śākapūṇi's opinion that Vanaspati is Agni.

To support Kātthakya's opinion also, Yāska has given a Ṛk as an example:

अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना दैवेय ॥ (*aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā daiveya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1)

That is, "O Vanaspati (sacrificial post), in the sacrifice the priests and the sacrificer anoint you with ghee consecrated by mantra": this addresses the post to which the animal is tied. In the 3rd, 6th and 11th Ṛks of this same sūkta also the Vanaspati is addressed as the sacrificial post, and it is well known that the deity of this sūkta is the yūpa. In the eleventh Ṛk of this sūkta, वनस्पते शतवल्‌शो विरोह सहस्रवल् शा वि वयं रुहेम (*vanaspate śatavalśo viroha sahasraval śā vi vayaṃ ruhema*), that is, "O Vanaspati, grow with hundreds and thousands of shoots", applies to Vanaspati as the tree. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-10, वनस्पते रशनया नियूय (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūya*), "O Vanaspati, tied with the rope that binds the animal", confirms the meaning of the word vanaspati as the sacrificial post. Therefore vanaspati means the sacrificial post; Agni is the indirect meaning.

What the nature of Vanaspati is must be learnt by much consideration. On the basis of this word some modern Western scholars have concluded that the violent animal sacrifice was customary in the Vedic age and that the Āprī sūktas are prayāja mantras connected with such a sacrifice. Looked at crudely, Vanaspati would be the post to which the sacrificial animal is tied. But on the question whether it is indeed the post to which the sacrificial animal is tied, the nature of Vanaspati can be determined after considering the Śruti sentences and on their basis.

. होता यक्षद्वनस्पतिमुपावस्रक्षद्धियो जोष्टारग्ं शशमं नरः । स्वदात्स्वधितिर्ऋतुथाद्य देवो देवेभ्यो हव्यानाड्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज । (*. hotā yakṣadvanaspatimupāvasrakṣaddhiyo joṣṭāragṃ śaśamaṃ naraḥ | svadātsvadhitirṛtuthādya devo devebhyo havyānāḍvetvājyasya hotaryaja |*) (Tai. Brā. 3.6 2-2)

The commentary on this mantra is as follows: वनस्पतिं यूपाधारभूतं दशमप्रयाजदेवतात्मकमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (*vanaspatiṃ yūpādhārabhūtaṃ daśamaprayājadevatātmakamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu*)—Vanaspati is that which is the support of the post, and is Agni, the tenth prayāja deity. May the hotṛ perform the sacrifice addressing him. Vanaspati has the epithets dhiyo, joṣṭā, svadāt, svadhitiḥ, devebhyaḥ, ṛtudhā havyavāṭ, yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ. Among these epithets, for धियो जोष्टा (*dhiyo joṣṭā*) the gloss बुद्धेः प्रीणयितारं (*buddheḥ prīṇayitāraṃ*) is given: one who gives joy to the intellect;

### Printed p. 644

svadhitiḥ—one consecrated with the svadhiti (the thunderbolt or) divine weapon; ṛtudhā—ऋतौ विहिते कालविशेषे अद्य अस्मिकन्कर्मणि स्वदादस्माभिर्दीयमानं हविः स्वयतु । किंच देवो वनस्पतिर्देवेभ्यो देवार्थं हव्या हवींषि हव्यवाड्वहतु । (*ṛtau vihite kālaviśeṣe adya asmikankarmaṇi svadādasmābhirdīyamānaṃ haviḥ svayatu | kiṃca devo vanaspatirdevebhyo devārthaṃ havyā havīṃṣi havyavāḍvahatu |*) The meaning of the mantra is: at this time of the sacrifice, may he offer to the gods the oblations offered by us. And by the epithet यज्ञस्य आयुःकल्पमानः (*yajñasya āyuḥkalpamānaḥ*) the meaning is: one who increases the life of the sacrifice.

By such epithets, in the Praiṣa-sūkta identity of Agni and Vanaspati is stated. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa it is indicated by the sentence प्राणो वै वनस्पतिः (*prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ*) (2-4). The author of the Nirukta first gives the explanation of the word vanaspati and then, in the Āprī sūkta, states what Vanaspati's nature is. In explaining Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3, showing the explanation of the word vanaspati occurring there (Ni. 8-3), वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा। वनं वनोतेः। (*vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā| vanaṃ vanoteḥ|*): he is famous as Vanaspati either because he is lord of the forests or because he is their protector, and the word is formed from the root van, which gives the sense "to obtain". Then, in discussing the nature of the deities of the Āprī sūkta (Ni. 8-18), तत् को वनस्पतिः यूप इति कात्थक्यः अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*tat ko vanaspatiḥ yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*), he states the two opinions, and to support Kātthakya's view he cites the Ṛk

अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना देव्येन । यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्ताद्यद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ॥ (*aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā devyena | yadūrdhvastiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattādyadvā kṣayo māturasyā upasthe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1)

In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has addressed Vanaspati as the post. Then, to support Śākapūṇi's view, the author of the Nirukta cites

वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् । स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवीहवं मे (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān | svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavaddhavīṃṣyavatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivīhavaṃ me*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-10)

Here too Sāyaṇa has explained it as the post; but the opinion of the author of the Nirukta is that it is the Agni present within the post. Durgācārya, explaining this Ṛk in the Nirukta, says एव मग्निर्वनस्पतिः । यत् पुनरेतदुक्तं यूपांजनीयायां यूपे वनस्पतिशब्दः इति । अत्र ब्रूमः—अग्नि रेवासौ यूपांतर्गतो यूपात्मना वर्तमानो यूपांजनीयायां वनस्पतिशब्देनोच्यते । (*eva magnirvanaspatiḥ | yat punaretaduktaṃ yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ yūpe vanaspatiśabdaḥ iti | atra brūmaḥ—agni revāsau yūpāṃtargato yūpātmanā vartamāno yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ vanaspatiśabdenocyate |*). Thus he has established that here Vanaspati is the Agni present within the post and not another. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā says:

वनस्पतिं तु यं प्राहुरयं सोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः । अयं वनानां हि पतिः पाता पालयतीति वा ॥ (*vanaspatiṃ tu yaṃ prāhurayaṃ so 'gnirvanaspatiḥ | ayaṃ vanānāṃ hi patiḥ pātā pālayatīti vā ‖*)

अग्निर्गृत्समदेनायं वनस्पतिरितीळितः । मंदस्वेत्यस्य सूक्तस्य षळ्चस्य तृतीयया ॥ (*agnirgṛtsamadenāyaṃ vanaspatiritīḷitaḥ | maṃdasvetyasya sūktasya ṣaḷcasya tṛtīyayā ‖*)

### Printed p. 645

यूपवत्तरुवच्चैव स्तुतिर्यास्य प्रसंगजा । सर्वेणांजंतिसूक्तेन तृतीये सा तु मंडले ॥ (*yūpavattaruvaccaiva stutiryāsya prasaṃgajā | sarveṇāṃjaṃtisūktena tṛtīye sā tu maṃḍale ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-26 to 28)

By these sentences he discusses the nature of the Āprī deity addressed in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-11: here Vanaspati means the terrestrial Agni; and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-2 Gṛtsamada too addressed this same terrestrial Agni by the word vanaspati; only in some Ṛks of the third maṇḍala is the meaning post or tree, and that too occasional. Moreover:

इहैष पवमानोऽग्निर्मध्यमोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः । अमुष्मिन्नेव विप्रैस्तु लोकेऽग्निश्युचिरुच्यते ॥ (*ihaiṣa pavamāno 'gnirmadhyamo 'gnirvanaspatiḥ | amuṣminneva vipraistu loke 'gniśyucirucyate ‖*)

Showing here that Vanaspati means the Agni of the middle world, he has stated conclusively that, except in a few places of the Ṛk-saṃhitā, in all the many other places this word indicates Agni and that there is no doubt about this.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आग्ने॑ वह॒ वरु॑णमि॒ष्टये॑ न॒ इंद्रं॑ दि॒वो म॒रुतो॑  ॒॑
> अंतरिक्षात् ।  
> सीदं॑तु ब॒र्हिर्विश्व॒ आ यज॑त्राः॒ स्वाहा॑ दे॒वा अ॒मृता॑ मादयंतां ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । अग्ने । वह । वरुणं । इष्टये । नः । इंद्रं । दिवः । मरुतः । अंतरिक्षात् ।  
> सीदंतु । बर्हिः । विश्वे । आ । यजत्राः । स्वाहा । देवाः । अमृताः । मादयंतां ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं नोऽस्माकमिष्टये यागायेंद्रं वरुणं च मरुतश्च दिवो
> द्युलोकादंतरिक्षाच्चास्मदीयं यज्ञमा वह । प्रापय । आगतास्ते यजत्रा
> यष्टव्या विश्वे सर्वॆ वेवा बर्हिरा सीदंतु । तत्रासन्ना भवंतु । ततोऽमृता मरणधर्मरहिता देवाः स्वाहा स्वाहाकारेण दत्तैर्हविर्भिमार्दयंतां । आत्मानं
> मावयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, bring for our sacrifice Indra and Varuṇa, and the Maruts, from the heavenly world and from the atmosphere: bring our sacrifice to them. The worshipful gods, all of them, having come, are to sit on the barhis (sacred grass), that is, be seated there. Then the immortal gods, free from the nature of death, are to be gladdened, to gladden themselves, by the oblations given with the svāhā-call.

### Printed p. 646

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*)—for the sacrifice
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuṇa
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Marut deities also
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from heaven (their dwelling place)
- अंतरिक्षात् (*aṃtarikṣāt*)—from the firmament
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring them to our place of sacrifice
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—the deathless
- विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*)—all those gods
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—upon the seat of darbha grass
- सीदंतु (*sīdaṃtu*)—let them sit
- स्वाहा (*svāhā*)—and with the oblation we offer with the utterance of svāhā
- मादयंतां (*mādayaṃtāṃ*)—let them attain satisfaction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, in order that Indra, Varuṇa and the Marut deities may take part in our sacrifice, bring them from their own abodes, heaven and the firmament, to our place of sacrifice. Let those deathless gods sit on the seat of darbha grass and rejoice in the oblation that we offer with the utterance of svāhā.

##### English translation
Bring, Agni, to our sacrifice Varna and Indra from heaven, and the Maruts from the firmament; may the adorable universal gods sit down on the sacred grass, and may the immortal deities rejoice in (the oblation presented with) the Swaha.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska's explanation of the word svāhā is as follows:
स्वाहाकृतयः । स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा । स्वा नागाहेति वा । स्वं प्राहेति वा । स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ॥ (*svāhākṛtayaḥ | svāhetyetat su āheti vā | svā nāgāheti vā | svaṃ prāheti vā | svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā ‖*) (Ni. 8-21)
The word svāhā has four kinds of etymological meaning:
(1) सु आहेति वा (*su āheti vā*). Su—well; āha—he says or utters. Because the mantra that ends in svāhā is uttered well, that is, clearly, it is called svāhā.
(2) स्वा नागाहेति वा (*svā nāgāheti vā*). Svā—one's own; vāk—speech. There is a Śruti sentence: तं स्वा नागभ्यवदज्जुहुधीति । तत्स्वाहाकारस्य जन्म । (*taṃ svā nāgabhyavadajjuhudhīti | tatsvāhākārasya janma |*) That is, because at the time of the homa the person offering himself adds the word svāhā at the end of the Vedic mantra, the Ṛk, it is called svāhā.
(3) स्वं प्राहेति वा (*svaṃ prāheti vā*). (The sacrificer or the priest) says: "I shall offer my own oblation"; sva—his own oblation, āha—he says he will offer. Therefore it is called svāhā.

### Printed p. 647
(4) स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा (*svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā*). Because the oblation he offers is offered by the utterance of the word svāhā, that is, because the oblation is given into the fire, it is called svāhā.
Having given the four kinds of explanation of meaning, he gives this Ṛk as an example.
सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः । (*sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*)
अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हनिरदंतु देवाः ॥ (*asya hotuḥ pradiśyatasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haniradaṃtu devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-111)
Its main sense: Agni, born just now (that is, just now installed in the sacrifice), sits in front of the gods and conducts the sacrifice, performing the duty of the hotṛ, namely the work of invoking the gods. May the gods eat the oblation offered by such a hotṛ, standing in the east, offered with the utterance of svāhā. Therefore the intention is that the word uttered at the end of the mantra when an oblation is offered, for the satisfaction of the gods, into the fire duly installed for the sacrifice, is called svāhā.
In some Āprī hymns the plural form स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhākṛtayaḥ*) is used. Because the svāhā is added and recited with the eleven prayāja mantras used in offering to the eleven deities of the hymn, the plural स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhākṛtayaḥ*) is used.
In the Purāṇas and similar works it is used in another sense. In the Mahābhārata, Svāhā is said to be the daughter of Bṛhaspati, son of the sage Aṅgiras. In the Purāṇas the goddess Svāhā is said to be the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati and the wife of Agni.
स्वाहा इत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यक्ष्यमाणदेवतानां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः । तद्वंति हव्यानि ॥ (*svāhā ityevaṃpūrvā kṛtiḥ karaṇamuccāraṇaṃ yakṣyamāṇadevatānāṃ tāḥ svāhākṛtayaḥ | tadvaṃti havyāni ‖*) It is an adjective of the word havyāni: oblations accompanied by the word svāhā, which is to be recited at the offering of the oblation. It is the word chiefly recited in the last Ṛks of the Āprī hymns. In some Ṛks it is also adverbial. That is, in Ṛk 1-13-12 स्वाहा कृणोतन (*svāhā kṛṇotana*), in Ṛk 1-142-12 स्वाहा कर्तन (*svāhā kartana*); in Ṛks 3-4-11; 7-2.11; 10-70-11 it is in the sense of the instrument; in 2-3-11 it is an adjective of havya, and in 10-110-11 an adjective of havis.
In explaining this word, some have held that by it the divine Svāhākṛti is indicated, others that by it Agni is indicated. In the Praiṣa hymn:
होता यक्षदग्निग् स्वाहाज्यस्य..................वियंतु होतर्युज ॥ (*hotā yakṣadagnig svāhājyasya..................viyaṃtu hotaryuja ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

### Printed p. 648
is recited. On this Sāyaṇa explains: योऽयं स्वाहाशब्दोदितः उत्तमप्रयाजदेवः अग्निः तं दैव्यू होता यजतु । (*yo 'yaṃ svāhāśabdoditaḥ uttamaprayājadevaḥ agniḥ taṃ daivyū hotā yajatu |*) By the word svāhā the eleventh prayāja deity, Agni, is meant. The four kinds of meaning given by the Nirukta author were stated earlier. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:
स्वाहाकृतीयजति प्रतिष्ठा वै स्वाहाकृतयः प्रतिष्ठायामेव तद्यज्ञमंततः प्रतिष्ठापयति ॥ (*svāhākṛtīyajati pratiṣṭhā vai svāhākṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhāyāmeva tadyajñamaṃtataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 2-4)
It is explained that, since the offering is completed by the svāhā-utterance, it is the support of the whole sacrifice, and it sets the sacrifice on a proper foundation. In the Bṛhaddevatā:
स्वाहाकृतयोऽनेकाश्च विदुषां मितयोऽभवन् । (*svāhākṛtayo 'nekāśca viduṣāṃ mitayo 'bhavan |*)
तत्सर्वं त्वयमेवाग्निर्भवतीति विनिश्चयः ॥ (*tatsarvaṃ tvayamevāgnirbhavatīti viniścayaḥ ‖*)
अयं हि कर्ता स्वाहानां कृतिस्तासामिहैकजा । (*ayaṃ hi kartā svāhānāṃ kṛtistāsāmihaikajā |*)
अयं प्रसूर्भूतितानां सर्वेषामयमव्ययः ॥ (*ayaṃ prasūrbhūtitānāṃ sarveṣāmayamavyayaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 3-29, 30)
Regarding the deity Svāhākṛti the opinions of the learned are many and differ. But however much they differ, on this one point all agree: that this deity Svāhākṛti is a special form of Agni. For Agni himself is the maker of the svāhās (that is, of the oblations or mantras offered with the word svāhā). He is the maker of all such mantras and also their deity; this Agni is the place of origin of all beings (creatures), that is, all creatures arise from him. Among all creatures he alone is without destruction, that is, he is imperishable. Thus the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā state their view.
In the Ṛks that consist of svāhā-utterances (the last Ṛks of some Āprī hymns), Pūṣan, the Maruts, Vāyu, Sūrya, Indra, Varuṇa and the other deities are all indicated. Above all, in the Ṛks
पुरोगा अग्निर्देवानां गायत्रेण समज्यते । (*purogā agnirdevānāṃ gāyatreṇa samajyate |*)
स्वाहाकृतीषु रोचते ॥ (*svāhākṛtīṣu rocate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-11)
सद्यो जातो व्यमिमित यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः । (*sadyo jāto vyamimita yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*)
अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदंतु देवाः ॥ (*asya hotuḥ pradiśyatasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradaṃtu devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-11)
Agni is praised as the leader (purohita) of the gods from the time of his birth, and, describing the power of the svāhā-utterance,

### Printed p. 649
आ याह्यग्ने समिधानो अर्वाजिंद्रेण देवैः सरथं तुरेभिः । (*ā yāhyagne samidhāno arvājiṃdreṇa devaiḥ sarathaṃ turebhiḥ |*)
बर्हिर्न आस्तामदितिः सुपुत्रा स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयंतां ॥ (*barhirna āstāmaditiḥ suputrā svāhā devā amṛtā mādayaṃtāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-11)
आग्ने वह वरुणमिष्टये न इंद्रं दिवो मरुतो अंतरिक्षात् । (*āgne vaha varuṇamiṣṭaye na iṃdraṃ divo maruto aṃtarikṣāt |*)
सीदंतु बर्हिर्विश्व आ यजत्राः स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयांतां ॥ (*sīdaṃtu barhirviśva ā yajatrāḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayāṃtāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70.11)
In these Ṛks the gods are gladdened by the mantra svāhā (the word svāhā); this shows that the word svāhā holds so divine a place in the sacrifice.

## Sūkta 71 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction (Pīṭhike)**
In this hymn the deity called Jñāna (knowledge) is praised. There are some occasions when the seers praised certain feelings that arise in the mind, regarding them as deities. Knowledge is one of them. Likewise Manyu (anger) is praised as a deity of feeling in hymns 83 and 84 of this same Maṇḍala, and Śraddhā in hymn 151 of this Maṇḍala. Likewise dāna, tapas (meditation), medhā, prajñā, kāma, satya, dama, śama, dharma, yajña, manas, saṃvatsara or kāla, śānti, ānanda and the like are also counted as deities of feeling. We have described these deities of feeling at length, with examples, in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 29, pages 310-314.
In the Bṛhaddevatā, the work spoken by the sage Śaunaka, it is said of this hymn in the 7th chapter:
यज्जोतिरमृतं ब्रह्म यद्योगात्समुपाश्नुते । (*yajjotiramṛtaṃ brahma yadyogātsamupāśnute |*)
तज्ज्ञानमभितुष्टाव सूक्तेनाथ बृहस्पतिः ॥ १०९ ॥ (*tajjñānamabhituṣṭāva sūktenātha bṛhaspatiḥ ‖ 109 ‖*)
Bṛhaspati in this hymn describes and praises that supreme knowledge by the meditation on which, as the eternal and imperishable supreme light, the yogī (or the ascetic) attains the state of Parabrahman.
जीवनार्थं प्रयोगस्तु मंत्राणां प्रतिषिध्यते । (*jīvanārthaṃ prayogastu maṃtrāṇāṃ pratiṣidhyate |*)
वेदतत्त्वार्थविज्ञानं प्रायेणात्र हि दृश्यते ॥ ११० ॥ (*vedatattvārthavijñānaṃ prāyeṇātra hi dṛśyate ‖ 110 ‖*)

### Printed p. 650
The use of Vedic mantras, that is, employing them to earn a living, is forbidden; no one should use the Vedic mantras for livelihood. In this hymn the supreme principle spoken of in the Vedas, and the knowledge that is the means of attaining it, are seen to be described.
आचार्यः केचिदित्याहुरत्र वाग्विधुषां स्तवः । (*ācāryaḥ kecidityāhuratra vāgvidhuṣāṃ stavaḥ |*)
यथाभिर्निंद्यतेऽत्रग्निः सूक्तेऽन्याभिरनर्थवित् ॥ १११ ॥ (*yathābhirniṃdyate 'tragniḥ sūkte 'nyābhiranarthavit ‖ 111 ‖*)
Some teachers say that in some Ṛks of this hymn there is praise of those who know the nature of speech (mantras), and in some others blame of those who do not know the meaning of the Veda.
यथैतामन्वविंदंत विद्वांसर्षिगतां सतीं । (*yathaitāmanvaviṃdaṃta vidvāṃsarṣigatāṃ satīṃ |*)
यथा च व्यभजन्यज्जॆ तदत्रोक्तं तृतीयया ॥ ११२ ॥ (*yathā ca vyabhajanyajjè tadatroktaṃ tṛtīyayā ‖ 112 ‖*)
That the learned and discerning man knows the nature of this goddess of speech, which the seers realised with the eye of knowledge, and how in the sacrificial rites the mantras that are of that divine nature were divided and used according to the rite, is stated in the 3rd Ṛk of this hymn.
प्रशस्य ते दशम्या तु विद्वानुत्तमया त्वृचा । (*praśasya te daśamyā tu vidvānuttamayā tvṛcā |*)
यज्ञे महर्त्विजामाह विनियोगं च कर्मणां ॥ ११३ ॥ (*yajñe mahartvijāmāha viniyogaṃ ca karmaṇāṃ ‖ 113 ‖*)
But in the 10th Ṛk the discerning learned man is praised. In the last Ṛk the seer describes the duties that the four priests have to perform in the sacrifice and their application.
On the use (viniyoga) of this hymn Śaunaka says in the work Ṛgvidhāna:
बृहस्पते प्रथममिति नित्यं ज्ञानस्तुतिं जपेत् । (*bṛhaspate prathamamiti nityaṃ jñānastutiṃ japet |*)
ज्ञानवान् भवति श्रीमाननंतां विंदते श्रियं । (*jñānavān bhavati śrīmānanaṃtāṃ viṃdate śriyaṃ |*)
अलक्ष्मीनाशनार्थं तु पयोभक्षो भवेद्विजः ॥ (*alakṣmīnāśanārthaṃ tu payobhakṣo bhavedvijaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, adhyāya 3, śloka 9, 72-7) **NOTE**
If one recites daily this hymn beginning बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*), excellent knowledge and incomparable prosperity are obtained. A Brahmin should recite this hymn daily, living on milk alone, to destroy poverty. If he does so, poverty is destroyed and abundance of wealth results.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहस्पत इत्येकादशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं । आंगिरसस्य बृहस्पतेरार्षं नवमी
> जगती शिष्टा दश त्रिष्टुभः । अनेन सूक्तेनर्षिः परमपुरुषार्थसाधनं परब्रह्मज्ञानं
> स्तुतवान् । अतस्तद्देवत्यमिदं । उक्तं हि बृहद्देवतायां । सुज्योतिः परमं
> ब्रह्म यद्योगात् समुपाश्नुते । तज्ज्ञानमभितुष्टाव सूक्तेनाथ बृहस्पतिः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The third hymn, बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*), has eleven Ṛks. Its seer is Bṛhaspati, the Āṅgirasa. The ninth verse is Jagatī, the remaining ten are Triṣṭubh. With this hymn the seer praised the knowledge of the supreme Brahman, which is the means to the highest human goal; therefore the deity is Knowledge. For it is said in the Bṛhaddevatā: सुज्योतिः परमं ब्रह्म यद्योगात् समुपाश्नुते । तज्ज्ञानमभितुष्टाव सूक्तेनाथ बृहस्पतिः । (*sujyotiḥ paramaṃ brahma yadyogāt samupāśnute | tajjñānamabhituṣṭāva sūktenātha bṛhaspatiḥ |*)

### Printed p. 651

> बृ. ७-१०८४ । इति । अनुक्रांतं च । बृहस्पते बृहस्पतिर्ज्ञानं तुष्टाव नवमी जगती ॥
> सूक्तविनियोगो गतः । देवासुवां हविःषु बृहस्पतिर्वाचस्पतिरित्यस्य प्रथमानुवाक्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावद्भिः । आ- ४ ११ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The reference is बृ. ७-१०८४ (*bṛ. 7-1084*) **NOTE**. The Anukramaṇī also says: बृहस्पते बृहस्पतिर्ज्ञानं तुष्टाव नवमी जगती (*bṛhaspate bṛhaspatirjñānaṃ tuṣṭāva navamī jagatī*). The use of the hymn has already been given. In the Devasū offerings, in the offering to Bṛhaspati Vācaspati, the first Ṛk of this hymn is the anuvākyā. It is set out in the sūtra: बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावद्भिः (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ haṃsairiva sakhibhirvāvadbhiḥ*), Ā. 4-11.

##### Anuvāda

This hymn बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*) is the third hymn in the sixth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Its seer is Bṛhaspati, son of Aṅgiras; the ninth Ṛk of the hymn is in Jagatī metre, the remaining ten Ṛks in Triṣṭubh. In this hymn the seer has praised the knowledge of the supreme Brahman, which is the means to the highest human goal. Therefore the deity of this hymn is Knowledge. In the work called Bṛhaddevatā the sage Śaunaka has said: सुज्योतिः परमं ब्रह्म यद्योगात्समुपाश्नुते । तज्ञा नमभितुष्टाव सूक्तेनाथ बृहस्पतिः ॥ (*sujyotiḥ paramaṃ brahma yadyogātsamupāśnute | tajñā namabhituṣṭāva sūktenātha bṛhaspatiḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-109); that is, the seer Bṛhaspati has praised in this hymn the knowledge that leads to the attainment of Brahman, through the practice of yoga (tapas), by realising which divine light of the nature of Parabrahman the yogī experiences the bliss of Brahman. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: बृहस्पते बृहस्पतिर्ज्ञानं तुष्टाव नवमी जगती (*bṛhaspate bṛhaspatirjñānaṃ tuṣṭāva navamī jagatī*). The use of the hymn has been stated earlier. Among the eight Devasū offerings made to the deities called Devasū, when the offering is made to the deity Bṛhaspati Vācaspati, the first Ṛk of this hymn is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं हंसैरिव सखिभिर्वावदद्भिः (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ haṃsairiva sakhibhirvāvadadbhiḥ*) (Ā. 4-11).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 71. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 2; Varga 23, 24. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 11.
Ṛṣi: Bṛhaspati. Devatā: Jñāna. Chandas: 1-8, 10, 11 Triṣṭubh; 9 Jagatī.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहस्पतिरनेन सूक्तेन विदितवेदार्थन्पालान्दृष्ट्वा स्मयमानः स्मात्मानं
> संबोध्याह । हे बृहस्पतेऽंतरात्मन् प्रथममुत्पत्यनंतरमितरवागुच्चारणात्प्रागेव
> नामधेयं नाम दधानाः पदार्थेषु निदधाना बाला यत्प्रैरत प्रेरितवंतः तद्वाचोऽग्रं भवति । यत्तत तातेत्यादिकं वाक्यं पूर्वमभिधाय पश्चादन्या वाचो
> वदिष्टंति खलु तस्माद्वाचोऽग्रं । अस्यां दतायामवस्थितान्पालान्पश्य । तथेदानीमेषां श्रेष्ठं प्रशस्यतमं यद्यच्चारिप्रं पापरहितं वेदार्थज्ञानमासीत् एषां
> तज्ञानं गुहा गुहायां निहितं गोप्यं तत्पृणा ॥ मकारलोपश्कांदसः ॥ प्रेम्णाविर्भवति । वेदाभ्यासकाले सरस्वती स्वार्थमेभ्यः प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । एवं विस्मये
> बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रमित्यादिकमारण्यकमनुसंधेयं । ऐ. आ. १-३-६ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Bṛhaspati, seeing with this sūkta that the children have understood the meaning of the Veda, smiles and addresses his own self: "O Bṛhaspati, inner self! First, immediately after birth and before any other speech is uttered, the children, assigning names to things, utter a name; that is the foremost part of speech. For they first say a sentence such as तत तात (*tata tāta*) and only afterwards speak other words; therefore it is the beginning of speech. Look at the children in this condition. Now, whatever of these is the best, most praiseworthy and free from fault, namely the knowledge of the Vedic meaning, that knowledge is hidden in a secret place (guhā); (Sarasvatī) makes it appear with affection." The sense is that at the time of Vedic study Sarasvatī reveals her own meaning to them. So in this wonder the Āraṇyaka beginning *bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ* is to be consulted: Ai. Ā. 1-3-6.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*)—O Bṛhaspati
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—immediately upon coming into being in the world
- नामधेयं (*nāmadheyaṃ*)—the name of things (or of persons)
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—designating and applying
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever name
- प्रैरत (*prairata*)—they utter, that
- वाचः (*vācaḥ*)—among all speech
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—is the foremost
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—among these utterances
- यत् (*yat*)—what
- श्रेष्ठं (*śreṣṭhaṃ*)—is the most excellent
- अरिप्रं (*aripraṃ*)—and free from sin
- आसीत् (*āsīt*)—is, and
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—among these, which
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in a secret place
- निहितं (*nihitaṃ*)—is placed
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- प्रेणा (*preṇā*)—with utmost affection
- आविः (*āviḥ*)—Sarasvatī reveals

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, the name of things or persons which, immediately upon coming into being in the world, they utter, designating and applying it, is the foremost of all speech. That which is most excellent and free from sin, and which is placed in a secret place, Sarasvatī reveals with utmost affection.

##### English translation
That, Brihaspati, is the best (part) of speech whieh those giving a name (to objects) first utter; that which was the best of those (words) and

### Printed p. 653
free from defect, (Saraswati) reveals it though secretly implanted, by means of affection.

> वाचः सख्यानि जानंति । वाक्ययुक्तानभ्युदयांल्लभंत इत्यर्थः । तस्मादेषां वाचि

> पश्याम इत्यर्थः । तितउ परिपवनं भवति ततवद्वा तुन्नवद्वा तिलमात्रतुन्नमिति वा
> सक्तुमिव तितउनेत्यादि निरुक्तमनुसंधेयं । नि. ४-१० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

तितउना (*titaunā*): that by which one sifts; or else, an outspread (tata) thing in which roasted barley is put is a titau. The affix ḍau is used, with the reduplicate treated like that of the desiderative. By the sieve so explained, as someone cleans barley-meal that is hard to wash, so the wise, the intelligent, the learned, purifying words by their stem and by their affix, wherever, in whatever assembly or gathering of scholars, they make speech with a mind endowed with wisdom (अक्रत (*akrata*) is a form of the root kṛ), there friends, those of like repute (sakhāyaḥ) who have knowledge of the śāstras and the like, know the sakhyāni, the knowledges arising among them. Or else: friends bound in friendship by speech know the friendships of that speech; that is, they obtain the prosperity that goes with speech. Therefore in their speech an auspicious, beneficent Lakṣmī is placed. अधि (*adhi*) is an indicator of the locative sense: we see the knowledge of meaning in speech. The Nirukta beginning सक्तुमिव तितउना (*saktumiva titaunā*) is to be consulted: Ni. 4-10.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तितउना (*titaunā*)—with a sieve
- सक्तु मिव पुनंतः (*saktu miva punaṃtaḥ*)—as one cleans barley grain
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—the wise
- यत्र (*yatra*)—when
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with their mind endowed with wisdom
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—speech
- अक्रत (*akrata*)—they refine
- अत्र (*atra*)—then
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—friends
- सख्यानि (*sakhyāni*)—their friendship
- जानते (*jānate*)—know
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these
- वाचि अधि (*vāci adhi*)—in speech
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—auspicious
- लक्ष्मीः (*lakṣmīḥ*)—welfare
- निहिता (*nihitā*)—is placed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As one cleans barley grain with a sieve, when the wise refine speech with their mind endowed with wisdom, then friends know their friendship. In their speech auspicious welfare is placed.

### Printed p. 654

##### English translation
When the wise create Speech throngh wisdom winnowihg (it) as (men winnow) barley with a sieve, then friends know friendship; good fortune is placed upon their word.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk Yāska has given an etymology:
तितउ । तितउ परिपवनं भवति ततवद्वा तुन्नवद्वा तिलमात्रतुन्नुमिति वा (*titau | titau paripavanaṃ bhavati tatavadvā tunnavadvā tilamātratunnumiti vā*) (Ni. 4-9)
Titau means a sieve. It is used to sift grain or flour. How it got this name: ततवद्वा । ततेन चर्मणा नद्धं । (*tatavadvā | tatena carmaṇā naddhaṃ |*) This sieve is made of some sheet with tiny holes in it, and a leather binding is put round the sheet; hence the sieve is called titau. Or तुन्नवद्वातुन्नैर्वा छिद्रॆः तद्वत् । (*tunnavadvātunnairvā chidrèḥ tadvat |*) because this sieve has tiny holes or perforations, it is called titau; or तिलमात्रतुन्नमिति वा-तिलमात्राणि वा तुन्नानि तस्मिन्निति । (*tilamātratunnamiti vā-tilamātrāṇi vā tunnāni tasminniti |*) because the holes in it are as tiny as sesame seeds, the sieve is called titau.
सक्तुमिव परिपवनेन पुनंतः । सक्तुः सचतेर्दुधावो भवति । कसतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य विकसितो भवति यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमकृषत प्रज्ञानं । धीराः प्रज्ञानवंतो ध्यानवंतः । तत्र सखायः सख्यानि संजानते भद्रेषां लक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि इति । भद्रं भगेन व्याख्यातं भजनीयं भूतानामभिद्रवणीयं भवद्रमयतीति वा भाजनवद्वा । लक्ष्मीर्लाभाद्व्या लक्षणाद्द्या (लप्स्यनाद्द्या) लांछनाद्द्या लषतेर्वा स्यात् प्रेप्पाकर्मणो लग्यतेर्वा स्यादाश्लेषकर्मणो लज्जतेर्वा स्यादश्लाघाकर्मणः ॥ (*saktumiva paripavanena punaṃtaḥ | saktuḥ sacaterdudhāvo bhavati | kasatervā syādviparītasya vikasito bhavati yatra dhīrā manasā vācamakṛṣata prajñānaṃ | dhīrāḥ prajñānavaṃto dhyānavaṃtaḥ | tatra sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni saṃjānate bhadreṣāṃ lakṣmīrnihitādhi vāci iti | bhadraṃ bhagena vyākhyātaṃ bhajanīyaṃ bhūtānāmabhidravaṇīyaṃ bhavadramayatīti vā bhājanavadvā | lakṣmīrlābhādvyā lakṣaṇāddyā (lapsyanāddyā) lāṃchanāddyā laṣatervā syāt preppākarmaṇo lagyatervā syādāśleṣakarmaṇo lajjatervā syādaślāghākarmaṇaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 4-9)
As grain (barley) is put in a sieve, sifted and cleaned; the word sakta is formed from the root सचति (*sacati*), meaning "to stick", because when it is washed it sticks together and is hard to wash. Or, when washed it swells or expands; so it may also be said that the word sakta is formed by reversing the letters of the word vi-kasita. As grain is cleaned by sifting in a sieve, intelligent and knowing people speak the words (or mantra) they utter after thinking well in the mind. Grain is cleaned by being put in a sieve. In the same way, the sentence, like grain, is put into the sieve of the mind of intelligent men and is purified by the movement of meditation; that is, the words spoken by the intelligent, having been well considered before being spoken, are reasonable and full of meaning.

### Printed p. 655
This is the sense. सखायः सख्यानि संजानते (*sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni saṃjānate*) means that by such well-refined sentences people know mutual friendly feeling. सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*) means समानख्यानाः (*samānakhyānāḥ*): those of one kind of opinion or refinement are friends. That is, the words and deeds of friends do not oppose one another but cooperate. भद्रेषां लक्ष्मिनिर्हिताधि वाचि । (*bhadreṣāṃ lakṣminirhitādhi vāci |*) In the sentences of such friends an excellent or auspicious mark (lakṣaṇa) is seen. The word bhadra means bhaga. भगो भजतेः (*bhago bhajateḥ*) (Ni. 1-7). Bhadra means that which is attained, auspicious, or enjoyed by living beings; or its coming into being is the cause of the experience of happiness; or it goes to those worthy of obtaining it and joins them: it is obtained only by the worthy. The word लक्ष्मीः (*lakṣmīḥ*) may be formed with the sense लाभाद्वा (*lābhādvā*) (obtaining), or लक्षणाद्दा (*lakṣaṇāddā*) (designating), or लप्स्यनात् (*lapsyanāt*) (desiring), or लांछनाद्दा (*lāṃchanāddā*) (indicating a mark), or from the root laṣ meaning "to desire", or from the root laj meaning "to shrink back"; or from the root lajjati with the sense अश्लाघाकर्मणः (*aślāghākarmaṇaḥ*), not boasting of oneself.
In the Nirukta statement above the formation or component meaning of the words तितउना (*titaunā*), सक्तुं (*saktuṃ*), सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*), भद्रा (*bhadrā*) and लक्ष्मी (*lakṣmī*) is stated. If grain is rinsed in a sieve, chaff, stones and other useless things go and clean grain is obtained. In the same way intelligent men, when they speak, first meditate in their minds, that is, think well, and speak only refined and meaningful words. Their sentences produce an effect on intelligent people like themselves and increase mutual friendly feeling, and in their sentences excellent and auspicious marks or signs are seen: this is the main purport of the Nirukta statement.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒ज्ञेन॑ वा॒चः प॑द॒वीय॑माय॒न्तामन्व॑विंद॒न्नृषि॑षु॒ प्रवि॑ष्टां ।  
> तामा॒भृत्या॒ व्य॑धदुः पुरु॒त्रा तां स॒प्त रे॒भा अ॒भि सं न॑वंते ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यज्ञेन । वाचः । पदवीयं । आयन् । तां । अनु । अविंदन् । ऋषिसु । प्रविष्टां ।  
> तां । आभृत्य । वि । अदधुः । पुरुत्रा । तां । सप्त । रेभाः । अभि । सं । नवंते ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 656

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाग्देवत्यपशोर्वपापुरोडाशयोर्यज्ञेन वाच इत्यादिके द्वे क्रमेण
> याज्ये । सूत्रितं च । यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन्निति द्वे देवीं वाचमजनयंत देवाः । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> विदितार्था धीराः पदवीयं॥ वेतेरचोयत् । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वाद्दुणाभावः ॥ पदेन यातव्यः पंथाः पदवीयः । तं वाचो मार्गं यज्ञेनायन् । प्राप्तवंतः । ऋषिष्वतींद्रियार्थदर्शिषु प्रविष्टां तां वाचमविंदन् ।
> अलभंत । अनंतरं तां वाचमाभृत्याहृत्य पुरुत्रा बहुषु देशेषु व्यदधुः ।
> व्यकार्षुः । सवान्मनुष्या नध्यापयामासुरित्यर्थः । एतादृशीं वाचं रेभाः शब्दायमानाः पक्षिणः पक्षिरूपाणि गायत्र्यादीनि सप्त छंदांस्यभि सं नवंते । अभितः
> संगच्छंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the sacrifice of the animal offered to the deity Speech, in the vapā and the purodāśa, the two Ṛks beginning यज्ञेन वाचः (*yajñena vācaḥ*) are the two yājyās in order. It is also laid down in the sūtra: यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन्निति द्वे देवीं वाचमजनयंत देवाः । (*yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyanniti dve devīṃ vācamajanayaṃta devāḥ |*) (Ā. 3-8). The wise who knew the meaning reached the path of speech, पदवीयं (*padavīyaṃ*), the road to be travelled by foot, by means of sacrifice; they obtained (अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*)) that speech which had entered into the Ṛṣis, who see beyond the senses. Then, having brought that speech together, they distributed it in many places (पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)): they made all men study it. This speech the रेभाः (*rebhāḥ*), the sounding birds, that is the seven metres such as Gāyatrī in the form of birds, approach and join from all sides.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाचः (*vācaḥ*)—of speech
- पदवीयं (*padavīyaṃ*)—the path
- यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—by means of sacrifice
- आयन् (*āyan*)—(the discerning) reached
- ऋषिसु (*ṛṣisu*)—among the Ṛṣis
- प्रविष्टां (*praviṣṭāṃ*)—established
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that principle of speech
- अन्वविंदन् (*anvaviṃdan*)—they obtained
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that principle of speech
- आभृत्य (*ābhṛtya*)—having gathered
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many regions
- व्यदधुः (*vyadadhuḥ*)—they distributed and spread
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that
- रेभाः (*rebhāḥ*)—sounding
- सप्त (*sapta*)—the seven metres, Gāyatrī and the rest
- अभि सं (*abhi saṃ*)—surrounding
- नवंते (*navaṃte*)—join together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The discerning reached the path of the principle of speech by means of sacrifice. They obtained that principle of speech which was established in the Ṛṣis. Gathering it together, they distributed and spread it in many regions. The metres such as Gāyatrī, sounding and having the form of birds, surround it and join together.

##### English translation
(The wise) reached the path of Speech by sacrifice, they found it centred in the Rishis ; having acquired it they dispersed it in many places; the seven noisy (birds) meet together.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the vapā and purodāśa offerings of the animal sacrifice made for the deity Speech, this Ṛk यज्ञेन वाचः (*yajñena vācaḥ*) and the next Ṛk उत त्वः पश्यन् (*uta tvaḥ paśyan*) are to be recited in order as yājyā mantras, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन्निति द्वे देवीं वाचमजनयंत देवाः (*yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyanniti dve devīṃ vācamajanayaṃta devāḥ*) (Ā. 3-8).

### Printed p. 657
As stated in the Nirukta passage on the previous Ṛk, the Ṛṣis directly realised and obtained refined sentences, that is mantras, through the performance of sacrifice; that is, the mantras were seen by them through the performance of sacrifice. Those mantras, together with the seven metres such as Gāyatrī, were recited in a body and spread in all regions: this is the main purport of the Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त त्वः॒ पश्य॒न्न द॑दर्श॒ वाच॑मु॒त त्वः॑ शृ॒ण्वन्न शृ॑णोत्येनां ।  
> उ॒तो त्व॑स्मै त॒न्वं१॒॑१वि स॑स्रे जा॒येव॒ पत्य॑ उश॒ती सु॒वासाः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । त्वः । पश्यन् । न । ददर्श । वाचं । उत । त्वः । शृण्वन् । न । शृणोति । एनां ।  
> उतोइति । त्वस्यै । तन्वं । वि । सस्रे । जायाइव । पत्ये । उशती । सुवासाः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्वशब्द एकवाची । एकः । उतशब्दोऽप्यर्थे । पश्यन्नपि मनसा पर्यालोचयन्नपि वाचं न ददर्श । दर्शनफलाभावान्न पश्यति । त्व एकः श्वण्वन्नस्येनां वाचं
> न शृणोति श्रवणफलाभावात् । इत्यनेनार्धेनाविद्वानभिहितः । तृतीयपादेन विदितवेदार्थमाह । त्वस्मा एकस्मा अपि तन्नमात्मीयं शरीरं वि सस्रे । स्वयं वाग्विविधं
> गमयति । आत्मानं विवृणुते प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जायेव यथोशती संभोगं कामयमाना सुवासाः शोभनवसना जाया पत्ये भर्त्र ऋतुकाले
> संभोगार्थं स्वयमात्मानं विवृणुते तद्वदेनां पश्यति शृणोति चेति विदितवेदार्थस्य प्रशंसा । अप्येकः पश्यन्न पश्यति वाचमित्यादि निरुक्तमत्र द्रष्टव्यं । नि. १-१९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word त्व (*tva*) means "one". उत (*uta*) is in the sense of "even": one, even seeing, even considering with the mind, does not see speech, because the fruit of seeing is absent. One, even hearing, does not hear this speech, because the fruit of hearing is absent. With this half-verse the unlearned man is described. With the third pāda he speaks of one who has understood the meaning of the Veda: to another, speech spreads out her own body in various ways; that is, she herself reveals and displays herself. The illustration: as a wife who desires union, well-dressed, herself uncovers herself to her husband at the proper season for intercourse, so speech to him sees and hears: this is praise of one who knows the meaning of the Veda. The Nirukta beginning *apyekaḥ paśyanna paśyati vācam* is to be seen here: Ni. 1-19. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वः (*tvaḥ*)—one (who lacks the capacity for direct realisation)
- पश्यन् उत (*paśyan uta*)—even though seeing
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—this principle of speech
- न ददर्श (*na dadarśa*)—could not realise
- त्वः (*tvaḥ*)—another (one without the ear fit to know the hidden principle)
- एनां (*enāṃ*)—this principle of speech
- शृण्वन् उत (*śṛṇvan uta*)—even though hearing
- न शृणोति (*na śṛṇoti*)—does not hear
- उशती (*uśatī*)—desiring the company of her husband
- सुवासाः (*suvāsāḥ*)—adorned with excellent garments and the like
- जायेव (*jāyeva*)—like a wife
- पत्ये (*patye*)—to her husband, displaying her beautiful form
- त्वस्मै (*tvasmai*)—to another (one who has the fitness to realise)
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—her body
- वि सस्रे (*vi sasre*)—she reveals

### Printed p. 658

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For some who do not know how to realise this principle of Speech, it is as though they had seen it without seeing it. Others hear it with the ear, yet, gaining no benefit from what they hear, it is as though they had not heard. But only for those capable of knowing this principle does the goddess of Speech reveal her own form, as a wife who desires her husband's company displays to him her beautiful body, adorned with garments and the like.

##### English translation
One (man) indeed seeing Speech has not seen her; another (man) hearing her has not heard her ; but to another she delivers her person as a loving wife well-attired presents herself to her husband.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first half of this Ṛk the censure of the ignorant man who does not understand the meaning of the Veda is set out; in the second half, how the goddess of Speech favours the man who knows the meaning of the Veda. In explaining this Ṛk Yāska says:
अप्येकः पश्यन्न पश्यति वाचं । अपि च शृण्वन्न शृणोत्येनामित्यविद्वांसमाहार्ध० ॥ अप्येकस्मै तन्नं विसस्र इति स्वमात्मानं विवृणुते । ज्ञानं प्रकाशनमर्थस्याहानया वाचोपमोत्तमया वाचा । जायेव पत्ये कामयमाना सुवासा ऋतुकालेषु ॥ (*apyekaḥ paśyanna paśyati vācaṃ | api ca śṛṇvanna śṛṇotyenāmityavidvāṃsamāhārdha0 ‖ apyekasmai tannaṃ visasra iti svamātmānaṃ vivṛṇute | jñānaṃ prakāśanamarthasyāhānayā vācopamottamayā vācā | jāyeva patye kāmayamānā suvāsā ṛtukāleṣu ‖*) सुवासाः कल्याणवासाः । कामयमाना ऋतुकालेषु । यथा स एनां पश्यति स शृणोतीत्यर्थज्ञप्रशंसा ॥ ( (*suvāsāḥ kalyāṇavāsāḥ | kāmayamānā ṛtukāleṣu | yathā sa enāṃ paśyati sa śṛṇotītyarthajñapraśaṃsā ‖ (*) (Ni. 1-19)
Many men are accomplished in the śāstra books such as grammar and literature, and have studied the Veda. But one of them (that is, some of them), though पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति (*paśyannapi na paśyati*) the वाचं (*vācaṃ*) (Vedic sentence or mantra) — though he knows it, that is, recites it with his mouth — does not see, that is, does not understand its meaning. That is, though he recites the mantra he does not know its meaning, or has no power to grasp it. Likewise another, though he listens to the Vedic mantra, has no knowledge of its meaning. Though he has eyes he does not see; though he has ears he does not hear. This concerned those without knowledge of the Vedic meaning. As for another man who knows the Vedic meaning well, the goddess of Speech makes plain to him her own true form, that is, the hidden meaning of the Vedic mantras. How? A woman adorned with fine garments and ornaments, desiring her husband's company, at the season of union (the time of intercourse) shows the beauty of her limbs to her husband; and as the husband is then able to see the beautiful limbs of his wife at the time of love-making,

### Printed p. 659
so the hidden meanings of the mantras too become clearly visible to the man who knows the Vedic meaning. The purpose of the simile of one's own wife here is this: a man may look at many women with his eyes, yet he is able to see the limbs of his own wife well only in privacy. Likewise the man who does not know the Vedic meaning, though he has mastered many other śāstras, is not able to know the secret meanings of the Vedic mantras; but only the man who knows the Vedic meaning is able to understand the secret meanings of the mantras, as only the husband can see his own wife in privacy. To make plain the power and capacity of the one who does not know and the one who knows the Vedic meaning, the seer gave the example of husband and wife with जायेव पत्ये (*jāyeva patye*) and so explained the meaning.
Concerning the word त्वः (*tvaḥ*) Yāska explains as follows:
त्व इति विनिग्रहार्थीयं सर्वनामानुदात्तं । अर्धनामेके । (*tva iti vinigrahārthīyaṃ sarvanāmānudāttaṃ | ardhanāmeke |*) (Ni. 1-7)
The word त्वः (*tvaḥ*) is a pronoun indicating contrast. It has the anudātta accent. Some say that this word has the meaning "half".
निपात इत्येके । तत्कथमनुदात्तप्रकृति नाम स्यात् । दृष्टव्ययंतु भवति । उत त्वं सख्ये स्थिरपीतमाहुः इति द्वितीयायां । उतो त्वस्मै तन्नं १ विसस्रे इति चतुर्थ्या० । अथापि प्रथमा बहुवचने ॥ (*nipāta ityeke | tatkathamanudāttaprakṛti nāma syāt | dṛṣṭavyayaṃtu bhavati | uta tvaṃ sakhye sthirapītamāhuḥ iti dvitīyāyāṃ | uto tvasmai tannaṃ 1 visasre iti caturthyā0 | athāpi prathamā bahuvacane ‖*) (Ni. 1-8)
Some say this word is an indeclinable. That is not right, for how could a word wholly anudātta be so? Like a noun it takes case and number endings. For example, in the sentence उत त्वं सख्ये स्थिरपीतमाहुः (*uta tvaṃ sakhye sthirapītamāhuḥ*) त्वं (*tvaṃ*) is used in the accusative; in the sentence उतो त्वस्मै तन्वं १ विसस्रे (*uto tvasmai tanvaṃ 1 visasre*) त्वस्मै (*tvasmai*) is used in the dative; and the word is also used in the nominative plural, as seen in the sentence आदघ्नास उपकक्षास उ त्वे (*ādaghnāsa upakakṣāsa u tve*).
अथापि समुच्चयार्थे भवति । पर्याया इव त्वदाश्विनं । आश्विनं च पर्यायाश्चेति ॥ (*athāpi samuccayārthe bhavati | paryāyā iva tvadāśvinaṃ | āśvinaṃ ca paryāyāśceti ‖*) (Ni. 1-9)
The word is also used in the sense of conjunction ("and"). For example, in the sentence पर्याया इव त्वदाश्विनं (*paryāyā iva tvadāśvinaṃ*) the word त्वत् (*tvat*) has the meaning "and" (that of च (*ca*)).

> अधेन्वा । चरति । मायया । एषः । वाचं । शुश्रुवान् । अफलां । अपुष्पां ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वमुतैकमपि सख्ये विदुषां संसदि । या सत्कथा सा सखिकर्मत्वात्सख्यमित्युच्यते । सा च वाचा क्रियते । अतो वाक्संबंधाद्वाक्सख्ये स्थिरपीतं मधु

> विज्ञातार्थं पुरुषं वाजिनेषु । वागिनेश्वरा येषां ते वाजिना अर्था वाच
> आयुत्ताः खलु । वाग्जेयेश्वर्थेषु नापि हिन्वंति । अपिशब्दोऽन्वर्थे । केचिदपि
> नानुगच्छंति । अयमेवातिशयेन विद्वानित्यर्थः । यद्वा । वाजिनेषु सारभूतेषु
> निरूपणीयेश्वर्थेष्टेनं न हिन्वंति । न वहिः कुर्वंति । एनं पुरस्कृत्यैव सर्वं

> अफलामपुष्पां । वाचोऽर्थः पुष्पफलं । अर्थवर्जितां । यॆद्वा । वाचोऽर्थो

> श्रुतवान् स चरति । यथा वंध्या पीना गौः किं द्रोणमात्रं क्षीरं दोग्दीति मायामुत्पादयंती चरति यथा वंध्यो वृक्षोऽकाले पल्लवादियुक्तः सन्पुष्यति फलतीति
> भ्रांतिमुत्पादयंस्तिष्ठति तथा पाठं प्रब्रुवाणश्चरतीत्यर्थः । अष्टेकं वाक्सख्यॆ स्थिरपीतमित्यादि निरुक्तमनुसंधेयं ॥ नि. १-२० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains त्वमुतैकमपि (*tvamutaikamapi*): one man in the assembly of the learned. A good discourse is called friendship, because it is the act of a friend, and it is carried out by speech; hence "friendship" here is connected with speech. स्थिरपीतं (*sthirapītaṃ*): he in whose heart the honey has been firmly drunk and stays; or else, they speak of him as one of firm attainment; or else, they call him one who has understood the matter, as in the world a man who has grasped a matter is called one who has "drunk" it. Further, such a man who has understood the matter, in the वाजिनेषु (*vājineṣu*) (matters that are the province of speech, which are controlled by speech), they do not oppose; the word अपि (*api*) has the sense of "not at all": some do not even follow him; the meaning is that he alone is pre-eminently learned. Or else, in वाजिनेषु (*vājineṣu*), the essential matters to be investigated, they do not set him aside: they consider the whole Vedic meaning with him in front. Thus the knower of the meaning is praised. Next the second half censures the mere reciter. This man who has not understood the meaning goes about with a deceit that is the likeness of speech, अधेन्वा (*adhenvā*), devoid of being a milch cow, not milking desires in the places of gods and men. What is he doing? अफलामपुष्पां (*aphalāmapuṣpāṃ*): the meaning of speech is its flower and fruit; he has heard speech devoid of meaning. Or else, the meaning of speech is the sacrificial and the divine: knowledge arising in the sacrifice is याज्ञ (*yājña*), knowledge arising in the deities is दैवत (*daivata*); he has heard speech devoid of that, i.e. of knowledge of ritual and the like, merely by recitation. He goes about like a barren fat cow, creating the illusion that she will give a measure of milk, or a barren tree that stands creating the illusion that it blossoms and bears fruit, though it has shoots out of season; so he goes about declaring the text. Sāyaṇa adds that the Nirukta beginning *apyekaṃ vāksakhyè sthirapītaṃ* is to be consulted (Ni. 1-20).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वं उत (*tvaṃ uta*)—one man
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—in the company of the learned
- स्थिरपीतं (*sthirapītaṃ*)—as one of special knowledge
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—those who know say
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—such a man
- वाजिनेषु (*vājineṣu*)—in matters of speech
- न अपि हिन्वंति (*na api hinvaṃti*)—no one opposes or slights
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—the man without knowledge
- अधेन्वा (*adhenvā*)—being without sap
- अफलां (*aphalāṃ*)—fruitless
- अपुष्पां (*apuṣpāṃ*)—and flowerless
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—speech
- शुश्रुवान् (*śuśruvān*)—having heard it without meaning, by mere hearing
- मायया (*māyayā*)—with ignorance
- चरति (*carati*)—goes about

### Printed p. 661

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The learned call the man who can realise the principle of Speech one of special knowledge in the company of the learned. No one opposes or slights such a man in matters of speech. The man without knowledge, devoid of sap, hears speech that is fruitless and flowerless, merely with the ear and without meaning, and goes about full of ignorance.

##### English translation
They call one man firmly established in the friendship (of Speech), they do not exelude him from (the society of) the powerful (in knowledge); another wanders with an illusion that is barren, bearing Speech that is without fruit, without flowers.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

What was said in the previous Ṛk is here explained again more clearly. But in the first half of the Ṛk the praise of the knower of the Vedic meaning is stated, and in the second half the censure of one who is not a knower of the Vedic meaning. Yāska gives the explanation of this Ṛk as follows:
अप्येकं वाक् सख्ये स्थिरपीतमाहू रममाणं विपीतार्थं देवसख्ये रमणीये स्थान इति वा विज्ञातार्थं यन्नाप्नुवंति वाग्जेयेषु बलवत्स्वपि। अधेन्वा ह्येष चरति मायया वाक्प्रतिरूपया नास्मै कामान्दुग्धे वाग्दोह्यान् देवमानुष्यस्थानेषु यो वाचं श्रुतवान् भवत्यफलामपुष्पामित्यफलास्मा अपुष्पा वाक् भवतीति वा किंचित्पुष्पफलेति वा अर्थं वाचः पुष्पफलमाह । यज्ञदैवते पुष्पफले देवताध्यात्मे वा ॥ (*apyekaṃ vāk sakhye sthirapītamāhū ramamāṇaṃ vipītārthaṃ devasakhye ramaṇīye sthāna iti vā vijñātārthaṃ yannāpnuvaṃti vāgjeyeṣu balavatsvapi| adhenvā hyeṣa carati māyayā vākpratirūpayā nāsmai kāmāndugdhe vāgdohyān devamānuṣyasthāneṣu yo vācaṃ śrutavān bhavatyaphalāmapuṣpāmityaphalāsmā apuṣpā vāk bhavatīti vā kiṃcitpuṣpaphaleti vā arthaṃ vācaḥ puṣpaphalamāha | yajñadaivate puṣpaphale devatādhyātme vā ‖*) (Ni. 1-20)
उत त्वं सख्ये स्थिरपीतमाहुः (*uta tvaṃ sakhye sthirapītamāhuḥ*)—here the word स्थिरपीतं (*sthirapītaṃ*) means आपीतार्थं (*āpītārthaṃ*), *gṛhītārtham*: one who has taken in the meaning of the Vedic mantras, that is, one who has understood well. They say that such a man who knows the Vedic meaning is on friendly terms with the sentences, that is, the mantras. Those who know say that there is a deep friendship between the knower of the Vedic meaning and the Vedic mantras; and the knower of the Vedic meaning, understanding their meaning, plays with the Vedic mantras in joy, or roams happy-minded in friendship with the deities, or in excellent sacrificial places.
नैनं हिन्वंति अपि वाजिनेषु (*nainaṃ hinvaṃti api vājineṣu*)—वाजिनेषु (*vājineṣu*) means वाग्ज्ञेयेषु (*vāgjñeyeṣu*): in situations understood or discussed through sentences, that is, in debates and in assemblies of the learned, in critical discussions concerning sacrificial acts and the like or concerning the Self,

### Printed p. 662
no one can follow, that is, equal, this knower of the Vedic meaning. The meaning is that no one can defeat him by engaging him in debate. This is the intended explanation of the first half of this Ṛk.
Now in the second half, the man who does not know the Vedic meaning is explained by two comparisons.
अधेन्वा चरति माययैषः (*adhenvā carati māyayaiṣaḥ*)—the word धेनु (*dhenu*) means a cow that gives milk. Here the meaning is the goddess of Speech who, like a cow, milks, that is, gives, all desired objects. Whatever fruit the goddess of Speech bestows among gods, men and the rest on those who know the meaning of the Vedic mantras (वाचं (*vācaṃ*)), that fruit does not come to one who does not know the Vedic meaning. That is, the goddess of Speech does not give desired objects to him. Such a man goes about merely reciting, मायया (*māyayā*), with an artificial (unreal) pretence, sentences, that is, Vedic mantras, अधेन्वा (*adhenvā*), which like a cow do not yield the desired objects, without any use. How is that?
वाचं शुश्रुवान् अफलां अपुष्पां (*vācaṃ śuśruvān aphalāṃ apuṣpāṃ*)—this man who merely hears (without meaning) or recites the mantras has no benefit at all from mantras whose meaning he does not know, just as there is no use from a tree that has neither flower nor fruit. Here the words अफलां अपुष्पां (*aphalāṃ apuṣpāṃ*) are adjectives of the word वाचं (*vācaṃ*). वाचं (*vācaṃ*) means the Vedic mantras; what is it for Vedic mantras to have fruit or flowers? It is said: अर्थ० वाचः पुष्पफलमाह । याज्ञ दैवते पुष्पफले, देवताध्यात्मे ना (*artha0 vācaḥ puṣpaphalamāha | yājña daivate puṣpaphale, devatādhyātme nā*). For the words, that is, the Vedic mantras, the meaning itself is said to be the flowers and fruit. Or else the performance of the sacrificial act and the favour of the deity are said to be the flowers and fruit. On a tree the flower first sprouts and gradually becomes the fruit; likewise, when the sacrifice is first performed with meaningful Vedic mantras, it is in the form of a flower and turns into the fruit that is the favour of the deity: this is the intention. Or else knowledge of the Self is also said to be the flowers and fruit. From knowledge of the Vedic meaning arises knowledge of the Self. Here, to one who merely recites the Vedic mantras without meaning, the goddess of Speech (that is, the Vedic mantra) gives no desired object; and he, obtaining no flowers or fruits that should come from knowledge of the Vedic meaning (success of rites or excellent knowledge), goes about in vain. Or else the fruits he obtains, that is, the one who does not know the Vedic meaning, are very small. This is the intention of the explanation.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्ति॒त्याज॑ सचि॒विदं॒ सखा॑यं॒ न तस्य॑ वा॒च्यपि॑ भा॒गो अ॑स्ति ।

### Printed p. 663

> यदीं शृणोत्यलकं शृणोति नहि प्रवेद सुकृतस्य पंथां ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । तित्याज । सचिविदं । सखायं । न । तस्य । वाचि । अपि । भागः । अस्ति ।  
> यत् । ईं । शृणोति । अलकं । शृणोति । नहि । प्रवेद । सुकृतस्य । पंथां ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सचिविदं । शचिशब्दः सखिवाची । सखिविदं । योऽध्येता स वेदस्य सखा संपदायोच्छेदनिवारकत्वेन वेदं प्रत्युपकारित्वात् । तादृशमुपकारिणमध्येतारं वेत्तीति
> सचिवित् । तमभिज्ञं सखायमध्येतृणां पुरुषाणां सार्थबोधनेनोपकारित्वात्सखिभूतं वेदं यः पुमांस्तित्याज परार्थविनियोगेन परित्यजति ॥ त्यजतेर्लिट्यपस्पृधेथामानृचुरित्यादिना निपातितः ॥ तस्य पुरुषस्य वाचि सर्वस्यां लौकिक्यां शास्त्रीयायां वाच्यपि भागो भजनीयः कश्चिदर्थो नास्ति । ईमयं पुरुषो यद्वेदव्यतिरिक्तं शृणोति तदलकमलीकं व्यर्थमेव शृणोति । हि यस्मात्कारणात्सुकृतस्य
> पंथां पंथानं न प्रवेद । श्रद्धाराहित्यादनुष्ठानमार्गं न जानाति । तस्मात्तदीयश्रवणमपि निष्फलमित्यर्थः । द्वितीयचतुर्थपादयोरभिप्राय आरण्यके दर्शितो न
> तस्यानूक्ते भागोऽस्तीत्यादिना । ऐ. आ. ३-२-४ । तथा तं योनूत्सृजत्यभागो वाचि
> भवत्यभागो नाके तदेषाभ्युक्ता । तै- आ. २-१५-५ । इत्यध्वर्युभिश्च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सचिविदं (*sacividaṃ*): the word सचि (*saci*) means friend; so "one who knows a friend". He who studies is the friend of the Veda, because by preventing the interruption of the tradition he does it a service. The one who knows such a benefactor, the student, is सचिवित् (*sacivit*). The man who abandons (तित्याज (*tityāja*)) that knowing friend, the Veda, which is a friend to students by teaching them the meaning, by applying it to another's purpose, has no share, no part to be enjoyed, वाचि (*vāci*), in all speech, worldly and scriptural. Whatever this man hears apart from the Veda, he hears as अलकं (*alakaṃ*), false, in vain. For he does not know the path of the well-doer (सुकृतस्य पंथां (*sukṛtasya paṃthāṃ*)): lacking faith, he does not know the way of performance; hence his hearing too is fruitless. The sense of the second and fourth pādas is shown in the Āraṇyaka by *na tasyānūkte bhāgo 'sti* and so on (Ai. Ā. 3-2-4); likewise by the Adhvaryus: तं योनूत्सृजत्यभागो वाचि भवत्यभागो नाके तदेषाभ्युक्ता (*taṃ yonūtsṛjatyabhāgo vāci bhavatyabhāgo nāke tadeṣābhyuktā*) (Tai. Ā. 2-15-5).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सचिविदं (*sacividaṃ*)—one who knows the value of a friend, that is, the value of speech in the form of a friend
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—the man who is a friend to the Vedic mantras
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- तित्याज (*tityāja*)—abandons (neglects)
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that man
- वाचि (*vāci*)—in speech (in conduct)
- भागः (*bhāgaḥ*)—any honourable part
- न अस्ति (*na asti*)—there is not
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this man
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever speech
- शृणोति (*śṛṇoti*)—he hears
- अलीकं (*alīkaṃ*)—falsely (uselessly)
- शृणोति (*śṛṇoti*)—he hears
- हि (*hi*)—because
- सुकृतस्य (*sukṛtasya*)—of those whose deeds are good
- पंथां (*paṃthāṃ*)—the path
- न प्रवेद (*na praveda*)—he does not know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the conduct of the man who abandons the man who knows the value of speech in the form of a friend, the friend of the Vedic mantras, there is no honourable or true part. Whatever speech this man hears, hearing it is of no use to him. Since he does not know the path of those whose deeds are good, it is in vain.

### Printed p. 664

##### English translation
He who has abandoned the friend who knows the duty of a friend, in
his Speech there is not a particle (of/sense); what he hears, he hears amiss;
for he knows not the path of righteousness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The words of a man who knows the Vedas and the meaning of the Vedic mantras, and who is like a friend to them, are scorned in neglect by some other man. In the speech and conduct of that man there is no excellent element at all. All that he says and hears is untrue. He has neither inclination nor faith for good deeds. He does not follow the path of good men. This is the main purport.

#### Ṛk 7

> अ॒क्ष॒ण्वंतः॒ कर्ण॑वंतः॒ सखा॑यो मनोज॒वेष्वस॑मा बभूवुः ।  
> आ॒द॒घ्नास॑ उ पक॒क्षास॑ उत्वे ह्र॒दा इ॑व॒ स्नात्वा॑ उ त्वे ददृश्रे ॥

> अक्षण्वंतः । कर्णवंतः । सखायः । मनःजवेषु । असमाः । बभूवुः ।  
> आदघ्नासः । उपकक्षासः । ऊं इति । त्वे । प्रदाः इव । स्नात्वाः । ऊं इति । त्वे ।
